It is only recently that they have entered our forests. Our healers have been unable to heal him. Please do what you can." Eleana sat on the side of the pallet and pulled the blanket down to assess the damage. This child had suffered far worse than any of her friends and Eleana was amazed that he was still alive. She found a small area beneath his left collarbone that was injury free and lay her palm on his chilled skin. She searched his body for internal damage and shuddered. A moment later, she sighed and removed her hand. -Ky II, tell Aemir to send for Tobit and Karnak. I will need you here as well. See if you can bring something that you can burn things in safely.- Eleana returned her hand to the boy's shoulder. "I will need you to bring Ky II to me. He knows what I need. I will be able to keep him alive until you return." The female left without comment. She returned a couple minutes later with Ky II who carried a metal box with him. "Taelann sent word to Karnak and is getting Tobit. Is he fertilized?" "Yes. Thank you for making me rest last night. Even with Tobit, I will need all my strength to save him." "What do you mean by fertilized?" the female asked. "When thantors kill, the bodies they don't consume, they fertilize. Aprean has at least three larvae within him. Karnak will be able to remove them while Tobit and I keep him alive. It's not a pretty sight. You may wish to wait in the next room." The female raised her chin, and stated, "I am not leaving my son. I trust you will do what you need to heal him, but I will stay with him while you do it." She stepped forward and lay her hand on Eleana's shoulder. "I am not without some magic of my own. I will provide you with the strength to finish this task." "I guess we should warn you," Ky II whispered as he sat on the pallet across the room, "Karnak is a thantor. He will be here to help, not harm."

The female shuddered, but remained determined to stay. Tobit arrived first, materializing in the room in front of Ky II. "An empty pallet? You asked me here to heal a bed?" Ky II shook his head and grinned. "Behind you." Tobit turned and looked at the elf lying on the pallet across the room. "It looks like he was playing in a wheat thrasher. What have you found, Eleana?" "Larvae. Karnak is on the way," Eleana said. Tobit turned to the female standing behind Eleana and bowed. "Tobit at your service. The child will be fine soon." The female bowed her head slightly, "Relta. Thank you for coming." Aprean convulsed violently under Eleana's hand. "It won't last much longer," Eleana whispered to him. Tobit surveyed the small room before addressing Relta. "Please, wait over there." He waited until Relta was seated beside Ky II. Then he slid in behind Eleana and completely removed the blanket covering Aprean. "Karnak will need to be where you are, Eleana. Move down to his feet. I'll take the upper part." Tobit took Eleana's dagger and placed it beside the child before sitting on the pallet at the boy's head. He noticed Relta's eyes widen at the sight of the blade. "It looks worse than it is, Relta. We will need to open his abdomen for Karnak to remove the larvae. We've done this before with some very good friends of ours. Your son will be fine," Tobit finished as Karnak arrived in the room. "This had best be important, young ones. Ky decided to take this opportunity to run off to Vienna rather than finish our task." "Larvae. At least three," Eleana said. Karnak hissed. "My own blood causing me such problems." He turned to Ky II. "Is your flame hot enough to incinerate them quickly and completely?" Ky II nodded, saying, “Yes.” "Sit here on the floor beside him. Let's finish this quickly. The scent of so many elves is making me hungry." Tobit used Eleana's knife and carefully cut open Aprean's abdomen. Karnak spread the wound wide with one clawed hand as the other entered the young elf's body and searched. "Keep him alive," Karnak hissed as he pulled the first larva out and dropped it into the box. Ky II's flames reduced it to ash instantly. The process was repeated twice more. "They said there were only three!" Relta exclaimed as Karnak

carefully immersed his hand into the child's abdomen for the fourth time. "Don't believe all that is said to you," Karnak answered as he pulled the fourth larva from the child and dropped it into the box. "I am done," he hissed as he vanished. "He gets all the fun and we are left with cleaning up the mess," Tobit said. Ky II laughed as he picked up the box. "Will you be joining us in the common hall, Tobit?" "No, I have a few other things to tend to. Feel free to send for me whenever you have need though," he added smiling. By the time Ky II had left the room, Aprean was healed and sleeping quietly. "I've put a sleep spell on him. He will not wake for a couple days. He'll need that time to regain his strength." Tobit smiled at Relta, then vanished. "Tha..." Relta stuttered. "Do they always leave that fast?" she asked Eleana. "You get used to it after a while," Eleana answered, smiling. "Do you wish me to help you clean him?" Relta smiled for the first time that day. "No, young one. You have done far more than I had expected. Please join your friends." Relta bowed before Eleana. "Anything you need from us will be provided." "Thank you, Lady Relta," Eleana muttered, blushing slightly. "Where is the common hall from here?" Relta guided her to the door. "Go straight until you reach the wide path, then turn right. It's not far." Eleana smiled and left to join the rest of the group. When she found them, Ky II was telling the others of Aprean's healing. To her amazement, she did not hear a single exaggeration in his tale. Several hours later, a group of elves arrived carrying provisions and clothing for the children. "I know you requested hides," Relta explained. "But you have given us back the only living heir of the former elders. These guards will see that you are cleaned up and make sure the clothing fits you well." "Bah!" Brek exclaimed. "More water to make Brek suffer!" Ky II ignited his left hand, "I could burn the dirt and gore from you if you'd prefer." Brek glared across the table at Ky II a moment. Then, he lowered his gaze and shook his head. "Which elf leads Brek to water this time?" he muttered. All, including Brek, laughed as they were led away to be

made ready for the next portion of their journey. Near sunset, they were ready to depart the village. Relta insisted that they allow a squad of elven hunters go with them to the edge of the Eldar forest. The march to the Western Wilds went quickly and the children set up camp at the base of the cliff for the night. The four elves kept watch while the others slept. By mid-morning of the next day, they were climbing the road that led to the town of Cragsguard.

10 With the exception of the outer wall, which Stumpy promised to rebuild, all damage from the recent earthquake had been repaired. The temporary shelters within the courtyard of Maltar Manor remained. Lord Maltar and his wife invited the townspeople to schedule times to use them as a means to take a short holiday from their normal lives, and enjoy the hospitality of the Maltar family. The townspeople warmly accepted their invitation and the three shelters were already booked for the next few months. Archos, Delmaria, and Taelann sat at the table closest to the door enjoying a late afternoon meal at the Cracked Anvil. They were immersed in the quiet conversations and laughter that filled the common room. Earlier in the day, Ky's triplets and their companions arrived in town safely, much to the relief of Taelann. After the meal, Archos and Delmaria returned to the farm. Taelann had decided to stay in town and moved to the bar to visit with Stan. A few hours later, Stumpy trudged down the stairs and through the room muttering into his beard. Without a word to anyone, he marched through the door and disappeared into the dusk-darkened streets. Moments after his departure, the dwarven lass Stumpy had brought to town entered the room from the stairs and sat at the small table in the back corner. Stan glanced at her and frowned. He placed an ale on the bar in front of an elderly man and walked to the back table. "I'm sorry, lass, but this table is reserved. Find another seat and I'll bring your dinner out to you in a moment."

"I like this table. Ye can find another for whoever it is reserved for. Bring me my meal." "I know that you are Lord Stumpy's guest and I admire and respect him greatly, but, if you do not find another seat, your welcome here will be over." Stan stood straight and tall, and crossed his arms across his chest. "This is my grandson's table. It has been his table for over two-thousand years and will remain so." "I am Mena, daughter of Brenson and Maasena, Lord and Lady of the Clan of Deep Stone. No barkeeper's whelp will deny me that which I want. This table is mine now. Bring me my meal!" Angry voices and shouts filled the common room for several moments. Stan stood glaring down on the dwarf until the shouting ceased. "If my grandson arrives and finds his seat taken, he does not stay. But before he leaves, he has been known to kill anyone stupid enough to sit at his table. I truly hope he decides to do that to you." Stan turned on his heel and stomped away. "You will receive no meals here." "If you don't bring me my dinner," the dwarf shouted, "I'll have Lord Stumpy kill you!" The common room fell silent for a moment, then, as if signaled, filled with derisive laughter. Tears of rage filled the young dwarf's eyes as she ran back to her room upstairs. Stan left his friend, Oren, in charge of the inn. "I'll be at the farm if you need me," he explained. Taelann left the bar and joined him.

11 Eleana surrendered the lead to Ky II. She knew her father wanted him to take care of this part of the quest. Ky II led the group directly to the blacksmith's stall upon entering Cragsguard. All but Ky II waited just under the edge of the roof as the heat from the forges assailed them. Ky II entered looking for the blacksmith. The blacksmith, a powerfully built man with short dark- brown hair, smiled as Ky II approached him. He lay his hammer on the anvil and wiped the sweat from his hands on his heavy leather apron before greeting the young elf. "Lad, it's fine seeing ya," he said, his deep voice thundering over the roar of the forge. "How be yer father these days?" Ky II grinned, "He's well, Banen. How are you?" "Couldn't be better! Come let's talk where I can hear ye," he added guiding Ky II back to the square. "What can I do for ye?" "My father wishes you to make some swords for my friends," Ky II answered nodding to the group. "We will all need practice wooden swords as well." Banen's large hand wiped sweat from his brow as he looked at the group of children waiting nearby. "How many of them there tykes be needing the real thing?" he asked. "Five," Ky II replied. "I'll tell ye what I'll do, lad. I'll make ye five of the best swords ye ever laid eyes on if you'll do that elven thing with one I made for meself recently. I'll even throw in the practice blades made special so they are like the real ones." Ky II pulled a handful of small gemstones from his pouch.

"Take these as well, Banen. My father will blame me for cheating you if you don't." Banen laughed, "Aye, I will take them. It would nae be good to anger your father! Let's get to work, shall we?" Ky II introduced Banen to Simon, Micah, Little Ky, Brek and Aemir. Banen took them one at a time to his forge. He used a length of raw-hide to measure their arms before selecting the steel to make the blades. As the steel heated in the forge, he had them try sample hilts until they found one that fit comfortably in their hand. As Banen placed the steel needed for the swords in the forge, Ky II, Eleana and Tal began to enchant Banen's blade. They sat near the square under the shade of the blacksmith's roof. Ky II lay the sword on the ground then placed his palm on the blade near the hilt. His hand flamed softly with a faint yellowish glow as he slowly heated the blade. Eleana immediately began tracing a rune on the heated section with her dagger while muttering the Elvish incantation that would allow the sword to accept her magic. When she finished, Ky II turned the sword over and they repeated the tracing on the reverse side. Tal traced his rune beneath Eleana's, grinning as he waited for Ky II to finish heating the blade. Unlike Eleana, he sang softly to the sword while he worked with his dagger. The third rune traced on the blade consisted of a combined effort of all three elves. Ky II and Eleana carved the complex rune as Tal sang the incantation. The humming of the sword as it drank in the magic seemed to harmonize with Tal. Finally, Ky II placed his enchantment near the end of the blade. Like his brother, he sang his enchantment, but much quieter, almost a whisper. Ruby flames danced across his rune when he finished. When they finished, they took the sword to Banen. His eyes widened and he smiled as he took the hilt into his hand. The sword hummed with recognition and power. The elves taught him the command words that would invoke the enchantments. "I feel I be cheatin' ye, lad," Banen roared above the furnace. "My services are free to ye anytime ye ever be needin' 'em from now on." Ky II grinned and shrugged. "A well made sword is easy to enchant, Banen. How are the others coming?" Banen presented the three finished swords to Ky II. "I hope they are to your satisfaction, lad." As Banen continued to work on the fourth sword, Ky II tested the balance and edge of the first three. Banen watched him out of the corner of his eye and did not bother to disguise his pride as the young elf nodded his approval of each of them.

"Yarlen!" Banen bellowed as he fitted the fourth blade into its hilt. A younger man stepped from the back area of the smithy. He resembled Banen though he had not acquired Banen's powerful build yet. "Yes, Father." "Take these four swords and those five lads to Casey. Have him make sheaths for these." Banen separated one of the swords from the others. "Have him make two for this here blade. The last sword ain't ready yet, tell him." He handed Yarlen a few of the gems Ky II had given him. "Use this to pay him." "Come along, lads," Yarlen shouted as he strode from the smithy into the square. An hour later, Banen stood before the group beaming at them. "Ye come back to visit me when ye can. Good luck to ye." Ky II handed Banen a scrap of parchment. "Give that to Grandfather Stan. Consider it an extra bonus for the swords," he added grinning. "Aye, lad! Thank ye much." Ky II led the group through town to Maltar Manor. The guard at the gate showed them their quarters and told them how to get to the dinner hall. Micah took his sword with him to dinner. He had never held a sword before, much less owned one and his fingers constantly traced the fine leather of the sheath and smooth steel of the hilt. "How is it that the wooden swords are heavier than the steel ones?" he asked. "The practice swords are weighted," Tal explained. "That way, when you use the real one it will feel more comfortable in your hand." "Your weapon has to be a part of you," Ky II added. He glanced at Micah's hand on the hilt and grinned. "We'll see if you cherish that as much tomorrow after we finish practicing." The long walk to town and the time spent near the hot forges had exhausted the group. Shortly after their evening meal, they retired to their rooms. None had any problem finding sleep that night. Well before dawn, Ky II woke and searched the manor supply room until he found seven padded tunics used for training squires and pages. He returned to the barracks and woke the others. All but Eleana were instructed to wear the tunics. Eleana's job would be to heal any injuries that occurred during training. Ky II led the group to the practice yard and sparred one-on-one with Simon, Little Ky, Brek, Micah and Aemir to determine their needs. Simon proved to be very practiced in defensive maneuvers

though lost his sword whenever he tried to counter an attack. Little Ky showed minimal skill but lacked the strength to be effective. Brek attacked ferociously, but had no concept of defense. Aemir also showed some skill in attacking but lacked in defense. Micah could barely hold his sword. Ky II's shoulders sagged as he frowned at the group. "Looks like I have about three weeks left to live," he muttered. "When dad comes to check on your training, he's gonna kill me." Tal put his hand on Ky II's shoulder. "From the looks of things, they can't get any worse. Anything you teach them will be an improvement." Ky II looked at Micah. "Tal, take Micah to the target dummies. There's no use trying to spar with him yet. Keep him over there until he can hold on to his weapon." "What about breakfast?" Micah asked. Ky II shook his head. "You will train before meals. When the morning session is done, you'll get breakfast. Then you will have an hour off and we start the next session. When that is done, you get lunch. One hour after lunch will be the third session and the last will be one hour after dinner. That way, you won't leave your food all over the ground. It will stay in your stomach where it's supposed to be." The first and second days went well. Tal spent his time working with Micah and helping Ky II demonstrate the moves he wanted to teach. At the end of the day, Ky II would run a three lap race around the yard. The last one finished had to clean the tunics before going to sleep that night. The next day started out well. Then Aemir did not show up for any practices after breakfast. "Training with those others is useless," he told Ky II when he returned at the end of the day. "Half of them couldn't kill a mudworm. The longer I train with them, the worse I'm going to get. Besides, you don't know how to train anything." By the time Tal and Eleana pulled Ky II from Aemir, Aemir had suffered a broken nose, several broken ribs and more than a few burns. Ky II glared at the unconscious high-elf a moment before pushing his siblings away and storming from the barracks. The next morning, Ky II left Aemir sleeping when he woke the others. He glanced at Aemir and grinned before leading the rest to the practice grounds. Micah started the morning with Little Ky who was given the chore to teach Micah the maneuvers he had learned. The second hour Micah worked with Simon to learn defensive techniques. Tal spent the entire session with Brek teaching control as Ky II alternated with Little Ky and Simon. They found Aemir when they went in for breakfast. An officer of the town guard stood over him and supervised as Aemir

scrubbed the hallway floors. "Since you don't want to train with us," Ky II said, "I thought you'd like to train as a chamber maid." Ky II grinned and walked into the mess hall. Ky II ran one more practice session that day and gave them the rest of the day off. They were so tired and sore that they could do little more than sit around and talk. When Ky II woke them the next morning, only Simon, Tal and Eleana followed him to the training grounds. The rest claimed they would rather scrub floors. Eleana hesitated, wanting to return to the others to find out why they did not come with Ky II. She noticed the hunched shoulders and bowed head of her brother as well as the fact that he had closed his mind to his siblings, and decided she would be needed for healing a lot today. With a sigh, she quickened her pace to catch up with the group, planning to learn the reasons for the others not coming at breakfast. Simon followed a couple steps behind Ky II, knowing his friend felt betrayed and deserted. Normally, Ky II's movements were smooth and relaxed. Simon noted that his friend walked stiffly, his muscles tightened almost to the point of trembling. He thought about telling Ky II why the others had not come, but could not bring himself to do that. Ky II would kill Aemir without a thought. Simon doubted he would have time to remind Ky II that killing Aemir would destroy Taelann as well. As they approached the training grounds, Simon glanced at the window in the barracks. He saw Aemir watching him. He also saw the knife the high-elf twirled in his fingers. That knife meant nothing to Simon, but it would mean a great deal to the three that stayed behind. He entered the training grounds hoping he could concentrate enough to learn something. He decided to find Taelann or Archos when the session ended instead of going to breakfast. One of them would know what to do. In the barracks, Aemir watched the small group until it entered the training grounds and could no longer be seen from the window. He saw Simon's glance and made sure his knife could be seen by the disobedient human. Micah, Little Ky, and Brek sat around a small table that occupied the corner of the room. Occasionally, they would glance at their practice tunics and swords, then to Aemir's back before returning to staring at the tabletop. Aemir turned from the window to look at the three huddled around the table, his long-knife twirling between his fingers. He walked to the door and sheathed the blade. “You three, come with me,” he ordered. “Brek not want to scrub floors,” muttered the goblin. “Stupid goblin, just be quiet and come on,” Aemir stated as

he stepped into the hallway. Aemir led them to the town library and had them sit on the bench set up outside Daelann's shrine. “Stay there until I return,” he ordered before stepping into the shrine. The three sat quietly for a while, afraid they might be overheard by Aemir. Little Ky noticed Micah trembling and placed his arm over his friend's shoulders. “I'm scared,” Micah whispered. “I don't ever want to sleep again.” “I was thinking of sneaking back to the farm,” Little Ky replied quietly. “He won't be able to do anything to us there.” Brek nodded. “Be quiet!” Aemir ordered, his face glaring at them from the pulled-aside curtain of the shrine. “I won't be much longer. Sit still and wait.” He disappeared again into the shrine. They sat quietly on the bench a while longer. None of them heard Taelann approach them, or dared to look up when he stopped in front of them. “What brings you three here this morning?” Taelann asked, smiling. Micah and Little Ky remained silent. Finally, Brek pointed to Daelann's shrine. Taelann studied them for a moment. He noted their fear and discomfort. “Is Aemir in there?” he asked. Brek nodded. “You three go to the Cracked Anvil and wait for me there. Don't worry. Nothing bad will happen to you, I promise.” Taelann followed them to the street outside the library then watched as they walked down the main road towards the Cracked Anvil. He waited until they were well on their way before vanishing.

12 Stumpy felt much better as he returned to the Cracked Anvil. He had spent the last couple hours working with the stone wall that had collapsed during the earthquake. The stone exhilarated him. He now looked forward to a cold ale or two. He imagined the wretchedly spoiled child in his care would be sleeping by now. He entered the common room and strode to the bar. "Evening, lad," he said as he chose a stool. "Where might Stan be hiding?" Oren related what had happened earlier that night then said, "Stan and Lord Taelann went to the farm. I imagine you'll find him there." "Bah!" Stumpy slammed his fist onto the bar. "I had me heart set on a cold ale. That whelp is nae helping herself with her attitude." The rest of his words were muttered into his beard as he headed to the kitchen. He found Stan with Delmaria and Archos seated at one of the two tables in the old council room. He yanked on his beard and approached the table slowly. "I've heard, lad," he said before Stan could start. "Please accept my apology. 'Twas me own big mouth that got me into this in the first place." "It wasn't you who insulted me and my grandson," Stan said. "That she-demon is the cause of my anger, not you. Sit down and tell us what happened." "It would be told better with one of your ales in me hand," Stumpy offered hopefully. "Besides, the whelp needs to be fed. I'll see

that she has better manners this time." Stan stood. "This could be quite entertaining. I'll be there in a moment." Stumpy mumbled something under his breath and returned to the Cracked Anvil. Stan thanked Archos and Delmaria for their company and followed Stumpy through the portal. He greeted Oren then waited behind the bar. Stumpy had already gone upstairs to retrieve Mena. His voice could be heard as he tongue-lashed the child. Several moments later, she came down the steps with Stumpy close behind. She started to head to the small table reserved for Ky, but this time, Stumpy's firm grasp of her earlobe stopped her. She yelped as he yanked her in the direction of the bar. "To the bar with ye, lass. Your apology best be true," Stumpy added as he guided her through the room. She glanced at Stan then turned to say something to Stumpy. "Don't be looking at me. Stan's the one that will be feeding ya if he has a mind to." She glared at Stumpy a moment then turned and muttered an apology to Stan. Stumpy waited until Stan nodded, then took her to a table. "This seat here will do ye fine, lass, and I'll not be hearing any whining from ye either." Stumpy roughly pressed her onto the bench then returned to the bar. Stan placed a cold ale on the bar in front of Stumpy and asked Oren to serve Mena her meal. "I believe you promised me a tale," he said as Stumpy emptied the mug of ale. "Ain't much of a tale, but I'll tell ye anyway." Stumpy waited until Stan refilled his mug, then began. "When that earthquake hit the other night, I went to check on the local dwarven clan. They insisted that I attend a feast for what I did for Maasena and the other women and children of the clan when Rachk'sha pressed the men into service. Good dwarven ale loosened me tongue and the tales of great deeds done by The Nine filled the hall. Brenson and Maasena decided then and there that my training their daughter would be a boon to their liking. I swear by the Great Mother Stone, the ale they served me loosened my wits and I agreed. The lass seemed so sweet and charming at the feast." Stumpy glanced at Mena, then mumbled, "If only I'd have known..." Stan refilled Stumpy's mug and said, "She can stay. I do hope you keep a good collar on her though. I'll not have her sitting at Ky's table." "I hear ye. I'll be giving her a lesson or two on courtesy before ye see her in the morning." When Mena finished her meal, Stumpy took her back

upstairs. After several hours of lecture, he locked her in her room and returned to the bar to quench his thirst. "It may be a while 'ere that wall be finished. Next to your ale, working with that stone is the one thing that will give me pleasure." Stan laughed, "With the ward up, the wall is really unnecessary. I doubt anyone will mind you taking your time with it."

13 Ghostspawn walked through the night, headed west. Near dawn, he approached the ruins of a town. The near-total destruction of the stone walls and buildings fascinated him. He could not imagine the amount of power required to destroy something that large so completely. He spent hours searching through the rubble, kicking aside burnt boards and charred bones. He found nothing of value until he searched the southern end of the town. The rubble there appeared to be higher quality than anything he had seen thus far. As he rummaged through crumbled marble and broken glass, he discovered a few gems and several decent weapons. He spent hours admiring the gems. They were larger than any he had ever seen before, their facets sparkling in the late afternoon sunlight. By the time the sun had set, he had acquired four sapphires, three diamonds, seven emeralds and two rubies. He found a belt with pouches on the sides and packed the gems in them. Then he went to a small grove of trees north of the town to rest. He sat through the night staring at the scar in the field at the bottom of the hill, yearning to be able to cause such destruction. Somehow, he decided, he would acquire the power. The cat-god had been correct. There was nothing special the way he was now, just a goblin who would not die. By the time dawn's first breath chilled the air, he knew what he must do. When he finished his search of the ruins, he would find someone to teach him magic. Then he would command real power. This new motivation excited him. He returned to the southern end of town and searched with enthusiasm. First, he replaced

his short-sword with a long-sword adorned with a gem-encrusted hilt. Its leather scabbard had tooled dragons decorating its length. This, he thought, was the weapon of a god. Afterwards, he discarded his rags and replaced them with a black satin tunic and leggings. The lack of more gems in the rubble proved the only disappointment. Content that he salvaged all he could from the ruins, he continued his westward journey, intent on finding one who would teach him magic. Knowing if he could not entice them, he would force them. He traveled through the cool of night, finding out-of-the-way spots to hide and rest during the days. Occasionally, he would encounter others, mostly humans. He avoided groups, staying out of sight until they had passed. Those that traveled alone, he killed and robbed. By the end of the first week, he had a pouch full of gold coins and an ample supply of fresh meat. By this time, he was walking through an ancient forest. Stunted undergrowth sparsely covered the areas between the giant trunks of the trees. Dim light during the day contrasted with the pitch black of night. He continued his pattern of walking during the night. There were no paths or roads to keep track of and his night vision kept him from stumbling into trees or shrubberies. Besides, he felt as if he were being led by an unseen guide. He sought magic and if someone could guide him through this forest, they had magic. He embraced the nudges that corrected his path, and continued walking through the night. Two nights later, Ghostspawn followed the guide to a clearing. He stopped inside the fringe of the forest. Centered in the clearing, a cabin waited. Its rotting log-walls barely supported the sagging roof. The two windows visible from his vantage had been boarded up from the inside. A tattered animal hide covered the doorway. He crept back into the forest, but stayed close enough to the clearing to watch the cabin. Sitting with his back against a tree, he pulled a hunk of meat from his pack and absently chewed on it while considering the situation. The cabin's appearance disappointed him. He had expected something far more elegant from someone with the power to guide his footsteps from three days walk away. Nearly an hour passed as he watched the house. The meat from the forearm he chose to eat had long since given way to the bone. As he began to suck the marrow from the bone, the hide covering the doorway jerked to one side and a woman stepped into the clearing. She wore a tattered dark brown tunic over a pair of faded, thread-bare, red leggings. Her white hair was matted and disheveled. In her left hand she carried the lower portion of a human

leg covered in mold and showing signs of decay. She took several steps towards the forest where Ghostspawn sat. Scratching her crotch with her free hand, she stated, "You intrigue me. How is it that after following my summons all this way, you can choose to sit out there in the forest?" For a few minutes she stood nibbling on the toes. She continued, "Come in. If you chose to follow my summons, then you must wish to speak. I'll not be speaking in this cursed sunlight!" She took a healthy bite from the calf and returned to the cabin. Ghostspawn waited a few moments, then tossed the bone aside and followed her. She knew magic, and he would have all she knew, one way or another.

14 Ky watched Herr William from his table in the back of the room. The walk to Cragsguard had taken twenty years of age from Herr William. Ky also noted that Herr William looked happy. The magic of the Cracked Anvil enveloped the old choir master like a warm blanket, welcoming him, and warming him. Ky finished his meal and walked to the bar. “Thank you, Grandfather,” he said, placing the emptied plate and mug on the bar. He tilted his head slightly, then added, “I'll be in for breakfast tomorrow.” Stan smiled, “It will be a pleasure to see you, as always. Maybe we'll get a chance to talk a bit.” Ky nodded, “If not at breakfast, sometime tomorrow.” He turned to the Old Man and Herr William. “Come, I will introduce you to Little Ky's mother. Rooms are ready for you at the farm.” “The farm?” Herr William asked. “I would love to see that. Little Ky spoke of it so often, I feel I should know it by heart.” “It's changed a little since he was in Vienna with you, on the inside anyway,” Ky explained, grinning. Herr William and the Old Man finished their ale, then followed Ky into the kitchen. He showed them how to operate the portal, then stepped through ahead of them. The council room was empty when they arrived. They followed Ky through the small parlor and into the kitchen. “Have a seat. I'll let Illya know you're here.” Herr William sighed as he let his gaze settle on every detail

of the room. “It's exactly as I envisioned it,” he muttered. The Old Man settled into a chair at the table and watched his friend. He thought Herr William might have difficulty adjusting to this rustic world of no electricity. Seeing Herr William react to the farm changed his mind. Herr William explored the room beginning with the counter top along the front wall of the kitchen. His eyes shone brightly and he had an impish grin on his face. He held up one of the wooden bowls and showed it to the Old Man. “Handmade,” he muttered. “Isn't it wonderful!” The Old Man simply smiled and nodded as Herr William continued along the wall to the water pump. “A real water pump!” he exclaimed. “Trees be fallin'! What else would it be?” The Old Man laughed, “Maybe a chrome-plated faucet with hot and cold running water. Herr William, this is Daphnia. She lives here and helps keeps things running smoothly. Daphnia, this is Herr William from Vienna.” “It is an honor to meet you, Frau Daphnia,” Herr William said bowing. “Nice meetin' you too, Herr William. But I be just 'Daphnia.' There ain't no 'frau' part, whatever that is.” “And I am just 'William,' now. I see no further need for the 'Herr' part.” “Trees be fallin'! Have a seat and I'll be makin' ya some tea.” Herr William had just seated himself beside the Old Man when Ky returned with Illya. He stood again as Ky introduced them. “Herr William, this is Illya, Little Ky's mother. Illya, this is Micah's father, Herr William, who helped take care of Little Ky while he was trapped in Vienna.” Illya smiled and hugged Herr William. “Welcome to the farm. I hope you plan on staying awhile. I'd love to hear about my son's stay in Vienna.” “I'm not sure where I'm staying yet,” Herr William explained. “But while I'm here, please call me 'William.'” “Until you are sure of where you are staying, you will stay here at the farm,” Illya said smiling. “He has a place in Cragsguard,” Ky explained as he sat. “It's the old bakery beside the alchemist's shop. It's been empty about thirty years.” Seeing Illya frown, he added, “Another couple days won't matter.”

“I would love to stay!” William said. “If there is room, of course.” “There always be bein' room here,” Daphnia explained as she placed the tea on the table. “People show up from all over the place and there always be bein' room.” The conversation at the table lasted until dawn. Outside, thunderstorms rolled over the farmhouse, pelting the roof with heavy rains. The storm's best efforts did little to dampen the spirits within the kitchen. Stories of Little Ky were traded. Finally, William began to show signs of fatigue, though he wished to visit longer. “Today is not the last day ever,” the Old Man laughed. “You can continue with your visiting tomorrow and the next day as well.” Ky and Illya showed William and the Old Man where their rooms were. “I'll bring Micah here tomorrow,” Ky promised. “I'm sure you'll want to see him.” “And Little Ky as well?” William asked. Ky grinned and nodded. “Sure. I think they all could use a break from training.” “All?” William asked. “You'll see tomorrow,” Ky said as he turned away. William closed the door to his room as Ky went through the portal to the Cracked Anvil. Ky found the common room empty. It was early yet and the storm still dumped heavy rain on the town. He walked to his table and sat. He knew Stan would bring him breakfast soon and he looked forward to talking with his adopted grandfather. He leaned back in his corner, closed his eyes and relaxed. A few moments later, he heard footsteps coming down the stairs. He ignored them. Very few people noticed him and those that did knew better than to disturb him. The footsteps stopped near his table. “If I can't sit there, neither can you,” a female voice said. He opened his eyes in time to see a young female dwarf grab his ankle and yank him off the bench. Thunderous footsteps hurried down the steps. “An elven freak,” Mena spat, “sitting where the daughter of the Lord of Deep Stone can't sit. I'll not have it!” Stumpy burst into the common room and froze, his hands yanking at his beard as he muttered incoherently. He watched Ky slowly stand, the elf glaring at Mena.

Mena ignored Ky's glare and frowned at Stumpy. “What are ye muttering about, Lord Stumpy? Imagine if Stan had seen this derelict street waif sitting at his grandson's table, he'd have been very upset.” She turned on Ky and added, “An ugly elven freak like ye should have been killed at birth!” “K-Ky...” Stumpy stammered. “I thought dwarven courtesy dictated an introduction before insults where traded,” Stan said from beside the bar, not bothering to hide his smile. “Stumpy,-” Ky started to say. “Lord Stumpy to you, elf!” Ky gestured slightly with his hand and Mena flew across the common room and crashed into the table near the door. “Stumpy,” Ky whispered. “Who is this soon-to-be dead dwarf?” “Please,” Stumpy muttered, “I beg ye nae to kill the lass. She is the daughter of Brenson and Maasena of Deep Stone. They left the lass in my care for training.” Stumpy followed Ky across the room, his hands absently yanking out fistfuls of beard. “I guess I need to talk to them,” Ky said as he sent Mena through the door into the muddy square outside the Cracked Anvil. “Tell them I'm coming.” “I'll be takin' the lass with me,” Stumpy pleaded. Ky shook his head. “I'm not done with her yet. She'll be alive when we get there.” Ky gestured again and Mena sputtered as she rolled face first into a deeper puddle of mud. “If you hurry,” Ky added as he stepped outside the door. A couple more handfuls of Stumpy's beard fell to the floor as he vanished. Ky walked to Mena, grabbed a handful of her hair and raised her head. A dagger appeared in his other hand and he grinned as Mena's eyes widened. “Silence,” Ky commanded. Mena struggled to speak, but the command word Ky had spoken denied her access to her voice. Ky lowered the dagger to Mena's throat, then slowly shaved her beard. “Now, little dwarf, you are a freak as well. You will never be able to regrow your beard.” Ky tilted his head slightly and smiled at her. “Stumpy will be happy. You are more fun to keep alive, now.” Stan wiped a mug clean as he stood at the doorway

watching his grandson. His smile broadened as Ky shoved Mena's face into the mud again, holding her there for a moment before vanishing. He returned to the bar and placed the mug on a shelf. “It's going to be a good day,” he thought as he wiped down the bar.

15 Brenson and Maasena had just settled down to their breakfast in the great hall of Deep Stone when Stumpy appeared before them. Brenson noted the condition of Stumpy's beard and began to rise. Before he could inquire about the cause of Stumpy's distress, Mena appeared several feet above the table, then crashed onto it splashing mud on both her parents. “Mena!” Brenson roared. As Brenson and Maasena tried to help their daughter, Mena fought them pointing to a place beside Stumpy. Ky released his command word so Mena could talk. “That elf did this to me,” Mena whined. “Lord Stumpy did nothing to stop him.” The young dwarf began to sob as she cried, “He even cut off my beard!” Brenson shook the mud from his hands and growled, “I demand an explanation!” Stumpy turned to Ky who seemed to be very content to stand one step back and let Stumpy handle things. Muttering, Stumpy turned back to Brenson. “I'm afraid the lass deserves what's been done,” he said. “And likely much more.” Stumpy extended a hand in Ky's direction. “I present to thee, Lord Ky, God of Chaos, and grandson by virtue of his life-mate to Stan of Cragsguard.” Brenson and Maasena each bowed. Ky remained motionless. Stumpy continued, “Earlier this week, Mena insulted Lord Ky's heritage by insulting Stan of Cragsguard. This morning, the lass

threw Lord Ky to the floor, then verbally insulted him using the phrases 'derelict street waif' and 'ugly elven freak.' I heard the lass speak both with mine own ears.” Stumpy took a deep breath and frowned. “The fact that Mena is still among the living is testimony to Lord Ky's greatness,” he added softly. Brenson glared at Mena. “Are these accusations true?” Mena's pale face turned from the elf that stood behind Stumpy and regarded her father. “I nae knew him for a god.” Both Brenson and Maasena collapsed into their chairs, shamefully gazing at the floor. Ky finally stepped forward and addressed them. “According to dwarven law, if the child performs a crime, the parents are guilty. Is that not true?” Brenson groaned and admitted, “It is true.” The dagger appeared in Ky's left hand. “So, if I decide that the only way to erase this insult is to shave your beards with this blade,” he paused long enough for both Brenson and Maasena to flinch, “the blade which will permanently shave your beards, then you must agree to my terms. Is that not true?” Brenson muttered, “Aye, that is true as well.” Ky stood silent and still for several moments. Then, with a slight flick of one hand, sent Mena sliding off the end of the table along with Brenson and Maasena's breakfast. He took a step closer to the table. “I will offer you a choice. The insults of your daughter will be forgotten if I shave both of your beards or Mena becomes a servant of my children until I feel she has learned manners.” Ky caught and held both Brenson and Maasena's gaze until they cringed. “That could be a very, very long time,” he added softly. “I will give you a few moments to decide.” Ky walked to the far end of the hall and waited. Brenson and Maasena traded heated whispers. They did not argue on which they would choose, but on how to add to their decision to prove their hearts were behind it. Finally, Brenson and Maasena stood, both frowning deeply. “Lord Ky,” Brenson called. “If it please thee, we have decided.” Ky returned to the table and waited, idly twirling the dagger between his fingers. Brenson declared, “We are both humbled that you have kindly let us decide our fate. We choose that Mena be a servant to your children. In addition, we ask that your children come to our feast hall so that we may honor them with the same fervor that our

daughter has dishonored you. She, of course, will attend as their personal servant.” Ky bowed. “I accept. I will return for Mena later today. See that she is properly dressed for her new position.” Ky grinned at the sobbing dwarven child, then vanished. Brenson slowly sagged onto his seat and addressed Stumpy. “My Lord, it grieves me greatly that my daughter has shamed you as well. Name our repentance and it shall be done.” Stumpy thought for a moment, then said, “Lord Ky's children have ne'er seen the glories of a dwarven forge. Ye will bring them before the forges and have the best smiths make for them a weapon to be proud of.” Maasena rested her hands on the table and leaned forward. “Did Lord Ky teach you the spell you cast to protect us when we were trapped by the feline god?” She waited until Stumpy nodded. “And did Lord Ky cast the original spell that kept us safe until you arrived?” Stumpy nodded again. “Thank you, My Lord. Please let Lord Ky know that our daughter will be ready and his children will receive no grief from her.” “Aye, Maasena, wife of Brenson, Lord of Deep Stone. I will tell the lad.” Stumpy bowed and vanished.

16 Taelann materialized before the bridge that led to the elven capital, Alle-Stecan. He quickly crossed and walked to the city gates. The destruction caused by Ky during the battle with the dismemberers still remained with the exception of the wall. The elves had rebuilt it. Since Taelann's last visit they had carved a twenty-foot high rendition of Ky's symbol upon the wall: an arc of lightning behind a blazing oak leaf. They also added a small shrine at the base of the wall. Dawn had barely finished painting the sky and already, a small crowd of elves waited for their turns inside the shrine. The guards saluted Taelann as he passed through the gates. One of the guards bowed and asked, "Your destination, My Lord?” "I wish to speak with Sage Tas'lin. Please tell him that it is very important." "I will deliver your request, My Lord. Please go to the palace. I'm sure he will want to meet with you there." "Thank you," Taelann replied as the guard sprinted away. Taelann quickly walked to the palace. Within moments, he arrived at the palace gates. The guard he had spoken to met him there. “Sage Tas'lin is expecting you. Follow me, please, My Lord.” Taelann followed the guard through the garden to a vine- covered wall. The guard led him to a small open doorway and bowed as Taelann entered. He found himself in another smaller garden with two sparkling fountains and a cottage resting beneath the caress of a weeping willow's branches. Sage Tas'lin waited on a bench grown from the trunk of the willow.

“Good morning, Taelann. I've taken the liberty to summon Lord Ky for this discussion since he will be pivotal in the solution to your problem.” He gestured to the bench as he added, “Please sit down.” “Good morning, Sage Tas'lin,” Taelann said as he sat. “I'm not surprised that you know what I wished to speak with you about. I am surprised that you summoned Ky and actually expect him to arrive. Last I heard, he was in Vienna.” “I'm surprised you can not feel when Lord Ky is or is not on this world,” Sage Tas'lin replied. “Perhaps you need further training.” “I would consider it an honor to train with you,” Taelann said, then asked, “How do you know Ky will answer your summons?” “Besides the issue with Aemir, I have some memories for him,” Sage Tas'lin said. Sighing, he closed his eyes making his face appear to be an endless mass of wrinkled flesh. Taelann scanned the garden while Sage Tas'lin meditated on the past. He had never seen a place so manicured. Every flower appeared to be positioned to enhance the beauty of the flowers around it. The two fountains had statues of elves in their centers, one male, one female. The waters trickled through the fingers of their outstretched hands. The cottage had been constructed with stones. Two windows with arched tops stood like sentries on either side of the oak door. Sage Tas'lin smiled as Taelann returned his attention to the old elf. “I built this cottage over three thousand years ago. The city of Alle-Stecan grew around it. The bench you sit upon is the same bench I sat on to compose all the elven histories. This bench is also where I taught many talented elves.” He paused a moment, then added, “Lord Ky is in the city. We will begin as soon as he arrives.” A few moments later, Ky entered the garden. He scanned the area and found Taelann and Sage Tas'lin seated on a semi-circular bench beneath the ancient willow tree. He started to walk towards them, then froze. His mind fell back through the centuries as he watched himself enter the garden. Ky followed Prince Stel-Towen into the garden. Ky thought about his welcome here in the elven capital. The prince had told him in Cragsguard that he would be honored and not judged by his appearance since he bore the sword the prince had given him. That was not the case. Although the elves did not turn him away at the city gates, they kept their distance and spoke in soft whispers behind his back. He felt more tolerated than anything else. The

prince assured him that would change after this meeting. Ky came here seeking help. He did not know where else to go. The king refused to see him, but Stel-Towen listened to his problem. He arranged this meeting with Sage Tas'lin and carefully instructed Ky on how to behave when they met the old elf. The Sage sat in the center of a semi-circular bench beneath a willow tree. Stel-Towen stopped outside the area encircled by the bench, knelt and bowed his head. "Greetings, Master. I have brought the child I spoke of when I returned from Cragsguard." "I see that," Sage Tas'lin replied. "Rise and take your seat." Ky waited until Prince Stel-Towen had seated himself on the far end of the bench then stepped forward and knelt before the Sage. He waited, not saying anything as Prince Stel-Towen instructed. He could feel the Sage's eyes on him and it was several moments before the Sage spoke. "Tell me your name, child." Ky whispered, "Ky." "Speak louder," Prince Stel-Towen ordered. "I heard him," Sage Tas'lin said. "Rise and remove your hood so that I may see the demon our young prince has welcomed into our city." Ky pulled his hood back as he stood. He kept his head lowered, gazing at the ground in front of his own feet. "I see you've been well trained to despise yourself. Look at me, child." Ky looked into Sage Tas'lin's eyes and held his stare. They remained staring at each other several moments before Sage Tas'lin smiled. "You also have a strong-willed spirit, I see. Sit across from Prince Stel-Towen and tell me what brought you here." "May I sit here?" Ky asked. Sage Tas'lin nodded. Ky sat on the ground before the elder and related the fate of Little Ky to him. Sage Tas'lin patiently listened as Ky revealed every detail of his son's demise as well as all Ky had done in his effort to restore Little Ky. He also talked of the alchemist in Cragsguard and how he disappeared at the same time. "Normally, I would not take a child as an apprentice. Your problem intrigues me, so, this time I will make an exception. Return to your farm and wait for me there. I will be there within two weeks." "Thank you, Sage Tas'lin," Ky said, standing. He bowed then added, "I will wait for you there."

Ky blinked away the memory and approached the bench. Kneeling and bowing his head, he said, “Greetings, Master. It has been too long.” “Rise, child. You are the master now.” Ky stood and shook his head. “I had no idea that it was you that taught me. I think I remember where I placed my notes.” “Please, sit down. We'll have time to reminisce later,” Sage- Tas'lin said, smiling. He waited until Ky was seated across from Taelann, then instructed, “Today we are here to deal with a problem that young Aemir is experiencing. I ask that you remain, Ky, until we've decided how to deal with the problem.” Ky nodded. “Taelann, please explain what you observed this morning that brought you here.” “I went to Daelann's shrine in Cragsguard. Little Ky, Micah and Brek were seated outside the shrine. They appeared terrified. Aemir was in the shrine. I sent Little Ky, Micah and Brek to the Cracked Anvil and made sure they would not be found until I return. Then I came here to seek advice. I think Aemir has done something to cause this fear, but I cannot find reason in his thoughts." "Are you sure he is the cause of their fear?" Ky asked. "Yes. Aemir did something that frightened them. I can't understand why he would. I came to speak with Sage Tas'lin hoping to gain some insight," Taelann replied. "The problem is the situation that has been delegated to Aemir. I will explain," Sage Tas'lin stated. "Aemir was the eldest of the two twins. By elven law, that made him the heir to his family's fortune and position. He had been raised with that in mind. Aemir received everything first and was always in charge. Anything left over went to Aemar. Aemar even had to rely on Aemir for education and Aemir is not the best of students. "Now Aemir finds himself living in his brother's station. He is no longer pampered or treated like royalty. The other half of the problem is that now he sees what his brother's life had been like. He is burdened with a great deal of guilt since his brother never knew anything but second best, if that. The time he is spending in the shrine he is apologizing to his brother for the way he mistreated him. Aemir feels that he is to blame since he is the only surviving member of the family. "The first part of the problem can be solved by proving that Ky II, Eleana and Tal are the best of teachers. That is what Aemir

expects because that is how he was raised. If you can demonstrate that they are indeed worthy of his attention, then he will provide no further disturbances to the training process. "The second problem is more complicated. For now, time at the shrine to visit Aemar should be placed in his schedule. He will also need to commence his lessons with me. Since I do not wish to separate the group, I will instruct them all, including the goblin and the wayward dwarf." Sage Tas'lin looked towards Ky, then said, "I'm sure you can find a way to prove your triplets' worth. The sooner you do that the better. It would be best not to do it as a display specifically designed to impress Aemir. That would alienate him from the others and cause even further damage." Ky nodded, then moved to one of the fountains to think as Sage Tas'lin turned to Taelann. "You will need to make sure Aemir apologizes to Little Ky, Brek, Micah and Simon. Afterwards, be there when he needs you. You can do this with the twin-speak you share with him. There is no need for you to join that group, though I do suggest you limit your responsibilities with the Combined Council." "Thank you, Sage Tas'lin," Taelann responded bowing his head. "What of the immediate problem?" "Trust in Ky. He will handle it." Sage Tas'lin summoned a large tome and quill. Without any further glance at Taelann or Ky, he began writing. Taelann knew that the meeting had ended. He stood and bowed low before the Sage, then left the garden. He waited near the wall a few moments until Ky joined him. "What is the plan?" Taelann asked. Ky grinned then answered, "Gather the four of them and bring them to the training grounds. I will meet you there. Give me a few moments to get things started before you arrive." Both Ky and Taelann vanished.

17 Taelann returned to the library and sat on the bench outside his brother's shrine. He could sense Aemir's presence within. As he waited, he considered whether he or Daelann were the eldest and if the same situation applied to them in their early lives. He concluded that it did. High-elven society had always put the most importance on the first born male child. Taelann's thoughts returned to Aemir. His new twin was now the younger of the two, a role reversal he probably was not ready for. Being just another member of his group did not help matters either. Scanning the library, Taelann's glance rested on Symplex's shrine. He felt compelled to pay Symplex a visit. Before entering the shrine, he searched his twin's thoughts to determine how much time he would have. Satisfied that Aemir had no intention of leaving soon, Taelann visited with Symplex. Pushing aside the curtain, Taelann stepped into the small alcove that housed the body of Symplex. A stone sarcophagus covered with the resting form of the warrior stood in the center. The detail gave the appearance that the body lay beneath a thin coating of marble. Taelann expected to see Symplex's chest rise and fall with slow and steady breathing. Beyond the sarcophagus, a bench, finished with padded leather, waited before the shrine that was flanked by two sets of dark gray plate-mail. Two crossed greatswords adorned the wall above the helm that glowed with an inner light. Taelann approached the bench and sat. "Welcome, my friend. Thank you for coming." Symplex's voice

spoke from the helm and had the same calming quality it had during his life. Now, it seemed even more calming without the warrior's body connected to it. "You can speak freely here. Your words will not leave the shrine." "Greetings, Symplex. Did you summon me?" Taelann asked. Symplex laughed. Taelann remembered how his friend would use that same laugh to ease tension within the Council of Nine. He felt himself relax. "Mortals I can summon. I can only request to see you." Symplex replied. "Ky left a few minutes ago. He suggested I share with Aemir some memories of Ky II's training. I could summon Aemir, but I thought it would be better if you suggested he come to me." "I agree. I'll send him in as soon as I get him to leave Aemar," Taelann said. "Aemar will release him after we finish speaking. Come visit me more often," Symplex requested. "I miss talking with you and I'm sure you have some excellent stories to tell." Taelann stood and replied, "I'll be back. There's a tale of a young dwarf in Stumpy's care that you might find amusing." "I look forward to it." Taelann smiled then bowed before the helm. He left the shrine and took a seat outside Daelann's shrine. A moment later, Aemir pushed the curtain aside. He stood a moment, staring at Taelann with wide eyes. Then his shoulders drooped and he sat down beside his new brother. "So you know?" he asked. "Yes," Taelann replied. "I came to visit Daelann this morning and found Little Ky, Brek, and Micah sitting here. They didn't speak to me, but they were frightened and you were in the shrine. I sent them to a safe place and talked with Sage Tas'lin. Ky was there as well." "I was supposed to train with Sage Tas'lin," Aemir muttered. "Instead, I have to train under a child." "You are a child as well." Aemir shook his head. "I've received my inheritance." Taelann shifted slightly so that he could face Aemir more directly. He closed his eyes a moment, then said, "Aemar has not received his inheritance. How is you have yours?" Aemir sighed. "I thought being a high-elf like myself, you would understand the elven way better." "It has been many centuries since I spent time with my people. Explain what you mean." "By law, only the oldest twin is truly accepted as an adult. The younger is allowed adult status only if his family wishes to be shunned by everyone else. Aemar is my younger brother so he was not

given inheritance." "I see. It is different with gods. Ky II, Tal and Eleana will all receive their inheritance regardless of law. They would have it already if their lives had not been threatened when their tenth season arrived. Ky had to deny them their inheritance to keep them safe." "So what happens now?" "I get the feeling that you think Ky II is not good enough to train you. I would like you to speak with one of his trainers before we do anything else. Symplex's shrine is there next to mine," Taelann said pointing. "Ask him about Ky II's training." "What if he doesn't want to tell me?" Taelann smiled. "He will. Go speak with him." Aemir dragged his feet to Symplex's shrine, then turned. "Is Lord Ky going to kill me?" he asked. "I don't think he will this time," Taelann answered, then added, "But no one can tell you what Ky is going to do until he does it." Aemir's gaze found the floor as his hand absently pulled the curtain aside. He stepped into Symplex's shrine and slowly walked to the seat before the glowing helm. He expected Symplex to greet him. After a few moments of silence, Aemir glanced around the small alcove. His dark-green eyes widened at the sight of the armor that stood on either side of the small altar. Then, he looked above the glowing helm at the crossed greatswords mounted on the wall. "You must have been some warrior," he whispered. "Thank you, Aemir, and welcome." Aemir stared at the swords a moment longer before focusing on the glowing helm. The voice he heard did not sound like a warrior. It was more soothing and friendly than he expected. "You know who I am?" "Your brother, Aemar, has spoken of you many times. He admires you greatly." "You can talk to him?" "Yes. Lady Selia, Lord Daelann, Aemar and myself speak with each other frequently. I'm sure that is not the reason for you coming here this morning. How can I help you?" Aemir sat quietly a moment, then asked, "Did you train Ky II?" "Yes. I was both teacher and student of Ky II. Why do you ask?" "He's the youngest of triplets. He's not even a person. Why should he train me?" Silence filled the shrine for several moments before Symplex answered. "I consulted with Daelann so that I could give you the best answer possible. When the three of us died, we regained our memories of

our previous lives. Unlike Taelann, he remembers the flaws of elven society." Another moment of silence followed. "Ky and his children are not subject to those laws and customs. You are a member of that group, so you are no longer subject to them either. That is something you need to get used to. I would like to share a couple memories of Ky II's training with you. The first one will be early in his training with me. The second will be near the end. Keep in mind that Lady Selia trained the triplets before they came to me. I will be fighting all three in the memories. I want you to watch Ky II whether he is fighting or watching." The inner glow of the helm brightened slightly and a mist formed in the air before Aemir. The young elf watched as Symplex greeted the triplets in what appeared to be a trampled practice ground. Aemir noted that the triplets looked very young, too young to be fighting a warrior the size of Symplex. Aemir watched Symplex closely as he talked with the triplets. He noticed that Symplex did not have the grace of the elven warriors Aemir had known, but Symplex had an animal-like suppleness about him that hinted at great agility and strength. Aemir listened intently as Symplex explained the task. "I know Lady Selia will have trained you in disarming your opponent. It is probably the first thing she taught you. To see where I need to begin your training with me, I want you to try to disarm me. When one of us is disarmed, I will move on to the next. Eleana, I will begin with you." Symplex unsheathed one of the two greatswords he wore across his back and wielded it one-handed. Eleana unsheathed a dagger as Ky II and Tal backed away to give them room. Lord Tobit stepped between Eleana and Symplex. "I will be officiating and healing if the need arises. That means you three don't have to hold back as this brute tries to take your toys away." The triplets laughed and Tobit continued. "The match ends on my word. Eleana, Symplex, you may begin as soon as I get out of the way of those pointy things." As soon as Tobit stepped away, Eleana and Symplex began circling. Eleana stayed low, close to the ground and whirled in a series of quick short movements around Symplex's blade. Symplex countered her moves easily, appearing almost relaxed. Then, with the clang of steel sliding on steel, Eleana lunged. Afterwards, the two combatants moved with crane-like grace and cheetah-like speed to the music of steel on steel. Several moments passed before Symplex disarmed Eleana and Tobit ended the match. "Very good," Symplex said. "You are going to be fun to

work with. Tal, you're next." Tal took his place in front of Symplex and unsheathed his longsword. His right foot slid back into a defensive stance and he waited. Symplex nodded and pressed the attack. Tal seemed to flow like water from one spot to another, always opposite Symplex's sword-arm making Symplex fight across his body. Several times during the bout, Tal rendered Symplex off balance, but could not disarm him. Finally, with a quick spinning two-handed sweep of his great-sword, Symplex sent Tal's longsword flying across the practice grounds. "You will be a challenge. You are the rare defensive type that likes to finish what others start. I'm going to enjoy training you as well. Ky II, you're last." Ky II stepped in front of Symplex, slightly slouched, with his hands at his sides and waited. "You will need to have a weapon for me to disarm," Symplex instructed. Ky II tilted his head slightly and whispered, "Disarm the weapon I attack you with." Symplex readied his weapon and waited. Ky II became a blur of motion as he rolled under the greatsword and with a flash of sunlight on steel, the young elf's longsword slashed across the back of Symplex's forearm causing the first blood spill of the day. Symplex tossed the sword to his other hand and engaged the elf. The ring of steel beat a chaotic rhythm that had no sense of rhyme as the two combatants whirled around the practice grounds. Of the three battles, this one lasted the longest as Symplex contorted and twisted his body to counter the attacks of Ky II. At the end, both had received numerous cuts and it was Ky II's sword that lay in the dust. "Gain a little more strength," Symplex panted, "and that ploy of disarming me by cutting off my arm will work. You will be the greatest challenge. You fight with the same unpredictable manner your father uses. You just need to learn a little discipline to make it victorious." The memory faded leaving Aemir seated wide-eyed, staring into the space where the battles played before him. Symplex waited to let Aemir absorb what he had shown him. "What did you learn about Ky II?" Symplex asked. "He tried to cut your arm off," Aemir murmured. "Yes," Symplex replied, his voice having an edge of humor to it. "Besides that, what can you tell me about Ky II?" "He's ruthless and I've never seen anyone move like that before." Aemir paused a moment and thought about the entire

memory. "It was hard watching him while you were fighting the other two, but when I did remember, he seemed to be ignoring the other fights. At one point during Tal's fight, he was drawing in the dirt with his fingers." "Exactly. Ky II does not rely on knowing his opponent. He relies on his own abilities. He did not like being the last one to spar me because he may have learned something of the way I fight. I saved him for last because I knew that in advance. I am going to shorten the next memory. All you will see is my fight with Ky II. Taelann is waiting with the other three boys in the library. Are you ready?" "Yes, I'm ready." "This will be a fight to submission. It will tell you one other thing that's very important to know about Ky II." Again, the helm brightened slightly and a mist formed before Aemir. This time Ky II looked a little older. Aemir wondered if the battle he was watching would ever end. Neither Symplex nor Ky II showed any signs of submitting. Finally, Ky II managed to trip Symplex, roll across Symplex's chest and pin his neck to the ground with his sword. The memory faded as Tobit began to see to the many wounds both had acquired. "When you first arrived, I told you that I both taught and learned from Ky II. You have seen an example of both. Do not doubt that he can teach you. There is only one other better than he and that is his father." "Will Lord Ky kill me for what I've done?" Aemir asked quietly. The shrine was silent for a few moments, then Symplex answered, "There are two things, and only two things, you can count on Lord Ky doing. The first is he is very loyal to and protective of his family. The second is he is very loyal to and protective of his friends. He expects that same loyalty and protection in return. You are lucky that you are twin to one of his friends. You are also lucky that he has had some council in how to handle this matter. I don't believe you will be killed this time. I will give you a peace offering for him. It will bring back some memories for him as well as for Taelann, though Taelann's will be more memories of frustration," Symplex added sounding amused. A small hourglass appeared beside the helm on the altar. "Take that with you. Taelann will know what to do with it. My personal record with it is twelve. Taelann will explain what that means. Good luck to you, Aemir. If what Aemar says about you is half true, you will grow to be quite spectacular. Just learn to make better decisions so that you will grow." "Thank you," Aemir said as he took the hourglass. "May I return to talk with you again sometime."

"Of course. Feel free to visit any of us here. We all love the company." Aemir bowed before the altar then turned and left. Outside, he met Taelann with Little Ky, Brek and Micah. The three boys were wearing their practice tunics. Taelann held Aemir's. "You will need this," Taelann said as he handed Aemir the tunic. Aemir took the tunic as he said, "I'm sorry. I really wouldn't have hurt any of you. I won't do anything like that again." Little Ky glanced at Taelann, then replied, "Taelann explained it a little for us. I think we can forget it this time." "Thanks," Aemir said with a slight grin. He handed the hourglass to Taelann and put his practice tunic on. "Symplex gave that to me to give to Lord Ky as a peace offering. He said you would know what to do with it." Taelann turned the hourglass in his hands as his eyes momentarily glazed. "Not the proudest memory I could have received," he said smiling, "but Lord Ky will like it." As they walked to the exit of the library, Aemir said, "Symplex said his record was twelve. What does that mean?" "It means," Taelann explained, "he lasted twelve turns of this glass in combat with Lord Ky." "Do you have a record?" Aemir asked. "Three," murmured Taelann as they stepped into the morning sunlight.

18 Ghostspawn pushed the hide covering aside and stepped across the threshold. He paused one step in and examined the room. The interior of the cabin was dimly lit by six candles held aloft by skeletal hands. All the furnishings and shelving were built on skeletal frames. The counter-tops, table-top and shelves had been fashioned from living flesh. A faint pulse could be noticed if one watched long enough. Skeletal fingers held the flesh in place. The only other exit from the room stood across from the entrance. Skulls formed the door's frame. The doorway itself was blackness, black so intense, the candle that burned beside the doorway failed to illuminate any of what lay beyond. The room did not mirror its owner's filth. Everything stood neatly organized and labeled with runes. A heavy mix of herbal fragrance dominated the room. Ghostspawn's scan ended with a shelf that housed glass jars. Each contained a small creature or some portion of a body floating in liquid. His hostess smiled at him from her seat at the table that stood in front of the shelf. He noticed then that her skin was as white as her hair. "Sit, goblin. We need to get to know each other better." She waved her hand and the chair opposite her stiffly shuffled away from the table on its skeletal feet. "I know enough of you. You have magic and you will teach it to me," Ghostspawn ordered as he sat. At this, the woman laughed. Her laughter sounded almost melodic, yet there could be heard something discordant and off-key as well. Ghostspawn scowled across the table.

"I have seated at my table a goblin demanding that I teach it magic. Goblins are not known for common sense, much less intelligence." She paused and laughed again. "I find that quite amusing. Don't you?" "I am not just any goblin," snarled Ghostspawn. "Oh? Can you read and write? Do you know the runes? Have you an education?" Ghostspawn scowled more deeply, then declared, "I am immortal. That's all that matters. You will teach me magic." Her pink eyes turned cold and she pointed the foot she had nibbled upon at the goblin. When she spoke, her voice was soft and cutting. "You are in my house, goblin. Your immortality only means you may make a long lasting bit of furniture, if I decide to foul my decor with your decrepit hide." She glared at the goblin a moment, daring him to speak. When he remained silent, she sighed and sat back. She bit off a piece of the foot she was holding before tossing it into an iron pot that sat beside the shelf. She examined Ghostspawn as she chewed. "You look, smell, and have the manners of a goblin," she said softly, "but," she added then paused. Again she examined him. "I sense something elven about you. Tell me about yourself and I may decide to honor your desire to learn magic." Something in the woman's voice compelled Ghostspawn to relate his history to her. She watched him as he spoke, yawning occasionally or shifting in her chair to stay awake. Her eyes widened slightly and she leaned forward at the first mention of the "cat god." She remained on the edge of her seat for the rest of his tale. "So, Karn-Rachk'sha bowed before this ghost-elf you spoke of. I find that quite interesting." She leaned back and smiled at the goblin. "I believe I will teach you the art if The Grove accepts you." "What is the grove?" Ghostspawn asked. "The Grove is where you will be tested," she answered, glancing to the skull-framed doorway. "We have a few hours before we can begin your test. Until then, we will begin your education of the runes." "Why not tell me about you?" Ghostspawn suggested. "You will call me 'Mistress.' That is all you need to know of me." She left the table and retrieved several long slender bones, velum and two bottles of dark red ink. She placed them on the table and explained, "These are the tools for making basic runes. The velum is made from the skin of sheep. Sheep are weak, like those who are incapable of doing the magic. The bones are from the feet of young maidens. They are delicate and dainty like their former owners. You must be gentle with them. The ink is made mostly from blood. There

are other things in there you need not know about yet. "The runes you will learn are the tools of simple magic. If The Grove approves of you, I will teach you the more powerful ones. Let us begin with the rune for sickness. Each rune is made of several strokes. This is the first stroke," she said as she drew a curved line at the top of the parchment. She pushed the parchment in front of Ghostspawn and instructed, "Practice that. When you can do it to my satisfaction, I will show you the next stroke." She watched as Ghostspawn made his first couple attempts, then sat across from him shaking her head. "I see where goblins get their ignorant reputation. This is going to take a while." Ghostspawn scowled at her, then continued drawing the stroke, changing his grip on the delicate bone several times. Finally he found he could handle it best if lightly grasped between two fingers. After several hours, he spent more time stretching his fingers than practicing the stroke. "That's enough for today," Mistress said. "I fear those clumsy fingers will just break the bone if you try any longer." She gathered the ink and bones and put them away. "We will leave the parchment here should The Grove approve of you. Now, return to the forest. I need to prepare for our journey to The Grove." "How do I know you won't leave me out there?" Ghostspawn asked as he stood. "You don't," Mistress answered, smiling. "I will call you when I'm ready," she added as she pulled the hide away from the door. As soon as the goblin passed over the threshold, she dropped the hide and stepped to the window. She watched him through the cracks in the boards until he sat beside a tree just beyond the clearing. "You will be most useful to me, my goblin friend," she muttered as she turned away. She waved her hand towards a gap between two of the shelves. A small trapdoor opened near the wall. "Bhk-at, I have need of you," she said. Moments later, a small elf, barely six inches tall, climbed from the trapdoor. "Yes, Mistress." "I love looking at you, Bhk-at. All the tastiest morsels are visible beneath that transparent skin of yours. It's a shame you are so small." She admired the small elf a moment, then continued, "I need some information, my small friend. There is an elven being, called "The Ghost" that even Karn-Rachk'sha bows before. He would be a bit much for what I have in mind, but he has children. My informant mentioned the town of Cragsguard. Please, see what you can find out

for me." "There is the usual price, Mistress," Bhk-at explained. "Have I ever failed to deliver, my friend?" Mistress asked with a smile. "Never," Bhk-at said. "I like things agreed upon up front, though." "I will supply your usual request and a large bonus if the information you bring me is as useful as I believe it will be." The elf nodded and returned through the trapdoor. Mistress walked to the shelf where the herbs were stored and selected some wolves bane, widow weed and mint. Then, she touched a small catch on the side of the shelf. The shelf swung inward revealing a small bathing room. She entered and muttered an incantation to heat the water before sprinkling the herbs into it. Her clothing melted from her milky-white skin as she immersed herself within the water. The waters swirled around her, cleansing her body for the trip to The Grove. When the water grew still, she stepped from the tub. A deep-crimson gown of satin covered her nudity as she returned to the main room. The shelf slid to its original position as she mentally sent a message to the waiting goblin. She waited for him at the skull-framed doorway. Ghostspawn pushed through the hide and entered. He stopped and stared at the transformed woman that stood across the room from him, his mouth slowly forming a sharp-toothed grin. "You will need to save your appraisal of me until later," Mistress stated. "Listen carefully as your continued existence will depend on what I tell you." Ghostspawn stepped to the table and seated himself. "I'm listening," he replied. "Good. We will be traveling to The Grove. It is a living, breathing entity and it does not like to be disturbed. You will be tempted to stray from the path. If you do that, you will remain wandering around for the rest of eternity. The Grove is the guard for the pathways of the gods. To reach it, you must walk straight forward. Your journey will not be as easy as it sounds and I will not be able to help you. I will be concentrating on getting myself there." She paused and watched his reaction. She first noted that his grin had faded. Her words had found the intelligence she hoped would keep this goblin alive. She needed him for her plans. She considered not going to The Grove, but that would be futile. The Grove was essential to her success. She continued, "If you can, close your eyes while you walk. That will dispose of the major temptations. The path is straight. Put one foot in front of the other and you will make it. Once you arrive, remain silent. You do not want to impress The Grove with your

ignorance. Come." Ghostspawn walked to her. She grabbed his shoulders and aimed him at the door. "You will go first so I do not have to wait as long for you to arrive. Remember to walk straight ahead and do not turn from the path." "If I go first, I'll be the first one there," Ghostspawn protested. "You would think. The first time always takes longer. I will be waiting for you when you arrive." She made sure he was facing the correct direction, then said, "Surely, being a goblin, you have no fear of the dark." Then she pushed him through the doorway. A moment later, she stepped through as well.
