19 William awoke as the sun's rays crept across his face. He remained still for several moments waiting for the calls to awaken the students that could be heard throughout the school. Normally, the wait would have been only a few seconds. Not hearing them, he absently reached for the canopy to push it aside so that he could see the clock. His hand floundered in the air beside the bed unhampered by the canopy he expected to find. Finally, he sat up and searched the room. A small table sat beside his bed supporting an oil lamp and a wooden cup half-filled with water. Across the room, he found a rustic desk and chair. Strange clothing lay folded on the desk. William turned and sat on the edge of the bed, his feet resting on the bare wooden floor. He noticed the nightshirt he wore. He had not worn a nightshirt since his childhood. He picked up the cup to sip some water and felt the small imperfections that told him it had been handmade. William drank the water and smiled. The memory of his walk through the Austrian woods with the Old Man which led him to Cragsguard, his visit at the Cracked Anvil and finally, his night spent in the kitchen telling tales of Little Ky and Micah flooded back into his awareness. "Ah, the farm," he muttered. "I wonder if anyone is awake yet." Stretching, he walked across the room and examined the clothing on the desk. It reminded him of a medieval costume as he put it on. He found a comfortable pair of soft leather boots near the door. After sliding them on, he quietly walked to the kitchen.

Archos rose as William entered the kitchen. "Good morning, William. I trust you slept well," Archos greeted. "Very well, thank you," William replied. "Please, have a seat. Illya will have your breakfast in a moment." Illya and Daphnia entered the room as William walked to the table. Illya went to the counter and began spooning steaming oatmeal into bowls as Daphnia sat beside William. "Trees be fallin' but you'll be havin' a busy day today," Daphnia said. "What might you have in store for me, Milady?" "Milady!" Daphnia exclaimed. "Ain't nobody be callin' me 'milady' ever." Her cheeks took on a rose hue as she continued. "Ain't me that has plans, but I won't be mindin' joinin' you if you ain't be bothered with me." "I would enjoy your company," William replied as Illya served them their breakfast. "Delmaria will be your guide this morning. The children's return to the farm will be a little delayed due to some problems that Ky is solving," Archos explained. "You will be going to visit the wild- elves. The Old Man mentioned you would like to hear them sing." "I wish I knew that bark trick of Ky's. I would love to record that." "We anticipated that and the wild-elves will do the bark for you. We will teach you how to invoke it when you return." "The wild-elves, what do they look like?" William asked. "If you see them," Delmaria answered as she entered the room, "they will resemble Ky somewhat. Chances are, you will only hear them." "Good morning, Milady," William said as he and Archos stood. "Good morning," Delmaria said with a smile. "We will be leaving after breakfast. Ky should be bringing the children sometime early this afternoon which will give us an hour or two." "An hour or two. What time is it now?" William asked. "Nearly noon," Archos replied. "Noon! I can't remember the last time I've slept that late. I must have been tired," William said. Archos laughed and said, "Well, you arrived here late last night and then you spent quite some time trading stories with us. It was only an hour or so before dawn when you went to sleep." "So what is this problem Ky is solving?" William asked. "We really don't have enough details to tell you much now,"

Delmaria answered. "I'm sure Little Ky and Micah will tell you all about it when they get here. Ky's methods for solving problems are usually quite memorable. If you are ready, we can go now." "Daphnia will be joining us, if it isn't a problem," William replied. "No problem at all," Delmaria said as she led them to the front yard. "Neither of you has traveled through a portal yet. It is a bit uncomfortable and disorienting, but that won't last long. Please take my hand." William and Daphnia each clasped one of Delmaria's hands and the group vanished.

20 Ky watched the practice from the top of the keep wall. He knew it would be futile to begin his demonstration before Aemir arrived, so he waited. Tal and Simon were sparring in the center of the field. Ky smiled as Simon continuously tried to get closer to Ky II who sat huddled in the corner. Eleana worked on dagger throwing nearby. By the time Ky sensed Taelann and the other children approaching, Simon had managed to move the sparring match about half the distance towards Ky II. Ky ported to the corner directly in front of Ky II. He heard the others stop as he stared down at his son. He waited long enough for Tal to restrain Simon from interfering. "I thought this task was assigned to you," Ky whispered. Ky II did not move nor look up. "Am I wrong?" Ky asked. "It was my task. I failed," Ky II said, still not moving. Another few moments of silence passed as Ky waited for Taelann and the other children to take their positions by the wall. Stumpy arrived with Mena a few seconds afterwards. Ky had to wait a moment longer for Sage Tas'lin to enter the training grounds. "Get up and defend yourself," Ky commanded as he took a step back. Ky II's eyes widened as the command forced him to his feet. His fingers closed around the hilt of a longsword. He stumbled from the corner, following his father to more open ground. He caught a glimpse of those that had arrived just as Ky attacked. Ky II fended off the first three strikes before he was disarmed and he found himself

breathless with his father's sword pinning his neck to the ground, emerald flames dancing between their faces keeping the wound from killing Ky II. "Symplex tells me you were a much better sparring partner than I was," Ky whispered. "Either he lied or he was insulting me. Or is it you aren't trying?" Aemir seized Taelann's sleeve and said, "He knows it's my fault. Why is he punishing Ky II?" "Ky believes that when something happens within a set group, the leader is responsible,” Taelann explained, pointing at the hourglass. “Pay attention and use the hour-glass Symplex gave to you." Ky II screamed as Ky withdrew his sword and backed away. Ky II glared at his father as he grabbed his sword and stood. This time, he led the attack. He managed several lightning-fast strikes that were all turned aside before his sword flew across the grounds and he found himself pinned to the ground again, this time his father's sword through his chest. He groaned as Ky leaned on the hilt. "If I didn't know better," Ky whispered, "I'd think you never trained under Symplex. You are fighting with your emotions. You have no focus. I'll give you one more chance to do it right before I decide you have to be locked in the dungeons of Chaos to keep you from embarrassing me." Again Ky II screamed as his father withdrew the sword and backed away. Ky II slowly got to his feet and retrieved his sword. He held it loosely as he surveyed the others watching. He saw Taelann take something from Aemir who sat staring at him and did not even notice the removal of the item. Little Ky's and Micah's faces were ashen white as they stood against the wall watching. Even Brek stood unusually still watching the proceedings. He saw Stumpy whispering into a young dwarf's ear and beside them, Sage Tas'lin concentrated on scribing something in a large tome that sat on the old elf's lap. On the other side of the training grounds, he saw Tal and Eleana restraining Simon. He looked into Simon's tear-streaked face for a moment before taking a deep breath and turning back to his father. Ky II readied his sword and began to circle his father. His breathing was even and slow as he stared into his father's eyes. Seconds later, the rapid ringing of the swords filled the grounds. Neither combatant scored a clean hit when they separated. They circled again for the last time. The ringing of swords and the swift movement of the two elves seemed to last forever as the others watched. It became difficult to tell which elf was which as their deadly dance progressed. All the while, Taelann turned the hourglass and counted as the rest stood transfixed.

A few seconds after the nineteenth turn of the glass, an arc of blood and green flame spewed forth from Ky II's throat. Ky grinned at his son lying on the ground at his feet. "You have been practicing," he whispered as he extended his hand to help him up. "Go calm Simon. I have something else I need to do here." Ky II grinned and ran to Simon. Simon broke free from Tal and Eleana and ran to meet his friend. He pinned Ky II's arms in his hug and cried into the elf's shoulder as Ky turned to Taelann and Aemir. Taelann put the hourglass back into Aemir's hand and whispered, "Nineteen." Aemir almost dropped the hourglass. He held it out as Ky approached and said, "Symplex wanted me to give this to you. He said his personal record was twelve. You just did nineteen with Ky II." Aemir watched as Ky took the hourglass. A slight grin marked the only sign that Ky had received a new memory. Ky put the hourglass into his pouch. Aemir continued, "I'm sorry for what I did. I was wrong and won't make that mistake again." "Apologies, no matter how heartfelt will not get you out of punishment," Ky replied. "Since you place so much value on high- elven culture, I will punish you as the high-elves would." Taelann screamed in pain. "No, please! It was me, not Taelann," Aemir yelled over the screaming. Aemir knelt before Ky begging him to stop long after the punishment had finished. When the young elf finally realized that it was over, Ky spoke to him. "Normally, threatening a member of my family or any of my friends would result in a very slow and very painful death. It could sometimes last years. Remember that. And remember what pain your brother will go through because you find the faults of your race more important than friendship and loyalty." Ky watched Aemir a few seconds, then nodded. "Bring the others to me, I have something to tell them." "Thank you," Taelann said. "He would not have survived that." "Don't thank me," Ky said as he led Taelann to Sage Tas'lin. "I did what I knew would cause him the most pain." "I hope you don't have to do it again," Taelann said. "So do I." Ky sat beside Sage Tas'lin and waited for the children to gather before them. Sage Tas'lin continued to write, apparently

ignoring all that was going on around him. "When Ky II is finished with you," Ky explained to the children, "Sage Tas'lin will become your teacher. This will happen after the inheritance ceremony. I would prefer not to have to come to the elven capitol to discipline any of you." Ky paused a moment as Sage Tas'lin vanished. "You have two hours to train before I take you back to the farm for a couple days off. After that break, I expect all of you to train so that you can last as long as Ky II did in a sparring match with me." Stumpy approached the group with Mena behind him. "I brought the lass," he muttered. Ky pointed to the dwarf. "This is Mena. She is your servant. She will clean your tunics, prepare your baths, serve your meals, make your beds and do anything else that needs to be done. Since you don't have to do any of that stuff yourselves, I expect you to train harder." "Should we train her as well?" Eleana asked. "I'll leave that up to you. My opinion is a clump of horse manure would be of more value to you." Ky fished the hourglass from his pouch and turned it in his hand. He glanced up and saw the children still standing in front of him. "Go train," he said as he waved them away. "Did Aemir count right?" Ky asked Taelann. "I did the count. Ky II lasted nineteen turns," Taelann answered with a smile. Stumpy mumbled into his beard as he looked at the hourglass. Ky looked at the dwarf a moment then said, "Eight for you." "I remember, lad. That eight was hard earned too." All three laughed. They watched the training session. The children did all they could to impress the spectators. By the end of the session all of them were blood and sweat soaked, but smiling. They ran to Ky and waited. "Mena, there is someone special at the farm," Ky said. "Make sure they are presentable to meet this person. You have twenty minutes to have them all ready. Afterwards, you can clean the tunics and tend to their practice weapons. When you finish, go to the Cracked Anvil for your evening meal." He spoke to the rest of the children. "I will meet all of you at the Cracked Anvil in twenty minutes. Don't," he paused a moment, then whispered, "make me wait. Ky II, wait here a moment." Ky II waited as the rest of the children ran to the barracks. Ky handed him the hourglass and instructed, "Take this and show it to Symplex. Tell him your record is nineteen. Return that to me when I

meet you in the Cracked Anvil." Ky II sprinted from the training grounds to the library. He entered Symplex's shrine and stood before the glowing helm. "Greetings, Ky II. Be seated and stay awhile." "Next time. I have to meet Dad at the Cracked Anvil soon." Ky II held up the hourglass. "He wanted me to show this to you and tell you my record is nineteen. What does that mean?" "It means that you've made me very proud as one of your teachers. My record is twelve. That means that the hourglass was turned twelve times before your father defeated me. Nineteen is an accomplishment to be very proud of. How is Aemir?" "Fine. Dad said something about high-elven culture and punished Taelann instead of Aemir. Aemir wasn't very happy about that." "Thank you. Aemar will be relieved that his former brother is okay. Come back when you have more time to visit. I want to hear all about your nineteen." "I will. See you soon,” Ky II said as he darted from the shrine.

21 William watched as the world around him blurred. He felt his stomach try to escape through his throat, then found himself standing in a forest glade. A small stream bubbled up from the ground to his left and danced into the trees behind him. Thousands of wild flowers swayed softly in the late-morning breeze. "Beautiful," he muttered. "Trees be fallin'!" Daphnia whispered. "I've never been seein' the like before." Delmaria smiled at them. "Sit there on that log. I'll let the elves know you are ready." She waited until William and Daphnia were comfortable before walking across the glade into the woods. William and Daphnia waited quietly for a few moments. Then they heard a soft voice that could have been mistaken for a gentle breeze caressing the leaves of the trees surrounding them. Another voice joined the song, then others. The two sitting on the log found themselves embraced by the song the elves sang for them. Both William and Daphnia listened with tear-filled eyes. The first song ended and was immediately followed by another. By the end of the third song, William and Daphnia were hand in hand. Delmaria watched them from just within the forest. She smiled as they moved closer together. The wild-elves also noticed and sang love song after love song. Delmaria had never heard them sing so long for anyone. She also felt the magic that the elves weaved into the music. They did not entice William and Daphnia into a love affair, but they made the couple seated in the glade feel as if they belonged together. After over an hour, she signaled to the elves that it was time

for them to go. She waited for the elf that had recorded the music on bark for William. He arrived shortly after the last song ended. "Thank you," Delmaria said. "I believe that this was a very special moment in their lives. I'll give the bark to them and take them home." The elf shook his head. "I'll present the bark to them." Delmaria curtsied and smiled. Together they crossed the glade. William saw them coming and stood, lending Daphnia his hand as she stood. William stared at the elf that arrived with Delmaria. The elf's clothing consisted of a living vine that afforded the elf adequate modesty as well as an intriguing costume that emphasized the elf's lithe yet muscular build. William noted that the elf's golden hair matched his eyes. The pupils were surrounded by a blazing golden iris that resembled the dawn-awakened sun. William bowed when the elf arrived. "Thank you," he said. "I've listened to beautiful music all my life and have never heard anything that could compare to the beauty my ears have been blessed with this day." Delmaria served as translator. The elf smiled hearing William's compliment. "You are a friend to us from this time on. I hope the memory bark keeps you company when you cannot join us here in this glade." Delmaria smiled as she related what the elf said, adding, "You have gained the right to come here again. For a human, that is a great honor. It is rarely granted." She asked the elf a question then said, "The invitation is open to both of you." "I can't wait to tell Micah of this," William said as he accepted the bark. Delmaria translated again and explained to the elf who Micah was. "If you wish to bring your child when next you visit, you may. We will withhold an open invitation until we meet him." After Delmaria related what the elf said, William thanked him and bowed. The elf turned and vanished before he had taken two steps. "It's time to return to the farm. The children should be arriving there soon," Delmaria said as she took William's and Daphnia's hands. Seconds later, the glade stood mirroring the newly born love between William and Daphnia. The flowers seemed brighter and the crickets sang in harmony with the soft whisper of a spring breeze that conducted the dance of both blossom and leaf.

22 Bhk-at knew of Lord Ky. The deep-elf had heard of the Chaos god and many of his adventures. This would likely make finding information on Lord Ky's children much easier. Bhk-at summoned six elves he knew he could trust and assigned them to three teams. The first team he sent to Chaos since they had access to the Pathway of the Gods. The second team he sent to investigate the Eldar Elves. The third he sent to Cragsguard. Now, his task was to wait for the information concerning the children of the Lord of Chaos. He was unsure of what he would get, but hoped it would be enough to satisfy Mistress. The third pair of elves arrived in Cragsguard early in the morning. They split up hoping to hear something about Lord Ky's children. They planned to meet at the ruined wall behind an abandoned building shortly after noon. Instead, they met at the barracks that housed the town guard near the manor house. Talk of the children being in town was everywhere and it all mentioned that they were staying here. They found the room the children were staying in and searched it. They determined that eight children occupied the room. Whether all were spawned by Lord Ky or not, they could not tell. Then one spotted four of the children in the training grounds below the window. He signaled to his partner and the two sat on the windowsill and watched the morning's activities. Three of the children below were elves. The fourth was human. One of the elves sat hugging his knees in a corner while another worked with the practice dummies. The third appeared to be training the human. Although the one practicing with dummies appeared to have great skill with a long-knife, the watchers could see nothing really special about any of them. They were about to go in

search of the other four children when Lord Ky appeared. They watched him approach the elf huddled in the corner. From the window, they could not tell one from the other. "I'm going to get closer. I'll meet you at the wall," the first whispered as he climbed from the windowsill. He darted across the room and disappeared into the hallway. The other remained on the windowsill and watched as Lord Ky apparently killed the other elf. The deep-elf's eyes widened to see the victim rise and pick up his sword. The watching elf decided that this would be a child of Lord Ky. He studied the proceedings closely as Lord Ky pinned his son to the ground a second time. Again, the child stood. He hesitated, glancing at the two other elves holding the human between them. Then he retrieved the sword and Lord Ky and his son fought again. The third battle seemed to last forever as the deep-elf watched from the window. He had not noticed that five other children, a dwarf and two high-elves had entered the training grounds until the fight ended. He studied each of them carefully. Only the three elves that had been there all morning appeared to be Lord Ky's children. A training session began after a short meeting. The deep-elf watched and began to evaluate the talents the other two elves had. The three were definitely in control of the training. The one he thought to be female was a healer. The other showed signs of being a talented fighter similar to the one that fought Lord Ky. When the training ended, Lord Ky met with the children again ending with eight of them leaving the grounds at a run. The one that fought Lord Ky stayed behind. Lord Ky spoke with him a moment, then handed him something. Then Lord Ky's son left the grounds as well. The deep-elf continued to watch until Lord Ky, the high-elf and the dwarf left. He started to head for the meeting place when he heard the children thundering into the building. He jumped from the sill and concealed himself where he could spy on them. The first to enter the room was a young female dwarf. The deep-elf watched her as she sped through the side door to where the bathing tubs were. The other children followed a few seconds behind her. "Remind me never to pick a fight with him!" Aemir exclaimed as he started yanking off his practice tunic. "Who?" Tal asked. "Your brother! I've never seen anyone fight like that before." "I wonder what's so special at the farm," Micah said. "Don't know. Guess we'll find out when we get there," Little Ky replied. The conversations faded as the children rushed into the

wash room. The deep-elf, noting where Tal and Eleana had dropped their tunics, quietly cut a small piece from each. He took great care to make sure some of their blood was on them. He wrapped his cuttings in another small piece of cloth and ran from the room. Bhk-at should be very pleased with his trophy, the deep-elf thought. Seconds after the deep-elf left, Mena entered the room and collected the practice tunics and wooden swords. After the children left for the farm, it would be her task to make sure their gear was clean. She had seen the sparring match between Lord Ky and his son and did not wish to be on the wrong end of either of their swords. She waited until Ky II arrived, collected his gear, then left to tend to her assigned tasks. Eleana saw to all their wounds as they bathed. Soon all the children were cleaned and dressed in their best tunics. They left the barracks and headed for the Cracked Anvil discussing the practice session they had had that morning. Although they were sore, they all expressed the desire to continue with the training. They entered the Cracked Anvil laughing and singing. Ky was at the back table talking with Stan, so they sat at the large table near the door and waited. Each was trying to guess who awaited them at the farm. Over and over again they would glance at the small table in the back as they talked and joked with each other. They grew louder as the wait progressed, as if their volume would let Ky know they were there. Finally, Ky and Stan walked to the table. "I didn't know you were here!" Stan exclaimed. "I'd have brought you some lunch." Stan laughed with the children, then added, "Have fun at the farm. When you come back, it'll be a lot of hard work." "Let's go," Ky said as he headed for the kitchen. The children knocked over one of the benches in their rush to follow Ky. They laughed as they picked it up and ran to catch up with Ky. Seconds later, the Cracked Anvil quieted to the normal conversations that filled the common room every day. Near the wall, the two deep-elf spies shared with each other what they had learned. Their smiles of accomplishment exposed their sharpened teeth. They scampered over the broken wall and returned to the underground.

23 Ghostspawn stumbled across the threshold into darkness muttering curses. He would have gone in freely had Mistress given him a chance. Instead, she felt the need to shove him through the doorway. He wondered why she told him to close his eyes. There was nothing to see here. He started walking through complete blackness. Raising his hand before his face, he sought to see it. Even after it made contact with his face, he still could not see it. Only the sound of his footsteps on the cold stone path gave him the notion that he was making progress. After a while, he began to wonder if he were going the right way. There had been none of the promised distractions or temptations to sway him from the path. There had been nothing but blackness. He yawned as he continued walking. The longer he walked, the more his pace dragged. Then he felt the magic violently decimate his being. It ravaged his body, raped his spirit and pillaged his mind. No part of him was sacred. He also knew he walked the correct path. He let his anger at the intrusion fuel his footsteps. He no longer doubted that he would arrive at The Grove. -You are a freak of someone else's magic. You have no right to come here. Return from whence you came!- "I am Ghostspawn. It was I that captured The Ghost when the cat-god could not!" -A lowly thantor captured The Ghost. You were no more than bait.- "I stopped the cat-god using his own weapon against him!"

-You were but the tool of a greater god's curse. You are nothing. Begone!- "I am a guest of Mistress! I will not turn back!" -Then to Mistress you will go.- Although Mistress' cabin was lit only by a few candles, the sudden light after an eternity of darkness caused Ghostspawn to stagger. He recognized the room immediately. He saw the skull- framed doorway to his right and almost turned to it as he walked through a chair. He closed his eyes and continued straight. As he suspected, he did not collide with walls or shelves. Abruptly, the magic left him. He felt that the path would be easy now. He believed he had passed the test. After a while, he opened his eyes again. The blackness had returned. More time passed though how much the goblin could not determine. Then, a form became visible in the distance. Ghostspawn marveled that he could actually see it when he still could not see his own hand when placed in front of his face. "You should consider yourself honored, freak," the figure said. "I've time to deal with you now. The Ghost is not here to send me away or protect you. Your request that I destroy you will be honored." The figure in the distance laughed as hundreds of goblins with torn throats clawed their way through the stone floor and advanced on Ghostspawn. He ignored the goblins as they approached believing them to be no more substantial than Mistress' cabin had been. Although they caused no damage when he passed through them, they chilled his body making him feel the very marrow in his bones was ice. Ghostspawn closed his eyes and covered his ears. Time after time, he felt a goblin spirit pass through him. He thought the protectors of The Grove were trying to freeze him to the point he could walk no more. Eventually, this trial passed behind him. He shivered as he continued walking. His thoughts raced to guess what the next hurdle would be. He had plenty of time to consider as he walked with closed eyes. "You seem lost," a whisper from beside him said. Ghostspawn ignored it. He recognized the voice and decided The Ghost would not bother being in this place. The whisper bothered him though. It sounded too much like the real thing. Ghostspawn kept his eyes shut and his feet moving. "You do realize you're going the wrong way, don't you?" the whisper asked. "You are close, but not quite on the right path. Come this way." "How would you even know where I'm going?" muttered Ghostspawn as he continued forward. "How is it you doubt that I would?" the whisper answered.

"I'm going the right way or you wouldn't be here," Ghostspawn spat. "Maybe I'm here to help. You don't know for sure do you?" the whisper answered. "I do know. I'm not changing my path!" Ghostspawn replied. Silence followed for a few moments. Then the whisper said, "Good. You keep to your path. I wouldn't want you knowing the way to my home anyway." These words troubled the goblin. He was not sure if The Ghost had really spoken them. The voice encouraged him to continue on his chosen path. He wondered if that would happen if he were going the right way. He thought about it for a while as he walked. Nothing more came from the darkness. He thought the first part of his walk, before the trials began was long. This time the nothingness seemed to stretch into days. He almost decided to turn a little to his right as the whisper suggested when a hand rested on his shoulder. "You can stop now," Mistress said. "You are at the entrance to The Grove." The actual physical presence of the hand on his shoulder was the only thing that stopped the goblin. Nothing before had actually touched him. He dared to open his eyes and found Mistress standing before him. Behind her, a cave entrance framed her form. "I'm proud of you, my student. For a while, I did not think you capable of getting here." She turned and indicated the cave. "It's a short walk from here. I remind you not to say anything. I will do the talking for both of us." "How do I know this isn't another trick to lead me astray?" Mistress laughed, then said, "You don't." Without further comment, she turned and entered the cavern. Ghostspawn could see no other option, so followed. The cave he entered glowed softly with a pale blue light. A thick layer of sand covered the floor. Natural walls and ceiling, eroded by water alternated with intricately carved sections depicting mazes of great complexity. Trying to follow the paths carved in just one of the mazes would take centuries and lead the seeker to madness. A hundred feet later, an arched bridge stood over a rapidly moving stream that encircled a large cavern. Mistress led Ghostspawn to the apex of the bridge and instructed him to kneel and wait. Ghostspawn did not argue. Mistress walked to the base of the bridge and began singing softly. Ghostspawn used this time to examine the cave. The stream under the bridge he knelt upon circled the cave. Ghostspawn could find no outlet or where the water entered the cave. Nine other identical bridges crossed the stream at equal intervals. Each led to a

cavern similar to the one he had just walked through. The central portion of the room had a diameter of three hundred feet. Twenty feet beyond each bridge stood a massive stone pillar of black-veined marble. In the center stood an eleventh pillar, twice as massive as those surrounding it. Sparkling blue sand covered the floor. The smoothly cut ceiling could be seen around the edges. The central portion was lost to view by the pale blue haze. Ghostspawn turned his attention to Mistress. The song she sang had found a complicated rhythm and her body began moving in time with it. The dance was both mesmerizing and erotic. The goblin watched as she moved to the closest pillar. She danced circles around the pillar until it began to vibrate and emit a sanguine glow. Mistress danced towards the second pillar, the rhythm of her song altering slightly as she approached. Her movements became more violent. Ghostspawn could visualize the sword and spear her hands conducted. The pillar responded with a rumbling vibration and a smoky-gray glow. Again, the rhythm changed as Mistress moved to the next pillar. Her body appeared to be fluid and boneless as she circled the pillar. The vibrations from this pillar resembled the endless crashing of waves upon the shore and it emitted a greenish-blue glow that flowed across its surface. Mistress' song slowed, her tones becoming sullen and dark as she moved towards the next pillar. Her dance emulated grief and sorrow as wails found their way into her melody. The pillar reacted, vibrated slowly and emitted a black glow. As Mistress moved to the fifth pillar, Ghostspawn noticed that sections of the central pillar mirrored the glow of the surrounding smaller ones. The multi-hued glow of the large pillar obscured the goblin's view of the dance. He vaguely saw Mistress leaping and twirling until the pillar vibrated, sounding like a tornado as a cloudy glow of swirling whites, grays and blacks surrounded it. The song changed again as Mistress approached the sixth pillar. This time it resembled a lullaby. Mistress resembled a maiden dancing in a field of newly blossomed flowers. A soft rhythmic vibration accompanied the fresh greenish glow from the pillar. Ghostspawn could barely hear the song over the roar of the vibrating pillars as Mistress approached the seventh. Her dance seemed without rhythm as her body bent low then erupted upright. This pillar vibrated with a deafening roar as yellow, orange and red flickered over its surface. The echoes of the vibrations made it impossible to tell if Mistress still sang. The eighth variation of the dance slowed as Mistress appeared to be caressing a lover while she swirled around the

pillar. A soft vibration and pinkish glow awakened from this pillar. Mistress moved to the ninth pillar, her movements small, slow and deliberate. The pillar responded with a deep-toned vibration and brownish glow. As Mistress moved to the tenth pillar her movements became sporadic yet had a celebratory feel to them. Ghostspawn imagined her a barmaid dancing for soldiers at a victory feast. The pillar vibrated and gave off a purplish glow. Finally she moved to the center of the cavern and danced around the massive pillar glowing with a kaleidescope of colors. She repeated each dance she had performed for the smaller pillars, changing after each circuit was complete. The vibrations within the hall roared louder and stronger as she progressed. Ghostspawn felt the vibrations in the bridge he knelt upon, saw the effect on the sands within the cavern and the churning waters of the stream. He found himself struggling to breathe. Then silence. The glows remained around the pillars, but the vibrations ceased. Ghostspawn held his breath as he stared wide-eyed at Mistress kneeling before the central pillar. Her forehead rested on the sand and her arms stretched towards the giant stone. The goblin found himself trembling, as if the vibrations of the pillars continued within his body. It was not until Mistress beckoned him to join her that he remembered to breathe. The goblin's legs refused to carry him, so he crept across the sands until he drew nigh to the stone, then copied Mistress' pose. He stayed there, more out of need than respect, and waited. He did not notice when Mistress stood, but he heard her words. "I bring before you my apprentice. He is a goblin who has managed to steal immortality from a god greater than the old ones, a god even Karn-Rachk'sha and Tasenta-Somar bow before. Surely, you will find a place for him." The vibrations erupted again as the pillars held council. Ghostspawn shut his eyes to keep the dancing sands from them. Slowly, one by one, the eleven pillars stopped vibrating. Mistress smiled as she noted that the last to vibrate was the pillar of war. When that pillar finally ceased, she helped the goblin to his feet. "Come, it is time to go," she whispered. "We do not wish to overstay our welcome." Ghostspawn meekly nodded and followed Mistress from the hall.

24 Eight hungry children followed Ky through the portal from the Cracked Anvil. They arrived to find lunch prepared, courtesy of Illya with the help of Laena and Delmaria. They rushed towards the two tables, then stopped midway. A strange object caught their attention in the reading area. Lunch forgotten, they quickly gathered around the large table-like furnishing with its backless stool. "What is it?" Eleana asked. "Don't know," answered Tal. "It's a piano," Micah stated as he brushed his fingers across the ivory keys. "Oh," said Ky II. "One question, though. What's a piano?" Both Micah and Little Ky laughed. "It's for making music," Little Ky explained. "What's it doing here?" "How's anyone supposed to carry that around?" Ky II asked. Ky interrupted their examination of the piano and sent them to the table to eat. Frowning, they moved to the table glancing over their shoulders at the piano. When they were seated, Ky left the room. During the meal, Micah was riddled with questions about the instrument. Finally, he promised to try to play it after the meal was over if Ky would allow it. They spent the rest of the meal quietly attempting to inhale their food. Meanwhile, Ky searched for William. He found him and Daphnia strolling through the orchard. He waited on the steps for an opportunity to get his attention. William appeared to notice nothing but Daphnia. Ky started pacing across the porch, taking great care to

find every loose board that would creak or squeak. Still, neither William nor Daphnia looked his way. Finally, he summoned his bow and readied an arrow. Delmaria stepped through the door as Ky released the arrow. "Ky!" Delmaria exclaimed a second too late. The arrow flew into the orchard and embedded into the trunk of a tree about a foot away from William and Daphnia. William threw his arm around Daphnia and dived for cover, using his body to protect her. When he looked up to see where the arrow had originated from, he saw Delmaria running across the yard towards them and Ky leaning on one of the posts with a bow in his hand. As Delmaria approached, William helped Daphnia to her feet, apologizing all the while. Ky jumped off the porch and walked to the orchard. "Trees be fallin'! That black-eyed demon child needs a learnin' in manners," Daphnia stated as she brushed leaves and grass from her dress. "Why didn't you just call them?" Delmaria asked when Ky arrived. "Not much of a surprise if I go yelling his name all over the farm," Ky said, then turned to William. "The children are here. The piano has their attention at the moment." "The piano is here?" William asked. "For now. I'll move it back to your place in Cragsguard when you are ready to go there. Where's the Old Man?" "I haven't seen him today," William said, his face taking a pinkish tint. "With all the excitement, I didn't even notice him not here." Ky glanced at Daphnia. "So it's called excitement, now." "Never mind, Ky," Delmaria said as she led William and Daphnia towards the house. "You've caused enough mischief already." Ky shrugged and followed. Delmaria and Daphnia waited in the kitchen as William followed Ky into the parlor. Ky stopped William in the parlor then stepped into the old council chamber. He found the children eating their meals in gulps, barely trying to chew it up as it entered their mouths. "Eat slower," Ky said. "You're going to sit there until I say otherwise. You might as well have something to do while you're there. Micah, I need you for a moment." Micah quickly glanced around the table before slowly walking across the room with wide eyes and a slight tremble to his hands. He stopped a few feet away from Ky and stared at the floor as he waited. "Take this," Ky whispered as he held out a folded piece of

loose-leaf paper, "and wait for me in the parlor." Micah took the paper and opened the door just wide enough that he could slip through. It closed as soon as he was in the parlor. He stood staring at the door trying to figure out what he had done to gain Ky's attention. His mind filled with all the ways he could have failed the elf's expectations of him. A tear formed in his eye as he thought that he might even be sent back to Vienna. "Is that for me?" William asked. William's eyes were also tearful, but his were tears of joy. It took a moment for him to find his voice, the sight of his son, the son he had thought beyond his reach forever, had filled his throat with emotions that denied him speech. Micah understood the words that held a heavy Austrian accent. He glanced at the paper he held before turning to see if his imagination or his ears had actually heard them. Seeing Herr William seated in the room made him doubt his eyesight as well. Regardless, he walked across the room and held out the paper. Herr William accepted the note, unfolded it and read it aloud, in German. August 1987 Dear Herr Wiliam and teechers, Thank you for adopting me and letting me come to your school. I will work really hard. You really made me happy bringing me heer. Love, Micah. When William finished, he looked at the boy standing in front of him. "Sadly, schools are not allowed to adopt children. Only an adult can do such a thing." He paused a moment, then with quaking voice added, "I hope you don't mind that it was I that actually adopted you." Micah shook his head, still not sure whether to believe his eyes and ears. "Also, I hope you don't mind that I've come to stay here with you. I'm told I have a wonderful apartment in Cragsguard." The realization of the circumstances finally reached Micah and his emotions exploded as he dived into William's embrace, both suffering from uncontrollable crying. Daphnia had been waiting in the kitchen and rushed to the doorway to see what was wrong.

"Trees be fallin'! What did that evil demon-eyed elf-child do to the boy?" She rushed into the room to console William and Micah. Micah blurted out, in German, "He gave me my father!" and returned to crying into William's shoulder. "Poor child! Can't even speak right now!" Daphnia exclaimed. William's tears changed to laughter and he explained the situation to Daphnia as best he could under the circumstances. In moments the three sat sharing their happiness. Meanwhile, Archos arrived through the portal from Cragsguard, followed by the head-librarian of Alle-Stecan. They walked to Ky who handed the librarian a piece of loose-leaf paper and a pencil. The librarian frowned at the materials, but accepted them. "You realize that I am only here because Sage Tas'lin asked me to come?" Ky shrugged and nodded to the door. "You'll find the thing to be copied in there." Before stepping away from the door, he turned to Archos. "The original is over two-thousand years old by our reckoning of time. You may wish to put your preservation spell on it." Archos smiled. "Of course." With no further comment, Archos and the librarian entered the parlor. They found William, Micah and Daphnia talking and laughing together. Archos began to introduce them to the librarian but was stopped. "I've no time for frivolities. Where is the document?" the old elf asked. Archos saw that William held Micah's letter. "Please, William, will you be so kind as to show this time-pressured elf the note?" William noted the glint of humor in Archos' eyes and presented the loose-leaf to the librarian. The librarian accepted the letter as if it were made from the most fragile of materials. A small desk and chair stood beside the bookshelves. The librarian scurried to the desk and placed the pencil and paper Ky had given him on the chair. He then removed a folded cotton cloth from his pocket and meticulously cleaned the desktop before placing the note upon it. Then, he placed the paper Ky had given him beside it, picked up his pencil and sat. Micah, William and Archos moved where they could watch the librarian's progress. Both Micah and William marveled at the exactness of the librarian's copying. It took quite some time for the old elf to scribe the unfamiliar writings onto the spare paper. "I will need a translation," he muttered when he finished. "I believe Micah can do that for you," Archos stated as he

guided Micah forward. Micah pointed to the first word only to have his hand pushed away by the librarian. "Kindly keep your grubby hands away from the original. Come on this side and point to the copy." "But I wrote it!" Micah said as he moved to the other side of the table. "When you wrote it, it did not have the historical significance it carries now," the librarian sputtered. "Do as you are asked!" Word by word, Micah translated the note, pointing out words that were misspelled as he did so. The librarian had him write the words correctly near the errors. When the task had been completed, the librarian picked up his copy and impatiently waited while Archos cast the preservation spell on the original. "Why is that so important now?" Micah asked. The librarian ignored the question. He believed that he had endured the child's presence long enough. He stood uncomfortably close to Archos tapping his foot. "I will explain later, Micah," Archos answered, smiling at the boy. "Are you ready to go?" he asked the head-librarian. The librarian's snort and Archos' laughter faded as Archos ported them back to Alle-Stecan. A few moments after that, the Old Man and Little Ky entered the room. Little Ky was almost as excited to see Herr William as Micah was. Shortly after the reunion and catching-up completed, The Old Man explained what Ky had planned for them. "Horses are waiting for us in the barn. We'll be going to Cragsguard to see your new home, William. Little Ky, Micah and Daphnia will be coming as well. After you are settled, Delmaria will be taking at least three of you to visit the wild-elves again. She is checking to see if Little Ky is welcome to go with you." "Micah has a wonderful voice," William stated, not hiding the pride in his voice. "I wonder if the wild-elves would enjoy a song from him." "It's quite possible they will," the Old Man replied. "I will take the boys and Daphnia to ready the horses. Ky would like to introduce you to the other children." "Ah, yes. He did say there were more," William said standing. "Are they in there?" The Old Man nodded as he started to lead Little Ky and Micah from the room. "Dad," Micah said before William could make it to the council room door.

"Yes, son?" "Nothing, I just had to call you 'Dad' once." He beamed a tremendous smile as he hurried after The Old Man and Little Ky. Daphnia excused herself to prepare for the journey as William opened the door to the council room. Ky led him to the table where the other children were still eating. "Stand when I introduce you," Ky instructed before turning to William. "This is Herr William. That is what I want you to call him. He is Micah's father and he cared for Little Ky and the Old Man while they were imprisoned." Ky pointed to Brek. "Herr William, this is Brek. He is a goblin in training to become a member of the Council of Darkness. He is unusual for a goblin in that you can not smell him, though that is a new thing for him." William held out his hand to Brek as the goblin stood. "A pleasure to meet you, Brek." Brek stared at the hand not knowing what to do with it. Ky thought for a moment not truly understanding the gesture either. "I don't think he has anything to give you, Herr William," Ky said. He waited until Brek was seated, then indicated Aemir. "This is Aemir. He is a high-elf and twin to Taelann by means of the Ceremony of Flesh-to-Flesh. Both he and Taelann lost their twins in the battle with Rachk'sha's minions. Now they are complete again. He is being trained to become a member of The Nine." "An honor to meet you, Aemir," William said smiling as the elf stood. "The human is my brother, Simon. He is being trained as well, but I believe he is to be a greater god, beyond a seat in either of the councils. We have to wait for his inheritance to know for sure." "Greetings, Simon," William said. "When will you acquire your inheritance?" "About three more years, Herr William," Simon answered. "The last three are my triplets. The eldest is Eleana." Ky waited while Eleana was greeted by William. "Then Tal." Again Ky waited. "And finally, Ky II." Ky led William to the piano and asked him to wait a moment. Then he gathered the triplets and whispered instructions to them. The triplets walked to the piano and waited as Ky had the others move to the piano as well. When all were there, Ky nodded to Tal. Tal began singing a song of the war between the humans and elves. When he finished the first verse, Eleana joined him singing a counter melody above his. Finally Ky II joined the song with yet another counter melody. William listened raptly as the three elven

children's voices filled the room. He marveled at how one was singing what seemed like a battle cry, full of ferocity and anger as another sang what seemed a dirge to the dying and the third voice seemed to emphasize the melancholy of the aftermath. The result left William drying his eyes on his sleeves. When they finished, Ky gave William a moment to recover. "Thank you! That is one of the most beautiful melodies I have ever heard." "They are curious about this piano," Ky said quietly. "I wonder if you would mind playing one of the Mozart tunes for them?" William smiled and replied, "I would be most pleased to entertain them. It is the least I can do." All of the children were enthralled with the sound as they watched Herr William's hands which seemed to be dancing spiders on the keyboard. He played them a composition that had a quick tempo and enjoyed watching them nod their heads and tap their feet in time with the music. At the song's conclusion, the children thanked William and several asked if he would be around to play more songs for them. "I'm sure I will be," William answered. "I will be happy to play for you whenever time permits." "Herr William." William turned to look at Tal. "I wonder if you would teach me to do that, please?" William turned to Ky and said, "I would love to teach any that wish to learn, if they have the time." Ky grinned as he regarded Tal. "He can come to you in the evenings to learn to play, as can any of the others that wish to learn. They have to wait until after their inheritance ceremony though." "This inheritance ceremony is unknown to me. Would I be asking too much if I were to ask to be there for it?" "You are welcome to come to it," Ky answered as he led William to the door. "Besides, it will give you a chance to visit Alle- Stecan and meet the king of the high-elves." Ky walked with William to the porch where the Old Man, Little Ky, Micah and Daphnia were waiting. The Old Man helped William onto his horse. "I can not thank the two of you enough for bringing me here. I have my son; the other children are enchanting, and I've met Daphnia. Life can get no better for me," William said, smiling. "Would you mind playing at the triplets inheritance ceremony?" Ky asked. "You mean before the elven king and all?" William asked. "Yeah, he'll be there too," Ky stated, nodding.

"I will begin practicing at once!" William exclaimed. "I hope I don't disappoint you." "You won't," Ky answered as he returned to the house. The Old Man led them north at a slow pace. It would take only a few hours to arrive at Cragsguard and none but himself had ever ridden a horse before. The journey through the wilds awed William. He had never experienced so much untouched nature before and he loved it. They talked and sang as they traveled. When they arrived at Cragsguard, the Old Man led them to the Cracked Anvil for dinner before taking them to William's new home. Stan was very happy to see the Old Man and Little Ky, and he treated William, Micah and Daphnia as family. When the group was ready to leave, Stan joined them, leaving Oran to care for the inn. "This used to be a bakery," the Old Man explained as he led them to William's new home. "If you would like to start that business again, I'm sure the townspeople will welcome you and your wares. I will of course assist you in getting started." "As will I," Stan added. "It will be good to have fresh breads to serve at the Anvil. That is if you want my business." William laughed, "It would be poor business, indeed, not to want the business of an inn as popular as yours, Stan. I believe I just might do that. Maybe Micah will help me when he isn't off learning how to slay horrible monsters and such." "I'll help too," Little Ky said. "I'm sure dad won't mind." "How can I go wrong!" William exclaimed. "I've too young lads to help, a steady customer and an old, trusted friend to guide me." The Old Man led them into the building. Ky had prepared it well for William. Even though the place had been deserted for over twenty years, it appeared to have been newly constructed. The maple floorboards glowed beneath a highly polished finish. A counter, also finished in maple, divided the front room. The outer portion of the room contained a shelf for displaying freshly baked goods. Behind the counter, a large stone oven stood in the center of the back wall. To its right stood a neat stack of wood and kindling. On the left, a doorway led to the private quarters. William and the boys took their time examining everything. All three wore smiles as they explored. Under the counter, they found the large wooden spatulas for placing and removing things from the oven. A small cash-box also rested on a small shelf there. William opened the box to find it already supplied with copper, silver and gold coins. Several covered bins of flour and one smaller bin of sugar nestled under the counter as well. When all were satisfied that the front room had been

thoroughly explored, they moved to the back room. Four padded chairs stood in a semi-circle around a large marble mantle. The fireplace already had wood ready to be lit. Beside it, a small bin sat with ample replacement wood. A shelf, loaded with books, stood across the room from the mantle. Beside the shelf, stood the piano. A thick woolen carpet, woven in brown, white and gray, covered the maple floor. At the back of the room, a stairway led to the upper floor. A door beside the stairwell led to a small private kitchen. Upstairs, they found two elegantly furnished bedrooms. William's belongings had already been neatly put away for him in the master bedroom. In the smaller bedroom, they found clothing for Micah and the LEGO® farm that Little Ky and Micah had built in the sun-room in Austria. "It's perfect," William muttered as they returned to the sitting room downstairs. "I could not have chosen a better place if I took a hundred years to search for one." "Remember, I live next door," the Old Man laughed. "It may not be as perfect as you think." William nodded and said, "Well everything must have at least one flaw." Both he and the Old Man laughed. Daphnia hurried to the kitchen to make tea for the adults and chocolate for the two boys as the others tested the chairs around the fireplace. Micah and Little Ky chose to sit on the thick rug in front of the mantle. William lit a fire and they spent the next few hours talking about Cragsguard. Stan left early to close up the Cracked Anvil. He was followed about an hour later by the Old Man. "Tomorrow will be a busy day for you," the Old Man explained. "Delmaria will take you to visit the wild-elves with Micah and Little Ky, if Little Ky is welcome, then I will take you around Cragsguard and show you where everything is." "If Little Ky can not go with us, what will he do while we are away?" William asked. "He will spend his time with me or Stan or at the library. Don't worry, William, we will keep him busy and happy until you return." William walked The Old Man to the door. "You are expected to return to the farm on the next day, by the way. That way you can visit with all the children for a couple days." "I look forward to it," William said smiling. "I will see you tomorrow, then." "That you will," the Old Man replied as he left. Stan had provided Daphnia a room at the Cracked Anvil. She left shortly after the Old Man. Afterwards, William escorted the two

boys upstairs and tucked them in. They, being exhausted by their busy day, had no trouble falling asleep to the lullaby William quietly sang for them. Then, he went to his own room and settled in for the night. Before climbing under his blankets, he muttered a small prayer of thanks for the great fortune bestowed upon him.

25 Shortly following William's departure for Cragsguard, the remaining children were sent outside to entertain themselves. Ky joined them and it was not long before Ky II managed to monopolize his father's time. Brek, Eleana, Simon and Aemir started a wild game of tag. Tal watched his brother and father for a short while, then climbed the cliff to sit among the trees just within the forest. He thought the others were too occupied to notice his departure, but Aemir saw where he went and followed. Aemir approached Tal slowly, stopping a short distance away. "Do you mind if I join you?" Aemir asked. Tal shrugged, then nodded. Aemir sat with his back against a tree near Tal and watched him a few moments. He could tell that Tal was troubled by something and worried that he had been the cause. He absently drew pictures in the dirt with a twig while he tried to find the words to open the conversation. Finally, he just asked outright. "Did I do something wrong?" Aemir asked, his voice little more than a whisper. Tal grinned a second before answering, "No." "What's wrong then?" Tal stood and turned to look down the hill at the farm. Brek and Eleana had moved behind the barn and were throwing knives at a target they had set up. Ky II and his father were seated near the orchard talking. Simon sat at the end of the porch watching them. "You really sound like you want to help," Tal murmured.

"I do," Aemir said. "Tell me what I can do." Tal pointed to Simon. "He's going to need a friend while my father is around. Ky II won't be paying much attention to him, and although Simon likes me, I don't think I could fill the void for him." Aemir stood and looked at the events taking place at the bottom of the hill. He had just this morning gained respect for Ky II and was troubled that he would ignore his friend in this way. "Why would Ky II shun Simon like that?" Tal glanced at Aemir and read the confusion and anger in his face. "Sit down. I'll explain as best I can. Don't blame Ky II. I'd be doing the same if I didn't think Ky II needed it more." The two elves sat on the forest floor. Tal played with a few twigs while gathering his thoughts. He wasn't sure how to explain what was happening to Aemir. He did not want to alienate Aemir from the others or from his father. "It's hard to explain," Tal said quietly, "but I'll try. You sorta have to know my father to understand. He isn't around much. When he is, Ky II spends as much time as possible with him as he doesn't know when he will get another chance. "Ky II always hears how much like dad he is. He feels that he has to live up to that. When dad is around, Ky II tries to get to know him more and more. I guess he feels he can do a better job of living up to everyone's expectations that way. I do my best to stay out of the way. Also, since Ky II had always striven to be like dad, he's never really had any friends. Simon is his first real friend. Ky II doesn't know anything about friendship. He doesn't know that ignoring Simon now is hurting Simon. All he is seeing is time with dad." "So it's that your dad isn't a good dad?" Aemir asked. Tal laughed. "Go look at them again. Tell me what you see." Tal waited as Aemir looked down the hill for a few moments. When Aemir returned, he looked more confused than earlier. "I really don't know what I was looking for. They are just sitting there talking." "If you didn't know what they were wearing, would you be able to tell them apart from up here?" Aemir glanced down the hill again, then shook his head. "No. They look exactly alike, except for their eyes." "Exactly. Ky II is a kid. Just like you and me. So is dad. Would you be a good father at your age?" Aemir's eyes widened as he stared at Tal. The thought that Ky was still a child never crossed his mind and probably would not have had Tal not said it. Aemir found it a very difficult concept to swallow. He moved so he could clearly see Ky and Ky II. After

watching them for a few moments, he looked at Simon. Even from this distance, Simon's pain and confusion were obvious to Aemir. He returned his attention to Tal. "I can be a friend for Simon. What about you?" "What about me?" Tal asked. "Do you have any friends?" Tal sighed. "I've had lots of friends. I sort of let them drift away after a while though." "Why?" "Since we're twins, I can read Ky II's thoughts, especially when he is upset and doesn't hide them well. You probably know this since you are a twin as well. When I had friends around, Ky II would have nightmares. At first I didn't understand them. They were full of loneliness. He would be in Chaos searching for someone, someone that was never there. Sometimes he would dream of other places, too. But they were the same. He was always alone and seeking someone. He would have these dreams whenever I had a friend around for a while." "So you give up your friends for your brother," Aemir whispered, not hiding the awe in his voice. "Wouldn't you?" "I don't know if I could. I wasn't the best of big brothers." Aemir's voice trailed off as he pulled his legs to him and dropped his chin on his knees. "Maybe, if you are successful with Simon, it will make up for that. I know you talk to Aemar a lot. Do you ever tell him how you feel, now?" Aemir shook his head. "I don't know how." Tal shrugged, "Easiest way is just to say it. Take Simon with you. It will be good for you and a nice distraction for Simon." "What if Simon doesn't want to go?" "If I know Simon, he'll go if you ask him to keep you company." "I'll try," Aemir said. "What about you?" "I might meet you there later. I want to be alone for a while," Tal said as he turned away and stared into the forest. Aemir stood and looked at Tal a few moments, then said, "I hope you do come. I think I could learn a lot having you as a friend." Tal's smile was his only response. Aemir took it as an expectation that he would see Tal later at the library and returned to the farm. Pausing a moment at the bottom of the cliff, Aemir decided that the direct approach would work with Simon as well as his brother. He put on his best smile and ran to the porch where Simon still sat. "Simon, I want to visit with Aemar. I was wondering if you

would come with me. He would really like to meet you." Simon looked one last time at Ky II and Ky then shrugged. "Sure, I'll go. We should let someone know where we are going though." Laena thanked them for letting her know of their intentions and the two boys used the portal to the Cracked Anvil to go to Cragsguard. They waved at Stan as they ran through the common room. "Will you join me there as well?" "Sure. I haven't visited either of them since," Simon's voice faltered a moment, then he finished with, "since they came here." Aemir led the way to Daelann's shrine where they could visit with Aemar. He pulled the curtain aside and waited as Simon entered, then followed him. Daelann's shrine differed greatly from Symplex's. Where the sarcophagus lay in Symplex's shrine, a miniature forest grew in the center of Daelann's. Bas-relief vines and wildlife decorated the side walls. At the far end, a bench rested in a well-manicured patch of grass. Daelann's sword supported a climbing vine growing from the top of the willow altar. Two statues stood on either side of the altar, to the right stood Daelann, to the left, Aemar. Simon had not been in the shrine before and took his time approaching the altar. The forest fascinated him. Aemir did not rush Simon, as he remembered Tal's words and wanted to keep Simon occupied as long as possible. Instead, Aemir explained that the weather above the forest would change to match the weather outside. When it rained upon Cragsguard, a small rain would fall upon the forest. Simon bent close to look under the canopy of trees and saw several miniature deer drinking from the river that flowed through the center of the forest. "There's really animals in there!" "They are only spirit animals," Aemir explained. "They mirror the wildlife in the forest near town." When Simon finished exploring the forest, he walked to the statue of Aemar. "He looked a lot like you," Simon stated. "I'll introduce you. Come, sit down." "Good day to you, Aemir and Simon," greeted Daelann. "It is good to see the both of you well."

"Hello, Brother of Worth. I'm really happy Ky didn't kill you," said Aemar. "Hi, Lord Daelann and Aemar." Aemir spoke quickly. He wanted to say what he came to say before Simon could lead the conversation away from him. "I've come to apologize to you, Aemar. I have not been the best of brothers. I know that I only did what I was taught to do, but I still feel that it was wrong. I am no better or more worthy than you." Aemir blinked the tears back and finished with, "In fact, I have been far less worthy than you ever were. Please, call me by my name from now on." The confession shocked Simon. He knew that Aemir's spirit person bore his guilt. He had seen it. Simon never realized what that guilt referred to though. What surprised him most is that Aemir made this apology with him present. Simon could read the honesty and heart-felt need for forgiveness within Aemir and hoped that Aemar did not discount what was said. Several moments passed before Aemar's voice answered. "Aemir, I have always looked up to you and wished I could be as strong and as successful as you were. I knew that if I followed your example, I would be a real person someday. I will accept your apology because Daelann tells me that you need me to. Otherwise, I see no reason to apologize. You are what kept me wanting to live." Aemir cried earnestly after hearing his brothers words. Simon slid closer to him and put his arm over Aemir's shoulders to comfort him. At Daelann's suggestion, the spirit of Aemar waited a few moments to give his brother time to cry. When Aemir finally gained some control and looked up, Aemar said, "I don't know Simon yet. Who is he?" Aemir brushed the tears from his face with his sleeve and glanced at Simon. "Oh yeah. This is one of my new friends, Simon. He's Lord Ky's brother and is training with us. I think Lady Selia brought him to the farm." "Hi, Simon. Thanks for coming with Aemir to visit." "Hi," Simon said, still watching Aemir. Aemir took a shuddering breath and smiled. "Well, talk to each other." Simon, Aemar and Daelann laughed. The two boys stayed in the shrine for over an hour trading stories with Daelann and Aemar. They explained that they wanted to visit Lord Symplex and Lady Selia before they returned to the farm and promised that they would return soon. Aemir's initial intention in coming here was to make Simon feel better. He was surprised that he had never felt so good as when

they left Daelann's shrine. Glancing at Simon, as they walked to Symplex's shrine with arms over each other's shoulders, he could tell that Simon's mood had changed for the better as well. To his surprise, he found himself gladdened even more by this. The visit with Symplex did not last as long as their visit with Aemar and Daelann. Simon and Aemir told Symplex all that had happened that morning in the practice grounds and later at the farm. Symplex asked occasional questions, but, for the most part, played the role of listener. They both promised to visit again soon before leaving to visit Lady Selia's shrine. They found Tal waiting for them when they left Symplex. "You came!" Aemir exclaimed as he saw Tal sitting outside Daelann's shrine. "Yeah," Tal replied smiling. "I said I might." "We're about to visit with Lady Selia," Aemir explained. "Will you come with us?" "Sure. I haven't spoken with her in a long time." As he had done with the previous shrines, Aemir pulled the curtain aside and let his friends enter first. Lady Selia's shrine had been finished in rose-veined marble. What it lacked in decor, it made up for in simple elegance. The only decoration was Selia's platinum armor which stood upon a low altar on the far side of the room. Although the bench was not padded like the others, the marble seat still made the visitor comfortable. She greeted them as soon as they entered. "Welcome, Simon, Aemir and Tal. It is a pleasure to see you today." The three boys greeted her as they sat. Aemir made sure to be in the middle so he could be beside both his new friends. "I'm surprised to see you here without Ky II, Simon. Where is he?" Both Tal and Aemir tried to cut her off unsuccessfully. "He's with dad at the farm," Tal explained as Aemir put his arm around Simon's shoulder. "That is still the way of things. Don't worry, Simon. Your brother, Ky, rarely stays in one place long. Ky II will be back at your side very soon. What brings the three of you here?" "Just visiting," Aemir said. "I've not had the honor of meeting you yet and wanted to. I asked if Simon and Tal would come with me." "I am glad you came." Selia replied, the smile evident in her voice. "Was Ky always the way he is?" Simon asked. "For the most part, yes. There was a time when I thought he

would change, but that was long ago." "So Ky II will be the same way," Simon muttered. "I don't believe so, though most everyone tells him he is just like his father. Ky II had something all his life that his father only experienced for a very short time. On top of that, Ky's experience ended rather traumatically. Ky II had Laena who taught him love and caring. His father never learned that. He came close when Little Ky lived at the farm with him, but that ended when Little Ky was taken away." "When did you meet my father?" Tal asked. A moment passed before Selia answered, "I met Ky when I was still a squire for the Temple of Light. I was given the mission that would prove my worth to become a knight. I would be happy to tell you that story if you have time." All three boys slid to the edge of the bench and begged Selia to relate the story. Selia laughed and said, "I would be very happy to tell it to you. I will use the memory vision to show you as well. Before I begin though, I wish to share with you another difference between Ky II and his father. Very soon, Tal, you and your siblings will receive your inheritance. Since the denial you received the first time was to save your lives, you will receive all the benefits of that inheritance. The most important being, you will continue to grow and mature. Ky will never do that. Even though his inheritance was denied out of fear and hatred, it cursed him to remain a child until the day he dies. Much to the disappointment of those that denied him that inheritance, that day will be long in coming, if ever." Selia paused as the three boys absorbed what she had said. After a few minutes, she continued. "Enough of that. Sit back and I will share my memory with you." When the boys were ready, a mist formed in the air before them. A steady rain poured down upon Selia as she climbed the road to the gates of the keep. She pulled her cloak tighter and shivered as she glanced up at the barely visible walls of dark gray stone that blended into the dusk and clouds. She walked as quickly as she could trying to keep her mud-soaked, leather boots from slipping beneath her in the muck that was the only road to town. Arriving at the gate, she was surprised to find it open. She paused under the wall a moment, taking relief from the pelting rain she had spent the day walking through. As she stood there, a guard approached her. "Your business, lass." "I seek an inn where a squire may afford a meal," Selia replied.

"Ain't much choice here, lass. Take the first right and follow the road to the square. Ye will find the Cracked Anvil there. Stan will take good care of ye." "Thank you, kind sir." Selia pulled the cloak about her and walked into town. In moments, she stood before the Cracked Anvil. If the guard had not named the inn, she would have passed it up thinking it beyond her means. She stamped the mud from her boots and entered. The common-room was close to full. Only two tables remained unoccupied, a small one in the back near the stairs and one that stood alone beside the fireplace near the door. The blazing fire and the warmth it provided called to her. She walked to the table, removed her cloak and sat in the chair closest to the fire. Checking her coin, she found she still had six silvers to her name. She placed one on the table as a young woman approached her. "Welcome. I'm Del. I'll bring your meal to you in a moment." "Please," Selia interjected before Del could get away. "I've only the one silver to spare for this meal." She held the coin out for Del. "That's fine," Del replied smiling. "I'll get that later, after you've decided we haven't poisoned you." When Del returned, she brought a large bowl of thick stew, a small loaf of bread and a tankard of steaming mead. "Are you sure this is for me?" Selia asked. "You are the only one sitting at this table," Del laughed. "Enjoy your meal." Selia savored every bite of the meal and was nursing the mead when Del returned to take the empty bowl away. "That was the best meal I've had in ages! Might you know a place I could stay for a couple of nights? I've very little coin and my needs are simple." "I'll ask my father if we have a room available," Del answered. Del spoke with the man behind the bar for a moment, then returned. "We have a room you can have. This will cover everything," Del added as she picked up the silver coin. "When you are ready, I'll take you up to your room." "I'm ready," Selia said as she stood and collected her cloak. She followed Del up the stairs to a small room about midway down the hall.

"Enjoy your night. Breakfast will be available in the morning when you come down. It's included in the price," Del added seeing that Selia was about to decline. The memory darkened as Selia entered her room. When it returned, Selia was descending the steps to the common-room. The common-room was packed. Every table, except the small one in the corner was full to bursting. Only one person sat at the smaller table. Selia approached the table. "Mind if I sit here?" she asked. "There's a seat at the bar," the child answered in a whisper that she almost missed. Before Selia could say any more, Del had arrived, placed a plate of food in front of the child and led Selia away. "I'll explain later," Del said. "Come, I'll bring your breakfast over to the bar." Selia had never suffered being seated at a bar prior to this. She found that at the Cracked Anvil, the bar served as another table during the morning breakfast rush. Everyone else seated here were enjoying their morning meal. There was no cursing or drinking. The conversation was light, respectable and quiet. Although it helped a little, she still felt a bit awkward. When Del returned with Selia's meal, she stayed as there were no others that needed serving at the moment. "That is Ky," Del said quietly. "That is Ky's table. No one else is permitted to sit there." Del saw the puzzled look in Selia's eyes. "Normally, we wouldn't cater to anyone in that fashion, but if it were not for him, I'd not be speaking to you today. My father, as you can guess, is quite fond of him. We've discovered that if anyone is sitting there, he leaves. He also has a tendency to disappear if he is disturbed." "How did a child save your life?" Delmaria laughed. "Very few still think of him as a child around here. You mentioned you'd be in town a few days. I'm sure you'll hear about that and many other things as well. He has become a bit of a legend here. The funny thing is that he hates the attention. So, what brings you to Cragsguard?" "I'm a squire for the Temple of Light. I'm currently working to complete my quest to earn my knighthood." "If you need help, let me know. I'm sure some of my friends will be happy to join you as well. A quest sounds exciting and there's been little excitement around here lately." "I have to see what I'm up against. If I can handle the task alone, it would be best. If I need help, I'll take you up on that offer," Selia said, smiling.

"I'll let you finish your breakfast. I need to do some work before my father starts thinking I quit for the day already." Del moved into the common-room and began chatting with the other customers as she cleaned tables, cleared plates, served drinks and meals. Selia watched the place for a while. She felt that she belonged here, though she wasn't sure why. After a short while, she left the Cracked Anvil and headed into the forest outside town. Once again, the memory faded. This time when it returned to view, the sun indicated that it was late afternoon. Selia was just returning to Cragsguard. Her face bore a frown and her pace was slow as she walked the side road to the Cracked Anvil. The inn was nearly empty when she entered. A few townspeople sat at tables here and there enjoying a late lunch or early dinner. She noticed that Ky still sat in the corner and that the proprietor of the inn sat across from him. She found a seat at a table near the door and put her head in her hands. Delmaria placed a meal on the table and sat across from her. "I take it your quest is proving more difficult than you thought." Del noticed that Selia's eyes were red and her cheeks still bore dampness when she looked up. "I don't believe it to be possible," Selia explained. "I will have to go back and hope I receive a different quest." "Can you tell me what your quest is? I may be able to help you." Selia sighed and pushed the meal to the side. "I've been asked to retrieve a book that was stolen from the Temple of Light several years ago. It was discovered that the thief was last seen around here. I found the thief this morning. He is among a colony of thieves north of town. There were also goblins and hobgoblins present. Even if you could raise an army, I doubt we could gain entrance." "Are you sure the thief is there?" a voice whispered behind her. "Yes, I saw him," Selia answered, still talking to Del. "He wears a jagged scar across his face where his right eye should be." When Selia realized that Del did not ask the question, she turned to see who did. No one was behind her. Shrugging, she turned back. "Stay a day or two," Del offered. "We may find a way for you to complete your quest." "And eat," Stan said. "Knights need their strength, not self- pity." Del laughed as she pushed the meal back in front of Selia.

"It seems my father has taken a liking to you. You best do as he says or you may find yourself washing floors for not cleaning your plate properly." Selia smiled and began to eat. "When you finish, I'll show you around town and introduce you to some of my friends. It won't get busy in here for another two or three hours yet. Dinner is usually a late affair here in Cragsguard." Again the memory faded. When it returned, Selia was seated at the bar talking with Stan. Selia was telling him about the Temple of Light when Del interrupted her. "I believe Ky wants to see you," Del said, the surprise in her voice evident in her face. "My suggestion is to listen to what he says, answer any questions, and otherwise be quiet. He's in a weird mood this evening." "Take my daughter's advice to heart," Stan added. "He is quite dangerous if you upset him." Selia leaned back so that she could see the table where Ky usually sat. She found him there, squeezed into the corner as if he wanted to be part of the wall. "Go on," Del whispered. "It's best not to make him wait." Selia left the bar and walked to the back of the room.
