She stopped a couple feet from the table. "You wished to see me?" she asked. "Sit," Ky whispered. He waited until she was settled then placed a coin pouch on the table. "Empty it." Selia picked up the pouch and emptied the contents onto the table. The child picked through the coins and gems. As he took three of the stones and put them in his own pouch, Selia noted that his forearm was wrapped in a bloody rag. "The rest of that is yours. Take these too," he said as he placed two packages on the table. One appeared to be a book, the other was round and soaked through with blood at the bottom. She opened the round package and gaped at the head of the thief she described earlier that day to Del. By the time she found her voice, the child was gone. She stood and searched the room. The child was nowhere to be found. Sighing, she replaced the severed head in it's bag and opened the other package. Inside she found the book she needed to complete her quest. The memory faded as she sat at the table and cried. "I didn't even know he was an elf at that point. But that is a good example of how Ky works. He heard that the quest was impossible so he had to complete it, or at least that part of it. If I had asked his help, he

probably would have declined. His deed also made the replacement task I was given far more difficult after I explained how the original task had been completed when I returned to the Temple of Light." "Did he kill all the thieves and goblins?" Aemir asked. "No," Selia replied, amusement in her voice. "I returned to the colony the next day. Everything remained the same. You'd have thought that nothing happened there." "Thank you for sharing that with us, Lady Selia," Simon said as he stood. "I think we should get back to the farm now. We told Lady Laena that we'd be back for dinner." "My pleasure. Come visit me again when you can." "We will!" exclaimed Aemir. "It was an honor to finally meet you." Tal remained seated and explained, "You two go ahead. I'll meet you back at the farm. I want to speak with Lady Selia a little more." "Okay," Simon answered. "We'll meet you there." Tal watched as Simon and Aemir left, then turned back to the altar. "I miss you," he said. "I'm here whenever you wish to visit me," Selia stated. Tal shrugged, "It's not the same. I miss you teaching me and talking to me. I miss when we sparred, too." "Unfortunately, there is nothing that can change that. You need a friend, one that you will keep this time. Ky II has a friend. I doubt his nightmares will return to torture the two of you. What about Aemir? He seems nice enough." "Yeah," Tal nodded. "He came to me today when he saw me go off alone. He might be a good friend." "I think since he made the first step, you should follow through. Sooner or later, you will need to think of yourself a little. Besides, you will probably provide as much good for him as he provides for you." Tal stood and smiled. "I sort of thought that, but wanted to make sure. See why I miss you?" "And do you see that you came here to see me and we worked it out?" Selia asked. "Yeah, I guess so. Thanks, Lady Selia. I'll be back to visit often." Tal turned and left the shrine. He felt much better as he walked through town on his way back to the farm.

26 Ghostspawn found the return trip from The Grove far more agreeable. First, none of the phantoms that haunted his walk on the way in bothered to appear on the way out. Second, the darkness, though present, was not so pronounced. He could now see the path before him as well as Mistress who led the way. Third, Mistress guided him now. He felt differently now as well. The encounter with the pillars had changed something in him. He spent most of the walk back to the cabin trying to figure out what exactly that change was. The most obvious evidence was the tingling sensation that covered his hands. He wanted to experiment, to concentrate on his hands to see if he could determine what caused the discomfort, but Mistress kept the pace of their journey quick. If he lost track of her, he felt he would be lost forever, especially since he noted that the path back was not the straight line that it was on the way in. "It won't be long," Mistress explained sensing his impatience. "It was the same for me the first time here." Ghostspawn thought about how long it had taken to get to The Grove. He did not believe Mistress' words at all. They had walked no where near the time it had taken earlier. He did not remember that she had arrived before he did. He only remembered thinking that he would never arrive at his destination. That same thought tormented him now. Frowning, he quickened his pace to keep up with Mistress. There had been no doorway, no change in the path whatsoever. One moment they had been walking along the path, the next they were walking through the cabin. Ghostspawn stopped

midway across the room, his eyes wide and jaw slack. Mistress turned to him. "And you thought I had lied to you. That is one of the things we need to work on first. Your thoughts can be read as easily as any parchment. Come with me now. I will show you to your cabin." She pulled the hide aside and waited for him to step outside. Ghostspawn could think of nothing to delay his eviction from the cabin, so obliged. Once outside, he followed Mistress around her cabin. Just barely visible, on the far side of the clearing, stood another small cabin that the goblin had not seen before. As they approached, Ghostspawn noted that it appeared to be in better repair than Mistress' cabin. She stopped at the door and muttered a few words that the goblin did not understand. A candle appeared in her hand, its flame flickering slightly in the night breeze. She handed the candle to the goblin. "This is where you will stay until I call for you. You are not to attempt to enter my cabin without me first inviting you. You will only find that even immortals can die and that your death will be slow and very painful. Do you understand?" Ghostspawn nodded and accepted the candle. "Good. You will also be able to practice here. There is magic here to protect the cabin from mishaps. I expect you to care for your new home. If you don't, you will need to find comfort in the forest when you are not with me." That being spoken, she returned to her own cabin. Ghostspawn opened the door and stepped inside. With his candle, he lit several sconces that he found around the room. Unlike Mistress' home, the furnishings were the normal wood variety. A table and two chairs stood in the center of the room. He found a bed with a straw-stuffed mattress against the side wall. Beside the door, stood a counter and water pump. An empty book shelf stood on the far side of the room. He did not explore beyond that as he was overcome with a great fatigue. He extinguished his candles and fell into a deep, dreamless sleep as soon as he lay upon the bed. Howling winds whipped around the cabin in an attempt to rip it apart. They were aided by over-hanging tree branches battering the roof. Ghostspawn woke both startled and with a ravenous hunger. He sat up and searched the room attempting to guess where he was and what he was doing there. His hands still tingled, now to the point of being slightly painful. This reminded him of the prior night's journey to the grove. Groaning, he stood and noticed a wooden platter of raw meat in the center of the table. He grinned as he scampered towards

the meal. The thought that it might be poisoned passed through his mind before he decided he did not care if it were. He grabbed the largest hunk of red meat and ripped into it with his teeth. As he ate, he wondered when Mistress would call for him. The winds that rattled the cabin negated any thoughts of exploring the surrounding woods. He slowed his eating, having nothing else to do until she summoned him. After he pushed the empty platter aside, he started to examine his hands. He barely had time to get a good look at them before Mistress summoned him. His determination proved stronger than the winds that tried to rip the door from his grasp and afterwards, blow him off course. Mistress met him at the door to her cabin, holding the hide covering aside until he stepped across the threshold. Ghostspawn immediately turned to her holding up his hands. "Hush," she said before he could ask his questions. "Seat yourself and I will explain what you wish to know, my shriveled old goblin apprentice." Mistress walked to her usual seat and waited for Ghostspawn to sit across the table from her. "I am pretty sure that your hands have a tingling sensation and may even be a little painful. Am I correct?" "Yes. Why?" "Is it only your hands that have these feelings of discomfort?" Ghostspawn nodded. "Yes, Why?" "Last night, The Grove Pillar of War decided that you were suitable to be a god. As a result, while you learn your powers, your body will transform to a more suitable resemblance of what the pillar expects you to be. The transformation will probably do two things. The first is it will strengthen you. Second, it may restore some of your youth. Being a god does not end with flinging magic power all over the place and gathering followers. You must look and be the part designated to you." Ghostspawn grinned and asked, "So am I the god of war now?" Mistress laughed. Ghostspawn felt that the laughter was less amusement and more derision. His suspicions were confirmed when she pointed her finger at him and laughed ever harder. The goblin glowered at her. This only seemed to make her more amused. Several moments passed before she regained her composure. "Don't be so upset, my little goblin apprentice. The more I find you amusing, the more I will want you around. Listen carefully and learn. Stop me if you have a question you think I will find amusing." Ghostspawn crossed his arms and leaned back in his chair.

He hoped her explanation did not confuse him any further. "Before we address your godhood, I wish to address the tingling and pain you will experience. If you were younger and spent less time sitting upon your shriveled ass these last thousand or so years, the transformation would last for two, maybe three days. Unfortunately for you, that is not the case. It will probably take two or three days for these sensations to spread to your entire decrepit body." She paused and smiled in anticipation of his pain. "I know not for sure how long it will last, but I would say no more than a couple weeks or so. I expect you to work through your discomfort. It will be ill-advised to waste time on self-pity." She waited until he nodded before continuing. "Now, about your pending godhood." She leaned forward. "If you desire to travel this path, then you must earn it. It will not happen next week, next month or even next year. The preparation and learning alone will take quite some time." "Finally, you just don't become a god. You must take the place of one of the existing gods. You must steal their power and take it for your own." "So I must kill a god and take their place?" Ghostspawn asked. Mistress answered his question with laughter. "You do know how to keep me amused!" A couple moments passed as Ghostspawn wished he could crawl under the chair and disappear. He was learning that being Mistress' apprentice would be quite demeaning. She stood and walked around the table to where he sat sulking. "I guess you plan to go out and hack away at a god with that mighty sword of yours. Then you will steal their essence as they die before your greatness," she said as she patted him on the head. "Excuse me while I fix us something to drink." Mistress gathered two mugs and a glass jug filled with a thick, black liquid. She poured a little of the liquid into both mugs and brought them to the table. "Drink that slowly, little goblin. You don't want to become ill," she said as she returned to her seat. "Gods are not so reckless that they would allow themselves to be killed. They have ways to prevent that from happening. Besides, even if you do manage to destroy a god, you've defeated your own purpose. Once the god is dead, you can no longer steal their essence. You must do that while they still live. If it were so easy as to kill one and take over, I'd have done it myself centuries ago." She paused long enough to take a delicate sip from her drink. Ghostspawn watched as her eyes widened in pleasure. She held the liquid in her mouth a few moments, savoring the taste. The goblin followed her example. His own eyes widened as the thick black fluid

slid across his tongue. He held it in his mouth as long as he could, swallowing only when he needed to take a breath. He raised his mug again to take another swig but was stopped by his mentor. "Slowly, my decrepit little friend. I won't warn you again. I will sit here and watch you with great pleasure as you become very, very sick." Ghostspawn put the mug back on the table and fondled it as much as his pained hands allowed him to. "What is it?" he asked. "You will learn to make it after you have learned a bit of herb-lore. In the meantime, just enjoy it in ignorance. You should find that quite easy to do." She placed her elbow on the table and rested her chin in her hand. "Now, back to becoming a god. In order to steal the essence of a god you must first weaken them and imprison them. Then you drain their spirit from them over time. In this way, you will not destroy yourself with an overdose of power." "How do I steal the essence?" Ghostspawn asked. "That is part of the magic that you will have to learn. That is very advanced and we will need to be patient. Until you learn the basics and some of the simpler advanced forms of magic, you will not even understand that which will enable you to drain a being's essence." Ghostspawn lifted his mug to take another sip. He paused and glanced at Mistress, waiting until she nodded before partaking in the drink. After savoring it as long as he could, he pushed the mug aside and leaned forward. "When can we begin my training?" Mistress smiled and replied, "Now, grotesque one." She slid her own mug to the side and folded her hands on the table. "We will start with a simple ignite spell before we return to rune practice. This will allow you to light your candles without the use of flint. It's not very powerful, but it is quite useful." She pointed to the counter where several thick candles sat. "Get us each one of those candles and we will begin." Ghostspawn quickly retrieved the two candles and set them on the table. When he was seated again, Mistress began the lesson. "This spell is simple. It has two components. The first is a short spoken phrase. When you become better, you can think the phrase and it will work for you. That is your goal for this lesson, which you will practice in your cabin when I send you there. The second component is concentration. You must concentrate on the wick of the candle so that your flame goes where it is supposed to go. I will not be pleased if you burn my table." Mistress spoke the words of the incantation one at a time, making sure the goblin pronounced each correctly before learning the

next. She then gave him two words at a time, then three, until he was able to say the entire phrase to her satisfaction. Afterwards, she looked at her candle and spoke the phrase. The wick appeared to grow the flickering flame from within. She coached Ghostspawn until, after dozens of attempts, his candle burned as well. Mistress made him light his candle quite a few times before she was satisfied that he would remember the spell. As she promised, they moved onto rune practice. Unlike the night before, Mistress stopped him at intervals and had him light his candle. Several hours passed before Mistress called an end to the rune practice. Ghostspawn's hands pained him greatly the entire time, but he worked through it, not showing his discomfort. He had decided to deny his teacher that small bit of amusement. That and the small bit of magic he had learned sent him back to his cabin a satisfied goblin. Mistress spied on him for a while, watching him practice lighting candles while he ate the raw meat she had supplied for him. She noted that he took her warning to heart in regards to the drink. "You may prove to be an apt student yet," she muttered to herself as she watched him practice the runes he learned that day. She closed her mental connection when a small movement between two of the bookshelves distracted her. Smiling, she knew that Bhk-at had news for her. "Enter, Bhk-at." The small trap door opened and the deep-elf climbed into the room. He placed two small packages on the floor at his feet and bowed. Mistress licked her lips at the sight of him and nodded. "Greetings, Mistress. We have discovered that Lord Ky has three children. Two are male. They are training in Cragsguard. My spies inform me that they are due to receive their inheritance sometime later this month. It will be a stately affair officiated by the high-elven king in the city of Alle-Stecan." "What gift did you bring to me?" she asked, glancing at the packages. "I fear that it is only a partial gift, Mistress, but my agents had to make a quick exit upon gathering it. Within these packages you will find blood samples of two of the three children, the girl and one of the boys." Mistress slowly rose from her seat. "Blood samples?" she asked, a smile slowly forming on her lips. "Aye, Mistress. They are cut from the practice tunics they wore that morning." "You have outdone yourself, Bhk-at. Is there any other information or rumors you could share with me?" "Only this and it is just a rumor. The children have recently

acquired a dwarven maid as their servant. We do not believe she is happy with the arrangements. From what we could gather, she would be most unhappy." "What type of blood do you and your lackeys thirst for?" Mistress asked as she walked to a shelf lined with small vials. "Choose correctly and you may take your reward with you now." Bhk-at smiled. "If it please you, Mistress, we would prefer elven blood this time. We know that it is hard to obtain, but we feel we have earned it." Mistress nodded as she searched through the vials. "I am sorry, Bhk-at, but I have none of that in my stock at the moment. It seems that I will be in need of a few elves in the near future though, so I will acquire some for you. Will ten vials properly show my gratitude." Bhk-at bowed. "Most thoroughly, Mistress. I will await your summons." Mistress could hardly wait until the small elf had climbed through the trap door. Part of the agreement that kept him working for her was that she could never come near enough to touch him. As soon as it closed, she rushed forward and examined the two packages. She could not believe her good fortune. After many years of trying to come up with a plan to acquire blood samples of one of the gods, two such samples were handed to her. She knew that her path was open to her now. It would not be long before she was counted among the gods. And she smiled, knowing that the perfect scapegoat to take all the guilt now lived in her spare cabin. Maybe it was time to teach the goblin the subtle art of essence stealing. At least it was time for him to witness it. She carefully placed her treasures in a small silver box and hid them in a secret room behind one of the bookshelves. Now was not the time. She would have to be as patient as she wished her shriveled little apprentice to be. When the small room was secure, she returned to the table and began making her plans.

27 A very soft rain fell on the town of Cragsguard. It was the kind of rain that no one minded. The droplets caressed rather than pelted, and here and there patches of morning sunlight played tag with the rain. William woke to the sound of the rain gently dancing on the wood shingles above his head. Sitting up, he stretched and tried to grab the threads of his waking dream. After a few minutes, he let it slip away as it did not wish to be caught. Yawning, he slipped into his robe and looked in on Micah and Little Ky. Both were still sleeping soundly. William smiled and set off in search of a washroom. He found it nestled behind the kitchen. The room was comfortably warm, heated by a small iron stove that stood against the far wall beside a large wooden tub. In the corner closest to him, a water pump and wash basin stood beneath a mirror. Under the pump, he found two iron pots with wooden handles. A shelf stood beside the door which held several towels and wash-clothes. William wondered about the lack of fuel for the small stove. He opened it and found the interior flickering softly with a warm red and yellow glow. No matter the angle he peered into the stove, he found nothing within that would feed the flames. He wondered whether he should thank Ky or the Old Man for this little bit of magic. His morning clean-up took a while. William knew that this would change as he became familiar with workings of this rustic world. After he had dressed, he woke the boys. While Micah and Little Ky were cleaning up and dressing, William looked across the square and saw that the Cracked Anvil had begun serving breakfast. He decided that breakfast there would be a great way to start the day and

grabbed some coins from the box beneath the counter. When the boys were ready, William led them across the square. Daphnia and the Old Man were already at a table when William and the boys arrived. Micah and Little Ky ran to the table and sat on either side of Daphnia, leaving William to sit across from them beside the Old Man. William smiled, knowing there would be no quiet time with Daphnia while the two boys were in town. Stan provided a splendid meal of juicy sausages and oatmeal spiced with apples and cinnamon. By the end of their breakfast, the rain gave way to a warm spring day with the sun peaking through high scattered clouds. They bade farewell to Stan and headed out to explore the town. The Old Man had once known the town well. During his long imprisonment by his brother, the town had grown and changed considerably. They spent the remaining morning hours exploring shops, meeting people and generally having a good time. Daphnia was very happy with the library. Her memories of Cragsguard had been as a temple maid. She was greatly pleased that the evil temple had been replaced with such a beautiful and peaceful building. While Micah and Little Ky were showing the others where they were training, Delmaria joined them, informing them that the wild-elves were ready for their visit. She had obtained permission for Little Ky to accompany them, explaining that the wild-elves were very intrigued at meeting one of Lord Ky's children. The Old Man returned to his alchemy shop after the others had gone. Delmaria brought them to the same clearing as before. She stayed with them this time. They all found seats on the same tree William and Daphnia sat upon during their last visit. Moments later, the songs of the wild-elves began. This days repertoire had been chosen with the two boys in mind. The elves knew that tales of love would not hold their interest, so they chose songs that spoke of great adventures. The stories within the music were lost in the language barrier for all but Delmaria. The other four enjoyed the performance no less, hearing the music as a vocal symphony that needed no verbal interpretation. The songs stopped after the third tale. Delmaria turned to William, "I told them that Micah would sing for them. It is time." William smiled as he addressed Micah, "Come share a song with the elves, Micah." Micah walked to William and asked, "What should I sing?" "Whatever you wish. I believe they will have heard nothing you would know," William answered as he turned Micah towards the field and gently pushed him forward. Micah could see no elves and was worried they would be

unable to hear him. He thought for a moment, then decided to sing "Schlaf, Kindlein, schlaf," the lullaby he used to sing for Little Ky in Austria. Micah closed his eyes and imagined a concert hall filled to standing room only with dignitaries and other important people. When he had the vision set in his mind, he began to sing. Micah's soprano voice drifted across the field. As soon as the last note faded, he bowed and returned to his seat beside Little Ky. The elves gave no indication of their appreciation for Micah's song. They answered with several more songs, including one love song that the two boys tolerated for William and Daphnia's sake. The music so entranced William, Daphnia and the boys that none of them noticed that an elf had come to Delmaria and whispered to her before disappearing back into the forest. When the elves stopped, Delmaria asked that Micah sing his song again. She explained that they truly enjoyed his song and many wanted to make a memory bark of it. This time Micah did not have to imagine an audience. As Micah moved to stand in front of William again, many elves entered the field from the forest all around them. Micah waited until they were all seated, then sang his song again. Micah bowed, smiling as he returned to his seat on the log. He had never seen elves like these. They somewhat resembled the Eldar elves, but had a wilder, more natural appearance with the exception of their eyes. Every color he could imagine was represented in the eyes of the elves in the field. There were even several of the females whose eyes slowly faded from one color to another. All the elves were clad in living vines, many of which were flowering. The elves remained before their visitors and sang several more songs. Afterwards, the elf whom William and Daphnia had met on their previous visit stepped forward. Delmaria introduced the group to him. The elf bowed slightly to each of them as they were introduced. After the introductions, the elf walked to Micah. Delmaria translated for him as he said, "Your song has brought us great joy. Please accept this gift as a token of our appreciation." A younger elf came forward, his amber eyes as wide as his smile. He placed a finely-made wooden chain necklace around Micah's neck. Miniature beech leaves grew from the chain. Micah stood speechless as he held it up and examined it. "It's awesome and it looks like it's alive," he finally whispered. Delmaria translated and the young elf laughed, replying, "It looks alive, because it is. It will remain healthy as long as you live to treasure it." The younger elf stepped back a few paces and waited as the

older one approached Little Ky. The elf knelt and bowed his head until it touched the ground at Little Ky's feet. Delmaria signaled for Little Ky not to move in time to stop him from protesting. The elf held this position for a moment before raising his head. "Greetings to you, first born of the Lord of Chaos. It is with great honor that we welcome you among us," Delmaria translated. "We have for you a gift as well and hope you find it worthy." The younger elf stepped forward, knelt and bowed as the older one had. After a moment, he lifted Little Ky's left foot and slipped a circlet of living vine onto his ankle. The vine tightened slightly so that it would not move. When the anklet was in place, he gently lowered Little Ky's foot and crept back. "The vine will keep illness from entering your body. It will also enable you to come here when you please. If Micah wishes to join you, take his hand before thinking the desire to return. Both of you are ever welcome here," the elf finished, smiling. "Thank you," Little Ky replied, his voice an awed whisper. He placed his foot on the tree beside him and both he and Micah examined the circlet, noting the tiny oak leaves that grew from the vine. "I feel we will be coming here to visit regularly," William said. "Is there a name we may address you by?" "It is our custom not to share our names with those not of our own race," explained the older elf. "You may choose a name you wish to address us by." Micah whispered something to Little Ky who nodded in agreement. "We will call him," Micah said pointing to the younger elf, "Amber if it's okay with him." The younger elf smiled and nodded when Delmaria translated for him. "Also, we were wondering," Micah said, his voice faltering a little. "Speak freely, Micah," Delmaria explained. "They hold all of you in high regard." "We were wondering if Amber could come back with us for the rest of the day. Little Ky can bring him back later." Delmaria translated adding that she would take the responsibility for returning Amber at the end of the day. She also added that he should bring some bark so that he could return with some music by William. Amber's wide-eyed expression clearly stated that he wished to go and the older elf approved. "Please have him back before the moon reaches its zenith," he said to Delmaria. "I'm sure that will be no problem whatsoever," Delmaria

replied. After the farewells, the group returned to Cragsguard. Delmaria went to the Cracked Anvil to spend the rest of the day with her father. Micah and Little Ky took Amber up to Micah's room where they spent time playing with the farm. William and Daphnia made some tea and visited with each other, seated in the chairs near the fire. As the sun's last rays graced the town, William gathered the three boys and they all went to the Cracked Anvil for dinner. Amber's presence caused quite a stir of curiosity, so much so that Stan moved them to Ky's table in the back of the room in order for them to eat in relative peace. Stan guessed that Ky would not mind his son and his friends sitting there. Still, many of the patrons craned their necks to get a look at the wild-elf seated in the corner. After dinner, they returned to William's house. Daphnia made tea for everyone as the three boys sat on the floor near the piano and listened to William play. Amber was fascinated by the instrument. Eight pieces of memory bark bulged in the pouch he wore at his waist when Delmaria came to return him to his home. The rest of the evening, William told tales and worked with Little Ky who wanted to learn to sing like Micah so that they could sing together the next time they visited the wild-elves. The next morning, they would return to the farm. William tucked the boys in, then spent another hour or so visiting with Daphnia. When Daphnia returned to her room at the Cracked Anvil, William checked on the boys and retired to his own room. All of them slept well that night, the voices of the wild-elves flowing through their dreams.

28 Although the triplets tried their best not to think ahead to their inheritance, the mention of it the day before brought it to the forefront of their minds. Breakfast conversation the next morning found them asking Aemir about his inheritance. "What was it like?" Tal asked. "I'm sure it was nothing compared to the celebration that yours will be. My father held a high status in Alle-Stecan, but not high enough to have the king officiate. It was great though." Eleana asked, "Did you feel any different afterwards?" Aemir shrugged, took a mouthful of oatmeal and thought a moment. "I don't think so," he said after swallowing. "I remember being really nervous. All kinds of things were told to me about responsibilities and such. That's when I learned that Sage Tas'lin would be teaching me. That kind of scared me," he said laughing. "What responsibilities did they tell you about?" This time it was Ky II that asked. "Part of my ceremony, my parents told all about my family line. It seemed like it would last forever. Then I was told that being the eldest male, it was my job to see that the line does not end." Aemir's gaze dropped to the table as he absently stirred the remains of his oatmeal. "My grandparents were killed in the wars against the humans many years ago. My father was their only child. I'm the last of my line so I guess I should really work on that." Tal put his hand on Aemir's shoulder and said, "I don't think you need to worry about that just yet. You've got lots of time to keep your family line going."

"Yeah, I guess so," Aemir replied returning to his breakfast. "Anyway, I'm really looking forward to going to your inheritance. I bet it's going to be spectacular. I mean, everybody's going to be there!" "Not everyone," Illya said as she cleared away the few empty bowls. "I trust all of you to come back and tell me everything about it. Grandfather Stan will want to hear about it too. He can't go either, but he will be here afterwards for the party." "We promise to remember everything! At least until we tell you about it anyway," Eleana said. Simon and Ky II finished their breakfast first, excused themselves saying they would meet everyone outside. As soon as they stepped through the door, Ky II saw Ky seated in a tree in the orchard. He grabbed Simon's arm and nearly dragged him down the steps. "I have a plan, but I think I'll need your help," Ky II explained as they rushed to Ky's perch. Ky lightly jumped to the ground as Simon and Ky II approached. His focus was on Simon. Before Ky II could mention his plan, Ky said, "I'll be visiting our mother today. Would you come with me?" "Um, sure. When are we going?" Simon asked. "Now is good," Ky answered. Ky II tried to get his father's attention before they vanished only to find himself standing beside them in The Garden. "You two wait here for a moment," Ky said as he walked along the path. "I'll be back shortly." Simon and Ky II sat beside the small stream that flowed at the base of The Garden. Simon asked, "So what was this plan you have?" "I was going to ask dad if he could somehow make it so Illya and Grandfather Stan could come to the inheritance ceremony. I really feel bad that they can't come." Simon smiled, "I like that plan. If we pester him enough, he might come up with a way." "Or kill us slowly and painfully," Ky II said grinning. "Both Illya and Grandfather will be there," Ky said as he approached. "They just don't know it yet and it will remain that way." The Lady walked beside Ky and sat by her favorite tree. She beckoned all to join her and tell her what they had been doing. The Garden being timeless, allowed Simon, Ky and Ky II to stay for quite a while. The Lady listened to their tales with great interest. When it was time to return, both Ky and Simon promised to visit again soon. Ky reminded Simon and Ky II that Illya and Stan were to know nothing of their trip to the triplet's inheritance. They returned to the farm just as the others were entering

the yard. Today was their last day of play before they returned to Cragsguard and training. Ky left, saying he had things he had to tend to and arrangements that needed to be completed. The children spent the morning playing tag and wrestling with each other. The gentle rain that had been over Cragsguard earlier, found its way to the farm and soon the children were covered in mud. This helped Aemir convince Archos to provide them with a place where they could swim. Archos created a pond behind the farmhouse. The children jumped in, clothing on to remove the mud from them. Then they put their clothes on the grass to let the sun dry them and returned to the pond. Even Brek enjoyed this type of bathing. They spent over an hour splashing around in the pond before they were called in for lunch. After lunch, Laena decided to spend some time with Eleana before she had to return to Cragsguard and training. Ky II and Simon occupied themselves with climbing trees in the orchard. Aemir, Tal and Brek played tag and wrestled on the side yard. During one of the breaks, Aemir brought up the subject of Ky. "I see what you mean by he doesn't stick around long." Tal nodded. "Yeah." "I've been thinking about what Lady Selia showed us yesterday. Is he still like that?" "Like what?" Tal asked. "Like he does stuff just to prove they can be done. That's why he did Lady Selia's quest for her." Tal grinned and answered, "You can't always trust what Lady Selia says about dad's motives. They never really got along well until very near the end. My guess is that dad did it that way to avoid going with a bunch of other people. He doesn't like being around lots of people." "Do you think your dad will be back before your inheritance?" Aemir asked. Tal shrugged, "It's hard to say. I think he will be checking on the training progress. Whether we see him or not is another question. I wonder what Mena did to him. I bet Lord Stumpy knows what happened." Brek interrupted the conversation, stating, "Brek need knife to throw at target." "Sure, Brek," Tal responded as he handed the goblin one of his long-knives. Aemir watched as Brek walked to the barn where the target rested against the back wall. "It's weird him training with us. He's going to go to the Council of Darkness, isn't he?" "We'll only be training together until the inheritance ceremony. After that, we'll be split up to train with The Nine or the

Council of Darkness." Tal paused a moment. "I think it's going to be really rough for you, Micah and Brek. You three are mortals and need to be made into gods." "What's that going to be like?" Aemir asked. "You need to ask Lord Symplex, Lord Daelann or Lady Selia that one. Laena, my brothers and Simon were born gods and don't have to worry about becoming them," Tal explained. "Will I be training with the evil gods and goddesses?" Aemir asked. "Hmmm, I didn't think of that. We all might be training with the Council of Darkness." Tal noticed Aemir's frown and added, "Karnak trained Simon, Laena and me for a while. It was fun." Then Tal laughed. "Don't tell him I said this, but if he makes you uncomfortable, just hug him." "You've hugged Karnak?" Aemir asked, his eyes wide. Tal shook his head, and answered, "I didn't. Simon did. It was funny to see Karnak's reaction." "I bet. Let's go throw some knives around with Brek," Aemir suggested as he stood and waited for Tal. "Okay. Maybe afterwards we can go swimming again," Tal said leading the way to the barn. After dinner, Simon, Aemir, Ky II and Tal spent the early evening in the pond. Eleana chose to read some of Delmaria's journals. By the time they were sent to bed, they were all looking forward to continuing their training. The two day break had strengthened friendships, and the prospect of making progress was good. The next morning, they met Little Ky and Micah at the Cracked Anvil. Ky met them as well with Mena. He informed them that they would attend a dinner in their honor in Deep Stone in two weeks time. He charged Mena with teaching them proper dwarven customs so that none of them embarrassed themselves or Ky. Stan provided them with breakfast and they headed for the practice field. The first practice session was light since they had eaten before it. After lunch, Ky II had them back on the previous schedule. The evening sessions were canceled as Tal and Little Ky would be going to Herr William for piano lessons. They would have to meet with Mena afterwards to learn dwarven customs. The group fell into a steady schedule and, with the lack of discord among the group, made great progress. Each found they had talents that they could share with the group. Although Ky II was still in charge of the training, he no longer was the sole instructor. The group tightened as they learned to work together and accept their own weaknesses. The two weeks prior to the dinner in Deep Stone passed quickly. All the children were disappointed with the passage of time.

The day before the dinner, Ky II canceled the practice sessions for the next morning and afternoon. Instead, he scheduled time with Mena so that the rules and expectations required of them during the dinner that night would be fresh in their minds. They practiced exceptionally hard that last day. None had any trouble falling asleep that night.

29 Bhk-at realized that Mistress was far more interested in Lord Ky's children than he first thought. As a result, he assigned four deep-elves to watch them and report back to him. A deep-elf kept the group of children under surveillance every hour of the day and night. Every move the triplets made was reported back to Bhk-at. The deep-elves learned early to keep their distance and to avoid Simon altogether. They were unsure how he noticed them, but they decided not to take any chances with hiding in the barracks lest Simon find them. Simon's ability was also reported to Bhk-at. He knew he had another little gem of information to pass on to Mistress. Bhk-at almost had Simon assassinated. He had hoped to receive more blood samples to pass to Mistress, blood samples that were labeled with names. He thought better of it, lest the group be put under the direct protection of the gods that payed them frequent visits. Instead, Bhk-at satisfied himself with cursing Simon every chance he got. None of his curses had any effect other than making him feel a little better. The steady schedule that the children followed allowed Bhk- at to report to Mistress exactly where they would be and when. He also noted when Mena was alone. She too, had been spied upon and the deep-elves learned that she was none too happy with her situation. Bhk-at knew that Mistress would be able to use her to get to the triplets. After two weeks of constant observation, Bhk-at prepared his report and headed for Mistress's cabin. He smiled thinking of the ten vials of blood she owed him already. His greedy mind considered that maybe he could even acquire some dragon's blood from her this time.

Arriving at the trapdoor, he sent the signal to let Mistress know he had information. She took her time responding, but when she did, the deep-elf could not help but smile as he climbed into her cabin.

30 Mena started her day making sure Ky's children and their companions had fresh clothing laid out and ready for their day in Deep Stone. Stumpy had taken her to Deep Stone before the children awoke so that she could prepare their places in the great feast hall of her father. Mena considered this next to the worst insult the black- eyed elf had exacted upon her. The worst had been the way he had taken her beard. She had never treated the other servants with kindness. Now she was one of them and was considered the lowliest of them, having to serve a goblin. She tried to ignore the other servants but could not help seeing their sneers and hearing some of their snide comments. Mena prepared the table where the children would be honored. By the time she finished, she was miserable. She knew she would have to meet them at the mountain entrance and began her journey through Deep Stone. Stumpy walked with her so she had to take the direct, most traveled route. Deep Stone had not had visitors in many years and many dwarves rushed through the halls. Mena noticed that all the dwarves they passed bowed respectfully to Stumpy. Then they added a rather demeaning glance in her direction. By the time she and Stumpy stepped into the morning forest, she had decided that she would exact some sort of revenge on the black-eyed elf and his children. It may not be this day, but she vowed to herself that they would know her vengeance. Taelann woke the children and took them to the Cracked Anvil for breakfast. William met them there, reminding them that they had to return and tell him all about their day. He joked with them

saying that he would receive no sleep until he heard their story. After their meal, Taelann led them to the city gates where horses awaited them. They would have to ride several miles to the north to get to the mountain entrance to Deep Stone. Taelann set a moderate pace knowing several of the group had never ridden a horse prior to this trip. Ky II, Tal and Eleana were assigned the task of leading Simon's, Micah's and Little Ky's horses. Taelann led Brek's himself as the horse was not comfortable carrying a goblin. Aemir had been trained extensively in riding. He offered to teach the others during the final week of training if they wished to learn. Even the triplets expressed interest in his offer. The children had difficulty staying still in their saddles, anticipating the day in Deep Stone. Taelann tried to curb some of their excitement by telling them tales about the southern realms of the elven kingdom through which they rode. His tales met with some success, but by the time they approached Stumpy and Mena, they were all talking at once about the wonders they would see during their visit to the dwarven realm. The triplets had never been within the dwarven realms, but they all had trained with Stumpy and related the tales he had told to them. Stumpy heard their approach long before he saw them. He signaled the guards waiting inside the great gates of Deep Stone. The two guards sounded their long, curved horns, the fanfare echoing deep into the dwarven realm as well as through the forest beyond. Brenson and Maasena took their positions within the entry hall to receive their guests. The sound of the dwarven horns silenced the children. The last part of their journey was spent trying to find the entrance to Deep Stone. Taelann knew they would not see it until the gates opened to receive them. He enjoyed watching them craning their necks and nearly falling from their horses to get a glimpse of their destination through the trees. Stumpy came forward to greet them. The children had never seen him quite like he appeared today. Rays of sunlight that managed to sift through the forest canopy flashed blindingly as they found the brilliant ring-mail worn by the dwarven god. On his side, he wore the double-edged, diamond- bladed axe Archos had crafted for him. None could remember the dwarf's beard ever being so neatly combed. The children leaped from the mounts, leaving them in Taelann's care, and rushed to Stumpy. Their wide-eyed expressions stated their great excitement and pleasure at being here. Stumpy gathered them around him for some last minute instructions. "Make sure ye return all bows. It will nae be good to insult your hosts. Also, Mena is your servant. Do not speak to the lass."

"That doesn't seem right," Eleana said. "Shouldn't we at least thank her or something?" "Nae, lass. Dwarven custom rules here. Servants are not spoken to." He glared at all the children one at a time. "Promise me ye'll stick to proper behavior." All the children promised, some more begrudgingly than others, but Stumpy was satisfied. He led them to where Mena waited and stopped them. Ahead of them stood the stony mountain side, nothing more. The children still did not see the entrance to Deep Stone and wondered how far they would have to climb to get there. Stumpy bellowed, "Hail, to thee, Brenson, Lord of Deep Stone. Ye've guests at yer doorstep. Will ye be welcoming them?" Several of the children took a step back as the mountain in front of them rumbled. A gap, thirty feet high, opened as the mountain side split revealing the finely carved entry hall of Deep Stone. When the great gates settled, Stumpy led them forward. They followed until they stood before Brenson and Maasena. To either side of them, stood ten dwarven honor guard. Stumpy introduced the children, starting with Brek. As each was named, they came forward, bowed and greeted their hosts. The last to be introduced was Lord Ky's first born child, Little Ky. "It has been many centuries since we've had such honored guests," Brenson stated, his deep voice filling the hall. "Although the circumstances are regretful," he added glancing at Mena, "the honor is in no way diminished. I hope ye will find your visit to Deep Stone satisfying." Brenson waited as the honor guard took their positions around the group, then led them into Deep Stone. As they traveled through the great halls, Brenson told them the history of Deep Stone, pointing out the carvings that related to his tale. He led them to their first destination within the fortress: the dwarven forges. A jovial dwarf dressed in a thick leather apron and gloves greeted the children. Brenson introduced him as Coran, then stepped aside as Coran led the group into the room. The children really enjoyed their ruddy-faced guide with the singed beard that came very close to dragging on the floor at his feet. The heat of the forges blasted them, but not one complained or even seemed to notice as they witnessed the dwarven metal-workers. They spent several hours in the forge. The dwarven smiths entertained them with mining songs sung to the rhythm of the clanging hammers. When it was time to head to the feast hall, each were given a single ring of dwarven mail. Brenson saw the reluctance of the children to leave Coran and assured them that they would see him at the feast. After he finally

managed to get them all to leave the forges, he led them to the feast hall. They were stopped at the tall wooden doors of the hall and asked to wait until they were properly introduced. The doors opened and Brenson entered with Maasena by his side. They could hear what sounded like hundreds of dwarves pushing their chairs back and standing. As Brenson and Maasena made their way to the head table on the far side of the hall, Stumpy instructed the children in dwarven entrance-etiquette. "Watch me," he muttered. "When your names be called, do exactly as I have done. Brenson will call me first as you are the guests of honor. Walk to the head table. Mena will be there to make sure you are in your proper seats." Brenson and Maasena took their places at the center of the head table. Maasena sat while Brenson made the introductions. "I present Lord Stumpy, God of the Underfoot." Stumpy walked forward and stopped just inside the hall, bowing low before continuing to the head table. The assembled dwarves pounded their mugs on the tables as Stumpy walked to his seat. The pounding continued, like the heartbeat of the stone, until Stumpy was settled. The hall fell silent. "I present Brek the Goblin, trusted companion of Lord Ky's children and honored guest of this night's feast." Brek followed Stumpy's lead and was met with the same pounding welcome. Brenson continued with Micah and Aemir. He gave them the same designation as Brek: trusted companions of Lord Ky's children. Then Brenson introduced Simon, brother to Lord Ky. When Simon was in his seat, Brenson introduced Ky II, then Tal and Eleana. "Lastly, I present, Little Ky, first born son of Lord Ky, God of Chaos." Little Ky stepped forward and bowed as all the others had. The pounding of the mugs on the table thundered through the hall as he walked to his seat beside Brenson. Little Ky was quite beside himself with this attention and asked Tal about it after the feast began. Tal explained that being first born, Little Ky would be held in highest esteem by all cultures. "Let this night's feast begin," Brenson roared. It turned out that Stumpy's warning not to speak with Mena had been unnecessary due to the extent with which the dwarves of Deep Stone honored their guests and the manner in which the servants strove to remain unseen during the meal. Mena took extra care not to be seen, approaching the tables only when necessary and avoiding the other servants whenever she possible could. The meal consisted of roasted wild boar and doe, a variety

of mushrooms, a thick, well-seasoned stew and freshly baked, dark-rye bread. Brenson broke out the best meads and ales for the feast. During the meal, dwarven lore presented by the best of story-tellers, entertained the children. Between tales, there were songs which all in the hall participated in, either with their voices or with their mugs upon the tables. The final bit of entertainment proved to be the best of the evening. The tale of the founding of Deep Stone was acted out in the center of the hall. This tale portrayed the heroic deeds of Torcar, First Lord of Deep Stone, and even included a mock battle between Torcar and a small band of followers against the undead legions of Alleness, The Grey Death. Lastly, Coran entered the feast hall to the pleasure of the children for he had truly impressed them with his carefree nature and ever-present smile. He was followed by several of the other dwarven smiths. Coran's group walked to the head table and bowed. Brenson stood and addressed the children. "Our master- smith, Coran, has prepared for each of you a gift. It is our hope that when you use these gifts, you will remember Deep Stone with kindness." Coran presented each of the children with a sword crafted by the best smiths. In addition, Eleana was presented with a brace of perfectly balanced throwing knives. After the presentation, Tal and Ky II held their own mock battle to the great pleasure of the dwarves. Though the children were tired from their day in Deep Stone, none wanted to leave. The trip back to the mountain gate took quite some time as they paused and asked about anything and everything they passed. Brenson and Maasena were very pleased to answer all their questions, much to Stumpy's frustration. Each question soon found Stumpy mumbling and muttering into his beard. This only encouraged the children to ask more questions. Stumpy actually sighed in relief when the group finally approached the gates. The children were a bit surprised to find the forest draped in night. The world below the mountain did not rely on the passing of the sun to keep time. The children had such a wonderful day that the many hours they spent there seemed to pass much more quickly than actually was the case. Taelann met them and led them back to Cragsguard. Through the entire journey, the children spoke of their visit below the mountain. Many times during the journey, they all showed Taelann the swords they were given. Although Taelann planned to take them directly to the barracks, the children had other plans. They decided, on Micah's suggestion, that they would visit with Herr William so that they could share the adventure with him while it was still fresh in their minds. Taelann finally gave in on the condition that Herr

William was indeed still awake. They found Herr William seated on the steps with Daphnia and the Old Man, waiting for their return. The Old Man assured Taelann that he would see the children safely returned to the barracks after their visit with William. Their stay lasted well into the night. When they finally arrived at the barracks, Ky II canceled the morning practice session. In spite of their excitement, sleep overcame them rather effortlessly. Their dreams that night were filled with great dwarven battles and even greater stone fortresses.

31 Mistress had a great deal of work to do in preparation for her plan. Most of it revolved around Ghostspawn. She wanted to make sure that she remained invisible, at least until it was too late to do anything to her. Her plan was to train Ghostspawn with the first of the two victims. He would be with her at all times during the siphoning of power and he would be plainly visible to the victim whereas she would not be. The one thing Mistress found regretful, was that she would have to reveal many things to the goblin that she had not intended to reveal. The first of these revelations would occur today. She needed to check her storehouse. Her plan required that she have at least two young wild-elves. Unfortunately, Bhk-at had failed to designate which blood sample came from the male and which came from the female. Mistress had no wild-elves in her collection. That much she knew. She needed to thin her stock to free up the cages where she would keep the wild-elves while she completed other preparations. Instead of summoning the goblin to her, Mistress went to his cabin to collect him. On the way to the cabin, she thought of some of the things already set in place. While Karn-Rachk'sha struggled with the god councils, he had employed Mistress to tend to random annoyances that may have acquired too much information. Portals were set up by Karn-Rachksha to waylay anyone who came to close to some of his temples, sending them to Mistress' forest. Those portals helped her fill her storage shed. She had plenty of spare meat for Ghostspawn to practice on. Granted, the portals Karn-Rachksha set up were gone now, but she still held the knowledge of how to set them

up. This bit of knowledge would help her acquire the elves she needed. Mistress entered Ghostspawn's cabin without announcement and found him curled up on his cot in great pain. She smiled, enjoying the sight of his suffering. Curbing her enthusiasm to get things going, she waited while he climbed from the cot. She could not help but be a little impressed with the goblin's determination. The pain he felt as a result of the trip to The Grove, she had felt many years ago. "Your lessons today will be far more advanced than anything we've attempted thus far," Mistress explained as Ghostspawn stumbled to her. "I think they will distract you from your pain, at least for a while." "I'm ready," Ghostspawn croaked. "I enjoy your enthusiasm almost as much as I enjoy your pain," Mistress purred. "Eat first, then come to me behind my cabin." She turned and opened the door. "We can't have you salivating on the stock." Ghostspawn ate quickly, washing his meal down with water. By then, he took his mind from the pain in his body and was able to walk properly. He found Mistress standing beside a blank wall behind her cabin. He noticed the ground was packed and bare of weeds and grass, showing signs of many comings and goings. "As part of your training, you will begin to tend to the stock. It is very important that they not die while in the storeroom. Occasionally, one does find a way to end their own life. That is to be expected." Mistress beckoned him closer, then added, "Watch closely so that you may enter the storeroom on your own in the future." There were five triggers that had to be released in a specific order. Mistress showed him their locations and how to release them. When the last of them gave a soft click, the back wall disappeared to reveal a stairway leading under the cabin. Mistress led the goblin down the stairs into a small room. She guided him to the counter that filled the side wall of the room. On the counter, herbs, vials of various colored liquids, a set of bowls of various sizes, and many bones that had been sharpened into knives, lay in a very organized manner. At the far end of the counter stood a water pump and basin. Mistress allowed him to explore the counter a moment, watching him closely to make sure he did not upset anything. When he turned back to her, she began his lesson. "Everything you have seen here has a purpose that will allow the knowledgeable to avoid wasting precious magical energy. The use of magical energy will exhaust even the gods if one is not careful." She picked up a small bowl of herbs, finely compacted into

sticks. "This incense is used to keep the stock subdued. You will learn how to make this before you rest tonight." She replaced the bowl and picked up another. This one had dried leaves in it. "This is the herb you will need to eat to keep the incense from affecting you. You will need to eat one of these each time you enter the stock-room." Ghostspawn nodded that he understood. "I am not fond of wasting precious materials. Unfortunately, stock that has had several necessary ingredients harvested from them will die from the procedure or the after affects of the procedure. This can be prevented in a number of ways, depending on what you are harvesting. This," she explained picking up a vial of thick liquid, "will keep the stock from dieing due to blood loss. It's creation is very difficult, beyond your abilities at this time. You will learn the proper method of creating the base for it this afternoon." She placed the vial back and indicated the others that stood near it. "The contents of all of these vials are used to keep the stock alive, each has its own reason for use though. You will need to learn them all and what they are used for." Mistress smiled at the goblin and beckoned him to follow her to the far end of the counter. "These bones, likewise have individual purposes. If you use the wrong one, the results could be quite painful to you. The major part of becoming a god by theft, is stealing the spiritual essence of the god you will replace. Part of that requires the consumption of their blood. This bone," she said pointing to one of the smaller bones on the counter, "will be used for that. No blood will be spoiled or wasted that way." Mistress led Ghostspawn to the opposite side of the small room. The only furnishing here was a long, low table with a raised edge. On the inside of the edge a small trough had been carved. "This is where we will do the harvesting. This table holds some very special enchantments. Stock can lie on it for weeks without spoiling." She pointed to the door. "That is where the stock is stored." Ghostspawn followed Mistress to the counter. She handed him one of the dried leaves and took one for herself. Ghostspawn found the taste of it extremely bitter. He did his best to chew it thoroughly, following Mistress's example. His teeth were not made for chewing leaves, but he did the best he could. As soon as he swallowed it, he headed for the storeroom door. Mistress stopped him. "You must wait a few moments for the herb to take effect. If you enter too quickly, you will succumb to the incense and remain in the storeroom until I find you." She smiled at him. "That would slow down your progress as I only need to come here once a week or so to tend the stock. Since that will be one of your jobs, my presence down here will be even less."

About five minutes passed before Mistress allowed Ghostspawn to enter the storeroom. The room was dimly lit and a thick smoke made visibility even more difficult. Mistress led the goblin to the center of the room where a small copper stand stood. In spite of the sweet strong scent of the incense, the odor of stale sweat, urine and defecation persisted. Even after spending the last two thousand years in the dank caves of goblins, which were not known for their cleanliness, Ghostspawn found the stench overpowering. "This is where you are to light the incense. It needs to be refreshed once every week. I lit this one today. The next one, in seven days time, is your responsibility. Now, let me introduce you to my current stock. We will be moving a few around today to make room for some fresh meat." The goblin followed her around the room as she moved from one cage to the next. The room contained twenty cages, nineteen of which were occupied. The cages stood on small stands that allowed the waste to fall through the bottom onto the dirt floor. Each of the cages held one elf or human. Mistress explained that this was to keep them from harming each other. Very few of the stock were complete. Most were missing limbs or portions of limbs. One had no eyes. Two of them had been partially skinned, their muscles and organs exposed. Ghostspawn watched in fascination as Mistress set about the task of emptying two cages close to the door. The two humans that had been in those cages followed her commands without any sign of rebellion. They left their cages without thought and entered their new cages the same way. Finally, Mistress summoned an elf that occupied the cage nearest the door and led him to the front room. On her command, the elf climbed onto the low table. "Close the door, my little apprentice," Mistress instructed as she walked to the counter. Ghostspawn did as he was asked and joined her. He watched her as she placed ten vials and one of the bones on a small tray, then followed her back to the table. "This is an elf. His name is not important, though knowing the name when it comes time to siphon the essence from the god will be important. Elves have several attributes that will be helpful to you. They are very resistant to illness, are in tune with the natural rhythms of the world and have very acute senses. "We will begin your training by stealing those attributes from this fine specimen who has volunteered, unknowingly, of course. He will be on the table for about a week. In that time, you will learn many of the useful items that we can harvest from his body. Stock is not easily acquired, so nothing is to be wasted." She took the vial of thick liquid she had shown him earlier.

"The incense slows the body functions as well as addles the mind. That does not mean that the stock will not bleed to death if this is not used. It just means that their death will be somewhat delayed. Watch carefully. This is very difficult to make and I will not tolerate it being wasted." She removed the stopper from the vial and picked up a small hollow bone that had been marked at one end with a thin black line. She dipped the bone into the vial as far as the mark, then covered the opening at the other end and removed it. "Open your mouth," Mistress whispered. The elf followed her command and Mistress placed her fingers on his chin preventing him from closing his mouth. She held the bone over his mouth and let the elixir drip onto his tongue. Then she blew into the other end of the bone to make sure all the potion entered the elf. "Very good. Now rest here. I want the medicine to take effect before we go to work," she said, smiling at the elf. She led Ghostspawn to the pump. "It is very important that you clean your tools immediately. First, you don't want to have to make replacements. That would be a waste of magical energy." She paused to pump water into the basin. "Second, with the administering of potions and herbs, you need to give them time to take effect. Cleaning as you go will give them the time they need." Mistress cleaned the bone, then dumped the water onto the floor. She put the small vial and the bone away before returning to the table. She indicated that Ghostspawn should go to the far side of the table, and waited as he did so. "This bone is the one you use to extract blood. It is extremely sharp so you will not be using it until the pain of your transformation ends. One spasm caused by the pain could do quite a bit of damage. Later today, I will teach you the incantation that will drain the spiritual essence with the blood. Without the incantation, the only benefit of consuming his blood is to enjoy the taste of it." She put the bone back on the tray. "Before we actually take any of this elf's essence, I will teach you the best places to take blood." She pointed to the elf's neck. "This is where you will find the strongest flow. This should only be used if the other areas are not available. The arms have two places which also have a strong flow. Here," she said touching the elf's arm just above his forearm. "And here," she said pointing at his wrist. She moved down to the elf's feet. "The place best suited for our needs is here," she explained pointing to the vein that stuck out over the elf's ankle. "The flow is strong, but it is farthest from the heart and can be controlled better."

She opened a drawer on the side of the table and removed ten small vials. "Elven blood is very valuable. Before we perform the essence siphon, we will fill these vials." She passed Ghostspawn a handful of cork stoppers. "I will hand you the full vials. You are to put the stoppers in them. Be sure they are secure, then put the vials in the little gutter at the end of the table." Ghostspawn arranged the stoppers on the end of the table and watched as Mistress inserted the blade into the vein over the elf's ankle. She held a vial at the other end of the bone and then lowered the bone. Blood entered the vial in small, rhythmic spurts. When the vial was nearly full, Mistress lifted the bone slightly and handed the vial to Ghostspawn. She repeated the process until eight of the vials were filled, then removed the bone from the elf's ankle. "This is the last thing we will do here for several hours. The essence will make you slightly intoxicated. You will rest until that intoxication leaves. Then we will return to our friend here and harvest some other things we will need later today. Don't worry about him getting up and wandering off. He will be perfectly content to rest here and wait for us." She collected the eight vials and inspected the stoppers before placing them into a pouch she wore at her waist. She left two of the stoppers on the table and put the rest back into the drawer. "We will enjoy his essence once we have returned to your cabin. Stopper these two as you did the others." Mistress waited until Ghostspawn nodded, then muttered a long incantation. Near the end of it, she inserted the bone-blade back into the elf's ankle. The blood that entered the vials emitted a slight golden glow this time. After insuring that both vials were stoppered properly, Mistress cleaned the tools. Afterwards, she returned to the elf and turned his foot so that Ghostspawn could see the wound. "Notice that not one drop of his blood leaked from the wound," she said. "That is the proper way to do things. No waste." She collected the two vials and led the goblin to his cabin. "I noticed that those last two vials had a golden glow. What does that mean?" Ghostspawn asked as they crossed the yard. "You are becoming more observant. That is good. The color of the glow indicates the quality of the essence. Our elven friend has a very strong spirit. A golden glow is about the best you can get from anything less than a god." "What color would a god's blood glow?" "I will save that until you can see for yourself, little goblin. If my plans go well, you will not have to wait long." They entered Ghostspawn's cabin and sat at the table. Mistress handed him one of the vials. She removed the stopper from

her own and raised it. Ghostspawn followed her example. Together, they drained the contents of their vials. The lack of flavor surprised the goblin who expected blood to taste like blood, regardless of which color it glowed. The contents flowed down his throat like pure spring water, cold and refreshing. Ghostspawn felt the intoxication immediately. He placed his hands on the table to brace himself. Mistress laughed at him. "Go lie down before you hurt yourself," she chided. "When you awake, be sure to clean these vials and return them to me. I will await you in my cabin." She stood and Ghostspawn noticed that she was feeling the effects of the essence as well, though not as drastically. She left him to stagger to his cot. He almost missed it as he tried to sit. He fell back, his legs still hanging over the edge of the cot when he passed out. Mistress returned to her cabin and put the eight vials of elven blood away. Bhk-at would eventually receive five of them, but he would have to wait. Mistress did not want him thinking the blood was easy to acquire. Also, she knew him well enough to know that he would provide more information as an excuse to see her again if she made him wait long enough. She sat at the table and prepared for Ghostspawn's return. He would want more of the essence when he woke. Mistress knew exactly how addictive essence could be. She would make the goblin earn his next taste. For her plan to work, the goblin would need to extract the essence from whichever of the Lord of Chaos' children she would be able to snag. With this in mind, he would have to learn the incantation. She broke the incantation into parts she felt were small enough for the goblin's feeble mind to learn. After completing that, she began making a special potion. She knew of several mixtures that would put the child of the Chaos Lord in her control. Those easy to make were detectable. Her target made that option completely unacceptable. The one she needed for this task would take as long as three or four days to complete and would be totally undetectable. Having cleared a space on the counter, she began gathering the ingredients. As she gathered them, she made a list of those she needed to acquire. The elf in the stockroom would supply several of them. The rest had to be fresh and she would have to forage them in the forest when she was ready for them. Shortly after she completed her list, she heard the goblin approaching her cabin. Mistress met her apprentice at the door, blocking his way until he gave her the two vials. She inspected them to make sure he had cleaned them properly, then let him enter. "Sit at the table," she instructed as she put the vials aside. "You've much to learn."

"When can I get more essence?" Ghostspawn asked, standing near the door. "You will get more essence when you know how to harvest it. Now seat yourself so that you can begin to learn the incantation that will allow you to do that." Mistress grinned at the goblin's back as he walked to the table. His narrow-minded ambition made him very predictable. She watched him flinch with the pain of The Grove's transformation as he sat and she almost smiled. "The incantation you need to learn is very complicated. I will teach it to you in parts. The sooner you learn the incantation, the sooner you can attempt to extract essence from our friend in the stockroom. My guess is that your pains will end before you learn the spell properly. I would not wish you to ruin a fine elven specimen because you flinched in pain." Mistress took her seat across the table and began teaching him the words to the spell. They spent most of the evening working on the first part of the phrase. The only language the goblin ever learned besides his own, was the human speech spoken in the kingdom of Taran. It, like goblin, was a very guttural language compared to the elven words of the incantation. After hours of struggling with the words, Ghostspawn asked, "Can't I say the incantation in my own language?" "You most certainly can say it in your language," Mistress said, smiling at the goblin. "Of course the spell will have no effect since the goblin language, like goblins, has no magic. I thought your desire for more essence would motivate you to learn it properly." Her smile widened slightly and she leaned forward before adding, "Or maybe you are not intelligent enough to learn the spell at all. Maybe we should work on something easier, like lighting a twig with a tinder box." Ghostspawn scowled across the table at her, then continued to force his mouth to make the sounds it was never meant to make. By the time Mistress sent him back to his cabin, he had made some improvement. Mistress denied him knowledge of that, knowing her student would work even harder the next day. During the next week and a half, Ghostspawn spent nearly every waking moment working on the spell. The few times he did not, he tended the stockroom. The elf on the table fascinated the goblin almost as much as what Mistress had done to him. His first visit to the stockroom, Ghostspawn noticed that the elf's little and index finger were missing from his right hand. He observed that their removal had been done impeccably at the knuckle joint. After that, the goblin made it a point to observe the elf on a

daily basis. In addition to being curious as to what Mistress would do to the elf next, he found his visits motivating. At first, Ghostspawn could determine what had been taken from the elf quickly. One day, he discovered an ear missing, several more fingers on another day, a portion of his scalp that enabled the goblin to see the bone of his skull on yet another day. Then it became impossible for the goblin to tell what Mistress intended. Ghostspawn examined the elf carefully, and the only evidence that his mentor had been there was an incision that started at the base of the elf's neck and continued until it ended under his arm. The cut was barely visible, appearing to be a very thin line drawn on the elf, which made the goblin wonder if Mistress had done anything after she had made the cut. The next day, he found another incision that mirrored the first. Ghostspawn marveled at the precision executed to make the two cuts identical. On his next trip to the stockroom, Ghostspawn found that Mistress had made another cut. This one traced the contour of the elf's abdomen from his groin up to his hipbone, then down to his back. As he expected, the next day he found another incision on the other side of his lower abdomen. What Mistress was doing became a distraction to the goblin. Although seeing the elf reminded him of his first taste of essence, these incisions filled Ghostspawn's mind as he wondered what they meant. When he returned the next day, he found yet another incision. This one connected the upper and lower incisions, straight down the center of the elf's torso. Mistress had carefully cut around the elf's navel as if she were planning to remove it. Ghostspawn also noted that the first cuts were not healing. He examined all the damage Mistress had done to the elf and found that none showed any sign of change. The wounds appeared as fresh as they had when they were made. Mistress knew her student was visiting the elf and she kept him very busy for the next couple days. When she finally allowed the goblin time to return to the stockroom she spied upon him to treasure his reaction. Ghostspawn entered the room and froze. Mistress had removed the skin from the elf's torso and the goblin stood staring at the bare muscles as they slowly rose and fell with the elf's breathing. After several moments, he moved closer, finding it remarkable that the elf that lay on the table still lived. The sight of the red meat caused the goblin to drool. The goblin jumped away from the table as Mistress asked, "Is the sight of all that fresh meat making you hungry?" Ghostspawn absently wiped his mouth with the back of his hand, surprising himself by finding drool.

"How is he still alive?" he asked, more to change the subject than to gain knowledge. "The magic of keeping them alive while I take my needs from them took me many years to perfect. It is not something you can learn at this point. Tomorrow we will test your skill at harvesting his essence. Go now and practice." Mistress waited until Ghostspawn left the stockroom then approached the table. She looked into the eyes of the elf, noting the pain mirrored there and finding pleasure in it. "Your pain will not last much longer," she whispered as she gently ran a finger across his exposed muscle. "Consider yourself lucky. Most lie here for months. But I need some of your vital organs for a special drink I'm making. I doubt this part of you will survive long after I've taken your heart. Of course the shelf I made of your skin will live a very long time. I will be finished with the rest of you by the end of the week." The elf heard the words but could make no sense of them. All he knew now was pain. He had lost all sense of what it meant to be an elf, or even what it had meant to be an individual. His memories consisted only of the suffering and drug induced indifference that defined the world he now lived in. Had his thinking been clearer, he would not have considered the pale female creature who came to him and spoke softly to him as the means by which he would find some peace from the ever present agony. The other creature that came and went, often not speaking at all frightened him. In spite of the physical change that evolved the creature from an old, feeble looking monster to the younger, stronger looking, less monstrous-appearing being it was now, the elf considered it the far greater evil. He took consolation in his vague observation that the pale female seemed to be able to control the demon. "I'll be back to feed you later," Mistress said as she caressed his emaciated chin. "Don't go anywhere, you'll miss your dinner." That evening, Mistress worked with Ghostspawn with an intensity the goblin had yet to encounter from her. By the time Mistress sent him away, his voice cracked and wheezed from the strain of continuously repeating the incantation.
