Ghostspawn returned to his cabin and ate the raw meat he found on the table and drank several mugs of water before retiring to his cot. He doubted sleep would come to him on the eve of his first true test, so he ran through the incantation in his mind. Mistress had neglected to teach him the meaning of the words, or even where one word ended and the next began. The goblin considered putting his own meaning to them, but worried that the incantation would be ineffective if the wrong thoughts were in his mind. Instead, he concentrated on what he

wanted to happen, the golden glow of the elf's essence filling the small vials along with the elf's blood. When sleep finally found the goblin, it filled his dreams with the incantation and golden intoxication. After Ghostspawn left, Mistress set up her portal spell. She was now ready for the next part of her plan. The information Bhk-at had given her, along with the blood samples, made Mistress unsure of whether she would be receiving a male or a female child of the Lord of Chaos. As a result, she would need to prepare for both. What she did know was that they would be receiving their inheritance in under two weeks time. This knowledge let her know the ages of the children. She would need to capture one male and one female elf of approximately the same age for her plan to succeed. Bhk-at also mentioned that they resembled wild-elves. She smiled, thinking that at least that part would be easy. Wild-elves did not reside in towns or buildings. She would be able to locate what she needed without the risk of entering highly populated areas. This captive would be the double sent back to replace the offspring of the Lord of Chaos in her clutches. The double would have to be convincing enough to give her a week, at least. It would need to have the memories and at least some of the skills of the original. She would accomplish this with the first vial of essence extracted from the child of the god. The similarity in appearance would be no problem for her. She had spent hundreds of years altering the shape and appearance of both humans and elves. The furnishings of her cottage were living proof of her skill. Making one elf appear as another would be trivial for her, especially if they were approximately the same size and build. She smiled thinking of the challenge she had set before herself as she stepped through the portal. Mistress entered a twilight forest and immediately cast her invisibility spell. She frowned at the scenery surrounding her. Wild- elves, she knew, preferred their habitats completely natural. Yet their magic enhanced nature bringing her to the conclusion that they were a contradiction to themselves. Putting this thought aside she began to search for what she needed. At this time of day, most of the younger elves would be at play somewhere. She knew the males enjoyed swimming. The river that flowed nearby became her first destination. She was rewarded with a group of five elves splashing in the shallows. One of the five, an elf with bright amber eyes, fit her needs perfectly. She remained hidden until she could get him alone. Her luck proved even better than she had anticipated. A young elven female hid not far from her, watching the males swimming. Mistress readied the herb that would render her victim unconscious as she stalked the girl. A moment later, the young elven maiden lay behind the tree she had been using for cover to watch the

boys. Mistress cast a spell on the girl so that she would not be discovered while she waited for the amber-eyed boy. Before long, fireflies began to appear in the surrounding woods. Mistress knew they signaled the time when the boys would be returning to their families. The two youngest elves were the first to leave. A few minutes later, another left. Only the amber-eyed elf and one about the same age remained. Mistress decided that the extra would have to die as they appeared to want to return home together. Mistress waited until they were very close to where she hid, then threw a small dart that struck the unwanted elf in the throat. As the amber-eyed elf tried to catch his friend, Mistress used her herb on him. She retrieved her dart and dragged the dead elf back to the river and let the current have him. Returning to her two prisoners, she cut from their bodies the vines that clothed them. She knew they were magical in nature and did not wish her captives to be tracked by some magic in their vines. Clasping each by the hand, she cast the portal that would return them to her cabin. Once there, she carried them to the stockroom and put them in separate cages. Against her better judgment, she checked to see if the girl's innocence was still intact before she put her in the cage. Seeing that it was, she hoped the child she received from the Lord of Chaos would be male. Innocent females provided some of the strongest components Mistress used in her spells. She made sure to cast an extra lock on the girl's cage so her goblin apprentice would not be able to spoil her should he be overcome with the urges of his newly re-acquired youth. Satisfied that the elves were secure, she returned to her cabin to rest for Ghostspawn's venture into essence harvesting. The next morning, Mistress checked on the two wild-elves. Both were conscious but the incense had taken effect. She knew they probably would not even know who they were by now. Content with their situation, she summoned Ghostspawn. While she waited for him to arrive, she placed a rack that held thirty empty, stoppered vials on the edge of the table with the elf. Ghostspawn walked into the stockroom as Mistress pulled the bone necessary for the essence extraction from the counter. "There you are," Mistress said as she led him to the table. "There are thirty vials in this rack. Over the next few days, you will be attempting to extract two vials every hour. When you are not extracting essence, I will be harvesting parts that I need for other things. If you do not succeed," she said, glaring at the goblin, "you will replace this elf on the table and I will have to find another apprentice who is more capable."

The goblin swallowed hard as he took the bone from Mistress and positioned himself beside the elf's foot. He waited until Mistress removed the stoppers from the first two vials, then inserted the sharp tip of the bone into the vein over the elf's ankle. "I will handle controlling the flow for now. You concentrate on the magic." Ghostspawn took a deep breath and uttered the incantation. He relaxed his hand as Mistress guided the end of the bone to the vial. The first vial had no golden glow and the goblin's heart sank. "Try again," Mistress said. "Concentrate on what you want. Worrying about the spell not working will only make you fail." Again Ghostspawn uttered the incantation. This time he closed his eyes and put the image of the golden essence flowing into the vial in his mind. He felt Mistress move the bone, first down to the vial, then back up again. "Very good," Mistress muttered as she gently removed the bone from the elf's ankle. "Clean your tool and leave it on the counter for later. Return to your cabin and rest. I will call you when it is time for the next attempt." Ghostspawn stared at the vial Mistress had placed in the rack. He saw the faint golden glow and grinned. "It's weak, but it's a start," Mistress explained. "You will get that after your last attempt this evening. Hopefully, the next time you will be able to keep your eyes open. Now begone. I've work to do." Ghostspawn carefully cleaned the bone at the water pump then placed it on the counter. His mood was good as he walked to his cabin. As the day progressed, Ghostspawn became better at extracting essence. Mistress still had to guide the bone and vials, but the glow within those vials became stronger with each attempt the goblin made at extracting the essence. Each visit to the stockroom, he found less and less of the elf waiting for him. He had no clue as to what Mistress did with most of the parts that were removed. Some, he saw carefully lining the counter. At the end of the day, Mistress gave him a tray with a large piece of raw meat and the first successful vial of essence on it. The goblin assumed that the meat came from the upper portion of the elf's left leg. The thigh bone rested on the counter with several other bones. He also saw the elf's left foot bones resting on the counter, still connected to each other with the tendons. He wondered what piece of furniture it would serve to support. By the end of the second day, the goblin was rewarded with more meat from the elf as well as two vials of essence. He could now accomplish the extraction, with the exception of putting the stopper in the vials, without Mistress's guiding hand. The third day, he was left

to do the entire task without aid, using the rack to hold the vials until he could stopper them. The last extraction had to come from the elf's neck. His arms, legs and most of his lower abdomen were gone. Ghostspawn knew that the rest of the elf would be gone before the night was over. He had to wait for his tray at the end of the extraction. As he watched, Mistress carefully removed the elf's chest muscles and placed them on the goblin's tray. She added three vials of essence and told him not to disturb her for the next couple days. "Remain in your cabin," she ordered. "When I am finished what I am doing, I will let you know. I will tend the incense this time since I have to be down here for most of the tasks I need to complete." She glanced at the tray, then added, "You have three vials of essence. See if you can make them last a day or two." She turned away from him and the goblin left the stockroom. He thought back to his journey and the reason for making it. His prior desire to have the power to demolish a keep like the one he stumbled upon on his way here no longer mattered. He glanced at the three vials resting on the tray he carried and smiled. This, he thought, was real power. He wondered what else the albino woman would teach him before he decided to kill her. She would have to die, if for no other reason than the way she always talked down to him. Not yet though. He knew he would learn more from her before he would teach her proper respect. Mistress wasted no time in getting to work on what remained of the elf. As soon as the goblin had closed the door to the storehouse, she collected the tools she would need to harvest the last portions of his body. The elf's eyes had been dimming throughout that day. Mistress knew he would be dead before the night settled over the forest. She had stopped giving him the potion that kept him alive the day before. The potion she was making to gain control of the child-god needed one final component. The elven heart had to be beating to pump the lifeblood into the mixture. Still, Mistress took as much as she dared from the expiring elf's body before finally removing his heart. She rushed to the potion with his heart beating in her hand as soon as it was liberated from his chest. The more blood it pumped into the elixir, the stronger the final product would be. Several moments passed before the heart beat its final feeble effort. Mistress was quite pleased with the results, so much so, that she did not even despair the fact that she missed the elf's final breath. She cast the final spells on the elixir, then put a small quantity of it into a metal flask. The remainder, she stored in a cabinet under the shelf. The preservation spell she cast on it would keep it fresh for when she would need it again. As she returned to her cabin

with the flask, she thought about how she would get the potion into the victim. Bhk-at was one option open to her, but she knew that it would be an option with a very dear price. She was patient, though. There was still one week before the inheritance. That would give her time to think of something. Entering the cabin, she saw Bhk-at's signal. She put the flask on a shelf and placed the ten vials of elven blood beside the small trapdoor before sitting at the table. Then, she let the deep-elf waiting to see her know that she was ready to receive him. Bhk-at entered and saw the vials waiting for him. Smiling, he said, "Thank you, Mistress. I have more information for you, if you wish to hear it." "I don't believe I agreed to pay for more information, but if I find it as useful as your last bit of gossip, I'm sure I can come up with something to keep you happy." Bhk-at nodded, knowing that she may decide his news would be worthless. He told her anyway. Mistress listened, keeping her face set in an impassive scowl through his entire monologue. She found it difficult to look bored when he related the story of the dwarven servant to her. The ability Bhk-at described belonging to the human named Simon also interested her. Deep-elves were hardly ever detected. This child seemed to be able to find them even when they were quite some distance from him. At the end of Bhk-at's report, Mistress asked, "How much do you feel this information is worth to me? I'm sure you have something in mind." Bhk-at nodded. "Yes. I believe the information is worth a vial of dragon's blood. I know that dragon's blood is rare, but I think the knowledge of the human's ability to be at least worth that much. Then there is the beardless dwarf..." "I will consider your request. The boy's ability does intrigue me. I will let you know my decision when I have made it." Bhk-at knew that any further conversation could prove fatal. He bowed, grabbed the strap binding the vials of elven blood and departed. He also knew that Mistress would reward him for the information. It may not be what he asked for, but there would be some reward. As soon as the trapdoor closed behind the deep-elf, Mistress grabbed the flask from the shelf and cast the portal that would take her to Cragsguard. Before stepping through, she collected a few small gems and put them in her pouch. Smiling she stepped into the portal. She arrived in the canyon beneath the gates of the town. Concealing herself in magic, she climbed the path and entered the town. From what the deep-elves told her, it was easy to find the

dwarf's room. Mistress made herself comfortable in a chair that stood near the only window and waited. She knew the dwarf would be serving the elves in Deep Stone and would probably return late. Mistress used the time to rehearse convincing the dwarf to betray one of the elves. The dwarf's humiliation at serving the elves in her home made Mistress's rehearsals totally unnecessary. In a matter of minutes, Mena had accepted the task. Mistress instructed Mena to place the flask on her sill after she accomplished the deed, then gave the dwarf half the gems she had brought with her saying the rest would replace the flask. "What if they discover what I've done?" Mena asked. "Do not worry, sweet child. The potion is completely undetectable and it won't take effect until a week after it is imbibed. They will have no way of tracing it to you." Mena smiled, then asked, "What of the other two? I would like them to pay as well." Mistress stood and walked to the door. "In time, child. Be patient and you will see the fall of all three of them," Mistress promised. Mistress returned to her portal in the canyon. She looked up at the town and smiled before stepping through to return to her cabin.

32 William spent much of his time in the Cracked Anvil, waking early and staying up late, in the hopes of finding Ky in his corner. He was in no rush to start his bakery, planning to wait until Micah finished with his training so that he could help him run the shop. During his days visiting the Cracked Anvil, he heard many tales concerning the young black-eyed elf. Every story he heard, increased his desire to hear more. William learned quickly that Stan was the best source of stories about Ky. The barkeep never seemed to tire of relating Ky's adventures. The day after the children returned from Deep Stone, his vigilance was rewarded. William entered the common room just after dawn to find Ky seated in the back eating his breakfast. The legend of "The Ghost" gave William reason to hesitate, and he almost did not approach the table. Only the thought of what he wanted to do for Micah helped him keep his resolve. William stopped a few feet from the table and asked, "May I join you for a couple moments? I promise not to be long. I just have a question I think you could help me with." Ky looked up from his meal and noticed William trembling slightly as he waited for the answer to his question. Ky grinned and said, "You've been listening to too many stories. Join me. Grandfather will bring you breakfast." William smiled and remembered that breathing was a necessity of life as he sat across from Ky. "What you did for Little Ky has yet to be repaid fully," Ky said. Ky grinned again and added, "So what made you risk almost

certain and painful death to come to me?" "I take it all those tales about you are not exactly true, then." "They are true. Anyway the one's I've heard are. They just don't apply to people I like. I happen to like you. What is your question?" William thought for a moment. He had rehearsed this meeting over and over, but the stress of coming to the table made all his rehearsals sift through his fingers like very fine sand. He shrugged and said, "I've heard quite a lot about this inheritance ceremony that is planned for your triplets. It's a very foreign concept to me. I'm sure Micah is rather in the dark about it as well. I would like to give Micah an inheritance ceremony since this is his new home. Do you think that would be possible?" "Of course," Ky said. "How old is he?" "My guess is that he is approaching his eleventh birthday, for the second time," William answered. "Before he left Vienna, he was thirty." Stan brought a plate of food for William. "Will you be around much today?" he asked Ky as he placed the meal on the table. "Unless someone else has a major problem they need me to solve, I've no plans." "Excellent! I'll come visit when William is done with you." Stan patted William on the shoulder and returned to the kitchen. "Little Ky is about the same age, with the same twenty year gap that Micah has. When is Micah's birthday?" William laughed, "On earth, it would be June twenty-first. I'm not sure what the date would be here." Ky nodded. "What season would that be?" "Early summer," William answered between bites of egg. Ky ate in silence for a few moments. He looked forward to Little Ky's human inheritance almost as much as he dreaded what would happen when Little Ky received it. He had hoped to delay it as long as he could. It did not seem right to him to make Micah wait, and he thought both would like it if they received their inheritance together. He guessed that William was now thinking the same thing. Finally he said, "Little Ky was born in early summer too. Do you think they'd like to celebrate together?" "I think they would love that! When were you planning on giving Little Ky his inheritance? I can wait until then to give Micah his." Ky pushed his empty plate away and slid to the corner of his seat. "I was not really thinking about it. I was hoping it would go away." "I don't understand," William said. "From what I've seen, you

think very highly of Little Ky. Why would you deny him his inheritance?" "I don't know how it will affect him," Ky whispered. "I don't want him getting hurt." "What about the triplets? Are you worried about them as well?" Ky shook his head. "Both their parents are gods. They will be able to handle whatever happens. They also have over a thousand years of preparation. Little Ky is just a little farm boy, or at least that's how I thought of him. You've seen him and spent many years with him. If you didn't know me, would you think him extraordinary in any way?" The question caught William unprepared. There were many ways in which he thought of Little Ky that were extraordinary. None of them related to what might become of him during his inheritance. He thought for several moments, trying to find some way to reassure Ky that Little Ky would be fine. Before he could come up with anything, Stan sat across from him. "I couldn't help but overhear the conversation," Stan said, mostly to Ky. "I will share something that Illya shared with me. She, like you, is very worried about Little Ky and his inheritance. Long ago, she searched his spirit in a similar way she searched yours. The only difference is that her search of you was unintentional. She found within Little Ky the same concentration of great power that she found in you." "I heard about that," Ky whispered. "It's in Delmaria's journal about his birth." Stan smiled and continued, "Little Ky has strengths you did not have, and can never have. He is better prepared than even the triplets." Ky looked at Stan and frowned. "I will explain," Stan said. "Would you like me to leave?" William asked. "It would not be a problem if you do." Ky shook his head and said, "You're the one who caused this problem. You stay here until we solve it." Stan laughed and said, "William is not the one who wasn't fast enough to avoid that goblin's flames." "How would you know? You weren't there." "Neither was William," Stan said, still laughing. "Now back to my explanation. Correct me if I'm wrong." He paused until Ky nodded. "The triplets have been trained by The Nine, even Archos," Stan added scowling which was rewarded with a grin from Ky. "Little Ky has had none of that training." Ky nodded, his grin fading.

"The inheritance ceremony is to welcome the child to the family as a responsible adult. The only training the child needs is what it means to be a member of the family. Little Ky had ten years of the closest family he could possibly have. The triplets, and no blame meant here, did not receive that. After Little Ky was taken from you, you changed. I saw it as did many others that knew you well. You would never be a family-type person again. From what I can see, the triplets have done well and I believe Laena had quite a bit to do with that. Little Ky had both Illya and you. That is the difference that makes him better prepared." Ky was not completely convinced, but he could think of no arguments. He stared at the bench a few moments, then asked, "What would you suggest, Grandfather?" "I like the idea of this summer. If William agrees, we can have it at the farm." "I could think of no better place to have it, except maybe here at the Cracked Anvil," William offered. "Then we will have it after the first full moon of summer at the farm," Ky stated. He looked at William and asked, "Is there anything else you need?" "What type of item would be appropriate to give Micah? The things the wild-elves and dwarves gave him are so much better than anything I could come up with." "Give him what you feel he should get," Stan said. "He is your son and if you choose to give him a blade of wilted grass, he will treasure it forever. The item is not important. The fact that you regard him worthy enough to receive the item makes whatever you give him a treasure beyond anything else." "One last thing," William said. "Should I tell him about it?" Stan smiled and answered, "If you tell him, he will likely tell Little Ky. If Little Ky knows, then a certain unpredictable little elf I know won't be able to back out of it." This comment earned Stan a half-hearted scowl from Ky and a thoughtful nod from William. William smiled. "I thank you both. I will begin thinking of the gift I wish to give him. If you will excuse me, I will leave you to your tall tales of death and destruction." Stan laughed, as did Ky. William had never heard Ky's laughter and he liked it. He walked back to his home plotting ways to hear that laughter again. Considering all he learned of the small black- eyed elf, he realized that not many would have heard his laughter. He placed the sound safely in his memory, treating it as a special gift. Smiling, he entered the back room of his home. The spring weather here was warmer than he was

accustomed to, but he made a small fire anyway. It was more for the pleasant feeling he experienced sitting in front of the fire than for heat. Daphnia would be coming over shortly and he felt the fire would add to the visit. William smiled knowing that Micah would be too busy to interrupt his time with Daphnia for a few days. As he sat before the fire waiting for Daphnia, he wondered what he had done to deserve the life he found himself enjoying. Whatever it was, he considered himself very lucky to have done it.

33 Ky II woke early the next morning. He left the barracks quietly and ran through town to the blacksmith's shop. The gift of the dwarven swords reminded him of some of the training Selia had given him. Each member of the group had two finely made swords now. It only made sense that they learn to use them both. Ky II would rely on Tal a great deal for this part of the training as he learned much better from Selia. Ky II found Banen already working in the heat of his forge. He ran to him and yelled his greeting over the noise of Banen's hammer. "Good morning, Banen!" Banen glanced at the young elf and put his hammer down. "Good day to ye, lad. What might I be doing for you?" "I was hoping you could make another set of practice swords, if you aren't too busy, that is." "Don't be telling me you've done destroyed the first batch already! I know ye've been training hard, but they should have lasted longer than that." Ky II laughed and asked, "Can we talk outside so we don't have to yell at each other?" "Of course, lad," Banen answered smiling. He followed Ky II to the square then said, "Now, about those practice swords." Ky II showed Banen the sword the dwarves had given him as he explained. "Last night we were treated to a feast by the Deep Stone dwarves. After the meal, they gave us each a new sword." "So the one's I made are not needed. I see," Banen said

frowning, though he greatly admired the craftsmanship of the dwarven sword. Banen took the sword and examined it. "Ye will need practice swords more suitable to these weapons," Banen muttered as he turned back to the shop. "Actually," Ky II started. "No! I understand. 'Tis no way I can create a weapon to match the dwarven smiths." "Listen to me!" Ky II yelled. Banen turned to the elf, a look of surprise on his face. "We are going to use both the dwarven swords and the one's you made. I'm going to have Tal train us in how to use two swords at once!" Banen's surprised expression changed with the addition of his smile. "Lad, I'll be proud to make ye the practice swords you need. I'll have them ready for you in an hour." Ky II smiled, "I'll come for them before lunch then. Good day to you, Banen." "And a good day to you, lad!" Ky II returned to barracks to wake Tal. He looked forward to this part of the training. The others would like it as well. They seemed to prefer Tal's more ordered approach and Ky II had to admit that it had its uses.

34 Mena woke early, as was her routine. She knew both Tal and Simon had to have a drink of water waiting for them when they awoke. Most mornings, she let them get their own water when they went to clean their faces at the start of the day, though sometimes she woke early and had it next to their beds when they woke. Simon always made a point to thank her when she had it ready. Tal would thank her if he saw her before he started his other tasks of the day. This morning, Mena had a purpose in having the water waiting. She hid the little flask the albino woman had given her the night before inside her tunic and quietly walked to the children's room. She had heard one of them leave a few moments before she entered the hall and hoped it was not Tal. As Mena softly opened the door, she noted Tal still curled up on his cot. Smiling, the dwarf took Tal's and Simon's cups into the bathing room and prepared their morning drinks. She emptied the contents of the flask into Tal's cup, then put the flask back into her tunic. Then she added the water from the pump. When both were full, she compared the two and found she could find no difference in either their appearance of smell. She briefly thought of tasting them before returning to the room and placing the cups on the small night stands beside the two boys' cots. After placing the cups on the small stands near their cots, she quietly left, wishing to be elsewhere when they started waking. She knew they would be free from practice this morning and she wanted to avoid a constant stream of chores that usually came when they did not practice. Returning to her room, she hid the flask within her spare

clothing. She would put it on the sill after the children she served had gone to sleep. None of them had ever come into her room before, but she did not wish to risk a first time. Afterwards, she walked to the Cracked Anvil for breakfast. She saw Ky II in the blacksmith's shop as she walked across the square and quickened her pace until she was safely inside the inn. She saw Ky in his corner and found a seat at the bar to be as far from him as possible. Oren brought her a plate of food and she took her time eating. By the time she was ready to leave, Ky had gone. She did not see him go, but from what she had heard, no one ever did. She whistled tunelessly to herself as she returned to the barracks to start her day serving the children. She knew they would be waking soon and she wanted to make sure Tal saw her before he got caught up in the day's activities. The irony of him thanking her for having his water ready for him would make her even happier. Ky II and Tal were coming towards her as she entered the hallway. Tal did not disappoint her, thanking her as he passed. Mena delved into her chores happily after that. The opportunity given to her by the albino woman started her own mind working. Throughout the day, she plotted small things to irritate the triplets. By nightfall, she had several things in mind that she felt she could manage without too much retribution. She placed the flask on the sill and fell asleep dreaming of being free of her servitude.

35 Ky had seen Mena enter the inn. He paused a moment in his conversation with Stan to concentrate on her. Ky was still new to seeing what his brother, Simon, called 'spirit people.' What he saw in Mena's made him uncomfortable enough to tell Stan to keep his eye on her when she was here. Stan simply nodded, as if Ky had told him nothing he did not already know. Their conversation ended before Mena left and Ky fought the urge to torture her in some small way before leaving. Only the fact that she seemed to be doing what she was supposed to be doing saved her. He left the inn and walked across the square to William's new home. Entering quietly, he slipped behind the counter and into the back room. He frowned not finding Daphnia there. William was seated in front of the fireplace, so Ky walked to him. "Kind of warm for a fire, isn't it?" Ky asked. William jumped at the sound of the young elf's voice, then smiled. "It has a different purpose this morning. What can I do for you?" "The triplets will be getting dragons for their inheritance. Don't tell them, though. I just thought that if you want to give Micah a dragon, I can arrange it for you. Little Ky will probably get one as well." "Thank you for the offer," William said. "I'll keep that in mind. Is it unheard of to give them two items?" Ky shook his head. "Only one item for the ceremony. Afterwards, it's common for them to receive other gifts." "Excellent." William pointed to a chair. "I'm sorry. I've

forgotten my manners. Would you like to sit and visit a while?" "No. I have other things to do." Ky turned and walked to the door. He could see Daphnia coming through the door of the Cracked Anvil. He grinned and said over his shoulder, "Besides, I know you don't want to waste that fire on me." He vanished to the sound of William's nervous laughter. From Cragsguard, Ky went to The Garden. His last visit there, with Simon and Ky II, he had asked The Lady a question. She told him she would have to speak with Maker before she could answer. Ky hoped that she had time to do that as he stood on the path by the stream. The last time, he felt The Lady in his thoughts, welcoming him and guiding him to her. This time, he did not feel her welcome, though he did not feel unwelcome either. This was his first time to The Garden alone and he wondered what he had to do to see her. He struggled with the decision for a while and was about to leave and try again another time when he saw her walking down the path towards him. "Hello, Ky. I'm very happy you came to see me," she said smiling. She seated herself near the tree that shaded the small stream and beckoned her son to her. "This is your home. You don't have to wait on the doorstep for me to come to you. You are always welcome." "About that question I asked you..." "Come sit with me and we will talk about it," she replied. Ky hesitated a moment before stepping closer to her. She smiled and guided him to her lap and held him close. "You are my son, just as Simon is," she said, tightening her hug slightly. "I love you as much as I love him." She quietly stroked Ky's long black hair until she felt him relax in her embrace. Smiling, she hummed softly to him. Ky was not used to this type of treatment. Something in him wanted to make the moment last forever. She made no demands on him. She forced no expectations on him. She accepted him as he was without judgment. Finally, she loved him and he could feel it. He knew that Illya felt the same about him, but this felt different, deeper and more profound. Ky closed his eyes and leaned his head on The Lady's shoulder. "Why did I have to wait so long to feel like this?" he whispered. The Lady sighed. "I wanted, many times, to call you to me and hold you like this. Every trial you faced, alone and for the most part, unloved, caused great pain in my heart. Only your father's strength kept me from doing just that." "Does my father love me like you do?" This question surprised The Lady. She reverted to humming and caressing Ky's hair as she formulated her answer.

"Your father," she began, "is Maker. I'm sure Maker could take a form that could hold you as I am doing, but I doubt He would. He is not like you or me. He is the creator of all that is and although I feel He loves his creations, it is not the same love that a parent would feel for their child." "I thought you were the creator of the universe," Ky said. "That is true. I built our universe, but I did it with Maker's power and guidance. I will take you to Him another time. I think you will understand His ways better after you meet Him." They sat quietly several minutes. Simon had spoken to Ky about The Garden. He opened his eyes and tried to find the magic that Simon's description emphasized. Ky knew the magic was different from what he knew. It wasn't the magic of lightning, fire and violence. The magic here would be peaceful. His scan drifted across the small stream to the gently swaying birch and willow trees, then finally to the flowers that seemed to be everywhere accept the small path that led farther into The Garden. He was missing something and he knew it. "Simon said you would sing to him sometimes. He said he couldn't understand the words, but the song made him feel better. Will you sing to me?" The Lady started humming immediately. As she hummed she searched his soul to find what it was he needed. As she perceived what Ky sought, she added words to her melody. She knew the elf she held would not understand the language on an intellectual level, but the peace he sought would be found and understood by his spirit. Ky continued to search the garden for the magic Simon spoke of as The Lady sang. Over and over, his search would find its way to the small stream. Finally, he gently pushed away from The Lady's embrace and removed his cloak, letting it fall on the bank as he stepped into the cool waters. He had waded in streams before, but this was different. The water seemed to be caressing his feet as he stood there staring down at it as it flowed around his ankles. He was so enthralled by the swirling waters that he did not notice that The Lady had removed his loin-cloth until she placed her hand on his shoulder and gently urged him forward. Ky looked into the center of the stream which seemed to have become wider and deeper, then succumbed to The Lady's guidance and walked to the center. Slowly, he moved to a seated position, reveling in the feeling of the water swirling around him. The Lady's song seemed to enhance the feeling of cleansing that washed over him. Ky felt he could remain there forever. Hours passed as the waters washed the pain and doubt from his soul. The Lady knew when it was time for him to come back to

the bank, and held a towel for him. Ky sighed as he slowly walked to her and let her wrap the towel around him before pulling him back onto her lap. "I think you are ready for your answer now," she said quietly. Ky nodded. "Maker is not in agreement with what you wish to do for your children." She felt her son sag slightly within her embrace. She hugged him a little tighter and continued, "But He will not prevent you from doing it or me from helping you. He is concerned that it will put you at considerable risk, though. I believe He is not deterring us because He knows Simon will be like you before too long and will be able to fill the void if you are lost." "So I will see you at their inheritance ceremonies?" Ky asked. "Ceremonies?" The Lady asked. "The triplets, then Little Ky." The Lady smiled and said, "You didn't tell me about Little Ky. But I will be there for him as well." "I was hoping to avoid Little Ky's inheritance. William and Micah sort of made me face it. I don't want anything happening to him again." "Little Ky is the one with the least risk," The Lady explained. "Maker sees the triplets as the means to get to you. I can not see His logic, but I trust it." "Would you mind if I come back..." Ky paused and glanced at the stream. "Come back and..." "You may come here whenever you wish. The more you come, the happier you will make me. Bring your children as well. They can benefit from the stream as you have. It will be the one thing you share with them that they will treasure the most." "I should go now," Ky said as he climbed from The Lady's embrace and dressed. "Remember that your visits here are beyond the confines of time. I know you are ready to go now. I just want you to know that whenever you come here, there is no need to leave until you are ready." She gently kissed his forehead and returned up the path into The Garden. Before passing from his sight, she turned and smiled. "Take one of the small purple ones. Those are your brother's favorites." Ky laughed as he searched for a small purple flower. It would be his way of thanking Simon for giving him the desire to come here. Flower in hand, he returned to Cragsguard and walked towards the barracks. Ky met Simon who was headed to the library and asked if he

would come to the farm for a while. Simon shrugged and fell in step beside his elven brother, his eyes on the flower Ky carried. "It's for you," Ky said, handing it to him. "I was told you like these." Simon smiled. "Yeah, these are my favorites. Did you enjoy your visit with Mom?" They walked a while in silence, Ky trying the title 'Mom' on The Lady. He never had anyone that could be called that and he was not sure he was comfortable with having someone now. The many years of being without tainted the title in Ky's mind. He did know that Simon's relationship with her was quite different. "It was interesting," he finally murmured. "So, what do you want to talk about, then?" Simon asked. "When we get to the farm," Ky answered as he quickened the pace. When they arrived at the farm, Ky helped Simon collect a bowl and a bucket of water before leading him out to the garden where they could plant the flower and talk without interruption. Most of the planting was completed by Simon as Ky watched. After the flower was settled into the center of the bowl, Simon collected two larger flowers to plant with it. "Why are you putting them there?" Ky asked. "The little purple flowers are shy," Simon explained. "They like to hide under larger flowers." Simon finished adding the two other flowers then sat beside Ky. He had never looked at Ky's spirit person directly and thought this would be a good chance to do so. He knew what he would see would be powerful. Simon had seen that powerful presence in Ky's empty chair that night the Combined Council had interviewed him. What he found surprised him anyway. The power was there, completely undeniable, but beneath it, Ky's spirit seemed frail and lost. With most spirit people, he could sense good and evil. Both were absent in Ky's. He did not realize that he had been staring, until Ky spoke to him. "What's wrong?" Ky whispered. "I'm sorry," Simon answered. "I was looking at your spirit person. It's just, I don't know, not what I thought I would see, I guess." "You've always been able to see them, haven't you?" Simon nodded. "Yeah. They help me decide on who I should avoid or get to know. They show me the true intentions of people I meet. I've always been able to tell the good people from the bad ones by looking at the spirit person. Well, except for you," he added quietly. "What do you see when you look at me?" Ky asked. Simon thought for a moment. "A lot of power, more than

anyone else I've ever seen. But there isn't any good or bad in there. I don't see any purpose." Ky nodded, then asked, "Have you ever looked at Mena's spirit person?" "Yeah. I don't trust her." Ky actually smiled then. "At least I got that one right. I'll be sending her home tomorrow. We'll be heading to Alle-Stecan then." "You can see spirit people too?" "Since I got my inheritance. It's not easy for me. I have to really concentrate to see them." "Have you ever looked at mine?" Ky shook his head. "No. Ky II really likes you and I trust his judgment." Simon turned the bowl a little so he could clearly see the purple flower. After a few moments of silence, he asked, "Would you mind looking at mine and telling me what you see?" Ky turned towards Simon and concentrated. Unlike the others that Ky tried to see, Simon's was difficult to focus on, as if it wished to remain hidden. When he finally gained a true sight of it, he saw the same power that Simon probably saw in Ky, only Simon's was not quite awake yet. He saw Simon as an open person, leaning towards good. Ky was not sure what told him this, but he felt that Simon had a very strong base supporting his spirit person. When he turned away, his line of sight caught the flowers Simon had just planted. Ky pointed to the purple flower. "Have you ever looked at its spirit person?" Simon shook his head. "No, I avoid plants because they confuse me." "Look at it. That is what I see when I look at you, except yours is far more powerful and it appears to be waiting or something. It's like it is still sleeping or something." Simon glanced at the flower and smiled. They had always been his favorites in the garden, shy and small, wanting to avoid notice. Ky's observation made him realize how like them he was. He did not look at the spirit person of the flower; there would be plenty of time to do that later. "You said we are going to Alle-Stecan tomorrow. I thought we had another five days before we had to be there." "Yep. On horseback, it will take about five days. My visit to The Garden made me decide to do it this way. I'll be taking Tal, Eleana and Little Ky to The Garden to visit during the trip to Alle- Stecan. They haven't been there yet." "You should take Ky II also."

"He's been there, several times." "Yeah, once with me alone and once with you and me. He hasn't been there alone with you though. I think he would like that more than the other trips, especially the stream." Ky looked at Simon wondering if he knew what he had done in The Garden. "What about the stream?" he asked. "That is my favorite place. Whenever I'm worried about something or feel insecure, the stream washes it all away. It's even better when Mom is there. You should try it sometime," Simon added, grinning. "I already have," Ky whispered. "Well, I got to get ready for tomorrow. Part of that is finding Stumpy so he can take Mena back to her parents. I think if I saw her again, I'd have to kill her." Simon laughed. "Yeah, Stumpy is the better option, I think." They stood and Simon picked up his bowl of flowers. "I'm going to leave this here if Illya won't mind taking care of it for me. I don't think riding on a horse would be good for it, especially for five days." "I think she will. Delmaria will probably help too. See you tomorrow." "Thanks for the flower. Bye!" Ky watched Simon walk to the house to see to the needs of the flower, then ported to Deep Stone in search of Stumpy.

36 Simon returned to the barracks to find the others. Not finding them, he searched the practice grounds from their bedroom window. Ky II had already started a session so Simon quickly changed into his practice tunic and ran to the grounds. When he arrived, he told them that Ky informed him that they would be leaving for Alle- Stecan the next day. Ky II scanned the group surrounding Simon. He knew that many of them would want to visit with people they would not see for the next five or six days. He wanted to visit with Symplex and Grandfather Stan. The group would do what he told them to do, there was no doubt in his mind about that. When he scanned them again, he found them all looking at him for direction. "This changes our schedule a bit," Ky II explained. "Unless we extend the practice session this morning, we won't learn the basics of what Tal is teaching us. So we will practice until Tal thinks we know enough, then have lunch at the Cracked Anvil. After that, the day is free to visit with friends and family." "What are we working on?" Simon asked. "Fighting with two weapons," Tal answered. "Yours are over by the benches." "Two weapons! I still have problems holding on to one," Simon muttered as he went to retrieve his swords. "You're actually a lot better than you think," Tal said. "Hurry so we can get this over with. I want to see if I can get another piano lesson in before we go." Tal teamed Simon up with Micah as they both needed the

most help and kept them in the center of the line. Once he showed the group what he wanted to practice, he would spend most of his time supporting and guiding Simon and Micah. Ky II was working with Eleana to Simon's left. At one point, he started losing his focus and playing around. Tal smacked him across the back of his head. "Hey!" "I learned that from Symplex. Stop playing, I got things I want to do today." Ky II laughed, but regained his concentration for the rest of the session. Tal kept them almost two hours longer than usual before he was satisfied with the progress they made. They ran to the barracks and changed out of their practice tunics before heading to the Cracked Anvil for lunch. The lunch crowd had gone by the time they got there and Stan enjoyed visiting with them while they ate. Afterwards, Tal, Micah, Little Ky and Brek went to visit with William. Simon chose to go to the farm since Stan mentioned that Karnak was seen there that morning. Ky II mentioned wanting to speak to Symplex about some of the things he taught Tal, and Eleana went with him not wanting to miss that conversation. Aemir went with Ky II and Eleana, wanting to do some visiting as well. Simon found Karnak in the old council room speaking with Illya. They invited Simon to join them which he did after he checked on the flower Ky had given him. Karnak dominated the conversation asking questions about the training the group had been receiving. After Karnak was satisfied, Simon asked if he could get more practice at moving quietly. Karnak led Simon to the yard and worked with him for about an hour with Illya watching. "You are improving quite a bit, Simon," Karnak stated as he finished the practice session. "I can see you have more confidence in yourself now. Hopefully, Brek will have grown also. I am on my way to find him to begin his orientation into the Council of Darkness. You wouldn't happen to know where I could find him, do you?" Simon nodded, then laughed remembering that Karnak could not see the nod. "Yeah. He's with Micah, Little Ky and Tal visiting William in Cragsguard. I can take you there. I want to see the LEGO farm that Micah keeps talking about, anyway." "Lead on. As loud as you are when you aren't trying to be quiet, I'm sure I'll be able to follow you without error." They bid Illya farewell and went through the portal to Cragsguard. Karnak's presence in the Cracked Anvil caused a bit of discomfort in several of the patrons, but they calmed after Stan greeted him as a friend. The thantor god followed Simon across the square to William's home. They found Tal seated at the piano with

William. Daphnia sat in one of the chairs beside the fireplace, knitting. "Where's Brek and the others?" Simon asked. "Upstairs," William answered as he turned. Seeing Karnak, he jumped from the stool and ran behind the piano, exclaiming, "What is that!" Tal tried to answer, but was laughing too hard, so Simon introduced William to Karnak. "Herr William, this is Karnak, a friend of mine and leader of the Council of Darkness." Daphnia glared at Tal and said, "Calm down, William. The lad would not 'ave brought him here if he was dangerous. Trees be fallin'! You're gonna be hurtin' yourself for sure!" William bowed slightly and, using the piano for support, moved forward to greet Karnak. "My apologies. I've never seen anything quite like you before. The sight startled me." "I find your reaction to my appearance a compliment, Herr William. Now, I will collect Brek and allow you to regain your composure." "He's upstairs," William said. "I can get him for you." "There is no need to be concerned for the other children up there. I am quite capable of climbing stairs, probably more so than you at this time. I will get him." Karnak did not wait for an answer. He climbed the steps with a speed that confirmed that he could navigate them quite efficiently. Simon ran after him, making considerably more noise. Karnak had no problem finding the children as they played with the LEGO farm. He entered the room just as Simon reached the second floor. "Brek, it is time to initiate you to the Council of Darkness. I hope you have learned what Lord Ky's children have been trying to teach you without losing your inborn evil nature. You will need that where we are going." Brek approached Karnak with wide eyes and a sharp toothed grin. "Brek ready to see Council of Darkness. Will Brek be going to inheritance ceremony?" "We will both be there," Karnak answered as he put his clawed hand on Brek's shoulder. "Lord Ky has something planned for you and it would be best for your health if you not disappoint him by not being there." The two vanished from the room. Simon took Brek's place at the LEGO farm. Tal joined them after his piano lesson was complete. They stayed in Micah's room until early evening, then with William and Daphnia in tow, went to the Cracked Anvil for dinner. The rest of

the group showed up shortly after they got there. Stories were exchanged about the day's events. "Oh!" William exclaimed as the children were preparing to return to the barracks. "I forgot to tell you, Micah." "What?" Micah asked. "You will be receiving your inheritance early this summer with Little Ky. The ceremony will be held at the farm," William said smiling. "Alright!" Micah yelled as he threw his arms around William. William's news delayed their departure from the Cracked Anvil. Stan saw fit to help them celebrate with extra pastries for dessert. The celebration lasted for close to an hour. Stan held William back after the children left. "Come to the bar," Stan said. "I have some instructions for you from my grandson." William sat at the bar and accepted the ale Stan offered him, then asked, "What need I do that Ky wishes done?" "Part of what he wants done, I can help you with. That is the list of guests you would like to have attend Micah's inheritance. The other thing you will need to do, is write a formal letter. Address it to the librarian, Alle-Stecan, and give the date that Micah will get his inheritance. I suggest you invite the little grouch as well." "I think I've met him. Archos brought him to the farm to copy Micah's 'thank you' note. He really is a bit of a grouch," William added laughing. Stan nodded, then said, "Yes, but he's important. So you'll just have to suffer his presence." "I don't understand why Micah is getting all this special attention," William said and sipped his ale before saying, "Maybe you could enlighten me." "I could, but that would ruin the surprise. All I'll say is that it is because he is friends with Little Ky, my grandson is making sure that a parting is unnecessary." "I guess I'll have to wait for the surprise," William said. "Thank you for such a fine evening. I'll see you again soon." "I'm sure of it!" Stan said as William headed home with Daphnia following.

37 Ky arrived in a well traveled corridor near the feast hall in Deep Stone. The dwarves that witnessed his arrival bowed low and quickly decided they needed to be somewhere else. Ky frowned at their backs and entered the feast hall. He found a dwarf seated at a table in the back of the room sipping an ale. "I'm looking for Lord Stumpy," Ky said, his quiet voice stirring the dwarf from his mug. The dwarf took a moment to focus on Ky, then belched and replied, "Ain't me, lad," as he returned to his mug. Ky crossed his arms and stared at the dwarf. "I can see that," he muttered. He glanced around the room and spotted a finger-bowl on the next table. At least this dwarf did not run at the sight of him, Ky thought as he retrieved the bowl and dumped it over the dwarf's head. The dwarf sputtered angrily as he fought to stand. "Why ye be drowning me?" he yelled. "I'm looking for Lord Stumpy," Ky answered quietly. "I tol' ye lad, it ain't me!" the dwarf yelled. "Lord Stumpy would not need me to give him a shower," Ky explained. "I need to know where he is." Brenson rushed into the hall hearing the drunken shouts of the drenched dwarf. He hurried to the table wondering how the dwarf still lived. "Lord Ky," Brenson greeted bowing. "Come, I will help you with whatever it is you need." Brenson cast a withering look at the grumbling dwarf that was by now returning to his mug.

"I'm looking for Lord Stumpy," Ky explained to Brenson as he followed him. "Lord Stumpy is working at the lava forge. I will take you there," Brenson said as he led Ky into the hallway. Ky followed Brenson deeper and deeper into Deep Stone. They traveled in silence, Ky not having anything to say and Brenson deciding it best not to speak for fear of insulting the elf. The first portion of the trip, they passed through corridors that were busy with the comings and goings of many dwarves. The dwarves bowed low until Brenson and Ky passed. The sounds of awed mutterings followed the two travelers as they progressed. After a while, they passed a hall where the sound of hammers and the heat of forges could be felt. "Isn't that the forges?" Ky asked. "Aye, Lord Ky, those are the forges, but they are not the lava forge. That forge is deep within the keep and is only used by the most skilled of smiths. Lord Stumpy was quite beside himself when he learned of it." Brenson led Ky through a locked door. Two guards waited on the inside. They bowed stiffly, not even attempting to hide their scowls at seeing Ky entering this section of the realm. Brenson ignored them and led Ky down a series of long, stone stairways. As they progressed, the guards became more and more disrespectful. They refused to bow, scowling with their hands straying to their weapons. The last corridor they walked through opened into a moderate sized room housed by four guards and a captain. "Ye've outdone yerself, Brenson. I hope yer not thinking of taking that elf into the lava forge," the captain jeered. "Dolen, this be Ky, Lord of Chaos. He is here to see Lord Stumpy. Unlock the door and let us in," Brenson ordered. "We'll not be opening that door for any more outsiders, Brenson." "I am Lord of Deep Stone, Dolen," Brenson stated, his blue eyes glaring piercingly at the captain. "I order ye to open the door and stand aside." "Methinks it be time for a new lord of Deep Stone," Dolen bellowed as he readied his axe. The other four guards followed Dolen's example and readied their weapons. Brenson readied his axe as the guards surrounded him. "I don't have time for this," Ky said. "Tell Stumpy I need to see him. I'll wait here." "Too late for that, Lord Ky," Brenson stated. "I'll have to deal with this treason first." Ky noticed the key ring hung on Dolen's belt and summoned it. Afterwards, the captain was incinerated, becoming little more than

a small pile of ashes in less than a second. Even his weapon was reduced to ash. "Is there anyone else who thinks Brenson incapable of leading Deep Stone?" Ky asked quietly as he handed the keys to Brenson. The four guards dropped their weapons and backed away. Brenson unlocked the great stone door that led to the lava forge and turned to address the guards. "I could have ye all killed for treason," Brenson growled, glaring at each of them. After a moment, he tossed the keys to the nearest guard. "Ye will be the new captain until I decide on what to do with the lot of ya. Your actions from this point on will determine if I need to replace ye all with a more respectful lot." Without another word, Brenson turned and entered the lava forge followed by Ky who made sure he left a footprint in Dolen's ashes. The heat beyond the door was intense. Molten rock poured into the room on one side and flowed along the far wall before exiting through a crevice on the other side. Beside the flow, five anvils had been set up. Three of these anvils were in use. Tables and weapon racks stood between the door and the anvils. Brenson led Ky to the first anvil where Stumpy stood examining what he had been working on. "Ye've company, My Lord," Brenson bellowed over the roar of the lava. Stumpy turned to greet them with a bow. His beard and mustached parted in a wide toothy smile when he saw Ky. "That saves me the trouble of finding ye, lad!" he exclaimed as he walked to meet them. "I've made ye a gift to thank ye for nae killing the lass." Stumpy held out the weapon, a double-edged longsword suitable for someone of Ky's stature. Ky accepted the sword and ran his fingers down the flat of the blade. "Thank you. I didn't know you could do this type of work, Stumpy." "Bah! Ain't a dwarf worth his beard that can't forge a weapon." A twinkle of pleasure filled Stumpy's eyes as he watched Ky test the weapon. Then he turned to Brenson and said, "Tis a mighty fine forge ye have here." "Thank ye, Lord Stumpy." Brenson frowned and turned to Ky. "Lord Ky, if ye don't mind delivering yer message. The sooner I get ye out of here, the less of a mess I'll have upon leaving." "I'm sure Lord Stumpy and I would be happy to help you with that mess," Ky answered. "I know I'd like a chance to try out his craftsmanship." Turning to Stumpy, he said, "The triplets will be through with Mena in the morning. I just wanted to let you know that

you can return her to her parents at that time." Stumpy frowned and muttered, "Actually, I'll be having to start her training then." "Nae, Lord Stumpy," Brenson said. "Return her to us and we will see to some training she missed. After she has learned those lessons, then ye may follow through on her other training if ye so desire." "If that be yer wish, Brenson, then I won't be arguing!" They walked to the door where Ky stopped them and said, "Have your weapons ready before you open the door." "Surely you don't think them fool enough to try anything with ye here," Brenson observed. "I usually don't leave the same way I come. They won't expect me to still be here," Ky explained. "The lad speaks true, Brenson. I've heard them talk of the," Stumpy paused and cleared his throat, then muttered, "rude way he takes his leave." Brenson scowled and nodded, readying his battle-axe before opening the door. Twenty dwarves greeted them on the other side of the door, weapons drawn and eyes glaring. At first, they saw only Brenson and Stumpy come through the door and started to surround their intended targets. Then Ky moved forward to stand at Brenson's side opposite Stumpy. "Three against about twenty," Ky whispered. "Hardly seems fair. Couldn't you round up any more than this?" "I guess ye'll take the coward's way and use yer cursed magic," one of the dwarves spit. Ky grinned and tilted his head slightly before saying, "I won't if you don't." The mutinous dwarves muttered curses at the three standing at the door, but none of them dared start the battle. Ky, who is was easily bored, decided that now was the best time to get things started and charged into the center of the group. Stumpy and Brenson followed, each taking an end and working towards Ky. In a few moments, only the dwarf that uttered the 'coward' remark remained alive. He knelt before Ky with his chin propped up by the sword Stumpy had just made. "Very nice craftsmanship, Stumpy. I just want to test one more thing..." Ky spun and swung the sword in a downward arc, slicing the victim in half from the top of his head to his groin. "Yep. I think I'll keep this one," Ky said as he vanished. Brenson laughed. He had begun to like the elf as much as he already respected him. Together with Stumpy, he returned to the feast hall and began replacing the guard contingent for the lava forge. He
also called for ale which he and Stumpy enjoyed as they shared tall tales for the rest of the day.

38 Mistress was as content as she was tired when she returned to her cabin after meeting with the dwarf. She marveled at how smoothly things progressed for her. Ghostspawn, with her prodding, was developing into the perfect tool. Mistress almost felt disappointment knowing the Lord of Chaos would surely kill the goblin for what she was doing. Mistress knew of elven twin-speak. She also knew that images could be acquired from one twin if the other could see what was happening around him or her. The twin she planned to use to make herself a goddess would see the goblin, not her. Ghostspawn needed to learn a few more things before he would be ready though. Planning would wait until morning. Mistress had used quite a bit of magic over the past few days and it was beginning to wear on her. Even with the elf's essence, she could feel that she had over taxed herself. She worried that the excitement of her goal being so close would make rest difficult as she settled onto her cot. Instead, sleep overcame her very quickly. The next day, Mistress relaxed with the intent to save her strength for when the Chaos child arrived. She would need to be fully rested by then to do what needed to be done quickly. There was the trip to Cragsguard that night to contend with as well. The flask could not be left behind, nor could she leave the gems in the possession of the dwarf. During the day, she made lists of what needed to be done when. The only time she left the cabin was when she went to the storehouse and checked on her two newest acquisitions. She made sure both were well fed before leaving them. It would only cause more

problems if her planned double were emaciated when it came time to transform him or her to replace the Chaos child. Several hours after sunset, she set up the portal to Cragsguard. Like the previous night, she arrived in the canyon below the main gate and cloaked herself in shadows before entering the town and walking to the barracks. Mistress quietly entered Mena's room and found the dwarf sleeping soundly. The flask sat on the windowsill, the sign that the dwarf had done her job. Mistress smiled down on the sleeping dwarf and applied the herb that would make sure she did not waken. Then she quietly packed Mena's possessions and placed them on the cot with the dwarf. She searched the room until she found where Mena had hidden the gems she had given her the night before. Mistress put those in her pocket with the flask and moved to the front room of Mena's quarters. There she found several swords resting on a table with sharpening stones and oil clothes. She chose one that appeared to be dwarven made, then returned to Mena's cot. Mistress stared at the dwarf a moment while deciding whether or not to have her leave a note. Finally, she decided she did not wish to waste the energy needed to control Mena. Mistress arranged Mena's belongings and the sword on top her body, then took hold of her hand and cast the portal spell to return to her cottage. Once there, she tied Mena's hands and feet securely, gagged her, and left her in the middle of the floor. Mistress knew she would go nowhere until morning. Stepping over Mena, Mistress murmured, "Good rest, my sweet. It will be your last." Then laughing quietly, she retired to her own cot. When Mistress awoke the next morning, she started her day by consuming one of the vials of elven essence Ghostspawn had harvested. She knew by the amount of intoxication it caused that she was nearly at full strength again. Still, she did not wish to be bothered with dealing with the dwarf that lay on the floor in her kitchen. She decided that she would use the dwarf to teach her apprentice a lesson in destroying evidence, not that he would ever get another chance to use it, she thought, smirking. She summoned the goblin as she entered the kitchen. Seeing Mena awake, Mistress smiled at her and asked, "Shouldn't you be wiping some elf's butt around this time of day?" Mistress laughed at the fear in Mena's eyes and the futile struggling the dwarf attempted against the binding straps that immobilized her. Mistress stepped around Mena and placed an iron poker in the fire before taking her seat at the table to wait for Ghostspawn.

Ghostspawn took one step into the cabin and froze, gawking at the dwarf that struggled in the middle of the floor. Mistress stifled another fit of laughing at the sight of him. "Sit down, my little apprentice," she ordered. "It's time to learn a valuable lesson." She waited until Ghostspawn sat across from her, then asked, "Have you wondered how it is that I am never disturbed here?" "No," Ghostspawn muttered. "Of course you haven't. You are not intelligent enough to think that far ahead. That is why you came to me to learn." She paused, staring at the goblin as if daring him to contradict her. When she continued, her voice was almost a whisper and Ghostspawn had to strain to hear her words. "No one disturbs me because I leave no evidence that can be traced back to me." She pointed at the dwarf on the floor. "She is evidence. To help you understand this lesson, you will be disposing of that evidence for me." Ghostspawn glanced at the dwarf then waited. He knew that Mistress would tell him how she wished him to complete this task whether he asked or not. He also learned that if he did not ask, her instructions would be given without the usual insult. His silence was rewarded as Mistress detailed his instructions. "I understand that this dwarf has a knack for being very loud. Though it pains me, I will make sure she is quiet to make things a little easier for you. Afterwards, you are to take her into the woods, chop her up into very small pieces and scatter them apart as far as possible. Whether you choose to kill her before you start cutting her up, or let her suffer as you cut her up is entirely up to you. This task should take you most of the day. I will be watching your progress. If I am satisfied with your efforts, I will reward you with more essence. Be sure to bring back her clothing so that it can be burned." Mistress removed the poker from the fire and stabbed it through the gag in Mena's mouth. She kept it there, turning it to make sure that the dwarf's tongue was thoroughly burned away. "I find the smell of burnt dwarf distressing," she said as she handed the goblin a serrated knife. "Enjoy your day in the forest." Mistress held the hide that covered the door aside as the goblin dragged the dwarf from the cabin. She watched long enough for them to reach the edge of the forest. She smiled as she watched the goblin cut one of the dwarf's fingertips away. He had decided to let her live as he carried out his chore. Mistress sighed knowing the goblin would be a useful ally if he were not needed as a necessary scapegoat. When they were out of sight, Mistress returned to the

kitchen and began burning Mena's possessions. She decided to keep the sword and stashed it behind one of the shelves that hid a small alcove. She spent the rest of the day following the goblin's progress. She was unsure of whether her apprentice truly enjoyed this task, or whether he wanted to make sure he received essence on his return. She was sure that he excelled far beyond her expectations. She followed his progress until he was nearly done, then tended to the wild-elves in the stockroom, returning to the cabin before the goblin completed his task.

39 Sage Tas'lin slowly walked through the palace halls, leaning slightly upon his gnarled willow staff, intent on speaking with King Stel-Tasan about the upcoming inheritance ceremony for Lord Ky's triplets. He knew the King kept a regular schedule and hoped that he would not change his lunch habit today. If the King's schedule had not changed, Sage Tas'lin would find him just starting his lunch. Sage Tas'lin approached the King's private dining hall and found two guards on either side of the door. He knew the guards would not be there if the King was not inside and quickened his pace slightly. The guard closest to the door, opened it as Sage Tas'lin drew near and closed it behind him once he was in the hall. King Stel-Tasan looked up from his meal and frowned. "Must we discuss this now, Tas'lin?" Sage Tas'lin set his jaw and scowled as he pulled a chair to the opposite side of the table. Leaning his staff against the table he seated himself. "As a matter of fact, yes," Tas'lin stated firmly. "The law needs to be put into effect as soon as possible. You are delaying the matter. The longer you delay, the greater the chance that Lord Ky's triplets will have a very disruptive inheritance. I doubt you wish to incur the wrath of the Lord of Chaos." King Stel-Tasan sighed, pushed his plate aside and slumped against the back of his chair. Sage Tas'lin waited. He had spoken to the King many times during the past few weeks. There was nothing more for him to say. "I wish you could have waited until I finished my meal,"

Stel-Tasan grumbled wishing the old elf would smile, leave and return later. The scowl he received for his comment told him that Sage Tas'lin was going nowhere until the problem was resolved. "Bah!" Stel-Tasan growled. "Guard, send for Prince Stel-Ky. While we wait for him, I intend to enjoy my meal. There's plenty here if you wish to join me. It would be much better than you sitting there scowling at me like some sort of vulture." Sage Tas'lin obliged the King by nibbling on a salad and drinking water from a flask he brought with him. It took close to twenty minutes for the guards to locate Prince Stel-Ky as the King knew it would. The Prince had no real duties unless Lord Ky was in the city and spent much of his time wandering the countryside, practicing his archery, or studying the lore of magic. By the time the Prince arrived, the King had finished his meal. Prince Stel-Ky entered the room, walked towards the table, stopping at a respectable distance and bowed. "Sit down, Stel-Ky. We will be here a while," the King said, indicating an empty chair beside his own. Stel-Tasan waited until the Prince was seated then continued, "Sage Tas'lin seems to think that there will be trouble at the triplet's inheritance ceremony. Personally, I don't see how that could be considering all Lord Ky has done for this city. The evidence is still quite visible outside our gates." "My apologies, My Lord. It is probably my fault Sage Tas'lin is here now. This morning I reported to him about some rumors I had heard." "What rumors have you heard, Prince Stel-Ky?" "Allow me," Sage Tas'lin interjected. "Firstly, the triplets have been denied their inheritance. Regardless of Lord Ky's reasons, many feel that the denial should stand. Secondly, the onus of the youngest triplet is reappearing like a festering sore. Thirdly, is the rumors of an assassination attempt..." "What?" King Stel-Tasan roared and he jumped to his feet, knocking his chair backwards. "Someone actually thinks they can assassinate Lord Ky or his children!" "No, My Lord," Prince Stel-Ky explained. "They believe they can assassinate you for allowing this to happen. Your family is also targeted." King Stel-Tasan sighed and began pacing beside the table. "How long have these rumors been circulating?" "This morning was the first I've heard them, My Lord," Prince Stel-Ky explained. "I'd have reported them sooner had I heard them sooner." Stel-Tasan paced for several moments, a deep frown etched upon his usually cheerful visage. He stopped pacing behind Prince

Stel-Ky and placed his hand on the younger elf's shoulders. "I would guess that you are also a target," Stel-Tasan said quietly. "Aye, My Lord. I've heard that as well," Stel-Ky answered. Stel-Tasan righted his chair and sat. "First, we must notify Lord Ky." From Sage Tas'lin's nod, the King knew that the old scholar had already seen to that. Stel-Tasan acknowledged Sage Tas'lin's nod and continued. "Next we need to see about the security of the city. Prince Stel-Ky, you have a reputation as a trouble-maker and always have had that reputation. You are assigned to find the younger, more liberal guards. These will provide the security at the ceremony as well as along the route to the ceremony. I will assign the others to places that will keep them busy, useful, and out of harms way." He turned to Sage Tas'lin and asked, "What do you suggest concerning the law about triplets and twins?" "The sooner you put the law on the books, the more likely the problems will occur before the inheritance ceremony. If you wait until the day of the ceremony, as I know you had planned to do, I believe you put the entire city in jeopardy of Lord Ky's revenge. I know Lord Ky. I spent many years teaching him before he became the Lord of Chaos. Even then, he would have been a threat worthy of concern. Now, with the powers he recently acquired with his own inheritance, he could possibly reduce Alle-Stecan to rubble in a matter of seconds. "I also suggest you secure your family and yourself within the palace and that Lord Ky's dragon be released as a palace guard." King Stel-Tasan glanced at Prince Stel-Ky before asking, "Do you think that is really necessary?" "The Prince and I discussed it this morning. We even spoke with the dragon. If I did not think it necessary, I would not have suggested it." Stel-Tasan shook his head as he looked across the table at the old elf. "My guess is that you've already written the law so that no frailties could be exercised to escape it." Sage-Tas'lin simply nodded. "Very well. I will read over what you have written. If I find nothing I disagree with, it will be on the books this afternoon." The King slouched back in his chair and drummed his fingers on the table. "I find it hard to understand how such a law would cause so much trouble." "It is a change in our way of life. We, as a race, have never accepted change readily," Sage Tas'lin explained. "The same could be said for dwarves and humans I suppose. Though the humans seem to be the best at accepting change."

"Regretfully, I believe you must also be confined to the palace grounds," the King added. "I will see to my family while you acquire what you have written. We will meet in the throne room. Prince Stel-Ky, see to your task immediately and do it quietly. As soon as you are done, report to me with a list of the guards you have chosen. Recruit some of your friends if you need to, but make sure the area is secure with trusted companions." "Yes, My Lord. I will begin at once," Stel-Ky said as he stood and bowed. "I will summon Lord Ky's dragon as soon as I leave the palace. She already knows what she needs to do." Sage Tas'lin left the hall without further comment leaving the King to see to his family. Stel-Tasan sat for quite some time, his fingers absently drumming on the table. He knew that sometime in the future, this law, the law that required twins and triplets, regardless of birth order, be allowed inheritance and acceptance into society, would be considered a great breakthrough. The King also hoped that he would live long enough to see that time. He wondered if young Aemir even knew that he had inspired the law with his mischief in Cragsguard.
