Their voices rang through the forest as they sang, told stories and laughed through the first day of the journey. About an hour before sunset, they arrived in a meadow where Ky told them to set up camp. Ky, Tal, and Aemir tended the ponies as the rest of the group set up their tents and prepared dinner. Progress was slowed by stiff muscles caused by the non-stop ride through the day, but before the sun set, all were sitting around the fire enjoying their meal. As they ate, Ky considered which would be the first to find out the nature of the trip. He was unsure how Micah and Aemir would be affected by his plan and decided to experiment on Aemir, who, being an elf, would have the most stamina. For the first, though, he chose Eleana. He told the others that the meadow was safe and that he would be back shortly. He took Eleana's hand and the two of them disappeared. Eleana froze, her breath refusing to enter her throat, as she gazed upon The Garden for the first time. Her grip on Ky's hand threatened to crush the life from it. "You can breathe," Ky whispered as he fought to take possession of his hand. "There is air here." "It's so beautiful," Eleana gasped. "My hand," Ky whispered. "Sorry," Eleana said as she released Ky's hand and blushed. She remained where she stood slowly taking in everything around her. After a moment of letting her eyes peruse The Garden, she noticed The Lady coming towards them. Ky's gaze had wandered to

the stream. He stared at it wondering how many trips he would manage before he had to come alone and immerse himself again. Eleana's gasp brought him back from his reverie. He turned and saw The Lady as well. "That is your grandmother. Get to know her. I'll be back for you later." With that he vanished, leaving Eleana and The Lady to introduce themselves. Eleana could do nothing but stare as The Lady gracefully approached her. Her smile was warm and her sparkling green eyes were full of pleasure. When she came within reach of Eleana, her delicate fingertips strayed through the child's hair to her shoulder. Then she guided Eleana to the tree beside the stream and pulled her onto her lap. Eleana surrendered to The Lady's caress with the hope that it would never end. When she believed that nothing could make the moment more perfect, The Lady began to hum softly which caused the young elven lass to sigh, tears of happiness leaving wet trails across her cheeks. She was unsure of how much time had passed before The Lady spoke, but she felt it was not enough. "Welcome to The Garden, Eleana," The Lady said, the smile in her soft voice. "After your inheritance, you will be able to come here to visit whenever you wish. This visit is to prepare you for the gift your father intends to give you." She paused a moment, holding the child close. Then she said, "But first, I think you would like to walk with me and see more of The Garden." "Please," was all Eleana could say. "Before we begin, I wish you to know that time is not a welcome visitor here. You may stay as long as you wish. Your father will arrive when you are ready to leave regardless of how quickly he decides to return for you. Come, let us enjoy The Garden together." The Lady gently set Eleana on her feet and rose. Hand in hand, they strolled along the path, which to Eleana, never seemed to end. Each turn brought something new and beautiful. Whether it be a flower the child had never seen before or the way a tree swayed, Eleana found joy and peace everywhere they walked. The tour of The Garden lasted hours with neither The Lady nor Eleana suffering fatigue. The Garden seemed to sense when Eleana was ready for the purpose of the visit and the path they followed led them back to the stream. When they arrived, The Lady helped Eleana out of her clothing. "What your father intends," she explained as she helped Eleana undress, "requires that you be cleansed in a way that only this stream can cleanse you." She guided Eleana into the swirling water then returned to sit beside the tree.

Eleana was shocked by the feel of the water rushing over her feet. The water was cool, but not too cold and she could not escape the feeling that it was caressing her rather than just flowing past her. The Lady pointed to an area that had widened and deepened and Eleana waded towards it and slowly sat down. The Lady sang for Eleana as the waters took Eleana into its possession, flowing around and through the young elf. When the waters started to recede, Eleana sighed with disappointment. The Lady smiled and held a towel for her, saying, "Soon you will be able to come here and enjoy the pleasures of The Garden whenever you wish. Come child, let me dry and hold you a while longer before your father returns." Eleana did as The Lady requested. Moments after she sat within The Lady's arms, she drifted off to a renewing sleep dreaming of flowers and trees and birds singing sweetly as they fluttered about The Garden.

He placed his hand on Brek's shoulder and they vanished.

45 Ky crept into the tent shared by Little Ky, Micah and Aemir. He paused, watching the three sleep a few moments before committing himself to the task. Ky knew that Simon had taken the council to The Garden inadvertently and they had returned without problem. The council consisted of gods and goddesses. Aemir was not a god, yet, so Ky hesitated, unsure whether he should take the risk or not. Finally, he trusted The Lady to fix anything that might go wrong and he took hold of Aemir's hand. When they arrived, Ky checked to see if Aemir survived the journey, then released him from the sleep spell. As Aemir stirred, Ky returned to the camp knowing The Lady was approaching. Aemir awoke, his eyes fluttering as the sleep left him. When he realized he was no longer in the tent, he sat up and looked around, his eyes wide and his chin hanging slackly. When he saw The Lady coming towards him, he scrambled to his feet and backed up, almost falling into the stream. The Lady smiled and welcomed him. "Welcome to The Garden, Aemir. I'm so glad Ky chose to bring you here. Come sit with me and tell me about yourself." Aemir watched The Lady move to the tree that shaded the small stream as he tried to determine if he were dreaming or not. When The Lady was settled she smiled again and beckoned the young elf to her. "You are safe here. Please, come and sit with me." Aemir was unsure what to think, but he could sense nothing dangerous. He walked to The Lady and allowed her to guide him onto

her lap. She held him a few moments, humming quietly until she felt him relax. "Tell me all about you," she whispered. Aemir quietly began telling his life story to The Lady as if he desired nothing more in life than this moment in The Lady's arms. At each pause in the story, The Lady either commented on what Aemir had just told her or encouraged him to continue. Everything Aemir ever felt, believed and lived poured out from his soul. When his story ended, he felt more at peace than he thought he ever could. A slight smile pushed the corners of his mouth upwards as he rested his head on The Lady's shoulders and listened to her softly hum to him. "Ky has made a fine choice in you," The Lady explained. "There is a place among The Nine for you. Before you can take that place, you must be cleansed. Please, leave your clothing on the path and immerse yourself in the stream." Aemir did as he was bidden. He found the waters cool, but comforting. As he rested in the center of the pool, the waters playing gently under his chin, he wished he could remain there forever. The Lady sang softly, using words the young elf could not comprehend, yet he somehow felt the meaning of his existence hid somewhere within the melody. When The Lady held the towel for him, he left the stream satisfied, knowing he would be able to return at some later date. The Lady gently dried Aemir and helped him into his clothing, then held him as he fell into a peaceful sleep. When Ky returned for him, The Lady whispered in his ear as she had done with Eleana, then placed the sleeping elf in Ky's arms. "He will make a wonderful addition to The Nine," she said to Ky. "I look forward to seeing you soon." Ky faded from the path as The Lady returned to the center of The Garden.

46 Ghostspawn flinched again as he sat practicing the runes he had just learned from Mistress. She paced the room like a vengeful and trapped dragon waiting to strike the first unlucky victim that came into range. Her screeching curses burst through the otherwise silent room at random intervals causing the goblin to lose what concentration he had managed to muster during the quiet times. This last outburst came while Ghostspawn was trying to produce the most complicated rune he had learned. The small bone he was using to scribe the rune snapped which resulted in Mistress turning her foul mood on the goblin. The little patience Ghostspawn possessed had been frazzled into non-existence by then. The transformation of his body by The Grove had been complete for almost a week and with it, his fear of the albino woman teaching him magic had withered away to almost nothing. Weeks of pent up frustration burst forth from the goblin as he met Mistress in the middle of the room. They stood inches apart screaming at each other. The intensity of the vocal foray caused even the furnishings to cringe into corners. The verbal fight lasted only a few minutes before Ghostspawn shoved Mistress against the door frame that led to The Grove and stormed from the cabin shouting goblin curses over his shoulder. Mistress barely restrained herself from using magic against her apprentice. She had enough problems with the wild-elves and did not wish to have to find a new scapegoat as well. The argument brought the realization that she would have to treat the goblin as more of an equal. When he shoved her, she felt the power behind his

immortality. She knew she could not let him discover a way to channel that power against her. "Get back where you belong," Mistress commanded. She waited until the furniture had returned to its proper places then hurried to the stockroom. The wild-elves had begun to visibly wilt the night before. They were dying and Mistress could not figure out why. She stopped in the harvesting room to collect herself and take the herb that would keep the incense from affecting her. After a few moments, she felt calm enough to investigate why the wild-elves were not cooperating by staying alive and healthy. Mistress found the girl unconscious, sprawled on the floor of her cage like an uprooted weed waiting to decay to so much fertilizer. The boy was not in much better condition, but he was conscious. Mistress stood outside his cage glaring at him. She concluded that in a day or two, she would need to replace them. Her experience told her that abducting wild-elves now would be near impossible. It would be months before the wild-elves lowered their guard enough for her to even appear in their forests. "What is wrong with you?" she muttered more to herself than to the elf in the cage. "Dying," came the raspy reply. Mistress did not expect the answer so she stood staring at the elf again while she thought. Maybe he could tell her why they were dying, though she had little hope in that solution. It seemed to be too easy. Finally, she asked, "Why?" "Need sunlight and vines," the elf said, his voice resembling a dying man's last words. Mistress considered his answer, leaving the storehouse for a few moments so that the incense did not stifle her thoughts. Pacing, she wondered if this was the elf's way of trying to escape. She knew that wild-elves were crafty, yet she also knew that they were symbiotic with nature. Finally, she decided that they were useless to her dead and returned to the storehouse. "You," she ordered, speaking to the cage that held the girl, "restrain your captive and follow me.” “You," turning to the cage with the boy, "do the same." Mistress led the two cages to the fringes of the forest behind her house. There she ordered the cages to keep them bound by their wrists and ankles. Mistress knew the effects of the incense would last for months in the harvesting room. In the open air, she doubted it would last a week. As she worked on preparing incense for the two captives, she kept the reward she hoped to gain from these two elves in the forefront of her thoughts. Never before had she put so much

effort into keeping her captives healthy. She placed the two bowls and incense on the table and began gathering the other items she would need. The high-elf that she had used to train Ghostspawn had generously donated quite a few useful items to her. She gathered his skeletal hands and several of his leg tendons, placed them on the table with the incense, then searched the room trying to determine if anything else would be needed. Ghostspawn had watched as Mistress led the two cages and their contents to the edge of the forest. He knew about these captives and also knew they were the cause of Mistress's foul mood. He stepped from his cabin and sat with his back against the door to watch. A few moments later, Mistress emerged from the storehouse with a tray which she carried behind the cages. Muttering in frustration that he could not see what she was doing, he decided to get a closer look. Mistress caught sight of the goblin in her peripheral vision and purposely walked to the back of the cages where he could not see her. If she wanted to get anything else accomplished, she would need the goblin's assistance with keeping these elves alive and docile. She hoped his curiosity would bring him closer as she began to braid the elves' hair into the back of the cage so their heads would remain upright. Moments later, she saw the goblin approaching. Mistress continued to work. After their heads were stabilized, she used the tendons and hands to make holders for the incense. These she positioned just under the elves' chins insuring there would be little chance of them receiving too much fresh air. When she was finished, she walked to the front of the cages. Ghostspawn was already there, but she ignored him. "There," she said to the boy, "You will now have your sunlight." "Need vines," the boy whispered. "If I allowed you to have vines, you would use them to try to escape. No vines," Mistress said as she waved her hand to dismiss the request. The boy took several shallow, rasping breaths, then said, "Vines feed us." Mistress glared at the elf and wondered if she could accomplish making a high-elf look like one of the Lord of Chaos' children. Ghostspawn had thousands of years of experience torturing things. He stepped forward and examined the cages. He remembered having dangerous captives confined with the exception of their arms, legs or heads so that he could safely torture them. "If you can command the cages to have their feet stick out, we can let the vines grow around their feet and keep the vines

trimmed without much problem," Ghostspawn suggested. Mistress wondered how many surprises she would receive in one day as she considered the goblin's recommendation. She decided to give it a try after seeing the dull, unintelligent looking amber eyes of the elf. "We will need to keep a close watch on them," Mistress said, "so they don't have a chance to use the vines to get away. They are too important to our plans to lose." She ordered the cages to allow the feet and calves of the elves to stick out then asked the boy, "Will any type of vine work?" "Yes." Mistress grinned, and said, "I have the perfect vine in my cabin. I'm sure you will be pleased." Ghostspawn waited at the cages while Mistress retrieved the vine. She chose a poison sumac vine, reasoning that the elves would not wish to have it encompass their entire bodies. Besides, she thought, after all this work they caused her to do, they needed to suffer a bit. When she returned, she planted one vine between the heels of each elf, using their feet to support the upper branches. "You need to continue practicing your runes," Mistress stated when she had finished. "Praying that the Lord of Chaos sends us a male child will help me forget the bone you broke earlier." Ghostspawn followed her back to the cabin. He found scribing the runes a much easier task without Mistress's outbursts and he progressed well over the next hour. The two of them checked on the wild-elves at that time. Although their feet had acquired a nasty rash from the sumac, both elves looked much healthier. By evening, Mistress and Ghostspawn had fallen into a routine for caring for the two elves. Ghostspawn would tend to the hourly checks during the day as he had less adversity to sunlight than Mistress. She, in turn, would tend to them during the nighttime hours. That problem having been solved, at least for now, Mistress chose a human from her stock and had Ghostspawn continue to practice essence harvesting. He would now harvest the essence alone and bring it to Mistress for approval. By the end of the day, Mistress once again felt that her plans were moving along smoothly.

47 Karnak waited in the shade of two large boulders as Stumpy searched the canyon for any signs of surviving goblin tunnels. Although the thantor god could move about in sunlight, he preferred not to, doing so only when necessary. While waiting for Stumpy, Karnak noticed Erishen entering Cragsguard under a cloak of illusion. He would ask her about it later. Of all his council, she would be the last to do something that would upset him. Stumpy returned to him a few moments later, reporting, "There be one room, rather large, that survived the cave-in. I will open a tunnel to it farther up the canyon." "I'll wait here until you've opened the tunnel far enough to be out of the sun's direct light," Karnak said. "I will catch up with you then." While he waited, the alarm sounded in Cragsguard. Karnak searched for signs of Erishen. She was either on the far end of town, or gone. It was difficult for him to tell with all the noise of the guards distracting his senses. By the time Stumpy had cleared twenty feet into the tunnel, the guards had doubled on the wall and the portcullis had been lowered. Karnak's curiosity about what had happened in the town had to wait. He moved through the canyon and into the tunnel unseen by the guards above him. Stumpy had progressed thirty feet when Karnak arrived. "Is this one of the original tunnels, or are you creating a new tunnel?" Karnak asked. "Original, lad. I be thinkin' there be a lack of dead goblins,"

Stumpy muttered. "There is death down here," Karnak stated. "I can smell the decay." They moved onward, following the tunnel that led directly to the intact chamber Stumpy had found. The dwarf took his time, enjoying the effort of clearing the tunnel with his mastery of earth- magic almost as much as he had enjoyed rebuilding the wall at Cragsguard. "Almost there," he muttered. A few feet more and Stumpy gagged on the stench of the wall of dead goblins that clogged the passage in front of him. Muttering into his beard, he backed away as Karnak moved forward to investigate. Death was what Karnak did best and the manner in which these goblins had died intrigued him. He found no goblins that were killed by the cave-in. All of them appeared to have had their throats ripped out by the teeth of a goblin. "Interesting," Karnak hissed. "Stumpy, can you make a tunnel around this blockage? I may wish to investigate these more carefully at a later time." "Aye, lad. I just hope the chamber be not as clogged as this passage." Karnak nodded agreement and followed as Stumpy opened a smaller passage. Moments later they stood in the throne room. Stumpy produced a glow-stone. His vision underground was excellent, but he did not wish to accidentally step on anything repulsive. He stood and watched as Karnak searched the chamber. Opening tunnels was his specialty. This part of the chore was best left to the thantor. Karnak moved among the dead goblins that littered the chamber. He examined each corpse carefully. He found the corpse of a pregnant goblin and noted that the fetus had been ripped from the womb before the mother was killed. He softly growled thinking that even a thantor would not be this ruthless. When he found the rune near the throne, he called for Stumpy. "Can you read goblin runes?" Karnak asked. "A couple," Stumpy answered. "This is two runes," Karnak explained pointing at the wall. "The first one is very old and has been defiled by this second one that was written in that goblin's blood,” Karnak said indicating the goblin rotting at the base of the wall. “The newer one translates as 'born from' or 'child of' or 'spawn'. Unfortunately, it covers the older one to the point that I cannot read it." Karnak thought for a moment, considering the rune on the wall. Then, he turned to Stumpy and asked, "Would you mind searching the older tunnels for another instance of this rune? I do not

know if another exists, but it would get you out of here while I continue to examine the dead." "Aye!" Stumpy answered. "I'll be right on it." Stumpy returned to the tunnel he opened and walked back to a crossing tunnel he noticed earlier. The stone told him that the northern branch of the tunnel led to the oldest areas of the goblin caves. As Stumpy searched the older caves, Karnak continued his examination of the throne room and the passages clogged with corpses. He could feel traces of Rachk'sha's magic in the chamber, but there were no traces of magic on the corpses. Someone else had killed these goblins and Karnak began to wonder where that someone else was. Karnak found a half-eaten goblin and a small mound of dirt covering the goblins in the partially cleared passage. He wondered if the killer had triggered a cave-in and died underneath it. He would wait for Stumpy to determine that. What he did not find, was any way out of this chamber except for the tunnel Stumpy had made earlier. As he stood considering the mound of dirt, he heard Stumpy call him. Moments later, he stood before the old rune Stumpy had located. "Ghost," Karnak hissed. "That be what these goblins called Ky," Stumpy said. Karnak muttered a phrase of magic and traced the rune. Then he repeated the phrase and searched the ground in front of the rune. "Interesting," he muttered. "Care to share yer find, lad?" Stumpy asked. "Open your senses to magic, trace the rune and then search the floor, there," Karnak instructed. Stumpy did as Karnak requested and muttered a few curses into his beard as he traced the rune. He then searched the floor frowning as he stood. Even though the magic he found caused him pain, he repeated the process, needing to know if his initial findings were correct. He pointed to the rune, saying, "That is Ky's magic. Not pleasant at all," he muttered. "That," he added pointing to the floor, "could be Ky's magic, but it's been altered." "Step aside a moment," Karnak ordered. When Stumpy had moved, Karnak uttered the phrase of magic again and searched the floor where Stumpy stood when he traced the rune. The traces of Ky's magic were there, but very weak and fading. "My guess," Karnak explained, "is that tracing the rune, though uncomfortable, causes you to absorb some of Ky's magic. Whoever stood here and traced the rune earlier, did so many times.

The remnants left by you tracing the rune twice are already fading." "That nae be good," Stumpy muttered. "I have two more things to do before we go,” Karnak said, turning towards the throne room. “I want to check the floor near the rune in the open chamber, and I need you to check a small cave-in for me." Stumpy followed Karnak to the chamber of dead goblins. Karnak searched the floor under the rune and found nothing. He tossed the remains of the corpse used to make the new rune into the corner and searched again. Stumpy leaned forward to watch Karnak's progress, placing his hand on the seat of the throne as he did so. "Damned elf!" Stumpy yelled as he shook the pain from his hand. "Where?" Karnak asked. Stumpy nodded to the throne, muttering curses. Karnak felt the magic before his claws were a foot from the seat of the throne. He added a long guttural hiss to Stumpy's mutterings. Karnak doubted that he would find the body of this creature under the cave-in now. "I doubt my first guess is correct," Karnak said to Stumpy, "but I want to check anyway. It may provide a clue as to where this creature is." Stumpy followed Karnak into the partially cleared passage. Karnak pointed to the cave-in and said, "If you can clear that for me, I'd like to see what it covers." Stumpy began clearing the cave-in, then stopped. "What ye be lookin' for is not under the cave-in. A small tunnel's been dug that leads to the surface," Stumpy explained, pointing to the ceiling. "We will have to go up that tunnel then, unless you can find it from outside." "Findin' it outside will be easier than goin' through it," Stumpy said. "Good. I'll ask you to seal this when we leave. I may need to come back with Archos or Erishen and I don't want it disturbed," Karnak said as he led the way through the tunnel Stumpy had cleared, returning to the canyon. Stumpy sealed the entrance to the tunnel and led Karnak to the fringes of the forest on the opposite side of the canyon from Cragsguard. It only took Stumpy a couple minutes to find the exit of the small tunnel. Karnak searched for tracks to try to determine where the creature went. All he found was a few traces near the exit that told him the creature was a goblin. Beyond that, the trail was too old to follow. "I think we've found all we can at this time," Karnak hissed. "Aye, and I'll be needing an ale after being in that hole of

dead goblins for so long." They ported to the farm and waited for the others to return. Erishen was already there and once she explained what she had done in Cragsguard to Karnak, he nodded in approval. Erishen's cheeks flushed to a darker shade of green at Karnak's praise.

48 Ky woke the group early, and allowed them to eat a quick breakfast before breaking camp. He was enjoying being with them, which surprised him somewhat. He had expected them to pester him with questions, act noisily and obnoxiously, or just be a chore to be around. Instead, they entertained themselves, were rather quiet most of the time and they seemed to be enjoying the trip. The first part of the trip, they tried, with no success, to find out where Eleana had been taken the night before. Eleana could not even remember being taken anywhere. This ended when Little Ky asked Micah to sing. The rest of the morning and well into the afternoon, they took turns singing songs for each other and enjoying the countryside. Simon pulled away from the others to ride beside Ky. "You don't want them to know what's happening," he whispered. "I want it to be a special surprise for all of them," Ky whispered back. Simon grinned and decided riding beside Ky for a while would be a good thing. He had spent very little time with his brother and wished to know him better. They did not speak much, but Simon expected this. Ky was well known for not saying much. As late afternoon approached, Ky was about to slow the group enough so they could get snacks when the scenery around them flickered. Ky abruptly turned on the group, glanced at each of the triplets and cast a spell in Tal's direction. Ky caught his unconscious son before he slid off his saddle, and dragged him onto his own horse. "Eleana, take the reins of his horse," Ky ordered.

"What happened?" Simon asked. "Ride!" Ky commanded. Simon had once been the target of a command word when Karnak used one to make him hide in The Garden. The power of Karnak's word seemed tame compared to what his brother just did. The word touched everyone in the group and they galloped after Ky as if a horde of dragons were breathing down their necks. They continued their breakneck charge until well after sunset. Ky stopped them in a small grove of pine trees and immediately called Ky II and Eleana to him. "Shouldn't I see to Tal?" Eleana asked. Ky nodded, "And the horses. This must be done first." Ky taught Ky II and Eleana how to dispel their familiars, then ported them away from the camp to cast the spells. He checked to make sure both dragon familiars that were at the farm were gone before returning to camp. As Eleana and Ky II saw to the needs of Tal and the horses, Ky worked with the others to set up camp, reassuring them that the problem would not occur again. Dinner was quiet but most of the group had settled down. Ky did not offer any explanation as to what happened and no one felt brave enough to ask. Micah barely ate, spending most of the meal staring wide-eyed at Ky and trembling. Ky noticed his fear and knew that the command word was the cause. He was surprised Aemir was not behaving in the same way, but Aemir had already been to The Garden and Ky thought that visit is what strengthened the high-elf enough not to be terrified. After the meal, Ky took Micah aside and sat with him, asking him about his life in Austria and some of the things he and Little Ky did together. Micah began to relax after a while and Ky was able to convince him to sing a Mozart song for him. At the end of Micah's song, Ky smiled. "I think you need to eat a little more," Ky whispered. "We've still got a long ride ahead of us and you'll need your strength." Micah returned Ky's smile and followed him back to the fire where he realized how hungry he was. Ky gave the group an hour to relax before sending them to their tents and putting them to sleep. Simon remained at the fire with Ky. "Who goes tonight?" Simon asked. Ky glanced at the tents, then said, "Ky II." Simon watched as Ky entered Ky II's tent, then waited. Ky appeared beside him a couple minutes later. They sat silently, watching the fire a while. Then Simon asked, "What happened today?" "Someone used Tal's familiar to find us," Ky answered.

"Why would that be a problem?" Simon asked. Ky sat quietly, gathering his thoughts, then answered, "If I were traveling alone, the route we are taking would be dangerous, but I'd make it. Since I have all of you coming with me, I created a passage, a safe trail, through the wilderness. If someone successfully searches for us, the passage fails. I had to destroy Tal's familiar." "That's what happened to him," Simon whispered. Ky nodded, then said, "Whoever made me do that paid a rather painful price. Go to sleep, now." "What? No command word?" Simon asked, grinning. "Do you really want one?" Ky asked, returning the grin. "I'm going!" Simon said as he hurried to his tent.

49 Ky II recognized The Garden as soon as he arrived. His surprise came when he turned to Ky to find him already gone. He had little time to wonder about that because The Lady was already approaching. "It is wonderful to see you again, Ky II. Please, sit with me a while." Ky II had known The Lady from his visits with Simon and happily joined her when she sat beside the tree near the stream. The Lady asked him about the training and how the trip was going. He told her everything, one episode barely completed before the next started. As with the others, The Lady invited him to bathe in the stream, telling him it would be an experience he would fondly remember as long as he lived. Ky II wasted no time leaving his clothing on the bank and getting into the water. He did not stop and marvel at the feeling the stream created as it flowed around his feet. He splashed his way to the center of the pool and dived in head first. The Lady did not sing to him, instead she laughed as she watched the young elf playing and splashing in the stream. When she knew it was time, she held the towel for him, helped him dry himself and dress than sang a lullaby as he sat cradled in her arms. Each of the children Ky brought was special and provided The Lady great joy. Ky II was the first to make her feel like a little girl and she treasured his visit greatly. The only thing that kept her from being truly disappointed when Ky returned for Ky II, was that he brought Tal with him.

The Lady whispered in Ky II's ear before handing him to Ky. When Ky left, she greeted Tal. "Welcome to The Garden, Tal. I hope you enjoy your visit as much as I enjoy having you here." Tal smiled and bowed slightly, then let his gaze search through The Garden that surrounded him. "Perhaps you would like to see more of The Garden?" The Lady asked. "Please," Tal murmured. The Lady took his hand and walked with him along the path, stopping when Tal wanted a closer look at something. They talked about Tal and his life. The Lady found him to be very mature, but his maturity was tainted with a hint of sadness. Though the young elf did not say so directly, The Lady could tell that he spent most of his life making sure his brother and sister were happy, even at the expense of his own happiness. She felt drawn to Tal in a way she had not been with the other children. Towards the end of the walk, The Lady did most of the talking as she told Tal about the different flowers and trees that they passed. Tal showed his interest by asking questions and making The Lady stop until his quest for knowledge was satiated. When they arrived back at the stream, The Lady told him about it and the cleansing it would give him. "When the stream is finished with you, you will feel a peacefulness that you have never experienced before," she explained as she helped him out of his clothing. "As you bathe, I will sing for you if you'd like." "I would love to hear you sing," Tal said, grinning. Tal stepped into the stream as The Lady walked to the tree, humming quietly. Tal did not expect the pain he felt and glanced at her before moving farther in. He guessed the pain would go when the cleansing started. By the time he reached the center of the pool, he was shivering uncontrollably and in so much pain, tears streamed from his eyes. The Lady turned and started singing as he fell to his knees in the middle of the pool. The shock of seeing the reddish taint to the waters that flowed past Tal and the pained expression on the young elf's face made the song catch in The Lady's throat, almost choking her. She summoned him from the stream, half expecting to see his skin removed. With a kiss on his forehead, she put Tal to sleep, carefully dried and dressed him, then left him on the bank where Ky would find him. Lastly, she removed all memory of the stream from his mind. Then she ran through The Garden to the Arch of Mists. Ky arrived for Tal moments later. He stood confused at

finding Tal sleeping on the bank of the stream instead of in The Lady's arms. When he went to pick Tal up to return him to the camp, he noticed that Tal was shivering slightly. Ky searched The Garden looking for The Lady to find out what was wrong, but could not find her. He took Tal to the camp and returned to The Garden. The pathways seemed to go on forever as he searched for The Lady. Finally, he stood before the Arch of Mists. Ky guessed that this was the portal to Maker, his father. If The Lady could not be found to answer his questions, then his father would do. The Lady had just arrived at the fountain where Maker spoke. This visit, it was surrounded by a vile, stench-filled, bog. She was just about to bow when the sound of Ky trying to enter the portal filled the bog like thousands of claws scraping across slate. "What brings you, Lady?" Maker asked. She ignored the question and rushed back to the archway. Ky tried again and she cringed, covering her ears as she quickened her run. Usually, she did not have to return by way of the arch. Maker would send her back to The Garden when he dismissed her. Maker had not dismissed her this time, though she was not hindered in her rush to leave either. When she stepped through the arch, she found Ky, bloodied and battered, and ready to make a third attempt at entering the archway. She lifted her son and carried him back to the stream. Arriving, she set him down and knelt before him. "What did you do to my son?" Ky asked, his voice deathly quiet. The Lady swallowed, then said, "The stream. I don't know why, but it did not cleanse him like it did for you and the other children. I don't understand," she stammered, "he is such a loving child. It makes no sense." "What did Maker tell you?" The Lady shook her head, then answered, "Maker would tell me nothing. I know by the question he asked me. Maker knows all things and He asked why I came. I know no answer would be given. None that you or I could understand." Ky turned and stared into The Garden. He could not see the Arch of Mists from where he stood, but he knew where it was. His urge was to get through it and he knew he would eventually, but The Lady would try to stop him. He glanced at her knowing that he would have to hurt her badly to get another try. "Please, there are three more that need to see me. Bring them to me. I will speak with Maker and see what I can determine in between their time here. You will need your strength for the ceremony," The Lady pleaded.

Ky clenched his fists and growled deep in his throat, then left. The Lady closed her eyes and sighed, taking a long slow breath. When she opened her eyes, she found Maker standing before her. "I did not dismiss you," Maker stated. "You did not stop me from leaving either. You knew he would succeed if I did not stop him," The Lady explained. "The path the two of you have chosen leads to two possible ends," Maker said. "Both are marred with loss and pain. The one depends on Simon's strength, the other is on the shoulders of Arienna, your daughter." Maker waved His arm and The Garden wilted and rotted, filled with death and ugliness. The stream became a slowly bubbling pool of blood. "I know you recognize that this is what Arienna will do. Tread carefully, your fate is yours now. The Arch of Mists will be closed to you from this point onward." Maker vanished as The Lady watched her home return to its proper state through tear filled eyes.

50 Archos and Brek arrived in the council room shortly after Karnak and Stumpy had returned. Archos nodded in greeting then immediately headed for his room. "I have need of you Archos," Karnak said, moving to block his path. "Later," Archos answered as he stepped around Karnak and into the room. The door slammed behind him leaving the bewildered thantor fuming. Karnak turned to Brek, "Sit. I will need some explanations." Brek wanted to tell Karnak that he knew nothing of what Archos was doing, but decided against that and found a seat at the council table. Karnak paced for several moments before beginning his interrogation. "It is my guess that Archos has told you nothing of what he is doing. Is that correct?" "Brek was told nothing," the goblin answered. "Tell me exactly what you did while you were in the barracks." "Brek did what Lord Archos told Brek to do. Brek packed up everybody's stuff and all the blankets and practice tunics and anything else that wasn't permanent. Then Brek stacked all the stuff on one bed and waited for Lord Archos." "What do you mean by 'anything else that wasn't permanent?'" Karnak asked. "Brek packed cups, plates, parchments, cleaning rags, towels, soaps, and washcloths." Brek answered. "Interesting," Karnak muttered as he began pacing again. "Did you happen to see what Lord Archos was doing while you were

packing?" "Brek only saw a little. Lord Archos cast magic on everything I couldn't pack," Brek answered, then added, "The beds, tables, wash tubs, sinks, windows and walls." Stumpy asked, "Did ye find out whose sword be missin', lad?" Brek nodded, "Micah sword is gone. Brek packed all the other swords." "I'll let Brenson know while ye ask your questions, Karnak. I've a feelin' Archos will be a while in there." Stumpy emptied his mug and vanished. Karnak sat beside Brek. "You know that Stumpy and I visited your home today, don't you?" "Brek knows," Brek answered. "Lord Ky saved your life by bringing you here. All the goblins that were there are dead, except one," Karnak said, then paused to let Brek react to the news. Brek started pacing. After a few moments he stopped and said, "Brek was chosen to go with Lord Ky because Brek was weakest goblin. Brek had no friends there, no family. Chief goblin killed them for being weak." He paced a little more, then added, "I hope Chief goblin is dead." Karnak closed his clawed hand on Brek's arm and pulled him close. "Brek, we will need to know everything you can tell us about Chief goblin. I am going to take you to a safe, quiet place for you to think. Anything," Karnak paused, then repeated, "anything you remember, you must tell us. Do you understand?" "Brek will think," Brek stated. "Brek heard much about Chief goblin because Brek forced to serve him. Brek will think and tell you anything Brek can." Karnak hissed slightly, and said, "You will be an excellent addition to my council. I will come for you personally when we are ready for you." "Brek want parchments and charstick. Brek will make Lord Karnak proud." Karnak supplied the young goblin with what he wanted and sent him to the Council of Darkness meeting room. When the goblin was gone, Karnak began pacing again, wondering when Archos would come out of his room. Erishen entered the room to find another of Delmaria's journals she had not yet read. "Karnak, is something wrong?" she asked noticing him pacing. "I'm not used to being put off. I may need your magic later," he said. "Stay where I can find you."

Erishen smiled, "I'll be in the parlor awaiting your call." Shortly after Erishen returned to the parlor, Delmaria, Taelann and the high-elf druid returned from the wild-elves. The druid bowed and left. "Hello, Karnak. Has Archos returned yet?" Delmaria asked. "He has. He has barricaded himself in that room with the children's belongings. I take it you have need of him as well," Karnak hissed. "As a matter of fact, yes," Delmaria answered frowning. "I've known him long enough to leave him to his work when he does this. Shall we compare notes while we wait?" she asked, pointing to the table. "We will have to repeat it all when he arrives and I'm weary of talking," Karnak hissed. Delmaria nodded slowly, one eyebrow raising slightly, then said, "At least accept my hospitality and enjoy a drink with us while we wait." Karnak stopped and slowly turned to face Delmaria, a low growl escaping from his chest. Delmaria straightened her back and took a step towards the thantor. "We are friends, Karnak. You have worked with us during very trying times. Surely, you will not jeopardize that friendship now." Delmaria kept her voice even, letting the thantor know he was not intimidating her. "I'm sorry," Karnak hissed. "Archos angered me earlier. I should not have taken it out on you. Of course I'll accept your hospitality." Delmaria smiled. "That's much better. So what will you have? I'm in the mood for a challenge I have a chance of conquering." "Did I hear somethin' bout havin' a drink?" Stumpy asked. "Yes, though, my offer was for Karnak and Taelann," Delmaria answered laughing. "Bah! This dwarf ain't needin' your drinks anyway!" Stumpy approached the table and waved his arms around a few times. His never-emptying mug of ale appeared on the corner. He picked it up, drank it down, then watched as it refilled itself. "Now that be useful magic!" he said as a smile parted his mustache and beard. Before long, Erishen joined the group waiting at the table. They talked quietly, avoiding the problems they yearned to solve while waiting for Archos. When Archos finally came into the council room, his eyes burned ice blue. He looked around the table a moment then moved to stand behind his chair. "Where might I find Brek?" he asked. "I can bring him here in a matter of a second or two,"

Karnak answered. Archos placed a wooden cup on the table and replied, "Do so, please." He did not wait to see if Karnak chose to follow his request. Instead, he retrieved his scrying stone and one of the triplets dragons and brought them to the table. "You aren't thinking of looking into what Ky and the children are doing, I hope," Delmaria whispered. "I am thinking exactly that, I will explain later. It must be done. Now, where is Brek?" Karnak paused a moment then summoned Brek. "Save the information I asked you about a moment, Brek. Archos has need of you first." "Thank you, Karnak." Archos held up the cup. "There were two of these in the room next to beds. Who's beds were they near?" Brek took a moment to consider. "Brek not remember exactly but think Simon was one." He thought a few moments more then added, "Brek remember that Tal like water in morning too." "Tal and Simon," Archos muttered. He placed the dragon in front of the stone and invoked it. Those at the table got a glimpse of the group just before the scrying stone exploded. The dragon took the brunt of the blast, then Archos took the rest. His left arm and the left side of his face were severely lacerated by the stone shards. Delmaria rushed to Archos' side and cradled his head in her lap. Erishen vanished to find Tobit while Taelann left the council room at a run, heading for the front yard. Stumpy went to aid Delmaria with Archos as Karnak tried to calm Brek. Karnak's patience being short already, it did not take long for him to smack Brek hard enough to knock him out. Karnak approached Archos and asked, "Knowing what you knew about disturbing them, what could have caused you to provoke that attack?" "Examine the cup," Archos gasped. Karnak careful scanned the cup, searching for traces of magic. He found it, but could read nothing about its origin or purpose. "There is magic here, but what kind of magic is it?" he asked. "Erishen will know," Archos answered. Erishen and Tobit arrived a moment later. Tobit shook his head as he knelt beside Archos, saying, "I thought you told me you knew to duck when Delmaria started throwing dishes." Tobit examined the wounds then shook his head. "I wish I could at least ease the pain, but the one that did this left a warning. If I try to heal you, it will make it worse, and I will also share your injuries. Who did this and why?" "Ky. I did what he told me not to do. I saw no other path, so

I took it." With Delmaria's and Tobit's help, Archos was placed into his seat at the council table. He pushed the cup towards Erishen and requested, "Tell me what you find there." "I'm sorry I can't help you, Archos," Tobit said. "I must return to Alle-Stecan. Call me if you need anything else." "No problem, my friend. Be careful and safe," Archos said as he gripped Tobit's shoulder and squeezed slightly. As Tobit left, Erishen studied the cup for several moments, shook her head then studied it again. While she worked, Taelann returned and placed a piece of bark on the table. Karnak signaled for him to wait then returned his attention to Erishen. "It doesn't make sense. I've never encountered a potion as complicated at this," Erishen said frowning. "I can't even guess at its purpose." "I can only guess," Archos stated. "I think it is a control potion. I don't know what sort though. Did any of you see the group long enough to determine if they were all there?" "That and more," Taelann said, invoking the bark. The short vision into Ky's group played back in slow motion. All the children were accounted for and apparently very happy to be there. "What more did you see?" Archos asked. "Look again, this time don't look at the children, look at where they are," Taelann explained. The vision played again. This time they saw the scenery flicker slightly around the children. "What be they doin' in that forsaken place?" Stumpy muttered. "I'm lucky Ky didn't kill me. I almost got the whole group killed doing that," Archos answered. "I can't believe he would expend that much magic to go on a horseback ride with them. He must be doing something else. Something that is very important to the ceremony." "I saw something that looked, harsh, but I didn't recognize it. Where were they?" Erishen asked. "The region is called Crocus Hollow," Taelann answered. "I don't know if I could travel through there and survive. It's one of the vilest regions on the continent." Archos picked up the cup and examined it again. He shook his head and muttered, "Nothing about this magic is familiar to me. I wonder if it shows up in some of the other areas where we are having difficulties." Delmaria took the cup and examined it, then handed it to Taelann. Taelann examined it and nodded. "Maybe," he said.

"Do you think you could travel, Archos?" Delmaria asked. "Aye, I can do quite a lot. This attack was a warning, one I intend to take very seriously. Where would you be taking me?" "To where Amber and the girl disappeared," Delmaria answered. "I will go as well, whether the wild-elves like it or not," Karnak stated. "Afterwards, Stumpy and I have need of you, Archos." "I will see to Brek. Call me when you need me," Erishen said as she carried the goblin from the room. Delmaria took Archos and Karnak while Taelann took Stumpy. Seconds later, Archos returned and put the cup safely within his room. He noticed that the other two dragons had been dispelled as he prepared to rejoin the others. "Do not worry, my little friend. I will not make that mistake again," he vowed to the empty room, then vanished.

51 Ky spent the rest of the night pacing around the campfire. He still bore several of the wounds inflicted by the Arch of Mists, but did not care. His thoughts were consumed with finding the reason Tal was so ill-treated by the stream. Every avenue of reason he traveled brought him back to the death of Tal's familiar. Regardless of the fact that the decision was made to save all their lives, Ky could not help but turn his anger and frustration on himself. Shortly before dawn, Ky returned to The Garden. He had to know what The Lady thought of his conclusion. She had not been expecting him to come alone or she would have delayed his arrival until her home had completely recovered from Maker's warning. When Ky did arrive, he found The Lady crying softly near the bank of the stream. He could tell she had been crying a while and thought she still mourned what had been done to Tal. Then he noticed The Garden. It had almost completely recovered but the signs of its illness were still readily visible and the stench of decay still tainted the air. Although the stream flowed freely now, it still had a sanguine tint to its waters. "I'm sorry," The Lady said between sobs, "I did not wish you to see this." "Tal?" Ky whispered. The Lady shook her head. "Maker. He had not dismissed me when I left His fountain to stop you from harming yourself against the Arch. After you left, He came here..." Her voice became lost in sobs and she waved her hand in the direction of The Garden. "Why would Maker do this?" Ky asked.

The Lady took a deep, shuddering breath, then stood. "This is His way of warning us. He said there are two outcomes for what we plan to do. What you see here is the result of the one that will occur if we are not very careful. What did you come here for?" "I've been thinking about Tal," Ky started as he walked to the tree beside the stream. "Before he came here, I had to kill his familiar to keep the group safe. Is that why the stream reacted the way it did? Is it my fault?" The Lady followed Ky to the tree, placed her hand on his shoulder and answered, "I saw that injury. It was minor and would not have caused the stream to act as it did. Maker would know, but he will not tell us." "Can you not take me to Him?" Ky asked. The Lady sighed. "I'm afraid we are alone now. Maker has sealed the Arch of Mists and left us to our fate. What happens now is entirely dependent upon our strength." She ran her fingertips through Ky's long black hair and added, "I will need to see Simon after you bring me the others. We will need him to be very strong." "I will bring the next two tonight," Ky said, then surveyed The Garden. "Will it still be like this when they come?" "No. The Garden will be fully recovered from Maker's warning when you bring them." She kissed Ky on the top of his head, then said, "Go now, so that I may recover as well." Ky found himself back in the camp before he could answer. He also noticed that his wounds had been healed. Even though dawn was still about an hour away, he decided to wake the children and get started on the journey. He would feel safer once they reached the high-elven forests. He did not wish another incident like Crocus Hollow. The children did not complain. They seemed happy to be moving again, especially since the trip returned to the relaxed pace it had started with. Tal appeared to be recovering well from his trip to The Garden, though he still had small fits of shivering now and then. Regardless of this, Ky had Eleana ride near him throughout the day. By early evening, the group had traveled the distance Ky had wanted to cover that day. Rather than push farther, Ky stopped them, set up camp and let them have the rest of the evening to play, sing and tell stories. Simon, noticing Ky sitting alone watching, pestered his brother to join the play. It took a while, but Simon's boyishness finally won and a wild game of tag ensued. Ky's participation heightened everyone's enjoyment of the evening. When they finally settled around the fire, the happiness of the group was almost tangible. They stayed awake far longer than usual trading stories and singing songs, the most appreciated being the

duet William had taught Micah and Tal. They were nervous as they had never tried to sing it for anyone and they lacked the piano that was present when they learned the song. Ky enjoyed the song so much, he made them sing it again so that he could record it on memory bark. The moon had risen well above the horizon when Ky said, "You need rest. We have another long day of riding tomorrow." "Not so fast," Ky II said. "Yeah, you have to promise to play with us again tomorrow night before we'll go to sleep," added Eleana. "And," said Simon with a mischievous smirk, "you have to make the promise to Little Ky." This statement was met with a chorus of agreement from everyone at the fire. Ky glared at each of them for a moment, then shrugged. "Alright. Little Ky, I promise to play tomorrow night. Now, go to sleep." Cheers and shouts of joy echoed through the small grove as the children scampered to their tents. Ky watched them, shaking his head. As usual, Simon stayed with Ky by the fire as Ky put the rest to sleep. "I don't get it," Ky said to Simon. "What's so special about me playing with them?" "It's part of the family thing," Simon answered. "There's a big difference between being near them and being with them. They like it better when you are with them." Ky stared into the fire for a few moments, then said, "Maker has left us. The Lady will want to see you after Brek returns from The Garden. She said something about us needing you to be strong." Simon's breath caught in his throat as his head turned with a jerk in Ky's direction. "Maker is gone?" he gasped. "That's what she told me." Ky looked over the fire to the tent Tal slept in. "It has something to do with what happened to Tal when he was in The Garden. His trip there was not pleasant." "Have you tried to lift the memory from him?" Simon asked. Ky shook his head. "If I try that, he may remember. The Lady blocked it so he wouldn't." "Maybe I should go see her now," said Simon. "She's not ready for you. Wait until after Brek goes. I think she needs the time to prepare what she needs to tell you." Ky stood, using Simon's shoulder for support. He kept his hand on Simon's shoulder as he said, "It's time for me to take Little Ky. Wait for me. I won't be long." Simon nodded, saying, "I'll think about how to find out what happened to Tal while you're gone."

Ky woke Little Ky before taking him to The Garden. "It's your turn," Ky whispered as the sleep faded from his son's eyes. "You will like this," he added, hoping it to be true. They arrived at the usual spot near the stream. Ky led his son to the stream and knelt beside it. "Give me your hand," Ky said. Little Ky knelt beside his father and held out his hand. "Tell me what you feel," Ky said as he immersed Little Ky's fingertips into the stream. Ky watched his son's expression as the water flowed around his fingers. He did not need to hear what Little Ky felt. The wide-eyed wonderment and smile told him all he needed to know. "Never mind," Ky said smiling. "I've got my answer." Ky led Little Ky back from the stream a bit, then said, "Wait here. Someone very special wants to meet you. I'll be back later to take you back to the camp." The Lady had watched from a distance as Ky tested the stream with Little Ky. She could not help but feel pride in his actions. After Ky left, she walked down the path to greet her newest visitor. The closer she came to him, the more she felt hope swell in her heart, though she could not determine the reason. Her decision to make this visit last as long as possible was made before he could see her. "Welcome, Little Ky. I am your grandmother, and I am so happy to finally meet you." She leaned forward and kissed his forehead. "Hi. Are you the very special person I'm waiting for?" Little Ky asked. "I believe I am," The Lady replied, laughing. "Come, walk with me and we shall get to know each other better." Little Ky took The Lady's hand, saying, "I'm all yours. Where do we start?" The Lady marveled at how trusting this child appeared. She sensed that his trust was as sincere as the smile he wore. "That pathway looks interesting. Let's start there," she suggested. "Will we get to the stream again before I have to go?" "We will save the best part for last," she replied smiling. "Now, tell me everything there is to know about you." True to her vow to make this visit last as long as possible, The Lady created new sections in The Garden for them to explore. She found Little Ky to be a loving, open-minded, and honest boy, so completely different from his father that it baffled her. She also found herself opening her heart and feelings to him in ways that she had never done with anyone, even Maker. She felt she would never tire of his laughter and went out of her way to make sure it came often. After what would have been days, had they not been in The Garden, the path led them back to the stream. The Lady drank in his

excitement as they approached it. She led him to the bank and turned him so that his back was to the water. "After such a long walk, I'm sure you would like to splash around in that nice cool water for a while, wouldn't you?" she asked. "Yes!" Little Ky answered, his head turning back to the stream. "May I, please?" "Oh course. Leave your clothing here on the path. I will sit beneath the tree over there and sing to you while you play, if you'd like." Little Ky wasted no time removing his clothing and answering, "I would love to hear you sing for me." Even though she had seen Ky test the stream, The Lady took great care in observing Little Ky's reaction to the waters. She had loved Tal as much as she loved Little Ky. The stream treating Tal the way it did left a scar on her heart that would never heal. She did not wish to have another and did not relax until Little Ky was happily swimming in circles in the middle of the pool. Only then did she sit beside the tree and begin to sing. Little Ky continued to swim and play for a few minutes as The Lady sang. Then he began to concentrate on the song, relaxing in the center of the pool while the water gently played around his body. At the end of the song, The Lady held the towel for Little Ky and helped him dry and dress. Finally, as with all the children, she held him close and hummed a soft lullaby. She indulged herself with the warmth of his closeness for quite a while before marking the time when Ky could arrive to take his son back. When Ky returned, he immediately noticed the difference in The Lady's demeanor. He did not have to ask if all went well. Her face glowed with pleasure as she held Little Ky. Ky gently placed Micah on the path and took Little Ky into his arms. "You saw what I did last time," Ky whispered, "I'll leave that to you this time." The Lady smiled and whispered, "I will take every precaution. This one," she gently caressed Little Ky's cheek, "has given me new hope. I can't explain it, but he is very special." "He probably got it from his mother," Ky quipped as he vanished. The Lady laughed, though she felt Ky was more serious about the statement than he would have her believe. Then she looked at the boy that lay sleeping at her feet. He looked like a collection to sticks stuffed into a big pillowcase; however, he had large hands and feet which told her he had quite a bit of growing to do yet. She knelt beside him and stroked his cheek, waiting as the sleep left his fluttering eyelids.

"Hello, Micah. I am The Lady and this is my home. Ky brought you here to prepare you for the gift he plans to give you soon. Come, let us get to know each other better, though, with what Little Ky has told me, I feel as if I already know and love you a great deal." Micah sat up, saying, "You're Simon's mom, aren't you?" The Lady smiled and nodded. "I am. Simon and Ky are my children. Little Ky tells me you have the most beautiful singing voice. Will you sing for me?" Micah blushed. "I think he was exaggerating a bit. But if you want, I will." "That would make me very happy, but before we get into singing and taking a walk, I need to check something. Come to the stream with me." Micah went with The Lady to the edge of the stream and allowed her to guide his fingers into the water. The Lady smiled at his reaction, saying, "Maybe later, you will want to swim a little. But let's walk first. Sing me a song and I will show you my gardens." The Lady greatly enjoyed Micah's visit. She found his return to childhood was almost complete, although he still had traces of maturity that only came with adulthood. She felt these traces would fade before long and he would fully enjoy the second youthfulness he had been given. As much as The Lady tried to keep the conversation about Micah, he would change it to talk about William, his adopted father, Little Ky or Daphnia and what she had in mind with William. The Lady found Micah's jealousy amusing though she did all she could to convince Micah that William would not forget him even if something developed between him and Daphnia. Finally, she explained, "Micah, people have a lot of room in their hearts. Just like you have room to love William as your father and Little Ky as your best friend, William will have room to love you as his son and Daphnia as his wife if that does come about. Besides, William will always be your father and if he does join with Daphnia, you will have yourself a new mother as well." Micah was quiet for a few moments, then said, "I've never known my mother. I don't know what it's like to have one. I don't even know if she'll like me." "I believe Daphnia will find it very difficult not to like you," The Lady said, smiling. "You are a handsome and very charming young man. I would be proud to have you as my son." Micah grinned and confessed, "She may like me more if I stopped trying to get between them all the time." They both laughed. Micah was more willing to talk about himself after that. He sang several more songs for her as well. When they arrived at the bank of the stream, Micah left his nightshirt on the

path and splashed to the center of the pool. The Lady made sure the water would not do harm to him before relaxing beside the tree and singing for him. Although Micah was one of the quietest in the pool, he was also the most active. He spent the entire time exploring the pool with his hands and feet, sometimes sticking his head under the water to get a closer look at a rock he found and thought was interesting. When she held the towel for him, he had a small stone in his hand when he left the stream. "May I keep this?" he asked as The Lady started to dry him. The Lady looked at the stone, worn smooth by the current. To her it appeared to a stone that one could find at the bottom of any stream. She knew Micah saw something special about it. "Yes and no," she said as she dried his hair. "I will keep it for you and you may have it after the inheritance ceremony. Ky does not want you to remember your visit here until after that. Do you trust me enough to accept that?" "Sure," Micah said as he pulled on his nightshirt. He handed the stone to The Lady and let her cradle him in her arms. He fell into a peaceful sleep as she hummed the lullaby to him. Before long, Ky returned for Micah. "I will bring Brek right before the ceremony," Ky explained. "Karnak is training him but has promised to have him waiting at the gates to Alle-Stecan when we arrive there. After that, Simon will come." "If it is not a problem, I would like to add a little something to the ceremony," The Lady said, smiling at Micah. "I can't explain it now, but I promise it will be special, especially for this one." Ky raised one eyebrow and tilted his head slightly, which only caused The Lady's smile to widen. Finally he shrugged and said, "It's already going to be busy, might as well make it more so." "It may not be necessary, but I think, if my intuition is correct, that it will be very pleasurable for all involved." She began to walk back into The Garden. "I'll check a few things and will let you know for sure when you bring Brek." "Okay," Ky said before vanishing with Micah.

52 When Ky returned from delivering Little Ky to The Garden, he glanced at Simon who shook his head. Ky spent the next hour seated under a tree not far from the camp. Simon found him and sat beside a nearby tree. "I think I know a way, but I want to experiment first," Simon explained. "On who?" "Ky II would do it for me," Simon suggested. Ky nodded, so Simon returned to camp and quietly woke Ky II. As he led Ky II to where Ky waited, Simon explained what he wanted to try. As Simon expected, Ky II was happy to help with it. After some discussion around the tree, they decided to try to get one of Ky II's memories during the time he was delirious in Chao-tarris's cave. Ky would extract the memory using Simon as a conduit. Simon hoped that Ky II would not remember the memory since Simon was being used as the source to read it. It took several tries, but Ky managed to get one of Ky II's fever induced dreams through Simon. The method worked. Although the dream almost reduced Simon to tears, Ky II had no recollection of it at all. "What did you find?" Ky II asked, concerned at Simon's reaction. "We found that you are a very loyal friend," Ky answered, sparing Simon from having to explain. "I'm proud of you, that's all you need to know of it." Ky stood and turned towards the camp. "It's Micah's turn. We'll take care of the other problem when I return. Make sure you are asleep when I get back, Ky II."

As Ky walked to Micah's tent, Ky II muttered to Simon, "He tells me that he's proud of me and then expects me to be able to sleep." "I'll help you. It's the least I can do for a friend," Simon replied as he led Ky II back to his tent. When Ky returned, he found Simon sitting at the entrance to Tal's tent. Tal's head was only a few inches away from him. Ky sat beside Simon and nodded to let him know he was ready. It took quite a bit of effort for Ky to find the memory as The Lady hid it well. He hesitated before bringing it out. He considered his time alone in The Garden as very personal and private and could not help feeling that he was invading Tal's privacy by pursuing this memory. Ky's need to know what went wrong brought Tal's memory into his awareness. Ky found he could speed through the first part of it, giving it only enough attention to find where Tal entered the stream. The memory slowed just as Tal took his first step into the water. Both Simon and Ky relived the freezing cold and the excruciating pain that Tal felt. Simon broke contact as soon as The Lady summoned Tal from the water. They sat staring at each other for several minutes before they retreated to the tree to discuss what they just experienced. They talked most of the night though they gained no further understanding of what had happened. By the time Ky was ready to bring Micah back from The Garden, he had convinced Simon to share what they found with The Lady. Maybe she would be able to find meaning where they could not.

53 Archos reappeared to find the group had been joined by two wild-elves. He recognized one of them from his visit to the council. Karnak was searching not far from the bank so Archos quietly joined the others and watched. "Only one of the three died here," Karnak explained. "There was no struggle. His death occurred here. Then he was dragged to the river and thrown in." Delmaria acted as translator and asked Karnak if he could tell the race of the murderer. Karnak denied having knowledge of that and pointed to Taelann. "I know death. If the murderer died here, I would know them. The elf would be better suited to tell you about what came this way and lived." "Karnak, was the body dragged to the bank, then picked up and thrown in, or was he dragged into the river?" Karnak looked at Taelann a moment, wondering how this knowledge would be of any use to him. As Karnak followed the trail of the body, Taelann asked Stumpy to return to the farm and bring back the druid that had come earlier and Erishen. Karnak stood ankle deep in the river and turned to Taelann. "He was dragged at least this far, do I need to search farther?" "No, that tells me what I need to know. Now I hope what I intend to try will work." Taelann turned to Archos, and said, "You will need to do what you came for before I begin, or my work may erase the traces left before me." "This way, my dear," Delmaria purred as she led Archos to

where the vines of the two missing elves were found. "We know the person responsible for this was at this spot. Both Taelann and I sensed traces of magic here. The magic in the cup you showed us earlier might be similar, but we could not be sure." "Step aside, Milady, and I shall do all I can for you," Archos said, bowing. Delmaria gave Archos the room he needed and waited. Stumpy returned with the druid and Erishen, long before Archos finished his search. They watched quietly as Archos wove his spells into the fabric of the forest. "Where are the vines, now?" Archos asked as he stepped away from the area. Delmaria asked the wild-elf and was told they are with the families of the two elves. When Delmaria related this to Archos, he asked if he could have a small piece of one of them. The wild-elf agreed, only because they were attempting to find the missing children. When he left, Archos described what he found. "You were correct in thinking that the person who cast this magic and the one who created the potion that lingers in the cup are the same person. However, the magics are very different. The reason I know they are cast by the same person is they match the traces that were left in Mena's room in Cragsguard. Unfortunately, I have no experience with this type of magic and can tell you very little about it. What we do know is there is a connection between Mena's disappearance and the abduction of these wild-elves." "Surely, the lass didn't have the magic to do this deed," Stumpy sputtered, trying hard to hide the incredulous feeling he was having at the thought of it. "No, Stumpy. But, she did have access to magic and I think it was provided by whomever did this." Archos then spoke to Taelann. "I've learned what I can, proceed with what you intended, please. I believe we've other places to explore before our day is over." Taelann began positioning the group around the area so that as many different views could be obtained as possible. The wild-elf returned with a small piece of vine for Archos, and Taelann asked if he would participate. He told Delmaria that participation may result in seeing something that would cause emotional pain for the wild-elf and Taelann wanted him to know that in advance. The wild-elf agreed and took the last position. Taelann gathered the druid and Erishen together and took them to the center of the area. They would slightly obscure the vision of some of the watchers, but, Taelann hoped, they would not interfere with the events as they unfolded. "Your name is Galsir?" Taelann asked.

"Aye, Milord." "What I wish to attempt, I've only done once before, and that was with Daelann using twin-speak. It was difficult, but we made it work. As a druid, you can awaken the spirits of the plants and the river for me. As a ranger, I can read faint shadows of their memories. Erishen is the Mistress of Illusion. It is my hope that she will be able to make the memories I find visible for our friends to see. "Both Erishen and I will need access to your mind to make this work. I know I'm asking a lot, but it may help us find these missing elves. Will you agree to that?" Galsir slowly nodded, though his expression showed his discomfort. Taelann placed a hand on the druid's shoulder. "If you have any doubts, I will find another druid. You do not have to do this." "Milord, your council saved the lives of myself and my brother as well as all the other twins and triplets in the high-elven kingdom. This is a small price to pay for such a gift. I am merely nervous. I will not let you down." Taelann smiled. "Excellent. I promise we will not intrude, we just need access to work together." Before Taelann could explain what he wished Erishen to do, Erishen explained it to him. She added, "I love working with your council. You always challenge my abilities." Erishen cast the spell that would link their minds and allow them to speak with each other through a version of elven twin-speak. -Start awakening the spirits- Taelann thought. -Start over there,- he instructed, pointing to the area where the vines were found. As soon as Taelann sensed them, he had Galsir awaken the spirits of all the plants between that tree and the river. -Don't awaken the river yet. I'll let you know when I'm ready for that.- Erishen kept the link open in the background and started projecting the images that formed in Taelann's mind. Everyone began to see the spirits as they were summoned. -Close your eyes, Galsir,- Erishen thought. -The images are distracting you.- Slowly, the wild-elves last moments in the forest became visible. All that watched saw what happened that night, but the cause of the elves' disappearance remained illusive. Taelann continued to search the memories of the spirits hoping someone would catch a glimpse of the murderer. -The river, now,- Taelann thought. -Erishen, go into the river. You may be our only hope of seeing who did this.- Erishen understood and moved into the waters even though the mighty river spirit intimidated her. She waited and watched as the

dead elf was dragged into the center of the river and released. -I can only see the dead elf,- Erishen thought, dismayed. -Water displacement,- Taelann answered. Erishen immediately adjusted her vision and was able to make out the outline of most of the murderers body as she returned to shore. Afterwards, she returned to where Taelann and Galsir stood, and continued to project the vision until the other two wild-elves vanished. -We're done,- Taelann thought as he moved to catch Galsir who collapsed from exhaustion. Delmaria came to Galsir's aid as well. "I think we should all go back to the farm now. I will be able to extract the visions more readily if we are all there and relaxed." "Agreed," Archos said as he approached. "Karnak, as soon as we finish with this, I will go with you and Stumpy." "It may be better to speak with Brek first, since we'll be at the farm anyway. He may offer some insight that will make what I need you to do easier." Delmaria explained to the wild-elf what needed to be done and he agreed. He had them wait while he obtained a healer who would stay at the farm and see to the needs of the high-elves, particularly Galsir, who had given so much to assist the wild-elves. Within moments, the spirits that inhabited the forest were at rest again, and the group had returned to the farm.

54 Ky had thought the last day of the journey would see the end of the passage he created. He designed it to last as long as the safety of the group needed it. Ky knew they traveled through the high- elven kingdom. The fact the passage still protected them caused him to worry. He truly wanted to enjoy this last day with the children. After the ceremony, it would probably be very difficult to arrange such an outing where all of them would be present. Ky pushed the concern to the back of his mind, but it still nagged at him the farther they traveled. The incident in Crocus Hollow put the group well ahead of schedule causing them to arrive at the site Ky had planned to camp well before sunset. They could have easily made it to Alle-Stecan that day. Ky stopped them anyway. He had made a promise to Little Ky and he was truly enjoying himself. The end of the journey so close, Ky wasted no time in joining with the others as they played. They played tag, had stick-fighting contests and wrestled with each other until the moon rose, then settled around the camp fire for stories and songs. Ky had each of them sing for him, sometimes alone, sometimes in groups or pairs. After Tal and Micah sang their duet, the tables were turned on Ky. "We haven't heard you sing yet," Micah dared to say in a shy whisper. Ky thought for a moment, then retrieved the three pieces of bark he had made in Austria. As the memory of William played the songs, Ky's voice joined them. He had thought these memories to be something very personal and private. The feeling of happiness that he

got while sharing them with his children and their friends made him wish he had done so earlier. When he finished singing all three of the Mozart songs, he regretfully sent the children to sleep. Unlike the night before, there were no shouts or cheers. The children knew their time with Ky was ending, and they retreated to their tents with faces frowning, heads bowed, and feet dragging slowly across the ground. Ky hesitated before casting the sleep spell and was rewarded with a soft chorus of 'good nights' that lasted until all had said good night to everyone else in the group. After the last one, Eleana's, Ky put them to sleep. "Are you nervous?" Simon asked. Ky nodded, "And a little scared. I may need your strength tomorrow. There's a lot that needs to be done." "What are you planning?" "You'll see. Go to sleep. I'll need you rested, just in case." Simon placed his arm around Ky's shoulder and pulled his brother close. "I'll be there for you. You have no trips to make tonight. You should sleep as well." Ky grinned, "Being what I am has one advantage. I no longer have to waste time sleeping." "Doesn't sound so great to me. You get to sit here alone and worry all night," Simon said, still holding Ky. "Not tonight. I'll be going through the evening and making my bark collection grow," Ky answered, finally returning Simon's embrace. "Go to sleep, little brother. Tonight, at least this once, I will be very happy." Simon smiled and retired to his tent. Ky gave him a moment to get settled then put him to sleep as well. Afterwards, he went in search of a large fallen branch. He felt he would need a great deal of bark this night.

55 The Lady appeared in the front room of William's new home in Cragsguard, choosing a time when Daphnia would be there. She silently glided into the back room and found William at the piano playing a song for Daphnia who sat in a chair pulled up beside the piano.
