"Good day to you, William and Daphnia," she greeted, smiling. The Lady's presence did not startle them. It was as if they were expecting her arrival. William stood and bowed, offering his hand to Daphnia as she stood and curtsied. "Good afternoon, Milady," William greeted. "What can we do for you?" "If I may speak with Daphnia alone for a few moments, it would please me greatly," The Lady explained, indicating the two stuffed chairs by the fireplace. "Of course," William answered, smiling. "I'll go to the kitchen and make us refreshments while you talk." William kissed Daphnia's hand and left the room. "Come, child. Sit with me," The Lady offered. Daphnia flushed slightly at being referred to as child, but took it more as a compliment than anything else. She sat across from The Lady and waited. "I wish to ask you about your intentions towards Micah," The Lady explained. "Micah?" Daphnia asked. "Yes. Micah is quite concerned about the attention you are

getting from William. He is worried you intend to take his father away from him." "Trees be fallin'! I'd never be wishin' to be hurtin' that charmin' boy!" Daphnia grabbed the book that sat on the table beside her chair and began fanning herself with it. "I remember when he first be comin' here, I do. 'Twas me that got him his first scrap o' clothin'." "So if you and William were to marry, you would have no problem with Micah as your son?" Daphnia sighed and beamed a smile so broad, it appeared her face would break away from her lower jaw. "He'd be the sweetest boy to have as a son, he would. Trees be fallin' would that it come to be." She sighed again, her smile fading. "But if the boy be thinkin' I be takin' his father, how could I be marryin' William now?" The Lady leaned forward and took Daphnia's hand. "I will tell you a secret. When Micah and I talked this over, the conversation ended with him saying you would make a lovely mother. He has never known a mother, so your job will be quite difficult if you choose this path." "If it come to be, trees be fallin', I'd be the best mother on the planet for him," Daphnia said, again the smile returning. This time tears came with it. "I will need to speak with William. Maybe what I say will persuade him to take this path. Fear not, I know, as you do, that it is his wish." The Lady released Daphnia's hand and sat back, saying, "The best refreshments need a woman's touch, don't you think?" "Aye, Milady, they do," Daphnia said. "I'll be sendin' William out to speak to ye right away." Daphnia hurried into the kitchen and almost pushed William out of it in her haste to have The Lady speak with him. "Daphnia is the sweetest woman I know," William said as he sat across from The Lady. "Even when she gets a bit over persistent." "She is quite charming," The Lady agreed. "She will have the refreshments ready quickly so I will get directly to the point. Do you intend to marry Daphnia?" William's breath caught in his throat, stunned by the question. After a moment needed to regain his composure, he answered, "I would love to do just that, Milady. I fear that Micah may have a problem with it and he just recently found out that I had adopted him. I would not like to see his happiness marred." The Lady held out her hand to William, something concealed inside. William reached forward to receive it as The Lady explained. "This is the ring Micah's father gave to his mother on their engagement. And these," she said as she handed a small box to

William, "are their wedding rings. Micah's happiness will be enhanced at the joining of you and Daphnia. I will conduct the ceremony myself, if you agree, before Ky's triplets receive their inheritance." William stared at the simple engagement ring. He knew the history of Micah's parents. Three days after his birth, they were killed by a robber outside the hospital. William also knew that the rings were among the few items they had that were stolen. As this ran through his mind, Daphnia returned with a tray laden with sandwiches, a cheese wedge, and elven wine. William quickly slid the box into his pocket and took the tray from her. After placing it on the table, he knelt before Daphnia. "If it please you, Milady," William said as he placed the engagement ring on her finger, "I would ask the honor of our union as husband and wife." "Please me? Trees be fallin'! Yes!" Daphnia squealed wrapping her arms around William as he stood. "Yes! Yes! Yes!" They parted and begged The Lady's pardon at their rudeness. William guided Daphnia to the stuffed chair across from The Lady, then dragged the one that sat near the piano over and sat as well. "This ring be beautiful," Daphnia breathed. "It is yours until we replace it with our wedding ring, then it goes to Micah." William said. "That ring is his mother's engagement ring. I hope you don't mind giving it to him after the wedding." "I'll be so happy to be givin' it to the boy. How is it you got to be havin' this ring?" Daphnia asked. "This fine Lady acquired it for us. Our wedding rings are also from Micah's parents," William explained as he poured three glasses of elven wine. "Trees be fallin', William. We can be gettin' any ol' weddin' rings. Should we not be givin' them to the boy as well?" Daphnia asked. William served the wine and answered, "I know Micah, very well. The fact that we chose his parents' rings to mark our union will make him very happy. He will want them where he can see them, on his parents' fingers." "I not be knowin' such thin's. Won't the rings be remindin' him of his original parents?" William smiled and shook his head. "There is no need to worry about that. You will be the first mother Micah has ever had the chance to know just as I am his first real father. His parents died three days after he was born. He has no memories of them." "Trees be fallin'! The poor child!" Daphnia exclaimed as she began to cry. The Lady stood and placed her hand upon Daphnia's

forehead. "Do not grieve for Micah as he lost his parents before he had a chance to know them and grieve for them. I leave you now with my blessing upon both of you." She kissed both Daphnia and William on the forehead, then said, "I will see the two of you the day after tomorrow. Rejoice, for your union will bring as much joy to your son as it brings to the two of you." The Lady left them to celebrate, but before she returned to The Garden, she informed Stan of the news and requested that he give them a while alone before throwing them a party. Stan was happy to agree. He wanted to have time to make the party special anyway. Shortly before dinner time, he walked across the square and invited William and Daphnia over for dinner. He absolutely refused to accept a negative answer and gave them no time to talk either. "Your table is set and your dinner will be served in five minutes whether you are there or not," Stan announced as he left. William and Daphnia had planned on dining at the Cracked Anvil before The Lady arrived anyway. The events that happened since her arrival would only make the dinner more enjoyable. They had no idea that Stan knew their plans and were quite surprised at the greeting they received when they entered the inn. The table closest to the fireplace was set for them and decorated in honor of their wedding. Beside it, another table stood, laden with gifts from all the friends they had made since they arrived in Cragsguard. The common room was full of well-wishers. Stan even managed to find a poet that sang serenades, while playing a lute. Several hours after the party started, the Old Man showed up. William had not seen him in days and had begun to worry about him. Both Daphnia and William insisted he pull a chair to their table and join them. "Where have you been?" William asked. "After being locked away for twenty years, I had some catching up to do. I wanted to get it all done before the ceremony. I finished early and I'm happy I did. Congratulations on your engagement." "Thank you," William said. "I'm not sure how weddings are done around here. If they have them, would you agree to be my best man?" "I will agree to anything you ask, my friend, as long as you explain it to me," the Old Man answered, laughing. "Basically, you would be the keeper of the wedding rings," William answered. "He knows what you are talking about, William," Stan said as he refilled their wine. "He's just giving you a hard time. I think you should start opening your gifts. Some of these people actually sleep at

night." William and Daphnia laughed and did as Stan suggested. The party lasted several hours more. Shortly after the last guest left, Daphnia prepared to go to her room. "In a couple days, my love, Stan will have another empty room. I so look forward to when that time comes," William said, then kissed Daphnia's hand. "Trees be fallin', William!" Daphnia said, blushing. "Don't ye be gettin' me all excited right before I be wantin' to go to sleep." William squeezed her hand and answered, "I think you will get as much sleep as I will tonight. I'll have breakfast ready early tomorrow." He winked and returned to his home. Neither William nor Daphnia slept well, as William had predicted. Both lay awake thinking of the other and the happiness they would share. True to his word, when Daphnia arrived just after dawn, breakfast was ready.

56 While the group prepared to discuss their findings at the river, the wild-elf approached Delmaria. "The interior confinement of the house may hinder the healer's abilities. Is there a place nearby where he can set up that would not be too inconvenient for those that live here?" "Come. I will speak with Illya. I'm sure we can come up with something appropriate." Delmaria led the two wild-elves into the kitchen and introduced them to Illya. "Where would you suggest for the healer, Illya?" Illya led them to the porch. "Would he be comfortable in the orchard by the cliff?" Illya asked. Delmaria translated and the two wild-elves went to investigate Illya's suggestion. The healer remained in the orchard, quite happy with the arrangement. "I don't understand," the wild-elf said when he returned to the porch. "Wild-elves have always separated themselves from others. The outsiders we have welcomed in our entire history can be counted on the digits of one's hands. Yet, these gods, even the ones whose evil reeks through their very pores, are helping us. Why is that, Lady Delmaria?" "At the moment," Delmaria explained as they returned to the council room, "the disappearance of the two children seems to be connected with the disappearance of a dwarf that served Lord Ky's children. So your problem is related to the one we are working on. Even if that were not so, some of us would be happy to assist you

merely because we like doing that sort of thing. We are very accustomed to making adjustments so that we can fit everyone in." Taelann met them at the table and showed the wild-elf where to sit. "I will be recording the events since I could not see what was happening. Del, please extract the memories from each person and project it above the table. This should insure that nothing is missed due to forgetfulness. If you start all the memories at the time the spirits first started waking, I will be able to produce a panoramic display using the bark I record." "You may start with me and Karnak," Archos suggested. "That way the two of us can concentrate on what the rest of you saw without worry of losing what we saw." "It is best that you do not watch the individual memories," Delmaria said. "They may alter your actual memory. I will temporarily blind each of you until I've extracted the memory. Since Karnak can not be blinded, I will extract his first." The wild-elf was uncomfortable with both the blinding and with the intrusion into his memories. Due to his trust of Delmaria, he allowed both. Delmaria instructed each to concentrate on the moment the spirits of the forest awoke and let her take control of the memory after that point. She projected her own memory after extracting Karnak's, then moved to Archos. Taelann recorded them as the scene played above the table from each viewpoint. After all the memories had been recorded, Taelann led the group to the yard between the farmhouse and the barn. He arranged the pieces of bark so that each person's memory was in their respective place at the scene by the river. Taelann engaged the memories as the group watched. Several hours were devoted to finding some clue as to who had abducted the two elves. Only Erishen's memory provided such a clue. From the water displacement, they were able to determine that the abductor was female and probably human. Nothing else could be found. "It's more than what we had," Archos muttered, stroking his beard. "I believe the two wild-elves were taken for a reason, though I cannot fathom why. I doubt either will die until after that purpose is served." Archos paced for a few moments. "What is worrying me most, is that this same presence had been in Mena's room and is probably responsible for her disappearance as well. I also believe that the purpose of these abductions has something to do with Ky's children or Simon. The involvement of wild-elves leads me to rule out Simon and Little Ky. "I will now go with Karnak and Stumpy. We will keep the

rest of you informed if we come up with anything more." "Erishen, I will need you with us as well," Karnak said. "Let us go now in case our investigation takes longer than I anticipate. All of us must be in Alle-Stecan the morning after next." As Karnak ported Archos, Stumpy and Erishen to the canyon, Delmaria returned the wild-elf to his forest. On returning to the farm, she found a note from Karnak asking her to find out all she could about the Chief goblin from Brek. He suggested taking Brek and Taelann to the Dark Council chamber where they would not be disturbed. Delmaria considered his suggestion, but decided that Selia's shrine would be the best choice. Selia would be able to determine actual facts from legend. She noted her decision on the bottom of Karnak's note and left it at his place at the council table, then gathered Taelann and Brek and took them to Cragsguard. Karnak's group arrived in the canyon and were immediately noticed by the guards on the wall of Cragsguard. Archos was reminded that the town needed to be protected again. He knew that in spite of the guards' heightened awareness, the foe they were dealing with could come and go as she pleased with things the way they were. Stumpy cleared the tunnel quickly, then told them he would meet them up top. He had to retrieve Micah's replacement sword from Brenson. Karnak led Archos and Erishen into the tunnel, warning them that what they would find would not be pleasant. Neither Archos or Erishen could see well in the dark, so Archos produced a globe of light that hovered over their heads as they walked. “Not pleasant at all,” Archos muttered as they stepped into the throne room. “What am I looking for here?” “First, I would like to know if you can determine how many recent instances of Rachk'sha's magic you can find in this room,” Karnak said. After a few moments, Archos answered, “Recent, only one. From what I can tell, it was not directed at the goblins we see here.” “We'll return here in a moment. First we will go to a mark Stumpy found for me. I think you'll find it quite interesting.” Karnak led them through the tunnels to where the 'ghost' rune had been left upon the cave wall. “It's the goblin rune for 'ghost',” Archos observed. “It probably refers to Ky. It seems to be old enough.” “Good, you know the goblin runes,” Karnak hissed. “Please, trace the rune. Watch him carefully for I wish you to trace it as well, Erishen.”

Archos slowly traced the rune as Erishen watched, then backed away stroking his beard. He waited until Erishen was finished, nodding when she yelped and pulled back her hand in pain. “Ky obviously knew this rune as well,” Archos said. “We're not done yet. Search the floor for magic,” Karnak instructed, pointing. “There beneath the rune.” After Archos and Erishen did as Karnak requested, Archos said, “It's Ky's magic, but it feels slightly different. Maybe that is where he stood when he put the rune there and time has altered it. I really cannot say at this point.” “One could make that assumption. Let us return to the other chamber,” Karnak said, leading the way. “I take it that you don't believe that is the case,” Archos said as he followed Karnak through the tunnels. “What is your conclusion concerning how the magic traces are found on the floor as well as on the wall?” “I would prefer the two of you come up with that without my aid,” Karnak explained. “That way, I will know if the conclusion I've come up with is feasible.” Karnak led them to the rune beside the throne. As before, Archos checked for signs of Ky's magic on the floor in front of the rune. This time he found none. He examined the rune, and even in its defiled state he could feel Ky's power emanating from it. As he worked, Erishen placed her foot upon the board in front of the throne to get closer so that she could watch. The board sagged under her weight. A click was heard across the room, followed by a quick whistling sound of something flying towards them. She ducked just in time to have the bolt embed itself in the back of the throne. “Don't touch it!” Archos ordered. “That answers the question of how a goblin was able to capture Ky.” “Is that the same as the bolts that were provided by Rachk'sha?” Erishen asked. Archos nodded. “What did you do to cause it to fire? We need to make sure it doesn't happen again.” “I stepped on that board to get a closer look at what you were doing,” Erishen explained. “We'll take that one with us,” Archos said, then asked Karnak, “His magic is not on the floor here and I can verify that he did indeed put the rune there. Where might I find the next thread to this mystery?”

“I will warn you first. Your ability to sense magic is very powerful. You will need to be careful on the next stage or you will be seriously injured.” Karnak pointed to the seat of the throne. Archos took the warning seriously. He carefully searched the throne for traces of magic and sensed it well before actually touching the seat. He continued to probe, learning the structure of the magic. Finally, he stepped back stroking his beard. Erishen followed his example. When she finished she turned to Archos and Karnak. “I have not had the pleasure of Ky's continued presence, but if this is his magic that I sense on the throne, then it has been tainted or changed somehow.” “My guess is that it has been changed by being filtered through the body of whomever sat on that throne and traced the rune,” Archos speculated. “May we return to the other rune, please?” Karnak led them to the other rune then stepped aside to let Archos work. Karnak found watching Archos work one of the most enjoyable things about working with The Nine. The mage's precision and thought process fascinated the thantor. He watched as Archos performed the same tests he had performed with Stumpy earlier in the day, then learned as Archos took those tests further. The last thing Archos did was trace the old rune multiple times, then aim his finger down the open passageway. Lightning, weak, but still deadly, arced into the darkness. “Back to the other room, please,” Archos muttered, stroking his beard. When they arrived, Archos studied the new rune, the rune that defiled the original. After he finished his examination, he magically cut the area of wall away and sent it back to the farm where it would wait for him in his room. “We will need to come in here and annihilate all the old runes Ky left behind. First, though, we need to find the one who sat upon that throne.” Archos turned to Karnak, his blue eyes fierce. “You would make me a happy man if you told me you found his corpse in here.” “I wish that I could, my friend.” Karnak led them to the tunnel that had been dug to the surface. “The one we seek left by way of this tunnel. Erishen, do you know his pattern enough to be able to track where he might have gone from there?” “I know the pattern, Karnak,” Erishen purred. “I can only attempt tracking him. The more time that has passed since his exit,

the less chance I have.” “Let us walk out,” Archos said. “I wish to seal this properly so that we can be assured of no more offspring of The Ghost.” They left the goblin tunnels and waited as Archos sealed the area to insure no one would be able to get into the goblin lair until the 'ghost' runes were gone. Then Karnak led them to where Stumpy waited. While Erishen searched for traces of the goblin's magic, Archos sealed his escape route. The group followed as Erishen tracked their prey. Several hours later, they arrived at the ruins of LeVarren Keep. “I hope what we are tracking did not do this,” Erishen said as she scanned the ruins. “I will know soon enough,” Archos answered as he approached the town. “While I do this, see if you can find traces of him that would tell us which way he went next.” It only took Archos a couple minutes before he breathed a sigh of relief. “This is Ky's work. I wonder what they did to be the target of his anger.” “The young elf is thorough, isn't he,” Karnak observed. “When provoked. Usually, his attention would be distracted before he completed something this large. He must have been very angry.” Erishen discovered that the goblin continued in a westward direction after leaving the ruins. The traces told her that the goblin stayed in the area at least one day, maybe longer. After searching through the ruins, they met where the goblin's trail began anew. “I am worried about having something out there that has absorbed that much of Ky's power, but I think we need to return,” Archos said. “It is plain that it did not go near Cragsguard. It appeared to wish to get as far away from there as possible.” “I am in agreement,” Karnak said. “Besides, Delmaria is getting us information on this goblin from Brek. She probably has acquired enough for us to know if the goblin knows what it has absorbed.” Stumpy and Erishen agreed, so the group ported back to the farm.

57 Ghostspawn had been sent to trim the vines on the two wild-elves and Mistress found her thoughts considering all that could go wrong with her plan. There were many minor things that could cause delays, but only one that could ruin everything. She frowned. The loss of Bhk-at would mean the end of an alliance that had lasted decades. Unfortunately,. Bhk-at had several weaknesses. The first and foremost of those was greed. If Bhk-at actually put together enough of her plan, he would not hesitate to use that information to satisfy that greed. By the time Ghostspawn returned from his chore, Mistress had decided to end that threat. She also knew how to do it. Earlier in the day, Mistress had taught Ghostspawn some new spells. Her intention was to give him something that would ensure he did not get bored. The first of these was a lightning strike. The goblin truly enjoyed this spell as he cleared a few trees from the edge of the forest with it. Afterwards, Mistress taught him a simple ignition spell. She was surprised at how well he mastered it and at how effective it was coming from his hands. His blaze, though very small and focused, could melt a rock in seconds. Mistress imagined that this spell would be very effective against a small elf. When the goblin returned from his chore, Mistress took him outside for target practice. She wanted to make sure he would not accidentally burn down her cottage, or destroy something which she did not wish destroyed. After several targets were incinerated, Mistress was convinced enough of his ability to carry out her plan. “What was the last valuable lesson that I taught you?” Mistress asked.

Ghostspawn thought for a moment, then answered, “Never leave evidence lying around.” “Your intelligence seems to be growing. Soon you may even be considered average by human standards. There is another loose-end that I wish you to deal with for me. I want you to use the ignite spell that you have mastered well beyond my expectations.” Ghostspawn grinned at the prospect of using this spell against something that lived. “Where can I find this loose-end?” “I will summon him for you. You must act quickly and you must not miss. Do you understand?” Mistress asked. The goblin nodded. “I look forward to this lesson, Mistress.” They returned to the cabin and Mistress showed the goblin where to stand. The elf would have a difficult time seeing him as he climbed from the trapdoor. Mistress moved to the table so that when Bhk-at looked at her, Ghostspawn would be completely out of his line of sight. Mistress also wanted a clear view of Bhk-at to see the results of Ghostspawn's magic. “Bhk-at, I have your request for that last bit of information,” Mistress called. Seconds later the trap door opened and the small elf stepped into the room. Ghostspawn waited until it took a step away from the trapdoor as Mistress said he would, then cast his spell. The elf had no time to scream as the flames reduced him to ash almost immediately. Mistress smiled and sent the dancing goblin outside so she could clean up. She gathered the ashen remains of Bhk-at and put them in a small glass jar, then sealed the door so that it would not be used again. Afterwards, she went to watch the goblin dancing around the clearing. Something about what had just occurred had given the goblin more pleasure than she thought it should. He did not react this way after he finished with Mena. She would have to find out, that much she knew. Right now did not seem the time to do that.

58 Delmaria and Taelann had been waiting at the council table for nearly an hour by the time Karnak's group returned. Brek had been exhausted by the interview and now slept in Tal's room. Delmaria made sure he would not waken until morning when it would be time to go to Alle-Stecan. "We will need to know what you found out," Archos explained, "before we can make any major conclusions on what we found. The one exception being that the goblin did not go to Cragsguard." "Selia assisted us, which is fortunate," Delmaria said. "Most of what Brek considers knowledge is legend and propaganda. Although, there may have been some truth regarding the legends, it was buried so deep in exaggeration that even Selia could not find it. "I ended up extracting memories from Brek. Taelann has recorded them. Brek was a slave, regarded as worthless and kept around only as long as he did what was told. My guess is that he was given to Ky because his usefulness to the chief had nearly been exhausted. Keep this in mind as his memories are wrought with pain and fear. Brek considered the chief to be larger than life and saw him as such. There was no way to remove this from the memories I've extracted." Taelann arranged a few pieces of bark on the table and said, "Another thing we've learned is that Brek was kept near the chief to serve as fodder should the need arrive. The latter portion of his life was lived in two chambers, so we have a very limited view of what went on with the goblins in general. This fact also has its advantages.

Brek was witness to some very interesting events." "We will not show you all of what we acquired," Delmaria explained. "Not at this time anyway. The memories we have chosen to show you are the ones Taelann, Selia, and through Selia, Symplex and Daelann, and I think are most important." Taelann invoked the first memory. The first meeting between Rachk'sha and the chief goblin formulated above the table. The actors, as Delmaria had predicted, were distorted by the young goblin's perception of them. Parts of the scene lost the visual component and the voices became dreamlike and nightmarish, though enough of the meeting was preserved leaving no doubt that Rachk'sha knew of the memories and their effects on Ky's increasing power. The second memory showed the chief delivering Ky to Rachk'sha. The entire visual portion of this memory focused on Ky and the two thantors that stood to either side of him. Brek's empathy for the elf hanging on the wall permeated the memory. At the point where Rachk'sha sent all but Ky's feet away, Brek's image superimposed itself in the void hanging from the shackles. The third memory showed how the chief goblin used the poisoned bolts against Rachk'sha. Neither the goblin nor Rachk'sha could be seen from Brek's place in the adjacent hallway, but the conversation between them was faithfully remembered. The memory continued as Brek prepared food for the chief. The importance of this part of the memory is in what Brek overheard. Two goblins were speaking in hushed voices about assassinating the chief goblin. Their conversation turned to the many times his assassination had been attempted in the past and they decided it would not be worth their painful deaths to be added to the long list of failures. After the last memory played, Archos asked, "Are there any memories that show the chief goblin actually using magic of any kind?" "No. Brek never witnessed him using magic," Delmaria answered. "Why do you ask?" "We have discovered that this goblin has absorbed quite a bit of Ky's powers through the 'ghost' runes that Ky left in the goblin lair when he hunted there. I can not be sure of the nature of the magic the goblin was able to acquire," Archos explained. "I traced the rune about ten times and was able to produce one of Ky's lightning strikes with the magic I absorbed. It did not have a great deal of power behind it, but those would be quite deadly without much power." Karnak added, "We also know that Rachk'sha was present when Ky acquired Brek. It is my guess that he wanted to kill the goblin in return for that bolt in his back. The fact that this goblin still lives tells me that Rachk'sha could not succeed in killing him."

"After the inheritance ceremony, Stumpy and I are going to destroy all the remaining 'ghost' runes from the goblin tunnels. This will prevent any further siphoning of Ky's residual magic in the future," Archos said as he stood. "We are all due in Alle-Stecan in seven hours. I suggest we rest now. With all we've discovered, we will have to be extremely aware of the goings on around Ky and the children tomorrow." Taelann collected the bark and said, "I'll rest in Alle-Stecan. I want to get there tonight and meet with Sage Tas'lin so that I have an idea of what to expect tomorrow. I'll let you know in the morning what I find out." "I'll be relaxin' at the Cracked Anvil," Stumpy announced as he headed towards the portal. "See ye in the morn!" The farm made accommodations for those remaining for the night. Karnak was the last to leave the council room, wondering what he would have to do to make Brek a valuable member of the Council of Darkness.

59 Ky sat in front of the dead fire waiting for the sun to begin chasing the stars from the eastern sky. He had spent the last couple hours creating memory bark and sending it to a special drawer in his desk in Chaos. Sometime during the trip, he had gone from leader to member. He had found a part of himself he did not know existed: his childhood. He grieved knowing that the moment he rode through the gates of Alle-Stecan, he would lose it again. Ky vowed not to lose the memory of it. He made memories of games, stories, songs, and even expressions, anything he could grasp that would let him keep hold of the innocence he had enjoyed these last few days. As he waited for the sun, he searched his life for other times when he enjoyed childhood. The closest he found was during the time Little Ky was growing up at the farm. Even then, his role was father, not brother or playmate. These last two days he had been both brother and playmate and he wondered if he would ever get a chance to do it again. The first few stars faded on the horizon and Ky smiled. He was not at the elven city yet. He re-lit the fire and started making breakfast. The children began to awaken to the smells of the spiced oats that drifted into their tents. Eleana was the first to the fire and began cutting up apples, throwing them into a pot with cinnamon and syrup. As the rest of the group approached the fire, Ky summoned mugs of cold milk and pear juice. Ky had started the day early. After breakfast, he announced that they had a couple hours to enjoy themselves before they had to begin riding again. This was met with cheers and Simon tapping on

Ky's shoulder, yelling, "You're the ogre!" before darting out of reach. The small grove was filled with laughter and screeches of joy until it was time to finish their journey. The remaining portion of the ride would last about two hours. Unlike the previous days, where Ky rode ahead of the children, he rode with them. As the journey neared its completion, Ky began to worry about why the passage still protected them. He hoped there would be no problems with this day. He had too much planned. His worry quieted the group and the last few miles of the ride were spent in anxiety as to what they would find at its conclusion. When the passage finally dispersed, the group found itself within the walls of Alle-Stecan. Their sudden appearance startled those waiting for them as much as the city's sudden appearance startled them. Ky knew that something serious was happening outside the walls of the city and, if given half a chance, someone would try to distract him away from his plans. He slid off his horse and handed the reigns to Prince Stel-Ky, saying, "Take the children, except Simon, to the square." Turning, he found Brek and took his hand. The two vanished before anyone could say anything to either of them. Ky reappeared a moment later and found Sage-Tas'lin. "Make sure everyone that needs to be in the square is headed there now," Ky said. "All but the king will be there when you arrive," Sage Tas'lin said. "For the king's protection, we are keeping him in the palace until the ceremony begins." "Wrong," Ky said. "The king will go to the square now, or he will not go. Anyone not in the square when I get there, with the exception of Simon, will not be able to enter. See that the king is there," Ky finished, turning away to locate Simon.

60 "Wait here," Ky instructed as he and Brek appeared at the end of the path near the stream. "The Lady will explain things to you." Ky grinned and left. Brek only had to wait a few seconds before he saw The Lady approaching down the path. He tried to control the shaking in his knees with little success. No one had warned him of this trip and his own self-doubt had him believing it was a one-way journey. "Greetings, Brek. I am The Lady. I welcome you to my home. Come, take my hand and walk with me." Brek did as she asked. He decided he wanted to know right away what was happening, so he said, "Brek think Lord Ky found out Brek was only a slave that Chief wanted to get rid of so Brek here to be gotten rid of by Lord Ky." The Lady smiled at Brek. "My son knew who and what you were before he took you from the goblin caves. You would not be here if he wanted to get rid of you. You are here to be prepared for the next phase of your life." "Brek not understand. If Lord Ky knew Brek was weak and worthless slave, why Lord Ky choose Brek?" "Lord Ky can see more than what others see. He can look at someone and see their potential. He can see their spirit," The Lady said, her voice almost a whisper as if sharing a secret with the goblin. "What else worries you, my young friend?" "Brek has a spirit?" "Yes!" The Lady answered. "Your spirit is very strong. Now, about those other worries..."

They walked a while quietly, The Lady allowing Brek to gather his thoughts. When Brek finally voiced his concern, his voice was low, as if he feared being overheard. "Brek worried about Lord Karnak." "What about Lord Karnak worries you?" "Brek is supposed to be on Council of Darkness, yet Brek not really evil enough. Brek think Lord Karnak will not want Brek." They had returned to the stream by then, so The Lady put his concern aside for a moment and explained, "As part of the preparation for today, you will need to be cleansed. The stream will do that for you if it will accept you. I do not wish it to harm you, so we will test it before I let you swim." "Brek not like water." The Lady laughed. "That's okay. The important thing right now is to find out if water not like Brek. Please, put your finger in the stream and tell me if you feel any pain." Brek frowned, but did as he was asked. His frown disappeared almost immediately. "Brek not feel water like this before. Brek wonders if it is magic water?" "Yes, it is magic water. Did you feel any pain?" "Brek only feel pleasure from water. Brek feel no pain." "Good. Leave your tunic here and swim around in the center of the pool. While you do that, I will speak of your worry and sing you a song if you like." "Brek like," he said as he yanked his tunic off. The Lady watched him carefully as he rushed to the center of the pool and sat. His toothy grin assured her that the waters had accepted him. Smiling, she sat beneath the tree and eased his worry. "Lord Karnak only knows you as you were before coming here. Although you are a goblin, and evil by nature, you have yet to accept that for yourself. When Lord Ky finishes with you today, Lord Karnak will have a much better appreciation of you." Then she began to sing for the goblin. When the time was right, she held the towel for the goblin and helped dry him when he left the stream. She waited while he put his tunic on, then held him. Being held was something Brek had never experienced. He wondered if the feelings he experienced were goblin feelings, as they felt very unlike anything a goblin would feel. He had little time to think on the matter because The Lady's lullaby lured him into a deep sleep. Ky arrived with Simon a few moments later. As Ky accepted Brek, he whispered, "You won't forget about Illya and Stan, will you?" The Lady smiled. "They will be there. I promised you that." "What is the other ceremony you wished to add today?" Ky

asked. "William and Daphnia will be married today," The Lady explained. Ky almost dropped Brek. "When did this happen?" The Lady kissed Ky on the forehead and answered, "You weren't the only one having fun these past few days. While you wait, see if you can think of a good bridesmaid for Daphnia." Ky thought for a second, then said, "Illya. There is no other that could do it." He grinned and vanished. As soon as Ky had gone, The Lady led Simon deep into The Garden. They settled near the largest of the willow trees which had been Simon's favorite place to play. When they were seated, The Lady explained why she had asked to see him. "Maker has left us to our own devices," she explained. Simon's eyes widened and his mouth fell open in disbelief. "It is true. Before he left he told me that there are two possible futures for us. One is dependent on your strength. As much as it grieves me, I'm afraid you will have to end your years of innocence early. The other path is far too grim to even consider." "You know I will do anything to make you happy," Simon murmured. "Does the other path have something to do with Ky?" The Lady shook her head. "Ky is the cause of the two paths. He has nothing to do with their outcome if Maker is to be believed." "Who, then?" Simon asked. The Lady sighed, then answered, "You have a sister. Where you are kind, good, caring and loving, she is just the opposite. She is the one responsible for the other future." Simon shivered. "I hope I don't let you down." "I know you will do everything you can. I hope that you are ready when the time comes for you." The Lady smiled and hugged him tightly. "You have something to ask me. What is it?" Simon shared the memory he and Ky had taken from Tal. At its conclusion, he asked, "Do you know of any reason why that would happen?" The Lady brushed a tear from her cheek and answered, "Oh, that I did. We will have to watch Tal carefully today. Let me hold you a few moments more, then we must be going." "Will you sing for me?" Simon murmured as he rested his head on her shoulder. The Lady stroked Simon's hair with her fingertips and asked, "What song would you like to hear?" "Hmm... I think I want to hear the song about the finch that always missed the branch when he tried to land," said Simon. The Lady began singing. She remembered the song well even

though she had not sung it for him in a long time. It was Simon's favorite when he was very young and had to hear it every time he fell from a tree he was attempting to climb. After the song was over, The Lady helped Simon from her lap and told him, "I must see to Illya and Stan. I'll return for you when I'm done." She left him by the willow. Simon knew enough about The Garden to know he had time to investigate. The Lady would arrive when he was ready, so he walked along the paths to the Arch of Mists and found it dark and dead. A tear slowly slid down his cheek. He had met Maker only once, but he knew Maker was his father and he missed him. "Please come back to us," Simon prayed, then turned and walked back to the willow to wait for The Lady, wiping the tear away.

61 Sage Tas'lin scanned the square. Ky had left him with a hastily drawn diagram of what he needed. The Sage had to make a couple minor adjustments to make it work. It was in this square that Daelann and Aemar had received their spirit-sendings. It was the largest open area in the city. Sage Tas'lin thought about questioning the elf about why he wanted so much space and why it had to be outside, but reconsidered. He doubted he would have received an answer. The king's throne sat at the far end of the square closest to the palace, towards the back of a raised platform. To its right stood the strange instrument which William called a piano. Opposite the piano were eight chairs. Six of them were occupied by the children. The two ends remained empty, waiting for Simon and Brek. Two hundred seats lined either side of the square with another hundred across the back. The seats in the back were divided allowing the only entrance to the square. Sage Tas'lin liked this arrangement as it made security much easier. All of the guests were seated except for the two who would sit beside the Combined Council. Ky said they would be arriving shortly after he arrived. Again, Sage Tas'lin did not ask questions. As he checked to make sure the guards, chosen by Prince Stel-Ky, were in place, the prince arrived escorting Brek to his seat. -Sage Tas'lin, Delmaria, Daphnia and Illya will need a room near the entrance. Accommodate them. Delmaria and Daphnia are already heading to you.- Sage Tas'lin had never before received a message from Ky in

this manner and it surprised him for a moment. He barely had enough time to find an empty room in one of the buildings nearby when Delmaria and Daphnia arrived at the entrance. Sage Tas'lin showed them where to go, then returned to his place. Minutes later, Ky arrived. The small elf's appearance shocked the old elf more than the voice inside his head. Ky wore a dark green tunic bound at his waist by a golden belt. The tunic covered Ky's upper body down to the center of his thighs. On his back, he wore a cloak that appeared to be green flames somehow stitched together, that curled and billowed softly as he walked. The sage bowed as the elf passed him then watched as the elf walked across the square. It was then that the sage realized he had not provided a seat for Lord Ky. Until Ky arrived, many quiet conversations filled the square. They all ceased simultaneously as everyone stood and watched the elf walk to the platform. The king noticed the absence of a seat for Ky and offered the throne. Ky glanced at it, seeing a prison with bars made of responsibility and diplomacy, then declined, kneeling on the platform a few feet to the side of the throne. -I'm glad you could make it, Illya. I hope you don't mind that I volunteered you to be Daphnia's bridesmaid. She and Delmaria are waiting for you. See Sage Tas'lin at the entrance.- Illya smiled and tried to answer Ky's message but sensed that the communication was one way. She hurried across the square to find Sage Tas'lin. The Lady thought to Ky, -My son, Archos still bears the wounds from his error. May I heal them before we begin?- Ky glanced at Archos, then nodded. -Simon, I want you beside me. I will need your strength today,- Ky thought, as Simon was walking to his seat with the other children. Simon smiled and joined Ky on the platform. -What did she say?- Ky asked Simon. -She said she wished she knew why it happened. We will both be watching Tal closely today,- Simon answered. -Before I begin,- The Lady thought to Ky, -I ask you to think of a way to help your brother. He is not ready for what he will have to face if things go wrong.- -I will have some idea by the end of the wedding,- Ky answered. Ky stood and addressed the square, "Stand and greet The Lady." Then he thought to her, -Daphnia is having a problem. Get set up while I deal with it.- -Be gentle, my son,- The Lady replied as she appeared in the center of the platform. With The Lady's appearance, Ky's form melted in green flames and vanished. While The Lady set the stage for the

wedding, Ky arrived in the small room where Daphnia sat sobbing between Delmaria and Illya. Ky stepped in front of her and asked, "What is the problem?" "Trees be fallin'! Look at me. The dress be so beautiful and it be coverin' an ugly old hag such as I be bein'. Trees be fallin'!" she exclaimed as she burst into another fit of tears. "Stop!" Ky demanded, deciding that gentle would waste too much time. "Look at me," he said more quietly. "Look into my eyes and see what William sees when he looks at you." "Trees be fallin'! He must be thinkin' I be horrible." Ky grabbed her chin. "Shut up and look!" Ky's grip was strong and it shocked Daphnia. She looked into his eyes to beg him to let go and saw herself reflected there. The vision she saw was not ugly or old, though it was definitely her. She held onto the vision, her sobs slowly ebbing. "Ye would nae be lyin' to me, demon child?" Ky released her chin. "I am not the one looking," he explained. "I don't even know what you saw. I just took a chance." He stepped away from Daphnia and said, "You need to return, Delmaria, the ceremony is starting." With a smile towards Illya, he was gone, returning to his place on the platform. Delmaria ported to Archos' side and took his hand, smiling. As if waiting for her return, the elves began to sing the elven bridal song as Daphnia and Illya slowly walked to the platform where The Lady, William, and Tasenta-Somar waited. The Lady took her time, enjoying the wedding. After the vows she asked, "Is there anyone present who believes this union should not be sealed?" She waited a moment, then looked at Micah, "Anyone?" she asked. Micah smiled and quickly shook his head. "Then I pronounce this bond sealed by the rings they wear. Let their love grow from this moment onward." She smiled and said to William, "I believe it is time to kiss the bride." William nodded and raised Daphnia's veil, took her in his arms, and kissed her to the cheers of all gathered. -Time is not affecting us here. Feel free to celebrate.- Ky thought to William. Ky was the first to congratulate William and Daphnia. Afterwards, all that knew them got a chance to do the same. Daphnia's chair was moved beside the piano so the two could be close for the remainder of the day. When the celebration had settled, Ky thought to Simon, - Follow me,- then walked to the front of the platform. He motioned for Simon to wait, then stepped forward and knelt before The Lady. He

put his hands, palms upward in front of him and closed his eyes. Magic, in the form of fire and lightning arced in the air between his hand and solidified into a blazing sword which he raised and offered to The Lady. After she accepted it, he stepped back and nudged Simon forward. Simon followed Ky's example and knelt before The Lady and put his hands out before himself, palms up. That's where it ended for Simon. He had no idea how to summon magic to create a sword the way his brother had just done, so he waited. The Lady lowered the sword into Simon's hands. As he accepted it, it spoke to him. "I can not give you all the knowledge you will need at one time for your mind will not accept it and retain its sanity. Instead, I will give you knowledge when you need it. Grasp my hilt whenever you seek guidance." Simon bowed to The Lady and stepped back beside Ky. "Thank you," Simon whispered, then followed Ky to their seats beside the throne. Ky waited until The Lady had seated herself behind Simon, then moved to the center of the platform. He called Micah, Brek and Aemir to join him. "There are several paths one can take to become a god. The Nine and The Council of Darkness became gods and goddesses by replacing those before them. That method is carved from sorrow and blood. Today, these three will be walking a different path. They will be invited and deified without loss of blood. “The leader of The Nine, and the leader of the Council of Darkness, come forward to claim your newest members." Ky waited as Archos and Karnak moved to the platform. Archos stood behind Aemir, Karnak behind Brek. Archos told Aemir to kneel as Ky stepped towards them. Ky placed his hand on Aemir's head and the young high-elf glowed with a white aura laced with the colors of the rainbow. As Archos moved to stand behind Micah, Ky moved to Brek. Brek, seeing what Aemir had done, did not need Karnak to tell him to kneel. Ky placed his hand on the goblins head and Brek also began to glow. His aura was laced with a rainbow of colors; however, it was darker and more menacing to behold. Ky grinned and approached Micah. Micah knelt as Ky stepped in front of him. Ky's hand on Micah's head produced an aura that was pure white and brilliant. Ky returned to the center of the platform and signaled the three youths to stand. Then he bowed to them. When he stood, he told them to turn and face the square. Archos and Karnak returned to their places and on their signal everyone bowed before the three boys.

As they returned to their seats, Ky asked Little Ky, Eleana, Tal and Ky II to come forward. He spoke into each of their minds, telling them to remain standing and relax. The Lady and Simon moved to stand behind Ky as he approached Little Ky. Ky uttered a long phrase of magic which became tangible enough for even those seated farthest from the platform to feel. When he finished, Little Ky was bathed in glaring white flames. The flames stay with his son as Ky moved to Eleana and began another long phrase of magic. Eleana was bathed in green flames. Ky moved to Tal. Ky took a deep breath, then uttered a new phrase of magic. At its completion, Tal's body was bathed in arcs of lightning. Ky hesitated a moment before moving to Ky II. Again, he uttered a new phrase of magic which caused Ky II's body to be bathed in the flames of Chaos. Ky returned to the center of the platform and The Lady began to sing. Magic from the song joined the children with their father. As the song progressed Ky was bathed in the magical auras that surrounded the children. The auras enveloped the young Lord of Chaos becoming one aura, intensifying, and becoming blindingly brilliant until the song's end, then vanished. "That is my first gift to you," Ky whispered. "May it serve you well." The children did not need to ask the nature of the gift. They knew that their father had just protected them with his own life and his own magic. As one, they bowed, then rushed forward to hug their father. Ky gave them all the time they needed hugging each one until they relaxed the embrace. When the children were satisfied, Ky sent Little Ky back to his seat and nodded to King Stel-Tasan. The king came forward and began the inheritance ceremony as Ky, joined by Laena moved to stand behind Eleana. As the introductory portion of the ceremony was proceeding, The Lady spoke with Simon. -Do you understand what Ky has just done?- she asked. -Not really,- Simon answered. -Ky has given them a gift, a gift born of the love he has for them. He has protected them so if any mortal danger should come their way, it will be redirected to Ky. It is that deed, that selfless deed, that Maker predicts will cause immense pain and terrible suffering.- -How can that be?- Simon asked. -Maker believes the triplets will be used to bring about the downfall of Ky. That is why you must be strong. Use Ky's gift to you wisely, Simon. Also, believe in yourself. You will be everything Ky is now. You will have the same powers and abilities. Hopefully with the knowledge he has given you, it will be enough to make things right.- At this point, the king had moved to stand before Eleana,

who knelt and bowed before him. "I present, Ean-Eleana, first born of the triplets to Lord Ky and Lady Laena. Are her parents prepared to offer to her a gift that would mark her as ready to accept the responsibilities of adulthood? Should this child be accepted into adult society?" Ky slouched slightly and rubbed his chin, shrugging. Then he whispered something to Laena. She thought for a moment and whispered something back. They looked at each other a second, then nodded. "Barely," Ky answered, grinning, "but yes." Prince Stel-Ky came forward and handed the king a foot- long branch of oak. The king looked at it for a moment, then asked, "This?" Ky shook his head and raised his hand in the air. The sky above the square crackled with lightning as a rift opened, allowing a fifty-foot, golden dragon to soar above the crowd. The dragon circled the square once, then gracefully landed in the center. Then it began to rapidly shrink and took flight again, its target the branch in the king's hand. After the dragon had wrapped its tail around the branch for balance, King Stel-Tasan handed it to Eleana. Immediately upon accepting the dragon, Eleana's aura pulsated around her. Although it had a grayish tint, with streaks of darkness flowing through it, its brilliance was blinding. The king shielded his eyes and backed away as Eleana sat cross-legged on the platform and stroked her dragon. King Stel-Tasan approached Tal next, saying, "I present, Sean-Tal, second born of the triplets to Lord Ky and Lady Laena. Are his parents prepared to offer to him a gift that would mark him as ready to accept the responsibilities of adulthood? Should this child be accepted into adult society?" Once again, Ky and Laena whispered back and forth. This time the conversation lasted several minutes. It ended when Ky firmly shook his head 'no' causing Laena to cross her arms and turn her back on him. The king looked on in shock. He could not believe that after all the trouble to get this ceremony set up, Ky was going to deny Tal his inheritance. Tal and Prince Stel-Ky knew better and stood waiting patiently, both amused by the king's reaction. "Was that 'no' the answer to my questions?" King Stel-Tasan asked. "Of course not," Ky answered. "He's ready, let him have it." The king received a second branch, this one birch, from Prince Stel-Ky and waited. Once again the sky filled with lightning and burst open. This time the dragon sported platinum scales of pure

white. It circled the square once then landed. Just like Eleana's, this dragon rapidly shrunk and soared to the branch in the king's hands. The king offered the branch with one hand and shielded his eyes with the other. It was not enough. Tal's aura burst forth around the elf intensely white and more blinding than the sun. Ky laughed at the expense of the king, but his laughter was drowned by the exclamations of awe that filled the square from the guests. Although Tal sat cross-legged on the platform like his sister, only Ky, Simon and The Lady could look at him long enough to see him. "Praise Tasenta, there is only one more," the king muttered as he approached Ky II. "I present, Sean-Ky II, third born of the triplets to Lord Ky and Lady Laena. Are his parents prepared to offer to him a gift that would mark him as ready to accept the responsibilities of adulthood? Should this child be accepted into adult society?" Laena glanced at Ky as if to say, 'You would know best.' Ky whispered in her ear anyway then took a step back. Laena smiled at him then turned to the king. "He is ready," she said. "I'm not sure I am," the king murmured as he accepted the branch, this one ash, from Prince Stel-Ky. Ky raised his arm again. This time the sky erupted into flames, the roar of which became drowned out by another roar as Ky II's dragon entered the square. It was difficult to determine the coloration of the dragon's scales. They were dark, but changed color as the muscles beneath them moved. It followed the same path as the previous dragons. When it had landed on the dowel, the king presented it to Ky II. Ky II's aura was not as blinding as his sibling's. What it lacked in brilliance, it made up for in its mesmerizing rainbow of colors, both dark and light. Ky II joined his brother and sister, sitting cross-legged on the platform. When the king returned to his throne, Ky signaled William. The piano music filled the square with Mozart's “Alleluja.” At its completion, Ky joined William on the piano bench and sang Mozart's “Ave Verum Corpus” while William played. Then the celebration began. Ky knew he had to give the guests time to congratulate both the triplets and William and Daphnia. As the celebration progressed, Ky spoke with the king. "Celebrate as long as you wish, King Stel-Tasan," Ky whispered. "Time has been stopped in the square and will remain so until you end the celebration. We will not help you with the problems you are facing, but I know you have the tools to deal with it. There will be loss and sorrow, but you should prevail." "I take courage in your confidence," the king admitted. "I also know that I cannot rely on the gods every time a problem arises.

It would make us weak and we need to be strong." "One final thing," Ky said, grinning. "Thank you for today." The king smiled, answering, "Thank you as well. I know I will never forget the wonders I have witnessed today. You have given me memories that will last forever." As Ky turned away from the king, he noticed Simon walking away from Sage Tas'lin. Ky frowned and quickly walked to the Sage. "What are you doing?" Ky asked. "Just trying to determine for sure if Simon is your brother," Sage Tas'lin answered. Ky placed his hand on the tome that sat open on Sage Tas'lin's lap. A quick flare of white light encompassed the book. Then Ky grabbed Sage Tas'lin's collar. "Simon is just a boy. He will remain just a boy as long as he can. You will not steal his childhood like mine was stolen from me. Do you understand?" The old elf nodded, his face solemn. "My apologies, Milord. I meant no harm. I will do as you request." "You have no choice," Ky stated as he left the Sage. Ky kept himself apart from the celebration, watching from behind the scenes. He knew another party would be started as soon as the close group of friends left here. Although the magic he used today had weakened him, he knew that the elves had gained a greater understanding of him. Occasionally, one would see him and tap whoever was beside them, share excited whispers, then bow low before turning away. This happened whether they noticed Ky saw them or not. Ky also noticed that Karnak's interest in Brek had increased. The thantor appeared to be proud of the newest addition to his council. Karnak also had his eyes on Eleana which did not surprise Ky. Her aura spoke of neutrality with evil tendencies. Eleana, Ky knew, would also be a valuable addition to Karnak's council. Tal was destined for The Nine. There was no doubt from his aura that he would be the perfect replacement for Selia. Ky knew that Selia would be very proud of Tal, and planned to let her know as soon as possible. His other son, Ky II, would replace Ky as Lord of Chaos. Which council he sat on depended on which needed him most. It would be Ky II's decision, ultimately. After giving the elves ample time to celebrate with the gods, Ky announced that they would be leaving. Prince Stel-Ky immediately began clearing the center of the square. Ky rounded up Little Ky and Micah as the square was being vacated. Then he summoned his own dragon, this one having emerald green scales. Once the three of them were on the dragon's back, they took off, circling the city. Eleana

followed, bringing Brek with her. Tal followed her with Aemir. Finally, Ky II with Simon joined the circling dragons. The Lady made sure that Illya and Stan made it to the farm safely before returning to The Garden. Afterwards, one by one, the members of the Combined Council returned to the farm. Delmaria brought William and Daphnia with her. Illya, with the help of Tobit's family had prepared the farm for the private party. The area between the farm and the barn closely resembled the celebration after Little Ky's inheritance over two-thousand years before. Stan brought a wedding cake for William and Daphnia as well. Those that ported to the farm only had to wait half an hour for the children to arrive. They used the wilderness south of the farm to land the dragons, then raced to the farmhouse. Ky joined this party, finding it a perfect time to play tag, sing, laugh and tell stories. Only the other children had seen this side of the young elf. Soon, his playfulness became infectious. And the gods found themselves acting like children for a few hours. The high-elf refugees were invited to join the festivities. A few of them, particularly the children, accepted the invitation. Most of the others were content to watch or stay in their rooms and enjoy the company of their siblings and close friends. In early evening, dinner was served. William and Daphnia cut the cake afterwards and shared it for dessert. Tobit's family offered their cottage by the sea for William and Daphnia to get away alone for a week. After a trivial amount of persuasion, the couple accepted. They remained at the party until sunset, then said their farewells. "Be good, Micah," William said as he hugged the boy. "And be careful riding your skateboard." "But the Old Man is here," Micah complained, causing them both to laugh. "Trees be fallin'! Think ye can spare a hug fer yer mother?" Daphnia asked. Micah smiled and ran into her arms, almost knocking her over. Daphnia squeezed him tightly. "Um, mom, I'm skinny enough already!" Micah exclaimed squeezing back. "We'll be back in a week," William told Micah. "See you then!" Micah smiled and waved, then said, "Oh. While you're there, would you do me a favor?" "Sure. What do you need?" William asked. Micah tilted his head and grinned as he had seen Ky do, then answered, "I've always wanted a little brother." Laughing, he ran to catch up with the rest of the children.

"Trees be fallin'!" Daphnia exclaimed, fanning herself. William placed his hands across her shoulder and laughed. "Just think what he's going to be like after another week with Ky." Daphnia's reaction was lost as Tobit had ported them away. The high-elves left the party shortly after dinner. The other guests remained at the tables until William and Daphnia departed for the seacoast. Afterwards, Ky's group, which now included Illya and Brek wandered to a far corner of the farm where they built a small fire. "I can't believe you flew right into those high-elves outside the city this afternoon," Tal said. "I just wanted to see them. I forgot that The Lady was protecting the people in the square from the dragon's fear aura," Ky explained. "It looked like they were there to fight a war or something," Eleana added. "I think they were," Ky said. "They must be the reason why the passage didn't fall until we were inside the city." Tal asked, "What were you and mom talking about when it was my turn. It took you forever." Ky laughed. "After Eleana received her dragon, her aura nearly blinded the king. After seeing hers, I had a pretty good idea of what yours would be like. Laena was trying to convince me to give the king something to shield his eyes. I was enjoying watching him get blinded by you three, so I refused." "That was funny," Eleana said. "And then Tal glowed so bright, he outshone the sun!" Ky opened a small sack. He pulled a few pieces of meat out and tossed them to the triplets. "Make sure you keep your dragons fed. Feed them while they are small, unless you want to find a few horses every time they get hungry." "Are you sure they won't get hungry after they get big again?" Ky II asked. "This isn't enough to keep me from getting hungry." "Yep. I've been doing it this way for years. All seven of my dragons have always been happy." "Wow!" Micah said. "You've got seven dragons?" Ky nodded. "Who's turn to tell a story is it?" Eleana said, "I would say Illya or Brek. Neither of them have told a story yet." "They haven't heard any either," Ky said, grinning. "That means you get to start." "Why do I have the feeling that you knew I would do that?" Eleana asked.

"I didn't know who would do it. You just beat the others to it." The group stayed around the campfire for the rest of the night. The others at the farm only heard them when they sang and stopped their own conversations during those times to listen. Shortly after the children left the party, Archos and Karnak went into the council room to discuss what needed to be done. "When do you intend to let Ky know what is going on?" Karnak asked. "I don't," Archos said, raising his hand to calm Karnak. "I had an interesting conversation with The Lady this afternoon. Ky has problems to deal with so massive, you and I could not even fathom them. He is no longer one of us. The Lady is giving him a few more days to enjoy his newly found childhood before calling him away." Karnak began pacing, hissing quietly as he thought. "This creature is a creation of Ky's magic. How are we supposed to deal with it?" Archos smiled and answered, "I asked The Lady that exact question. She gave me something to think about. She asked me if the creature was created before or after Ky's inheritance. I told her that it most likely would have happened before. She said that he could only absorb Ky's latent power. Unless it finds some way to learn how to control magic, what it has absorbed will be of little use to it." "So we can destroy it. Is that what you are saying?" "Yes, though it will not be easy. The goblin will be immortal. But its immortality will be like yours and mine." Archos paused and stroked his beard a few moments. "Besides, I think we have an ally that will be quite helpful." "Who might that be?" Karnak asked, returning to the table. "The Old Man. He is one of the old gods, brother to Rachk'sha. His power combined with our magic should make the job quite doable." "Will he help us?" Archos nodded and smiled. "I've already asked him and he has agreed. We will have to find the creature first. Then he will help us destroy it before it can do any damage." "First we have to remove the 'ghost' runes from the goblin caves," Karnak said. "I will go with you when you do that. I would like to examine those bodies one last time. Then I think they should be burned." "I agree. Even goblins deserve that little bit of respect," Archos said as he stood. "Shall we return to the others." Karnak agreed. "It has been a very interesting day, has it not?"

"Aye, my friend. One I will not forget for a long time." They returned to the party. About an hour later, Tobit returned as well. He explained that he had stayed to show William and Daphnia around the small fishing village and to introduce them to a few of the people who lived there. He felt their stay would be much more enjoyable if they did not have to waste time finding things and had more time to have fun. The adult portion of the party lasted well into the night. As the party neared its end, they all helped with clean-up. No one worried about the children. They knew they were safe in Ky's care. Besides, there was very little on the planet that could stand against the four dragons that accompanied the children.

62 Ky's curiosity outside the walls of Alle-Stecan had a far greater impact than he imagined. The summoning of the four dragons was the only thing that could be seen from the hills around the city and many of the rebel elves bent on a civil war were disheartened before Ky and the children left. The flight of dragons that exited the city after the ceremony took the fight out of what remained. Within hours, the leaders of the rebellion were voluntarily surrendering at the city gates. These were brought before King Stel- Tasan for sentencing. By rights, the king could have locked them away for years. Instead, he sentenced them to help rebuild the homes they had destroyed as well as set up the inheritance ceremonies for the twins and triplets that needed them. They were given the responsibility of making suitable gifts that would signify their acceptance into society. These decisions did more to return peace to the high-elven kingdom than Ky's dragons. As the work started, Sage Tas'lin was given the chore to organize a welcome back celebration for all the refugees. By morning of the next day, a note was sent to Archos explaining that it was time for the high-elves to return home. By mid-morning, all the elven twins and triplets were being reunited with their families and friends. A second day of celebration was held in Alle-Stecan for them. Although this celebration was not on the same scale of what Ky had done the day before, many believed it to be much more rewarding. The king spent most of the day granting societal acceptance and was quite happy that he was not blinded even once by the recipients.

63 From their vantage on the roof of Maltar manor, the three deep- elves could see the barracks room where the children stayed, the practice grounds where they trained and also had a distant view of the entrance to Cragsguard. Normally, they would be positioned apart from each other, but no sign of the children had been seen in town over the past week and they had become bored. The only activity they witnessed was when an old bearded man spent a few hours in the children's room. The goblin had been with him, but the three elves they were sent to spy on were not seen. The other reason for their staying close together came about the same day the old bearded man came. Since then, the guards in town not only increased, but they became more vigilant. Two of the observation points the deep-elves had once haunted were no longer safe. This knowledge came at the price of one of the town's guards. This guard had found one of the deep-elf posts and quickly died as a result. His body provided the three deep-elves with blood over the past two days. Then they discarded his bloodless corpse over the back wall of the keep. They had sent word to Bhk-at about the bearded old man and now waited to hear what they should do. They expected to be able to leave Cragsguard since their purpose for being there was no longer present. This night, only a small sliver of the moon could be seen, that is, it could be seen when the heavy clouds did not block it from view. The three deep-elves sat quietly on the roof, having little to talk about and even less to do. Then they caught the scent of blood from

the back wall of the keep. They quickly checked the barracks window, then, seeing no change, went to investigate. They found a dwarf, bleeding profusely, yet still living, leaning on the battlements of the back wall. A trail of blood showed them that he had crawled to this spot before becoming to weak to go any farther. They considered the dwarf to be a gift from the gods and began to drink his blood before any more could be wasted on the stone walkway. Their thirst and the need for haste completely blinded them to the fact that the blood was tainted. They drained the dwarf's body, then lost their will to return to the safety of the roof. Instead, they huddled in the shadow of the dwarf and fell into a deep coma. Mistress waited and watched as the deep-elves drank themselves into a stupor. She had thought one of them would have been cautious, and was pleasantly surprised when they disappointed her. She had found the entrance to the dwarven citadel earlier that night. The dwarves were looking for something and it did not take her long to find the gates to their realm. She guessed that the young dwarf who had aided her with poisoning one of the children of the Lord of Chaos was the subject of their search. The dwarf that now rested on the wall of Cragsguard verified that for her before she brought him here. She told him she knew where the lass could be found and led him up here, feeding him poison disguised as dwarven ale. When they had gotten close to where she thought the deep-elves would be, she cut his larynx from his throat and amused herself watching him as he tried to crawl away. Then all three deep-elves arrived and drank the poison that she had put in the dwarf's blood. She marveled at how easily things were going for her. Mistress summoned a large bag and approached the dwarf and the three deep-elves. She had thought she would have to deal with the town guard, but he was not due to pass this way for a while. She knew, from previous experiments, that the dwarf would crumble to earth if cut into pieces. She also knew that the smaller the pieces were, the faster this decay occurred. She needed this dwarf to be around long enough to be found by the others, so she cut him into rather large pieces and placed them in her bag. Then she put the three deep-elves into another, smaller bag and left town. She did not bother cleaning the mess on the wall as she had no plans of returning to Cragsguard, and she knew a body lay outside the wall that would give reason for the blood. The next part of her plan would provide more of a challenge. She needed to put the dwarf and the deep-elves where they could be found by the other dwarves. Although she would remain invisible, the dwarf would become plainly visible while she set up her

ruse. Mistress also knew that the darkness of the night would not be her ally. Dwarves had excellent night vision. She had to be close enough to the entrance of the dwarven citadel so the dwarf would be found before he completely decayed. The deep-elves would be found with him. Mistress knew that the deep- elves would be blamed for the younger dwarf's disappearance. Mistress regretted not knowing of this realm of dwarves earlier. Had she known, she would have planted one of the young dwarf's possessions on the deep-elves. Regardless, she knew that these elves had no knowledge of her. Only Bhk-at knew of Mistress and he was not in any condition to reveal what he knew. Mistress got as close to the dwarven fortress as she dared and quickly set up the death of the dwarf. She made sure to embed one of the deep-elf's darts into the dwarf's neck. His beard would be one of the last things to decay and would keep the dart in place for her. Then she placed the comatose deep-elves nearby. Satisfied, she ported back to her cabin. She found Ghostspawn tending to the two wild-elves. The goblin had learned that the incense caused the elves to see things in a grotesquely distorted manner and used this information to torture the elves as he trimmed their vines or fed them. Mistress saw no peril in this and allowed the goblin his fun. She knew that it kept him interested in his task. She watched him from a distance as he worked. As she watched, she wondered about his fire spell. The spell she taught him should have been much weaker than what he was producing. At best, he should be able to set twigs aflame. Instead, his flames melted rock, both completely and quickly. She knew that the essence from the elf he had taken would increase his abilities, but it should not have had this effect. Her guess was that the magic he absorbed from the Lord of Chaos was enhancing his magic. She decided she needed to find out more of her apprentice's prior habits. Sooner or later, he would reveal how he had stolen The Ghost's magical powers. With that knowledge, she would follow his lead, stealing what she could while waiting for the child of the Lord of Chaos to arrive in the elven capital. Ghostspawn got the female wood-elf to scream one last time before turning away from them. He saw Mistress watching him and went to her. "Your shift began an hour ago, where have you been?" Ghostspawn asked. Mistress frowned at the goblin's tone, but decided to answer. "I was taking care of some loose-ends with our little deep-elf friend. The deep-elves will blame the dwarves for Bhk-at's disappearance and the dwarves will blame the deep-elves for the young goblin you had

such fun with the other day." "When is the god coming?" Ghostspawn asked. "Human essence is getting boring." Mistress laughed. "My little goblin friend, we can not hurry the god. He or she is scheduled to begin lessons with Sage Tas'lin. When that begins, we will have essence of god to quell your boredom." She led him to her cabin, saying, "Come, tell me about your old home." Ghostspawn felt compelled to do as Mistress asked. He followed her into the cabin and they sat at the table talking of his home in the canyon outside Cragsguard. She asked many questions, which the goblin answered. When the goblin began to speak of the 'ghost' runes that could be found throughout the tunnels, Mistress became very interested. Ghostspawn explained that the earliest ones, most of which had faded with time, were put up as a warning by the goblins that The Ghost had been there and goblins had died. When The Ghost realized they were doing this, he started putting the runes up himself. All the runes he put on the walls survived through time. Mistress could tell that the goblin was very proud of the fact that he knew where every one of these runes were and he had visited them frequently. Finally, Mistress had Ghostspawn teach her some of the goblin runes. They proved to be very simple, as Mistress expected. After learning several, she asked the goblin if his name had a rune. Ghostspawn was very happy to draw his rune for her and explained the two runes that made up his name. He told her again that the 'ghost' rune could be found throughout the tunnels he once called home. Unfortunately, Rachk'sha had caused an earthquake making it impossible to get to them. After several hours, Mistress sent the goblin to practice essence extraction while she tended the wild-elves. When she returned to the cabin, she pulled the rune Ghostspawn drew for his name to her side of the table and carefully traced it. She smiled at the tingling sensation her fingertips felt on completing the rune. She would have to visit these tunnels and seek one of 'The Ghost's' runes, even if it took her many nights of digging to find one.

64 Erishen and Delmaria decided to join Archos, Karnak and Stumpy and assist them in destroying the runes Ky had left on the tunnel walls thousands of years before. None of them held any enmity towards Ky for putting them there. At the time he was doing this, he barely knew any magic and considered himself as nothing more than an outcast elven child. Besides, the goblins paid for his needs and the runes on the walls helped with that. They did hope that only the goblin chief traced the runes and absorbed the latent power of 'The Seed.' Taelann was tracking the goblin as they worked. If anyone could track him, Taelann would be the one.
