While Stumpy excavated the tunnels, Karnak assisted Archos with moving the goblin corpses into the canyon where they would be burned. Erishen and Delmaria followed behind Stumpy to mark the runes and try to find the best way to destroy them. After working through most of the night, and past noon of the next day, Stumpy announced that all the tunnels were opened. Delmaria and Erishen had marked well over a hundred instances of the rune. They checked each one to make sure Ky's magic was indeed a part of it. While Archos, Delmaria and Erishen started the task of destroying the runes, Karnak and Stumpy began working on the funeral pyre. "What have you two ladies found in regard to how to destroy them?" Archos asked as they headed to the first rune. "It should not be difficult. Although they hold latent magic, they have no protections and I don't believe the magic is strong enough to cause a backlash," Delmaria explained.

Erishen said, "I agree with Delmaria. We could have had this done by now if you did not wish to do it yourself." "I intend to learn from what Ky has done," Archos said. "I have no doubt that either of you could have handled this task with little effort." "My only concern is whether our destroying them will weaken Ky." Delmaria wondered. "It shouldn't," Archos observed. "This is trace magic left behind by a powerful being. It has nothing to do with his current abilities." "What if we just deface the runes instead of destroying them. Would that make them lose their power?" Erishen asked. Archos stroked his beard. They had arrived at the first rune. "I guess there is one way to find out." He pulled a small dagger from his wrist-sheath and began to chisel into the wall inside the rune. The packed dirt gave little resistance. His progress went well until the blade of the dagger scratched the actual rune. Sparks erupted from the wall and Archos' dagger flew across the tunnel. "That hurt," Archos muttered as he retrieved his dagger. "I would not expect trace magic to react in such a way," Delmaria stated. Archos nodded, "Neither would I have, but after speaking with The Lady, I think we are dealing with very powerful trace magic. If I understand correctly, all of us working together would be incapable of creating the level of magic found in these runes." Archos studied the rune for a few moments, then chuckled to himself, saying, "Imagine what we would be dealing with if he actually intended to do something here. That elf never ceases to interest me." "May I borrow your dagger and attempt something, Archos?" Erishen asked. "Your attempt may prove painful. If that is not a problem, you have my blessing," Archos answered handing her the dagger. "I, like most female sea elves, enjoy a little pain," Erishen said, grinning. Erishen dug into the wall where Archos had begun, making his efforts deeper and slanted so the a space was made underneath the stroke of the rune. Then she did the same thing above the stroke, working until she had excavated an area of the wall under the rune. The latent magic did not interfere with her efforts. When she was satisfied, she handed the dagger back to Archos. "Could one of you produce a container for me? I will need some seawater for this next part." "Delmaria is best at that," Archos said. "Make it lightweight

in case this works." Delmaria smiled and muttered an incantation. The stone floor of the tunnel shimmered and grew upward into a bowl, it's sides extremely thin, but very strong. "Will that do, Erishen?" "It's perfect," Erishen said as she knelt beside the bowl. She placed her fingers on the rim of the bowl and it quickly filled with water. Then she said an incantation and backed away. A sea vine grew from the bowl and climbed the wall. "If possible, I think we should back away," Archos suggested when he saw what Erishen planned. "If scratching it causes those sparks, breaking it might prove deadly." As the vine wrapped itself around the exposed stroke, Archos cast a protective shield that filled the tunnel in front of the group. They watched as the vine tightened. The vine pulled on the small section of the rune until it broke from the wall. The rest of the rune exploded, destroying most of the wall as well as Delmaria's bowl and Erishen's vine. "I believe they are going to be more tedious than we originally thought," Archos said after the dust settled. Stumpy ran into the tunnel, muttering into his beard. "By the great Mother Stone! What ye three think yer doin' in here?" "Thank you for your concern, Stumpy," Delmaria answered. "Thanks to Archos planning ahead, we are all fine." Stumpy glared at Delmaria, muttering and mumbling as he crossed his arms across his broad chest. "Ye had us believin' ye blown yerselves up. Karnak summoned some guards off the wall to make sure the goblins burned and went for Tobit!" "These runes, my short friend, are proving to be as temperamental as their creator. We only tried to deface that one," Archos explained. Archos dispelled the protective barrier and started sifting through the rubble. After a few minutes, he had found all the pieces of the rune and was able to reassemble it on the floor of the tunnel. He carefully traced it with his finger and felt the same twinge of magic he felt when it still occupied the wall. "Let me rephrase that," he said backing away a step. "They are proving to be more temperamental than their creator. Even if we bust them up, they can be put back together and used. We will have to take them all out of here and put them where they will never cause us problems." "Chaos?" Delmaria asked. "Do you wish to carry over a hundred of these things to Chaos?" Archos asked, raising an eyebrow. "Put yer barrier back up and let me try somethin'" Stumpy

demanded. Archos muttered his incantation and told Stumpy that it was ready. Stumpy placed his hand on the floor and concentrated. The rock on the other side of the floor absorbed the rune, then began to rise in the shape of a dwarven warrior. "If the lad be willin' to open a portal for us, they can march to Chaos on their own," Stumpy said. "Besides, I can move rock all day and not break a sweat. By the time ye get done with yer finger- wagglin' ye'll be mighty exhausted." Karnak arrived with Tobit at that time. "No fair. I was expecting to put people back together again," Tobit said grinning. "I guess I'm not needed after all." "I think we do have a need for you, my friend," Archos said. "We'll be marching an army of dwarven warriors back to the farm and could use help protecting their flanks." "Bah! My army won't need no protectin'!" "I'm sure they are quite fierce, Stumpy, but the cargo they carry is very important. It must reach its destination." Over the next several hours, the group visited every instance of the 'ghost' rune within the tunnels. The army of stone dwarves grew and the sound of their marching feet behind the group became deafening. Stumpy made sure to equip each warrior with the most vicious double-bladed battle-ax he could. Shortly before sunset, they marched Stumpy's army into the canyon. The alarms were immediately sounded on the walls of Cragsguard. The number of guards on the wall increased to the point that they had to stand shoulder to shoulder. They watched as Stumpy arranged his army into smaller units. Archos opened a portal to a spot near the farm and stepped through. He was followed by one unit of stone dwarves. As Archos led his unit away from the portal, Delmaria appeared followed by her unit. One by one the stone dwarves were positioned around the perimeter of the farm inside the protective barrier. As the sun set, the last of the dwarves were set in place, completely surrounding the farm. Archos dispelled the portal and, with Karnak, went looking for Ky. They found him setting up the campfire with the other children. Sitting around the fire had become a nightly ritual which all the children, Ky included, looked forward to, even though they were still on the farm. "Good evening, Ky," Archos greeted. "When you have a chance, Karnak and I need a favor from you." "When I'm done here," Ky answered. "Where will you be?" "We'll be in the council room," Archos said, smiling. "We've

other riddles that need solving. Enjoy your evening." Ky grinned, "If that's your favor, it will be really easy to do. Where did all of Stumpy's dwarves come from?" "The goblin caves you use to haunt as The Ghost," Archos explained. "There is one dwarf for each time you wrote that rune on the wall. They are the reason we need the favor." Ky nodded, "Tell me later," he said as he joined the other children who already sat around the fire and were beginning to share stories. Karnak and Archos returned to the council room. Once there, Karnak observed, "He is a rather complicated and confusing elf. He still frustrates my efforts to find him or even trace his movements. I am glad there is no other like him." Archos chuckled and said, "He's been practicing stealth since shortly after his birth. Now he does it as naturally as if he were born with the ability, which he may have been. No one knows exactly what his true powers are. Having sight does not make finding him any easier. He has a way of not being seen when he doesn't wish to be seen." "It's good to know I'm not the only one with that problem," Karnak stated as he sat at the council table. "Which riddle are we going to work on tonight?" Archos crossed the chamber to the door that led to his and Delmaria's room. "The cup should occupy our time until Ky joins us." He stepped into his room and returned with the cup a moment later. "We did not check to see if traces of Ky's magic were here. If they aren't, we can assume the goblin chief did not visit the children's quarters at the barracks." Delmaria, Erishen and Tobit joined Archos and Karnak in the examination of the cup. They did determine, with some certainty, that Ky's latent magic was not present. They also concluded that the trace magic in the cup was a type none of them had experience with. "It's a shame," Karnak said after several hours of discussion, "that Mie'arma is no longer with us. His magic was necromancy. That is the only type I can think of we have not tried." "None of us here master the magic of nature, or poisons," Archos explained. "Those are two more options we need to look into. Stumpy is a master of earth magic. Though I doubt it would have been used here, I'll have him look at it when he returns from his visit with Stan's ale barrels." Taelann returned from his tracking and joined the group. "What did you find?" Archos asked. "I believe his trail has been confused with magic. I followed it west for several leagues, then it turns north. The trail disappears

about a league into Crocus Hollow. I stayed and searched as long as I dared. There are no signs of his demise, but there are no signs of him leaving either." "We will go with you to where his path turns north and search for traces of magic that might be there to confuse his trail," Archos said. "Crocus Hollow does seem like his type of place though." Archos slid the cup across the table to Taelann. "Do you find any traces of nature magic in this cup?" Taelann examined the cup carefully. After a few moments, he reported, "There is no pure nature magic here, though I vaguely detect evidence of some herbs. The one I can identify, takweed, is not used in anything that I know of. Maybe someone with potion making skill will be able to tell you its uses." "We can ask The Old Man. He is a rather skilled alchemist if legend is to be believed," Archos said. "I will also speak with Tiasha," Karnak said. "She is very skilled with potion making, though hers are more in the line of seduction than anything else." "How did your task go?" Taelann asked. "Thanks to Stumpy, all the 'ghost' runes are now here at the farm," Archos explained. "He converted them to dwarven warriors and they stand sentinel around the farm until we can get Ky to open a portal to Chaos for us. Then they will go there. I doubt they will cause any more problems after that." "I thought you were planning on destroying them," Taelann said. "They had different plans," Erishen stated. "Ky's trace magic doesn't like being destroyed." Delmaria refreshed the drinks and produced a meal for those present. Having exhausted their leads at the moment, they drifted into reminiscing until Ky arrived to create the portal to Chaos.

65 As the night around the fire progressed, Micah and Little Ky seemed to become more and more distracted. They both had skipped their turns for story-telling and singing and neither of them reacted to the other's stories as they had in nights past. Ky finally asked them what they were worried about. "We overheard something about our friend, Amber," Little Ky explained. Micah nodded, "We think he might be missing or in trouble." "Who is Amber?" Ky asked. "He's our wild-elf friend. He gave us these," Micah said, showing Ky his necklace and pointing to Little Ky's anklet. Ky put his fingertips on Little Ky's anklet and concentrated. He muttered an incantation, then another. Several incantations later, an image of a wild-elf appeared in the center of the group above the fire. Micah and Little Ky recognized him as the older wild-elf that had spoken to them. They told Ky it was not Amber. Ky asked Micah and Little Ky to switch places and repeated the process with Micah's necklace. The same elf appeared above the fire. "That's the wild-elf that made these for you," Ky explained. "I will help find Amber for you but not tonight. This is our last night together. Most of you will be going to Alle-Stecan tomorrow to begin your lessons with Sage Tas'lin. Let's enjoy this night and worry about your friend tomorrow." Both Micah and Little Ky smiled when Ky said he would help find their friend. They were far more active in the night's activities after that. About an hour later, Ky began to end the night's

gathering. He knew it would happen slowly and did not fight it. He wanted the group's time together to go on as much as the others did. "I thought all of us were going to Sage Tas'lin," Eleana said. "Who isn't going?" "Simon," Ky said. "I don't like the way Sage Tas'lin deals with him. Besides, Simon needs training in defense and needs to understand his powers better. I will train him for that." "What's wrong with the way Sage Tas'lin deals with me?" Simon asked. "Sage Tas'lin knows you are my brother. He will stop at nothing to find out all he can about you," Ky explained. "Your time with him will not teach you much because he will spend it trying to learn about you. Archos is like that, too. The difference is that Archos has respect for the subject of his curiosity. Sage Tas'lin only respects knowledge." "Why do I have to learn defense and what powers do I need to learn about?" Simon asked. Ky grinned and put his arm around Simon's shoulders. "You have many powers that you don't know about. I'll demonstrate one now since I know of it. The others we will have to figure out together, okay?" Simon nodded. Ky uttered a short phrase of magic and Simon, as well as Ky's right arm, exploded in a shower of ice. Before the other children could react, Ky held up his remaining hand and ordered them to watch and wait. Nothing happened for several moments as the children stared with wide eyes and slack jaws at the spot that Simon had occupied. Then they saw the area beside Ky begin to shimmer as if they were looking through a thin waterfall. Seconds later Simon reappeared, completely healed. "That hurt," Simon muttered. Ky nodded. "It still does," he answered glancing at his right shoulder. "If I had done that to anyone else here at the fire, there would be no way they could recover, even if they had a soul sanctuary. With you, wait a few minutes and your back telling me, 'That hurt.'" "Why isn't your arm healed?" Simon asked. "Because that power only works in extreme cases. I'm not even sure I have it. You can heal it for me," Ky said nodding to the fire. "It will teach you of another ability you have." "How?" "Take some of the flame from the fire and hold it on my shoulder," Ky answered. Simon picked up a stick that had flame on the end of it and

held the flame to Ky's shoulder. He pulled it away a moment, then tried again. "It's not working," he complained. "You didn't do what I told you to do," Ky said. "I told you to take some flame from the fire, not a stick." Ky took the stick from Simon and tossed it into the fire. "Ky II, show Simon how to take flame from the fire." "He can do that?" Ky II asked, moving closer to the fire. Ky nodded then he and Simon watched as Ky II put his hand into the flames above the burning logs. When he pulled his hand away, a small bit of fire rested in his palm. Simon did as Ky II had done, pulling his hand away a couple times, thinking he would get burned. Finally, he placed his hand into the flames and stared wide- eyed at the fire resting in his palm. "My shoulder," Ky reminded him, grinning. "Oh, yeah," Simon replied as he moved to Ky. "Sorry, I forgot." He moved the fire to Ky's shoulder then jumped back as it flared brightly for a second. When the flare vanished, Ky's arm was fully restored. "What would happen if someone did that to you?" Little Ky asked his father. "If the attack were unexpected, like what I did to Simon, the results would be about the same, except the attacker would have been destroyed and I would still have both arms. If I were expecting it, it would not have happened," Ky stated. Ky glanced at Simon then said, "When you find some clothing you really like, I'll show you how to fix it so that it isn't so easily destroyed. It should also be resistant to the hottest of flames like mine and Ky II's. That is unless you want to walk around without clothing every time you need to use fire to defend yourself," Ky added. "Then you wouldn't need to learn how to do it." Simon laughed. "I'll learn." "Tomorrow I'll be sending the rest of you to Alle-Stecan. After I work with Simon a little, I'll see what I can find out about your wild-elf friend," Ky added, glancing at Micah and Little Ky. "Ky II, give Simon one of your spare tunics until he learns to enchant his own, please. It should fit okay for now." Ky waited until the last of the children had gone before dousing the fire and heading for the council room to meet with Archos and Karnak. He entered the room and greeted everyone before sitting at the table. "What did you need me to do?" he asked. "We need to march Stumpy's dwarves to Chaos where the runes they carry will cause no more problems," Archos explained. "My understanding is if you open a portal and we send them through one

at a time, they will be arriving at random locations throughout the realm of Chaos." Ky nodded. "That will definitely happen. What are they supposed to do when they get there?" "That doesn't matter. Stumpy has instructed them to defend themselves," Archos explained. "I had him do that on the slim chance that someone might discover one and try to use it like the goblin chief did." Ky left the room and returned a few moments later. "The portal is up, it will last until this time tomorrow. What's with that cup?" Ky had noticed the cup Archos had taken from Cragsguard. It sat alone in the center of the table, away from all the plates and mugs that were being used for the dinner Delmaria supplied. "Take a look at it. There are traces of magic on it that we do not understand. Maybe you will find something we couldn't," Archos said, levitating the cup to Ky. Ky examined it for a few moments then put it down. "There's some kind of magic there, but I don't know what type. Where'd you find it?" "It was one of the cups the children used while they were in Cragsguard. I also found some of the same traces of magic in Mena's room. She has not been seen since." Ky reexamined the cup, then carried it from the room. He walked through the house to Ky II's room and entered. Ky II was still getting ready for bed, but Simon was already in his usual spot against the wall. Ky showed Simon the cup and said, "Do you notice anything about this? Anything magical?" Simon sat up and examined the cup, shaking his head. "No, why?" "Would you mind taking it to The Lady and see if she can tell us anything?" Ky asked. Simon smiled, "I wouldn't mind at all. Any excuse to go to The Garden is good for me." He climbed out of bed and put on the tunic Ky II had given him. "Where will I find you when I get back?" "The council room. Say 'hi' for me," Ky said, leaving the room. "Will do," Simon answered. Ky returned to the council room and sat, glancing around at what the others were eating. Occasionally, he would glance at Delmaria, then at the empty table in front of his seat, then continue to watch the others eat. Finally Delmaria could not contain her laughter any longer and summoned a plate of food for the young elf. Ky

managed to take one bite, then vanished. The Lady had summoned him to The Garden where she and Simon waited. Ky frowned as he looked at the two of them. "That food was good, you know," he muttered. The Lady smiled at him, saying, "I'll send Simon back so it isn't wasted. I need to speak with you about this cup. Simon, be sure to explain where Ky is when you return." "But I..." Simon managed before he vanished. "Sit with me, please," The Lady invited. She waited until Ky had seated himself against a tree across from her, then continued, "Your brother is not ready to do what needs to be done to determine the magic in this cup. You should have very little problem." "Can't you tell anything about it?" Ky asked. "I can tell that your sister would have some knowledge of the magic used within it. Other than that, I can't help you. You will need to visit your sister and convince her to give you the information you seek." "What sister?" Ky asked standing. "Arienna. She is far too evil for Simon to deal with. You have your powers and you know how to use them. Your nature also makes you the better choice to go to her," The Lady explained. “I had hoped that neither of you would have to meet her." "Where will I find her?" Ky asked. "I will send you to the planet she is currently twisting and corrupting. Seek her magical aura and you will find her quickly." The Lady paused a moment, then handed the cup to Ky. "Even though you are the better suited for this, I ask that you be careful. She is much older than both of you and may seek to destroy you if she can." Ky took the cup and stated, "I'll be back." The Lady kissed his forehead and watched him as he faded from The Garden.

66 Brenson paced between the head table and the three bound deep-elves that struggled on the floor in the middle of the great hall. He was waiting for Maasena to return with the bust of their daughter, Mena. These deep-elves would not acknowledge any language Brenson spoke to them, answering only in their own speech which the dwarves did not know. There was one language that Brenson knew he would understand. When Maasena returned he watched the three elves carefully. His wife placed the bust on the floor near the deep-elves. Brenson knew by the look on their faces that they recognized Mena. That and the fact that they were found by the body of a dwarf whose blood had been drained was all the evidence Brenson needed. "Choose two," Brenson said to Maasena, "and kill them as you see fit. I will need the third to send a message." He turned to one of the guards that brought the three elves to the hall and ordered, "Take the one that my wife leaves to the forges and torture it. Remember that I need it alive and able to travel." Maasena chose the first two in the line and had the remaining two guards carry them for her. She led them from the hall as Brenson marched to his seat, frowning deeply. He sent for his quill and several pieces of parchment. While he waited, his fist absently pounded a slow rhythm on the arm of his chair. Brenson knew what happened to dwarves who were not properly prepared when they died. He assumed that Mena was now one with the earth from which the dwarves were made. There would be no body at her memorial, but she would receive a service befitting the heir to the Lord of a dwarven realm. Brenson, with the help of Maasena would see that it would be done correctly and he hoped Lord Stumpy would honor them with his presence.

When his quill and parchment arrived, Brenson set himself to the task. He pulled the first piece of parchment to him and dipped his quill into the ink and wrote: I, Brenson, Lord of Deep Stone, hereby declare that the dwarves of Deep Stone are now at war with the deep-elves for crimes committed against us. Prepare yeselves, brave warriors. The battle will be joined soon. He slid the parchment across the table, commanding, "Have that copied and posted throughout our realm. Post this one on the great hall doors." A guard took the parchment and left the hall as Brenson reached for the next piece of parchment. Hail, Baran, Lord under Dragon Spit, This is to inform you that I, Brenson, Lord of Deep Stone have declared war upon the deep-elves. Three of their number were found beside the corpse of one of my subjects who had been drained of his life-blood. They are also accused of killing the heir of Deep Stone. They refuse to speak in a language that can be understood, but when a bust of my daughter was set before them, recognition shone within their eyes. Consider this note as warning. The deep- elves may not have the courtesy of keeping the war between them and Deep Stone. Brenson, Lord of Deep Stone Brenson reread the note and frowned. It contained none of the customary dwarven courtesies that messages between the great dwarven lords usually contained. He hoped Baran would take the content of the letter as reason for this transgression. Then he copied the note, addressing the second to Kersa, Lord under Firepit. After making sure he made no errors in the second note, he sent for two messengers that would deliver the declarations. Finally, he addressed a note to the king of the deep-elves. King Kht-dulm It is dwarven courtesy to inform an enemy when war is declared. For crimes by your people against mine, including the

demise of the heir of Deep Stone, I, Lord Brenson declare war upon you and your subjects. Brenson, Lord of Deep Stone Brenson folded the note as small as he could and placed it on the side of the table then began pacing again, waiting for the surviving deep-elf to return to deliver his note. As he paced, he thought about the messages he had sent to the other dwarven lords. Although Brenson did not ask, it was his hope that they would join him in this war. The deep-elves and the dwarves had long been at odds with each other. Both groups lived within the earth, and frequently territorial disputes put them at each other's throats. Brenson knew the hatred was there, he hoped that his declaration of war would bring the others into open hostility with him. The main deep-elf settlements were between Deep Stone and the other dwarven realms. Having Dragon Spit and Firepit fighting with him would put the blood-sucking elves at a serious disadvantage. Brenson also knew that the deep-elves had allies of their own. Just thinking about some of them, like the shade-slime, sent shivers down Brenson's neck. He hoped the war would not last long enough for them to become a part of it. Over an hour passed before the guard returned with the deep-elf messenger. The creature was barely conscious and its body was covered in burned tissue. Brenson handed the note to the guard and told him to take the elf into the forest, away from the gates of Deep Stone, release it and give it the note to deliver to his king. The guard bowed deeply and left with the elf and the note. Maasena returned hours later. Although her eyes shone with moisture, her bearded jaw was set and she wore a battle-axe at her side. She led her husband, who had continued to pace the floor the entire time, to the table. "From the time it took ye to complete the deed, I'd guess ye killed them one at a time," Brenson observed as he sat beside Maasena. "Nay. They refused to die quickly. The first I set to bleeding to death, but I could nae remember where a major artery to cut could be found. I had to make endless cuts upon his body until it finally drained completely. The second was confined in a small metal cage above the forge. The lad was uncomfortable with the forge's heat. He found his voice when the bars of his prison began to heat up." She paused, then said, as if she had just received a new bit of information, "Their flesh does not resist hot metal well."

They spent the rest of the evening planning a memorial service for Mena. Brenson let Maasena send the note to Lord Stumpy as she was better with courtesy than he. Both refused their meals that night. Throughout the next week, Deep Stone was filled with the sounds of hammering forges, marching dwarves, military maneuvers and battle songs. Banners were made with the likeness of Mena and Daruk, the dwarf that was found with the deep-elves. Most in Deep Stone held no love for Mena, but her death was taken as a death of one of their kin. Her assumed death became a rallying force for the Deep Stone warriors. The messengers sent to Dragon Spit and Firepit had returned. Both lords expressed their gratitude towards Brenson for informing them of his intent. Both lords also promised to support Brenson's efforts. Brenson was particularly relieved by this news. He knew that the deep-elves were now surrounded before the first battle had been fought. Lord Baran of Dragon Spit advised that Brenson send a note to the high-elves, reminding them of the dwarven support they received during their war with the humans. Baran himself would be seeking an alliance with the humans that lived at the base of his mountain home. Brenson knew the high-elves would already know of the impending war. His messengers had to travel through elven territory to deliver their messages. They would have been stopped and the messages read before given permission to travel onward. Before an hour had passed since Baran's reply had arrived, Brenson's messenger was on his way to King Stel-Tasan. The rest of Brenson's time was spent with his generals and stonemasons. The plan was to march underground, attacking the deep-elves in their homes. Tunnels were already being excavated and fortified. As soon as word came from Lord Baran and Lord Kersa that they were ready, Brenson led his warriors to battle.

67 Mistress waited in the forest outside the city of Alle-Stecan. Long ago, she learned about Sage Tas'lin and his methods of teaching. The old high-elf had been a famous historian and teacher long before the war between the humans and high-elves. His services were sought by everyone with a desire to learn. Unable to handle the demand, Sage Tas'lin wrote a manual and taught ten former students how to use it. Since then, that manual has been available in every city that housed a library. Mistress also knew that Sage Tas'lin was strictly unmoving with both the amount of time to be spent on each subject, and the order in which the subjects were taught. With this knowledge, she knew that herb-lore would be the first subject presented and that the children of the Lord of Chaos would be given an assignment at dawn and sent into the forests outside the city gates to complete it. Mistress even knew which herbs would be required on which days. She had already collected the first day's assignment. One of the children would be taken to her cabin. The wild-elf that replaced that child would need the herbs before being sent back to the city. While she waited, she collected things from the forest that she found useful. She did not need to pay great attention to learn when the child arrived. As soon as the child came within range of her, she would know who and what they were. The first lesson on the first day with Sage Tas'lin was an introduction to what they would be doing. Afterwards, they would be given time to settle into their new home. Mistress smiled as she collected a few elf-weed roots. The

second day would be the last for one of them. Her herb pouch being full, she settled beside a tree and waited, thinking of her trip to the goblin caves the night before. Someone had done a very good job of cleaning out all the 'ghost' runes. She also found no evidence of the dead goblins. She considered asking Ghostspawn about it, but put aside that thought. It appeared someone was looking for him. It would be best if he did not know this yet. She frowned thinking of the opportunity she had lost. Soon it would not matter though. She spent the next couple hours watching the city awaken. Shortly after dawn, she smiled. The image of a young male elf and the name 'Tal' filled her mind. Her wait was over and her desire for the male had been satiated. Now, not only would she have a godlike being to siphon essence from, but she would have an innocent female elf from which to harvest spell components. She returned to her cabin to make ready for her guest and to prepare Ghostspawn for his part of the deed.

68 Ky had not returned from his trip to The Garden so Archos assumed the responsibility of sending the children to Alle-Stecan. He gave them each a letter of introduction, knowing it was proper protocol for students of Sage Tas'lin. All but Simon, who remained at the farm waiting for Ky, arrived at the gates of the elven capital and were met there by the royal guard. From there, they were immediately taken to Sage Tas'lin. He accepted their letters and briefly explained how the training schedule had been set up. Afterwards, the children had the rest of the day to get settled in what was to be their new home for the next few years. Aemir had been to Alle-Stecan many times with his father and offered to show the others around, saying, "I can't promise you a complete tour, but I can give you a good start." Besides Aemir, only the triplets had been here more than once or twice so they all happily followed him around the city. The first couple hours Aemir showed them the few places he knew about: the library, the square, the various market areas, and finally, the public areas within the palace of King Stel-Tasan. After that, the group spent the rest of the afternoon exploring. Micah was the most impressed with the city. He still had memories of Austria and the choir school he attended, but the elven city was far more spectacular to his eyes than anything he remembered about Vienna. Whereas the architecture of his former home was grand and stately, the elven city was grand, but had a light, natural feel to it. Many of the buildings were joined with each other by huge, fully-leafed branches that shaded the roads on which they

walked. Micah marveled at their symmetry. They appeared to have been designed, both in their construction and their placement. The windows caught his attention as well. Micah tried, but could not find two windows that were alike. Most appeared similar to the stained-glass windows that adorned the cathedrals and churches of his home. The stained-glass windows always reminded him of a painting within a frame. The elven windows took the shape of the subject which made the whole building appear to be part of the finished artwork. Micah also noted that stone was used only for the bases of the structures and, on occasion, for the supports. Everything else appeared to be made from living wood with a natural finish of bark. Micah's fascination with the city resulted in him becoming separated from the group several times. Rather than become completely lost, he waited until they noticed him missing and returned for him. After the second time, the others decided it would be best to let Micah set the pace. Late in the afternoon, Prince Stel-Ky found them. "There you are," Prince Stel-Ky greeted. "I'm pretty much in charge of seeing that you eat and sleep and are generally well cared for. It's about time for you to have dinner and King Stel-Tasan wishes that you join him, this being your first day in the city and what-not. Anyway, I'm here to show you to your rooms so you can clean up." Eleana asked, "How did you find us? We've been all over the place today." Prince Stel-Ky laughed. "You can blame Brek for that. All I had to do is ask if anyone had seen a young goblin." He pointed up the road and added, "He's the only goblin in town today. You were easy to find." As they started walking, Brek said, "Brek wonders is other goblins here on other days." "Not in the city," Prince Stel-Ky answered. "With the exception of you, goblins are generally considered our enemies. We have decided to tolerate you." Ky II put his arm across Brek's shoulder and said, "Yeah. They are afraid of what dad will do if they don't tolerate you." Prince Stel-Ky laughed again. "You are quite right, Ky II." He turned them down a side street and added, "And you are Sage Tas'lin's newest students. He would not take kindly to any of you being absent." Several more turns and they noticed they were headed to the palace. Little Ky asked, "Aren't you going to show us to our rooms first?" "Yes, I am. You will be staying at the palace," Prince Stel-Ky

explained. "It's the safest place in the city and as Ky II said, we don't want something happening to you to make your father angry." From Prince Stel-Ky's description of where they were going to stay, the children expected something like the barracks in Cragsguard, though more comfortable because it was at the palace. Instead they were led to a garden on the opposite side of the palace from where Sage Tas'lin lived. Within it stood nine small cottages encircling a pool with a fountain in its center. Each cottage was shaded by an elm tree. A path wound its way past all manner of flowers and led to the doors of each of the cottages. "There's nine of them," Prince Stel-Ky explained. "We were expecting Simon to be with you. If he's coming later, save one for him. If not, you have a play room." He pointed to the pool and said, "You can swim in that during your free time. If you follow that path between those two cottages," he added, pointing to it, "you'll find a nice area for you to study or practice your martial skills." "This is real!" Tal said. Prince Stel-Ky smiled and pointed to a window above the garden. "That is where I live. If you need me for anything, just yell. I'll hear you sooner or later." He turned to leave, saying, "I'll be back in an hour to take you to dinner. Bye." Most of the children began to wander off to explore the garden until Eleana stopped them. "Wait! Clean up first, then we can explore. We'll meet at the pool and explore together." "Girls can be so bossy, sometimes," Micah muttered. Ky II laughed, "At least you didn't have to grow up with her," he said, gaining him a serious frown from Eleana. Ky II stuck out his tongue at Eleana, then said, "Come on. I know from experience it's best to just do what she wants even if torturing her is much more fun." They found their weapons, spare clothing and sparring gear waiting for them in the cottages. Helping each other, it did not take them long to find which cottage had been set up for whom. They bathed and changed, then met at the pool as Eleana suggested. When all were present, they explored the garden and the study area behind the cottages. They had just returned to the pool when Prince Stel-Ky arrived to take them to the king's hall for dinner. Eleana made sure she sat beside Brek at the dinner table. She did this more as a precaution than out of need. Brek had learned table manners well under Eleana's tutelage. King Stel-Tasan commented on their etiquette when the meal was finished. "Brek," King Stel-Tasan said, as he wiped his hands clean, "do all goblins eat with such politeness?" Brek shook his head and answered, "Brek think all goblins would with Eleana sitting beside them."

"I see," replied the king, smiling. "I'll remember that if we have a feast of state I wish you all to attend." After the meal, they returned to their cottages and put their good clothing away. The rest of the evening was spent in the pool. As the sun set, they returned to their cabins to sleep. Sage Tas'lin expected them to pick up their first assignments and be out the city gates by dawn. Just before dawn, they gathered at the pool, then headed for Sage Tas'lin's garden. The old elf met them outside the wall of his garden with their assignments and pouches to carry the herbs he wished them to collect. "All of these herbs," he said as he handed out the parchments, "can be found outside the city walls in the forest. I would expect most of you will have completed this task by lunch time. Return to me when you have everything on the list." Sage Tas'lin did not wait to see if they had questions. He returned to his garden and shut the door. The children stared at the door for a moment, then began comparing their lists with each other. They found that everyone of them had the exact same list. Beside the name of each plant they had to find, was a very detailed drawing of how it would look in nature. They also noted the second portion of the first day's assignment written at the bottom of the lists. After they returned the herbs to Sage Tas'lin, they were required to research each one in the library and write a detailed synopsis of its uses. As they slowly walked to the main gate of the town, still rubbing sleep from their eyes, Brek and Aemir decided to work together and so did Micah and Little Ky. The triplets decided to work alone, though they did offer to help anyone who needed it when their own herb collection was complete. The guards at the gate let them out by way of a small, side door that was used when the main gates were not open yet. Most of the children crossed over the bridge before heading for the forest. Tal, Little Ky and Micah decided to stay on the gate side of the ravine. They crossed most of the scarred land between the city and the forest together, then Tal went his own way as they approached the trees. Mistress watched the children leave the city, noting their yawns and stretches as they tried to push the sleep away. She expected them to stay together and was pleasantly surprised when they split at the bridge. Now she had only two extras to contend with and hoped her prey would leave them before they entered the forest. She smiled as Tal waved to the other two boys and walked away from them. Mistress waited until he was deep enough into the trees to be unseen from the city walls, then softly spoke his name, "Tal." Her

voice whispered in the morning breeze, just another leaf dancing amid the trees. Tal could not have heard it, yet he turned and began walking to her. The potion the dwarf had given him drew the young elf to Mistress. She guided his footsteps, herding and luring him to the portal she had set up. Within moments, Tal vanished. Mistress dispelled the portal and cast another that would take her to her cabin. Ghostspawn waited in the front room of the stockroom. Mistress had scribed a rune on the floor and instructed him to wait until the elf arrived. The only thing she could not tell him is which way he would be facing. The goblin hoped that she would be correct in assuming that the elf would be too much in shock when he arrived to put up a fight. All Ghostspawn had to do was cover the elf's mouth with the treated rag Mistress had given him and hold it there until he went limp. The goblin had to wait nearly an hour, his only company being the shell of the wild-elf that lay on the table. Ghostspawn did not recognize him when he entered the room this morning. Mistress had done most of the work to change his appearance overnight. The elf's build was slighter now, though far more muscular than it had been. The bright amber eyes had become emerald green and his hair which had been almost platinum in color and braided, now was dark brown and hanging free, almost to his waist. Every once in a while, Ghostspawn's gaze would wander to the elf on the table and marvel at what had been done to him. Every time he looked at the elf, the goblin would notice the dull, almost dead appearance of the elf's eyes. Mistress had stripped the elf's mind of all his identity and knowledge in preparation for receiving the god's identity. Then the memories of what would happen to him, the nightmares that Mistress placed in his mind, brought his focus back to the task he had to perform. Even though the goblin expected the elf to arrive, the actual arrival surprised him. He managed to recover before Tal, and quickly jammed the treated rag into Tal's face. Tal tried to fight the goblin, but the fumes took his consciousness before he could muster enough resistance. Ghostspawn used the rope Mistress had supplied him with and secured the rag over Tal's face. Ghostspawn yelled, "He's down," as he started removing Tal's clothing. Moments later, Mistress entered the room. "Very good. You managed to do that without getting yourself killed." She walked to where the wild-elf lay on the table. "Put him beside our friend here when you finish with his clothing," Mistress instructed as she pulled the wild-elf to one side of the table. Ghostspawn finished quickly, then placed Tal on the table

beside Amber, the wild-elf. As Mistress made sure they appeared identical, the goblin gathered Tal's things and put them on the table at Amber's feet. Mistress worked for over an hour making minor adjustments to Amber's appearance before she was satisfied. "Go see to the female and her vines while I finish," Mistress said as she started gathering what she needed. "By the time you finish with her, you should be able to start harvesting this one's essence." Mistress smiled as the goblin rushed from the room. She failed to tell him that she had used the control-incense here so that the wild-elf would do her bidding when it received Tal's awareness. She smiled as she carried the tray of instruments to the table. Having the goblin do her bidding without his usual snide remarks was a definite bonus. She put the tray on the table beside Tal and whispered, "This is going to hurt, but if you manage to stay still, it will hurt much less than if you move around." Using a sharpened bone, Mistress cut into her palm as she intoned an incantation. The cut was not very deep and less than a inch long, but it was enough to produce a small pool of blood in her cupped hand. Placing the sharpened bone aside, she picked up a long, needle-like bone and placed it into the blood, completely coating half its length. Mistress firmly grasped Tal's chin and turned his head to the side and held it there. The intonation changed, and became slower and softer, almost a whisper as she inserted the bone into Tal's ear, seeking his brain. When only the portion of the bone not covered with blood could be seen, Mistress carefully sucked on the end of the bone. Then she placed her fingertip over the opening and removed the bone while continuing her intonation. She emptied the contents of the bone into one of the small vials used for essence, then moved to Tal's feet. There she extracted a small amount of his essence and added it to the same vial. Now she moved to Amber and had him drink the mixture. Mistress's incantation ended as the vial emptied. She helped Amber from the table and told him to don the clothing that Tal had worn. While he dressed, she filled the pouch with the herbs she had collected for him so that he would have Sage Tas'lin's collection task complete. The effects of the transfer of Tal's memories and abilities would not take place until the final declaration of who Amber was supposed to be. Mistress knew that the wild-elf would probably survive only two or three weeks since he would have no memory of his need for the vines that kept him alive. By then, it would be too late to stop her. As she waited for Ghostspawn to return, Mistress cleaned

and put away the tools she had used. The goblin returned a few moments later. Mistress strolled to Amber and put her arm over his shoulders as she instructed, "My dear apprentice, I will need to deliver our little elf to Alle-Stecan. While I am gone, extract ten vials of essence and take it to my cottage. Wait for me there." The goblin grinned as Mistress cast the portal spell that would take her and Amber to the forest outside Alle-Stecan. Once there, she handed the wild-elf the pouch of herbs and whispered, "You are Tal, son of the Lord of Chaos. Proceed with your life." The young elf's eyes lit up with awareness as it walked away from Mistress. Mistress actually smiled as she returned to her cabin to wait for Ghostspawn. She knew that soon she would finally be the goddess she always dreamed she would be. While Mistress attended to Tal's replacement, Ghostspawn began collecting the bone and vials needed for essence extraction. His hands trembled as he set everything on the table at Tal's feet. Looking at the young elf that lay before him, his sharp-toothed grin widened as he anticipated the god-essence that would soon be his. This was no ordinary elf. This was one of the son's of The Ghost. The goblin paced, his back towards the table. It would serve no purpose if he could not get his hands to stop shaking. As he attempted to calm himself, he wondered if the essence would have the same painful pleasure he sought with the runes in his old home, and he hoped it would. After several moments, Ghostspawn still had not managed to calm himself. He decided pacing would not help, so he returned to the table. He would extract the essence from Tal's ankle as he had done with the elf and human he had practiced on. The goblin grasped the edge of the table and stared at the vein until the rest of Tal's body became blurred and unimportant. Then Ghostspawn began the incantation, concentrating on the words, convincing himself that this was yet another practice. When he finally picked up the bone, his hand was steady. Ghostspawn carefully inserted the bone into the vein and picked up the first vial. He did not know what to expect. The first elf he practiced on served essence which glowed softly with a golden light. The human's essence had a blue glow. Ghostspawn braced his hand on Tal's shin then slowly tilted the bone until it rested on the rim of the small vial. He was nearly blinded as the first platinum-white essence flowed into the vial. He raised the bone to stop the flow until his eyes adjusted, then filled the first vial and placed it in the stand. Knowing what to expect, the remaining nine vials were filled without problem. Ghostspawn fought the temptation to drink one of the vials

before meeting with Mistress. His memory of the intoxicating feeling which the essence produced, strengthened his resolve. He knew that he would not be able to refill the vial after drinking the essence. Mistress would know as well. The goblin preferred to avoid such problems, especially now that he was so close to his goal. Soon, he thought, I will be a god to be reckoned with! He carefully removed the bone from Tal's vein and smiled noting the lack of bleeding. Before cleaning the bone, he capped the vials and moved them to the counter by the door. Moments later, he left the stockroom with his treasure in hand. He hoped that Mistress had returned. Mistress had returned and the goblin found her pacing the floor when he entered the room. He grinned as he held out the stand with the ten vials. Mistress took the stand and frowned. "I thought I trained you better," she hissed. "What is this?" Ghostspawn had not noticed the change in the essence until Mistress indicated it. The platinum-white glow was gone. Now the vials appeared to be filled with a dark red substance that coagulated and slowly churned. Mistress dropped the stand on the table and advanced on the goblin. "That is not the essence of a god!" she screamed. "Where is the essence you were supposed to extract?" Ghostspawn took a step back and stammered, "It, it was glowing white! That is his essence. Something happened to it when you took it!" Mistress grabbed Ghostspawn's jaw and dug her nails into his cheek. "Are you accusing me of destroying that which I have worked so hard to obtain?" She glared into the goblin's wide-eyed countenance, daring him to agree. "Go to your cabin before I decide to add goblin bones to my decor!" She yelled as she threw him out the door. She waited long enough to know that Ghostspawn had indeed returned to his cabin, then returned to the table and yanked one of the vials from the stand. Mistress had to know what her apprentice had done wrong before sending him to acquire more essence. She studied the contents for several moments before deciding that she had never seen anything quite like what she held in her hand now. She pulled the stopper and held the vial to her nose, then took a long, slow whiff of the essence. Still, she could find nothing that would explain what had happened. She placed the vial on the table then sat staring at it. She could make the goblin ingest the essence, but she doubted he would be able to put into words what she needed to know. Her other choice was to extract the essence herself. She frowned, knowing that the subject of the extraction would likely know who was

extracting their essence whether they could see or not. The risk of taking the essence for her double was more than she wished to chance at this time. Tal's substitute would give her at least a complete week to figure out what went wrong. Mistress sighed. She would have to taste the essence herself to determine the problem. She raised the vial to her lips and hoped its contents would not kill her. Hours later, Mistress awoke on the floor beside the table. The empty vial lay a few feet away from her. She tried to sit, only to find the room spinning and her head so intoxicated she could not see straight. So, she remained where she lay, smiling. The vials did indeed contain the essence of a god. It was not the essence of the elf that she had lured here. She had sensed his power and this was much stronger. Somehow, her apprentice had extracted the essence of some other, more powerful god through Tal. Mistress waited until she could regain her seat at the table, then summoned the goblin. He, too, would need the strength that this essence would provide. He was her shield against vengeance. Besides, she wanted to see what the essence did to the little goblin.

69 When Simon awoke the next morning, he found Archos waiting for him in the kitchen. They exchanged, 'Good morning's' then Archos waited until Illya served Simon a bowl of steaming oatmeal spiced with cinnamon and apples. Archos watched the boy eat for a few moments. Simon had always been a curiosity to him and the knowledge he had gained since Simon arrived only made him wish for more. "Why is it you are not with Sage Tas'lin?" Archos asked. Simon fought to swallow a mouthful of oatmeal, then answered, "Ky doesn't want me to go there. He doesn't like the way Sage Tas'lin deals with me." Simon put another spoonful of oatmeal into his mouth just as Archos asked, "What are you doing about your training?" Simon scowled at Archos as he tried to swallow his oatmeal so he could answer the question. After nearly choking on it, he said, "Ky is going to train me." He thought about asking if Archos could wait until after he finished his breakfast, but could not think of a nice way to ask. "You can ask your questions after he eats," Illya stated. "Run along and let him finish his breakfast." This time, Simon waited to see what Archos would say before trying another spoonful of oatmeal. Archos stood and apologized, more to Illya than Simon, then said as he headed out, "I'll meet with you in the council room when you finish." When Simon heard the door to the council room close, he smiled at Illya and said, "Thank you."

"You need to learn when politely putting up with someone is not an option," Illya replied, grinning. "Archos is used to dealing with your brother. I doubt seriously if he would be insulted by anything you say." "I can imagine," Simon muttered, then returned to his breakfast. Illya watched Simon as he tried to rush through his oatmeal. Shaking her head, she sat across from him and explained, "This is your breakfast. Don't rush it. Archos will be there waiting for you when you are done and he'll probably find something else to ponder until you get there." She folded her hands on the table and finished by saying, "If I see you rush again, I'm going to take that away from you." With a little more prodding by Illya, Simon finished his breakfast in a more or less relaxed state. Afterwards, he hurried to the council room to find Archos. As Illya predicted, Simon found Archos flipping through a large, leather-bound tome. Smiling, Simon walked to the table and seated himself in the chair next to Archos so that he could see the book as well. Simon found the words impossible to read, but the images caught his undivided attention. Soon, his hands were preventing Archos from turning the pages so that Simon could study the pictures that both fascinated and terrified him. "I suppose this is revenge for me making you choke on your breakfast," Archos said, leaning back in his chair as Simon leaned over the book to see a picture on the opposite page. "Sorry," Simon muttered, settling into his own chair. "What's that book about, anyway?" "It's a tome that explains dark magic that I borrowed from Tiasha. I found traces of magic in Cragsguard and I am trying to figure out what they are," Archos explained, closing the book. "You found traces of dark magic in Cragsguard?" Simon asked. Archos nodded, then asked, "Can you tell me what happened to that cup Ky took from me last night?" "Ky still has it. He is going to see our sister to ask her about it," Simon answered, stealing a glance at the dragon carved into the leather cover of the book. "I have a couple questions for you, if you don't mind." "I never have a problem with anyone seeking knowledge," Archos answered, stroking his beard. "You have given me a question as well, but I will wait until you have asked your questions. What enlightenment do you seek?" Simon stared at the edge of the table a moment, then said, "Ky told me I was a creature of fire, like him. What does that mean?" "I cannot answer your question as fully as I would like. I find

that for every fact I know about your brother, Ky, there are at least ten more that I don't know," Archos continued stroking his beard as his eyes lost their focus. A moment later, he added, "From what I do know, my guess is that you can control fire, make it do your bidding, and that fire will heal you rather than harm you." Archos chuckled, then said, "Granted, experimenting with the healing portion of that talent may be somewhat painful. I would wait until Tobit or Eleana are available." "So if I wanted fire to burn that book, all I'd have to do is tell it to?" Simon asked as he pointed to the leather bound tome. Archos quickly waved his palm over the book which disappeared. "Actually, anyone with knowledge of magic could attempt that. That particular tome would be difficult though," he glanced at Simon, then added, "for most people, anyway." Archos left the table, muttering, "One moment, please." He stepped into the room he shared with Delmaria and returned a moment later carrying an empty table-sconce. He placed the bronze sconce on the center of the table. "We can experiment with this," he explained as he returned to his seat. Simon stood on his chair and looked into the sconce. "There's nothing to burn in there." "If my guess is correct, which it usually is, you won't need anything to burn." Archos patted the corner of the table, saying, "Sit up here and let us try a few things." Archos waited as Simon climbed onto the table and sat, cross-legged on the corner. "Let's start with something easy," Archos said. He pointed to the sconce and instructed, "Concentrate on the inside of the sconce and command a small flame to occupy it." Simon concentrated a few seconds. His eyes widened as a small flare erupted inside the bronze sconce. "It worked! Whoa!" "Of course it worked," Archos chuckled. "And you managed it without burning down the farmhouse." He stroked his beard a moment then suggested, "Let us see what else you can do with your little friend. Try commanding it to walk across the table to you." Simon frowned at Archos, asking, "You want me to make fire walk?" "Consider that flame to be your pet," Archos said smiling. "Pets can walk and so can that flame if that is what you want it to do." Simon shrugged and turned his attention back to the flame. He tried visualizing what it would look like walking across the table and smiled. He whispered, "Come here," and urged the flame forward with a hand gesture. The flame did exactly what he had imagined. Small flaming arms and legs appeared as it climbed from the sconce then strolled across the table to stand before Simon who grinned and

picked up the flame. "You went ahead of me a couple steps," Archos chuckled. "No problem though. As you just saw, you can also have the flame change form. You can even hold it without being burned. Put it down on the table and imagine attempting to make it look like Ky II." Simon brought the image of his friend into his mind and concentrated on the flame. The small fire wavered and shifted, taking the form of Ky II. Simon uttered another, "Whoa!" which was followed by yet another as Simon jumped down from the table wide-eyed, staring at the flame. "What's wrong?" Archos asked. "Is it supposed to have a spirit person?" Simon whispered. Archos smiled. "I did not really expect that it would, but if you are seeing one, I cannot say I am surprised. The fire you summon will probably be more along the lines of creatures rather than normal flame and magical flame. Therefore, if what you told me is correct, it would have a spirit person." Simon continued to stare at the flame and said, "I don't remember what I told you." "When we first discovered your ability to see someone's spirit person, you told the Council that all living things have them," Archos explained. "If you are satisfied with what you have learned this morning, I have a couple questions for you." "What about the flame?" Simon asked. "Send it home," Archos suggested. Simon nodded and the small, flaming version of Ky II returned to the sconce and sat. Simon then returned to his seat beside Archos. "It is still here," Archos said, smiling. "I asked it to go home and that's where it went," Simon explained. "I see," Archos muttered, stroking his beard. "Well, on to my questions then." Archos did not get a chance to ask his questions. As he thought of which to ask first, Illya rushed into the room and told him he had visitors. She was followed by the Old Man and Rachk'sha. Archos scowled as he moved around the table to put himself between them and Simon. "Relax, my friend," the Old Man said. "We need to speak with Simon a moment. That is all we are here for." Rachk'sha stepped forward and added, "We are not here to cause problems. We wish to determine the reason for something. That is all." "I am not sure I wish you to speak with Simon," Archos

answered, crossing his arms over his chest. "I'm sure if Ky does not wish Sage Tas'lin to speak with him, you," he purposely glared at Rachk'sha, "would definitely be on his no list." Rachk'sha ignored Archos and seated himself at the council table. The Old Man stepped forward and explained, "We know who and what Simon is. Sage Tas'lin does not. We are here because we are concerned about Ky." He gently guided Archos to his seat beside Simon. "Simon is beyond us. We can do nothing to harm him as he is yet in the age of innocence. He knows that if you need verification." Simon nodded to Archos as the small flaming version of Ky II climbed from the sconce and sat on the table in front of Simon, facing Rachk'sha. "You will have to suffer my presence," Archos stated. "I will not leave you alone with him." "That is more than fair," Rachk'sha purred. "Besides, it will save him the effort of explaining things to you later." The Old Man sat on the opposite side of Simon and placed a small golden box on the table. He took a deep breath, then asked, "Do you know where Ky is?" Simon nodded. "Can you tell us his exact location?" the Old Man asked. "No," Simon answered. "All I can tell you is he is far away from here. You wouldn't understand if I told you anything more." "It might help if we knew the reason for your interest in Ky," Archos suggested. Rachk'sha leaned forward and growled, "If that will make this go faster, then I will tell you." He waited until both Archos and Simon nodded. "Last night, as you reckon time, Ky left our realm. We know there is a place outside our realm that he and Simon can go and we can still sense him when he is there. He left there as well." Simon nodded. Rachk'sha purred, "Good, you know about that." His feline features appeared to twist into a smile. "A few moments ago, we sensed his powers again." Rachk'sha paused, staring at Simon who did not react. "We did not sense him, only his powers," Rachk'sha softly hissed. Simon climbed off his chair and stepped around the table. "What do you mean?" Rachk'sha watched the small flame move across the table to stay beside Simon as the Old Man answered, "We don't know. That is why we are here." The Old Man waited until Simon turned his attention to him, then continued, "Ky's powers are very great as is Ky's aura. We can sense them both when he is in our realm. What we sense now is just his powers. His aura is not present which makes us believe

he is not present." The Old Man tapped the box and said, "These are the ashes from Ky's funeral pyre in Austria. We are hoping that you can combine your magic with them to let us see Ky's actual location." Archos leaned forward and captured Simon's gaze, then said, "I will leave the decision up to you, but, if it were me, I would not be sharing any visions with Rachk'sha." The feline god sneered, "It doesn't matter if I am here or not. I will see what Simon shows if he decides to do this. It is just easier this way." The Old Man smiled and explained, "Rachk'sha and I are brothers. Unlike you and Ky, we have access to each other's thoughts and experiences. It takes a great deal of effort for either of us to block our intentions from the other. We are both here because I wanted you to know that my brother will be witness to what is shown." Simon glanced at Rachk'sha and the Old Man then shrugged, saying, "I would like to see where Ky is, though I have an idea. I don't know how to do it though so you're wasting your time." The Old Man placed his hand on Simon's shoulder and smiled. "I will teach you what you need to know, just as I taught Ky much of the magic he knows." He waited until Simon nodded, then added, "Please, return to your seat and relax. I will set things up for you." Simon returned to his seat as the Old Man pulled the table- sconce to the edge of the table. He then opened the gold box and tapped a few ashes into the bottom of the sconce. After making sure the box was securely shut, he slid the sconce back to he center of the table and turned to Simon. "The flame that follows you around," the Old Man said, pointing to the flame, "did you summon it?" "Yes," Simon answered. "Excellent. Do you know how to control it?" Simon shrugged and answered, "A little." "That should be enough," the Old Man said, smiling. "What I would like you to do is ask your flame to enter the sconce and show us the source of the ashes. It may show us something we already know. If so, then we will try something a little more complicated." Simon concentrated on the flame. Seconds later, it returned to the sconce and climbed into it. The four in the room found themselves surrounded by three groups of boys all dressed in the same outfit Ky wore when he returned from Austria. The table itself took the shape of a large fire with emerald flames shooting forth towards the boys. The vision faded quickly as Simon lost his concentration. "What was that?" Simon asked, his voice a high squeak.

The Old Man smiled. "That is what Ky's funeral in Austria looked like. It is not what we need to see though. For our next attempt, please try to confine the vision to the table top. We will not need to see it life-sized." Simon nodded as the Old Man leaned back in his chair and closed his eyes. Archos sat stroking his beard and Rachk'sha mindlessly stretched his claws on the tabletop. "It might work," Archos muttered. "What might work?" the Old Man asked. "Simon, ask your flame to show you the owner of the ashes," Archos suggested. Simon concentrated again, forgetting to keep the vision on the tabletop. The room darkened and expanded. Several torches lined the walls, their flames dancing and casting eerie shadows across the dark-gray stone floor. A large creature stood leaning over the small form of Ky, who lay unconscious on the floor. Before anyone could get a good look, the vision abruptly vanished. The last thing Archos, the Old Man and Rachk'sha heard was Simon muttering the name "Arienna." Before the thought of asking Simon who or what Arienna was could formulate in their minds, they noticed both Simon and his flame were gone.

70 Ky had no notion of what to expect. What made things worse is that The Lady could not send him to Arienna directly. Ky found himself on an alien world with nothing to guide him but his purpose. Cold and heavy rains pelted him as he searched his surroundings. The road he stood on had been paved with a dark gray stone that intensified the chill of the downpour. It ran slick and smooth in five directions. The buildings that lined the road had been constructed from the same stone and none had windows on the lower two floors. The few doors Ky could make out in the darkness appeared to be constructed from thick steel, their hinges longer and wider than his arms. A loud, constant roar approached him from behind. Turning, he could make out three lamps slowly progressing towards him. Ky moved to the side of the closest building and waited, willing himself invisible. The roar grew as did the stench of exhaust, as the machine moved closer. The thick leather tread it traveled on hammered out a deafening rhythm as it drew near. Ky could see that the main portion was composed of black steel. A small, rectangular pane of thick glass had been set into the raised section. Ky could not see within the machine, but his spirit sight detected two life forms. He watched it pass, moving straight through the intersection, until the thick cloud of fumes blocked the vehicle from his view. Returning to the center of the intersection, Ky searched down each length of road for something that might provide a clue to where Arienna would be. The little he knew of his sister drew him to the conclusion that she would dwell within a large building, like a

palace or castle, anything different from the standard residence. The darkness and the rain obscured his visibility to the point that he could find nothing but rows of gray stone and steel doors. Every direction he turned, he found the same thing. Frustrated, he started walking, staying close to the side of the road. Each crossroad Ky encountered, he would search in all directions seeking anything that broke the monotony of stone. Hours of walking passed and nothing changed. During that time, several more machines lumbered past him as he hid in the shadows and watched. For all Ky knew, they were all the same machine with new occupants. Moments later, Ky approached yet another intersection. Lightning danced across his fingertips as he looked around. Once again, he stood in the middle of an intersection with five roads. He found himself frustrated, cold, bored, soaked through with rain, and no closer to his goal than when he first arrived. Ky stood in the center of the intersection fuming. In the hours he had been here, all he had seen was gray stone and several noisy, lumbering machines. There were no plants, no colors, nothing that would give the slightest change to the scenery around him. Even the rain had been steady and heavy, without variation. When the next machine approached him, Ky waited where he stood. He no longer felt the need or desire to hide in the shadows, to move unseen through this world until he found his sister. Now, Ky wanted his sister to find him. He decided this machine would be the start of his getting her attention. He spent the last of his patience waiting for it to come close enough for him to feel the heat of the flames that he intended to follow the lightning with. The flames proved unnecessary. Seconds after the lightning struck the steel casing of the machine it exploded into a mushroom-shaped ball of flames that lit up the area for several blocks. Before Ky could see anything revealed by the flames, the shock of the explosion knocked him backwards, causing him to land hard on his back nearly a block away from where he had stood. By the time he recovered, the heat had evaporated the water on the road and walls, obscuring everything except the fire in a haze of steam. The fire itself had begun to pump thick, black, acrid smoke into the streets as the stench of burning rubber overpowered all other smells. Ky started forward, stopping after a few steps as his body became wracked with pain. He glanced at his chest and saw the blisters forming, then the skin around those blisters beginning to melt. He immediately immersed himself in the green flames that would heal the wounds and retreated down a side street. He had never experienced burning before and wondered what kind of fire would be capable of doing that to him.

He did not have much time to wonder as another of the machines rumbled towards him. He ran to the next crossroad, sent lightning into the machine and darted behind the building. The first one taught him not to wait. As Ky expected, the buildings protected him from the fury of the blast, but somehow they did not protect him from the burning. He paused just long enough to coat himself in green flames, keeping them around his body like a shield, then ran to the next intersection. Two of the machines now burned in the streets. The brilliance of their pyres served as beacons that Ky could use as landmarks. He knew this time he would not return to his starting point. His body glowed green as he ran through the streets. He wanted to be found so the glow aided his purpose. Three more of the lumbering machines fell to his lightning. The third of these managed to fire a projectile of some sort before being destroyed. It impacted against the stone building across the road from where Ky had taken refuge, exploding and filling the road with liquid flame. Ky felt the burning again through his shield and ran to get out of range. He sprinted through two more intersections and approached the next. There he finally found something different. He froze in the middle of the road. Two blocks away from him, three of the machines rumbled side by side. None was moving, but Ky could tell they were active and he had the feeling they were waiting for him. Behind them, just visible in the light shed by the machines, a set of gray stone stairs, faded into the darkness. His mind was brought back to the present by the sound of three projectiles leaving the machines. Ky recognized the 'thwop' sound they made and ran to take cover behind the closest building, intensifying his flame shield as he dived behind the wall. He grinned when the liquid flame engulfed the area. His shield protected him from the pain. He heard the rumbling of the machines change and the first sign of the rhythmic movement of the treads. They were coming for him. Ky peeked around the side of the building and sent lightning into the center machine then hugged the wall and waited. He remembered the shock-wave made by the first machine he destroyed and knew the wall would protect him from it. This time there were three explosions and the area lit up like midday. The heat from the blasts evaporated the rain before it could reach the ground. Ky watched the liquid flames race away from the explosions as the shock-wave roared through the intersection. He waited a moment longer, then crept around the corner. Thick, black smoke blocked any glimpse of the stairs Ky had seen earlier. The smoke also made it impossible for Ky to determine if there were any other way to reach the stairs. Hoping that his shield would protect him enough to

make it through, Ky started forward. He could feel the intensity of the heat. His cloak, although pelted with rain, remained dry. Ky took his time, one step followed by another, his body ready to retreat if the inferno he planned to travel through penetrated his shield. As Ky neared the blaze, he began to feel his skin burn. He backed away a few steps and searched for a way around the wreckage. The area appeared to be a cul-de-sac and both directions brought him closer to the wreckage than he wanted to go, but he felt that the stairs would lead him to his sister, so he took the side nearest him and ran, hugging the wall as closely as he could. His feet splashed through puddles of molten steel and his skin blistered as he sprinted past the wreckage. Once on the far side, Ky found a small protected alcove beside the stair. He crouched as far into the corner as he could and let the green flames heal the damage as he glared at the burning heap of machinery. The wall of the alcove blocked his view of the stairs, and made it necessary to make one more sprint close to the wreckage. Ky thought about the next part of his trek before moving. If he were in charge, more guards would be on the stairs. Ky did not like the fact that he would have to run into them blindly. He wondered if they were resistant to the strange fire that caused him so much pain. He finally decided to trust in his shield and slid along the cul-de-sac wall to make the turn into the stairs less acute. He hoped that whatever waited on the stairs would not expect him to make it past the inferno as he sprinted forward. Cursing through the pain, he jumped onto the first step. The height of the individual steps had surprised him, each being as tall as his mid-thigh. He sent a sheet of flames up the stairway as he rushed forward. Ky's guess that more guards would be on the stairs turned out to be correct. He also learned that they were not immune to the new fire as he passed the melted remains of the few that were stationed near the bottom. Nor were they immune to his fire as evidenced from the cries of pain that drifted down to Ky. The stairs made the climb tedious and tiresome. Ky slowed his pace after he had conquered the first ten steps. He had no idea how far he would have to go. Now that he was away from the inferno of the wreckage, the rain had managed to soak him again, making the climb even more difficult. Several steps later and more of the machines lumbered towards him from the road below. Lightning was magic, and tired him, but it was effective so he used it. He had no place to hide from the shock-wave that followed and Ky was thrown into the next step, knocking the wind from his body. He remained motionless until his breath returned, then sent more fire up the stairs and continued climbing.

Only piles of ash greeted him for the rest of his climb. At the top, Ky found a thirty foot tall steel door. He doubted knocking would gain him entrance, so he flared his body with the hottest flame he could and began melting his way through it. Three feet of steel later, he found himself in a massive entry hall. One step inside and he reverted to the green flame-shield. He found the room dimly lit, but dry.
